`Polyfold.StrongBundleChart.K`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleChart.continuous_fiber`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundleChart.Compatible`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleChart.Compatible.symm`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundleAtlas`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleAtlas.Equiv`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundleChart.compatible_of_locally`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleAtlas.equiv_iff`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundleAtlas.Equiv.trans`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleAtlas.equivalence`,
`Polyfold.IsStrongBundleRetraction.restrict`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleChart.restrict`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundleChart.Compatible.restrict`).** For $P : Y \to X$ with linear structures on the
fibres: a *strong bundle chart* is a chart $\varphi$ of the M-polyfold $X$, an sc-Banach space $F$,
a strong bundle retraction $R$ on a relatively open $U \subseteq C$ with base retract $O$, and a
homeomorphism $\Phi : P^{-1}(V) \to K = R(U \times F_0)$ with $\Phi(y)_1 = \varphi(P(y))$ and linear
on each fibre (hence continuous on fibres). Two charts are *compatible* if $\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1}$
and $\Phi \circ \Phi'^{-1}$ are sc-smooth between the overlaps on $[0]$ and, through the lift to
$F_1$, on $[1]$, and carry fibre components in $F_1$ to fibre components in $F'_1$. Atlases and
their equivalence as in V2.11; two atlases are equivalent iff every chart of one is compatible with
every chart of the other, and the relation is an equivalence relation (it rests on the locality of
compatibility: near a point of the overlap a transition factors through a chart of the middle atlas,
on $[0]$ and on $[1]$). A strong bundle chart restricts to every open $s \subseteq V$ (retraction
domain $U \cap r^{-1}(W)$ for $\varphi(s) = O \cap W$,
$K_s = \{(u, h) \in K \mid u \in \varphi(s)\}$, $\Phi$ unchanged), and restrictions of compatible
charts are compatible. A space is *Banachable* if it is linearly homeomorphic to a Banach space.
*Book:* Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50), pp. 67–68 (preprint pp. 51–52). *Hidden hypotheses:* $\varphi$ a chart of $X$ (the text: a
homeomorphism onto $O$); the $[1]$-transition condition. *Deviation (hypotheses explicit):* both
stated. The transitivity of the equivalence, which “an equivalence class of strong bundle atlases”
(Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51)) presupposes, and the restriction of charts, which the text uses silently (Lemma
5.1.2 (preprint 5.2)), are proved (Findings, Chapter 2, items 40, 42); a restriction whose retraction domain lies
inside a given open $W \ni 0$ of $E$ is not, since $U \cap W$ need not be invariant under $r$.

**V2.58 (Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51), strong bundles, $Y[0]$, $Y[1]$, $P[0]$, $P[1]$; `Polyfold.StrongBundle`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundleChart.toMChart`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleChart.Compatible.toMChart`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.atlas0`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.toMPolyfold0`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.isScSmoothMap_proj`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.doubleLevel`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.mem_doubleLevel_iff`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.oneChart`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.oneChart_compatible`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.atlas1`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.toMPolyfold1`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.isScSmoothMap_proj1`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.maximalAtlas`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.maximalAtlas_equiv`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.isChart_iff_exists_equiv`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.isChart_congr`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsChart.compatible`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsChart.restrict`).** A *strong
bundle* is a continuous surjection $P : Y \to X$, $Y$ Hausdorff paracompact, with Banachable fibres
and a strong bundle atlas. The charts $\Phi$ form an sc-smooth atlas of $Y$ (the M-polyfold $Y[0]$),
and $P : Y[0] \to X$ is sc-smooth. $Y_{m,k}$ ($k \le m + 1$) is the set of $y$ with
$\Phi(y) \in E_m \times F_k$ in the charts of the atlas around $y$; one chart around $y$ suffices.
The charts $\Phi[1] : y \mapsto (\Phi(y)_1, \Phi(y)_2$ lifted to $F_1)$, defined on $Y_{0,1}$ with
the topology they generate and onto the retracts $K[1]$, are pairwise compatible, their transition
maps being the $[1]$-transitions of Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50), and make $Y[1]$ an M-polyfold;
$P[1] : Y[1] \to X$ is sc-smooth. The charts of the strong bundle (compatible with the atlas) are
those of the maximal atlas, which is equivalent to the given one: a chart is one iff it belongs to
some atlas of the class, any two are compatible, restrictions of charts are charts, and equivalent
atlases have the same charts. *Book:* Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51) and the remarks after it, preprint p. 52. *Hidden
hypotheses:* the paracompactness of $Y[1]$ (proved, V2.64); for the chart-independence of
$Y_{m,m+1}$ and of $Y_{0,1}$, the $F_1$-condition on the $[1]$-transition (V2.57). *Deviation
(restated):* $Y[1]$ carries the topology generated by the charts $\Phi[1]$, as $X_m$ in §2.3 (preprint §2.2); the
charts are those induced by the given atlas. The notions defined through the charts compatible with
the atlas depend only on the class; those defined with the charts of the given atlas itself
($Y_{m,k}$, $Y[1]$ and its atlas, sc⁺-sections) are not shown invariant (Findings, Chapter 2, item
43).

**V2.59 (Definition 2.6.6 (preprint 2.52); `Polyfold.IsSection`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScSmoothSection`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.localRepOne`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsScPlusSection`).** A *section* is $f$
with $P \circ f = \mathrm{id}$; it is *sc-smooth* if it is sc-smooth $X \to Y[0]$, and an
*sc⁺-section* if in every chart of the atlas its fibre values lie in $F_1$ and its local
representative, lifted to $E_0 \times F_1$, is sc-smooth from $O$ into $K[1]$. *Book:* Definition
2.6.6 (preprint 2.52), p. 68 (preprint p. 53). *Deviation (restated):* sc⁺ is defined chart by chart; this is equivalent to the
text's definition: $f$ is an sc⁺-section iff $P \circ f = \mathrm{id}$ and $f = \iota \circ g$ for an
sc-smooth $g : X \to Y[1]$, $\iota : Y[1] \to Y$ the inclusion
(`Polyfold.StrongBundle.isScPlusSection_iff`).

**V2.60 (Definition 2.6.7 (preprint 2.53); `Polyfold.pullbackSpace`, `Polyfold.pullbackProj`,
`Polyfold.pullbackProj'`, `Polyfold.pullback_comm`, `Polyfold.continuous_pullbackProj`,
`Polyfold.isClosed_pullbackSpace`).** $f^*Y = \{(z, y) : P(y) = f(z)\}$ with the projections $P_f$,
$P'$; $P \circ P' = f \circ P_f$; $P_f$ is continuous, and $f^*Y$ is closed in $Z \times Y$ when $X$
is Hausdorff and $P$, $f$ are continuous. *Book:* Definition 2.6.7 (preprint 2.53), p. 69 (preprint p. 53). *Hidden hypotheses:*
none.

**V2.61 (Proposition 2.6.8 (preprint 2.54); `Polyfold.proposition_2_6_8`, `Polyfold.pullbackAtlas`,
`Polyfold.PullbackChartData`, `Polyfold.PullbackChartData.toChart`,
`Polyfold.PullbackChartData.transition_eqOn`, `Polyfold.PullbackChartData.transition_isScSmooth`,
`Polyfold.PullbackChartData.transitionOne_isScSmooth`,
`Polyfold.PullbackChartData.compatible_toChart`, `Polyfold.paracompactSpace_pullbackSpace`,
`Polyfold.pullbackFiberCLE`, `Polyfold.pullbackRetraction`,
`Polyfold.isStrongBundleRetraction_pullback`, `Polyfold.pullback_image`,
`Polyfold.isStrongBundleRetract_pullback`).** Let $P : Y \to X$ be a strong bundle and $f : Z \to X$
sc-smooth. Then $f^*Y$ is paracompact, and $P_f : f^*Y \to Z$ is a strong bundle whose atlas
consists of the pulled-back charts: for a strong bundle chart $\Phi$ over $\varphi$ and a chart
$\psi$ of $Z$ with $f(\operatorname{dom}\psi) \subseteq \operatorname{dom}\varphi$ and
$g = \varphi \circ f \circ \psi^{-1}$, the chart $\Phi_f(z, y) = (\psi(z), \mathrm{pr}_F\Phi(y))$
onto $K_g = \{(w, h) : w \in O_Z, (g(w), h) \in K\}$, the image of the strong bundle retraction
$R_g(w, h) = (r_Z(w), \Gamma(g(r_Z(w)), h))$. Its fibres are $P_f^{-1}(z) \cong P^{-1}(f(z))$ (a
linear homeomorphism). Transition maps of pulled-back charts are
$(w, h) \mapsto (\psi_2\psi_1^{-1}(w), \mathrm{pr}_F(\Phi_2\Phi_1^{-1})(g_1(w), h))$ and are
sc-smooth on $[0]$ and $[1]$. *Book:* Proposition 2.6.8 (preprint 2.54), p. 69 (preprint p. 53) ("the easy proof is left to the
reader"). *Hidden hypotheses:* $f^*Y$ paracompact (required by Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51), not mentioned);
proved from Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) for $Z$ and $Y[0]$. *Deviation (hypotheses explicit):* "natural structure"
is the atlas of all pulled-back charts. That the projection $P' : f^*Y \to Y$ is a strong bundle map
(sc-smooth on $[0]$ and $[1]$), which “natural” presumably also says, is not formalized (Findings,
Chapter 2, item 51).

**V2.62 (Theorem 2.7.1 (preprint 2.55), Smirnov's theorem; `Polyfold.metrizableSpace_of_locally`,
`Polyfold.metrizableSpace_of_partition`, `Polyfold.metrizableSpace_of_pullback`,
`Polyfold.cone_triangle`, `Polyfold.truncDist`, `Polyfold.paracompactSpace_of_metrizableSpace`).** A
paracompact Hausdorff space in which every point has a metrizable open neighbourhood is metrizable.
More generally, a space $Y$ with open metrizable subspaces $V_i$ and a locally finite family of
continuous $\rho_i \ge 0$ with $\operatorname{supp}\rho_i \subseteq V_i$, not all vanishing at any
point, is metrizable, with the metric $\sum_i |\rho_i(x) - \rho_i(y)| + \min(\rho_i(x), \rho_i(y))
\min(d_i(x, y), 1)$; and if $\pi : Y \to X$ is continuous into a paracompact Hausdorff $X$ whose
points have open neighbourhoods $U$ with $\pi^{-1}(U)$ metrizable, $Y$ is metrizable. Metrizable
spaces are paracompact. *Book:* Theorem 2.7.1 (preprint 2.55), p. 72 (preprint p. 56), quoted from Smirnov. *Deviation (stronger):*
proved, in the pull-back form used for $X_m$ and $TX$.

**V2.63 (restriction and locality of sc^k maps; `Polyfold.IsSck.of_subset`,
`Polyfold.IsScSmooth.of_subset`, `Polyfold.IsSc1.tangentMap_eqOn_of_subset`,
`Polyfold.IsSc1.of_locally`, `Polyfold.IsSck.of_locally`, `Polyfold.IsScSmooth.of_locally`,
`Polyfold.IsScSmooth.congr`).** On sc-domains: an $\mathrm{sc}^k$ map restricts to $\mathrm{sc}^k$ on
every smaller sc-domain, with the same tangent map there; a map that is $\mathrm{sc}^1$ (resp.
$\mathrm{sc}^k$, sc-smooth) on $U \cap W$ for an open $W$ around each point of $U$ is $\mathrm{sc}^1$
(resp. $\mathrm{sc}^k$, sc-smooth) on $U$; sc-smoothness depends only on the values on $U$. *Book:*
used without statement in §§2.1, 2.3 (preprint §2.1–§2.2) (Propositions 2.1.11, 2.3.1 (preprint 2.4, 2.10), Definitions 2.3.4–2.3.8 (preprint 2.13–2.14)). *Deviation (not
in the book):* infrastructure the text uses silently.

**V2.64 (the space $Y[1]$ and the inclusion $Y[1] \to Y[0]$; `Polyfold.StrongBundle.oneSet`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.mem_oneSet_iff`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.One`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.continuous_oneVal`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.metrizableSpace_one`,
`Polyfold.StrongBundle.paracompactSpace_one`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.isScSmoothMap_oneVal`).** For a
strong bundle $P : Y \to X$, $Y_{0,1}$ is the set of points whose fibre component lies in $F_1$ in
every chart of the atlas around them, and one such chart suffices. With the topology generated by the
charts $\Phi[1]$ (V2.58), the inclusion $Y[1] \to Y$ is continuous, so $Y[1]$ is Hausdorff; $Y[1]$ is
metrizable, hence paracompact; and the inclusion $Y[1] \to Y[0]$ is sc-smooth (in the charts
$\Phi[1]$, $\Phi$ it is $(u, h) \mapsto (u, \iota h)$). *Book:* not stated; the text takes $Y[1]$ to
be an M-polyfold on $Y_{0,1}$ (preprint p. 52). *Hidden hypotheses:* paracompactness of $Y[1]$, required by
Definition 2.3.4 (preprint 2.13). *Deviation (not in the book):* proved; metrizability by the pull-back form of
Smirnov's theorem over the paracompact base (V2.62), as in Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16).

**V2.65 (Proposition 2.1.13 (preprint 2.6), the 2021 statement; `Polyfold.proposition_2_1_13`).** Let
$r : U \to U$ and $s : V \to V$ be sc-smooth retractions onto the same retract $O$, $\rho$ an sc-smooth
retraction onto $O'$, and $f$ a map with $f(O) \subseteq O'$. Then (1) $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth on $U$
iff $f \circ s$ is sc-smooth on $V$; (2) if $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth, $T(f \circ r) = T(f \circ s)$ on
$TO = Tr(TU)$; (3) if $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth, $T(f \circ r)$ maps $TO$ into $TO'$. *Book:*
Proposition 2.1.13, p. 27 (preprint 2.6, p. 20); the 2021 statement of (3) has the hypothesis "$f
\circ r$ sc-smooth", which the preprint and 2017 statements lack and their proofs use. *Hidden
hypotheses:* $f(O) \subseteq O'$, contained in "$f : O \to O'$". *Deviation:* none. The Lean statement of
(3) in V2.5 already carried the 2021 hypothesis, so the 2021 change confirms the formalization's
reading. *Proof:* the conjunction of
`Polyfold.proposition_2_1_13_one` (both ways), `Polyfold.proposition_2_1_13_two` and
`Polyfold.proposition_2_1_13_three` (V2.5).

**V2.66 (Proposition 2.1.4, complete closed neighbourhoods in a retract;
`Polyfold.ScRetraction.exists_isClosed_retract_inter_closedBall`,
`Polyfold.IsScRetract.exists_isComplete_closure`, `Polyfold.proposition_2_1_4`).** Let $O$ be an
sc-smooth retract in $E$, with the metric $d_O(x, y) = |x - y|_0$ of $E_0$. Every $x \in O$ has open
neighbourhoods $V \subseteq W$ in $O$ with $\mathrm{cl}_O(V) \subseteq W$ and $\mathrm{cl}_O(V)$
complete for $d_O$; $W$ can be chosen inside any given neighbourhood of $x$. For a retraction $r$
onto $O$, $O \cap \bar B_\varepsilon(x)$ is closed in $E_0$ for all small $\varepsilon > 0$. *Book:*
Proposition 2.1.4, p. 22, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(stronger):* $W$ arbitrarily small. *Proof:* with $O \cap \bar B_\varepsilon(x)$ in place of the
text's $V'$ with $r(V') \subseteq V'$: for $\bar B_\varepsilon(x) \cap C \subseteq U$, a limit of
points of $O \cap \bar B_\varepsilon(x)$ lies in $U$ and is fixed by $r$; a closed subset of the
Banach space $E_0$ is complete.

**V2.67 (Definition 2.1.5, locally complete spaces; `Polyfold.AdmitsCompleteMetricOn`,
`Polyfold.admitsCompleteMetricOn_of_isComplete`, `Polyfold.AdmitsCompleteMetricOn.metrizableSpace`,
`Polyfold.AdmitsCompleteMetricOn.of_isEmbedding`, `Polyfold.AdmitsCompleteMetricOn.mono`,
`Polyfold.isComplete_inter_of_isClosed`, `Polyfold.IsLocallyComplete`,
`Polyfold.IsLocallyComplete.exists_subset`, `Polyfold.IsLocallyComplete.regularSpace`,
`Polyfold.IsLocallyComplete.t1Space`, `Polyfold.IsLocallyComplete.t2Space`,
`Polyfold.isLocallyComplete_of_completeSpace`, `Polyfold.isLocallyComplete_real`,
`Polyfold.isLocallyComplete_of_metric`).** A topological space $X$ is locally complete if every $x$
has open $V \ni x$ and $W$ with $\mathrm{cl}_X(V) \subseteq W$ such that $W$ carries a metric $d$
inducing its subspace topology for which $\mathrm{cl}_X(V)$ is complete. Then $W$ can be chosen inside
any neighbourhood of $x$, and $X$ is regular, $T_1$ and Hausdorff. A complete metric space is locally
complete ($\mathbb R$ in particular), and so is a metric space in which every point has open $V
\subseteq W$, $\mathrm{cl}(V) \subseteq W$, with $\mathrm{cl}(V)$ complete. *Book:* Definition 2.1.5,
p. 23, new in the 2021 edition, for a Hausdorff space $X$, with (1) the metric on $W(x)$ and (2) $V(x)
\subseteq W(x)$, $\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x)) \subseteq W(x)$, $\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x))$ complete. *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the Hausdorff assumption is not part of the definition; it
follows ($T_1$ from the metrizable $W$, regularity from the global condition $\mathrm{cl}_X(V)
\subseteq W$), so V2.70 and V2.71 need no Hausdorff hypothesis except for the conclusion $T_{3\frac12}$.
$V \subseteq W$ is a consequence, not a separate condition.

**V2.68 (Remark 2.1.6; `Polyfold.remark_2_1_6`, `Polyfold.IsLocallyCompleteRel`,
`Polyfold.IsLocallyComplete.isLocallyCompleteRel`).** If $\mathrm{cl}_X(V) \subseteq W$, the closure
of $V$ in the subspace $W$ is $\mathrm{cl}_X(V)$. The modified notion, in which $\mathrm{cl}_X(V)
\subseteq W$ is replaced by $V \subseteq W$ and completeness is asked of $\mathrm{cl}_W(V)$, is implied
by local completeness. *Book:* Remark 2.1.6, p. 23, new in the 2021 edition: the condition
$\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x)) \subseteq W(x)$ is global, and the modified definition is weaker. *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* "weaker" is proved here as the implication; that the modified
notion is strictly weaker is V2.91, an example (gap G.76, closed).

**V2.69 (Corollary 2.1.7; `Polyfold.corollary_2_1_7`, `Polyfold.isLocallyComplete_univ_retract`).**
An sc-smooth retract $O$, with the topology of $E_0$, is locally complete; so is $E_0$ itself. *Book:*
Corollary 2.1.7, p. 23, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Proof:* V2.66, with the
metric $d_O$ restricted to $W$ (`Polyfold.isLocallyComplete_of_metric`).

**V2.70 (Proposition 2.1.8; `Polyfold.IsLocallyComplete.of_isEmbedding`,
`Polyfold.proposition_2_1_8_1`, `Polyfold.proposition_2_1_8_2`,
`Polyfold.proposition_2_1_8_3`, `Polyfold.proposition_2_1_8_4`).** Let $X$ be locally
complete. (1) A locally closed subspace $A$ (open $\cap$ closed) is locally complete; (2) a space
homeomorphic to $X$ is locally complete; (3) an open subspace is locally complete. (4) A space $Y$
with an open cover $(Y_i)$ by locally complete subspaces such that every $z \in Y_i$ has an open $U
\ni z$, $U \subseteq Y_i$, with $\mathrm{cl}_Y(U) \subseteq Y_i$, is locally complete. More generally,
a space embedded in $X$ with locally closed image is locally complete. *Book:* Proposition 2.1.8, p.
24, new in the 2021 edition, for Hausdorff spaces. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):*
no Hausdorff hypothesis (V2.67). "Locally closed" is Mathlib's notion, equivalent to the text's use
("$U \cap A$ closed in $U$ for an open $U \ni a$"). *Proof:* (1)–(3) from the embedding statement;
(4) by transporting the metric of $W \subseteq Y_i$ to $W \subseteq Y$.

**V2.71 (Lemma 2.1.9 and Proposition 2.1.10; `Polyfold.lemma_2_1_9`,
`Polyfold.IsLocallyComplete.completelyRegularSpace`, `Polyfold.proposition_2_1_10`).** A locally
complete space is first countable and completely regular; if it is Hausdorff it is $T_{3\frac12}$
(Tychonoff). *Book:* Lemma 2.1.9 (countable neighbourhood bases) and Proposition 2.1.10 (Hausdorff
locally complete spaces are completely regular), p. 25, both new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* no Hausdorff hypothesis for complete regularity. *Proof:*
without sequences: the neighbourhood filter of $x$ is the image of that of the metrizable open $W$,
and the bump function is built in $W$ and extended by a constant outside $\mathrm{cl}_X(V)$.
Mathlib's complete regularity separates with $f(x) = 0$ and $f = 1$ on the closed set (the text's
$\beta$ is $1 - f$).

**V2.72 (Lemma 2.2.1, the levels of a connected relatively open set; `Polyfold.ScBanach.lvlSetInfty`,
`Polyfold.ScBanach.smoothSeq`, `Polyfold.ScBanach.toBase_smoothSeq`, `Polyfold.ScBanach.smoothSeq_mem`,
`Polyfold.ScBanach.smoothSeq_zero`, `Polyfold.ScBanach.image_lvlSetInfty`,
`Polyfold.ScBanach.joinedIn_lvlSetInfty_of_segment`, `Polyfold.IsPartialQuadrant.exists_smooth_near`,
`Polyfold.IsRelOpenInQuadrant.exists_ball_inter_subset`, `Polyfold.lemma_2_2_1`,
`Polyfold.lemma_2_2_1_infty`).** Let $U$ be relatively open in a partial quadrant $C$ and
connected. For every $k \in \mathbb N$ the level $U_k = U \cap E_k$, with the topology of $E_k$, is
path-connected; and $U_\infty$, represented as the compatible sequences $(v_m) \in \prod_m E_m$ with
$v_0 \in U$ (with the product topology, i.e. the topology of all the norms $|\cdot|_m$), is
path-connected. Smooth points are dense in every level $C_m$, and the image of this $U_\infty$ in
$E_0$ is $U \cap E_\infty$. *Book:* Lemma 2.2.1, p. 30, new in the 2021 edition, for $k \in \mathbb N
\cup \{\infty\}$. *Hidden hypotheses:* the topology of $E_\infty$, which the text does not specify.
*Deviation (explicit):* $U_\infty$ carries the inverse-limit topology. *Proof:* not the text's
polygon along a path $\sigma$ in $U_0$: the set of points of $U$ near which every point of the level
is joined to a fixed one is open and closed in the connected $U$; segments in convex pieces $B_\varepsilon
\cap C$ join smooth points, and smooth points are dense.

**V2.73 (Lemma 2.2.2, Definition 2.2.3 and Theorem 2.2.4; `Polyfold.lemma_2_2_2`,
`Polyfold.definition_2_2_3`, `Polyfold.theorem_2_2_4`,
`Polyfold.IsScRetract.locallyPathConnectedSpace`).** For a retraction $r : U \to U$ onto $O$, $x \in
O$ and $V = V' \cap U$ with $V' \ni x$ open in $E_0$, the set $W = V \cap r^{-1}(V)$ is relatively open
in $C$, contains $x$, and satisfies $W \cap O = V \cap O$, $r(W) \subseteq W$, $r(W) = O \cap V$.
Mathlib's local path-connectedness is the text's (every open neighbourhood of $z$ contains an open
path-connected neighbourhood). A retract is locally path-connected. *Book:* Lemma 2.2.2, p. 31,
Definition 2.2.3 and Theorem 2.2.4, p. 32, all new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Proof:* Theorem 2.2.4 was already proved for Chapter 7 (`Polyfold.IsScRetract.locallyPathConnectedSpace`),
joining nearby points by $\tau \mapsto r(o + \tau(p - o))$ instead of through Lemma 2.2.2 and the
components of $W(x)$.

**V2.74 (Definition 2.2.5 and Proposition 2.2.6; `Polyfold.IsAlmostLocallyContractible`,
`Polyfold.proposition_2_2_6`, `Polyfold.isAlmostLocallyContractible_univ`).** A space $Z$ is
almost locally contractible if for every $z$ and open $V \ni z$ there are an open $W$, $z \in W
\subseteq V$, and a continuous $\Phi : [0, 1] \times W \to Z$ with values in $V$, $\Phi(0, y) = y$,
$\Phi(t, z) = z$ and $\Phi(1, y) = z$. An sc-smooth retract is almost locally contractible; so is
$E_0$. *Book:* Definition 2.2.5 and Proposition 2.2.6, p. 33, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Proof:* the text's $\Phi(t, y) = r((1 - t)y + tx)$ on $W = B_\varepsilon(x) \cap
O$.

**V2.75 (the footnote to Definition 2.3.4 (preprint 2.13), paracompactness, and the convention of
Appendix 2.7.2; `Polyfold.IsLocallyFiniteSetFamily`, `Polyfold.IsParacompactStar`,
`Polyfold.isParacompactStar_iff`, `Polyfold.definition_2_3_4`, `Polyfold.isParacompactStar_real`,
`Polyfold.IsParacompactBySubcover`, `Polyfold.not_isParacompactBySubcover_real`).** A space is
paracompact* if every open cover has a locally finite open cover refining it, with no separation
axiom; this is Mathlib's paracompactness, so "Hausdorff paracompact*" is exactly the hypothesis of
the M-polyfold structure (V2.12); $\mathbb R$ is paracompact*. Under the reading "every open cover has
a locally finite open **sub**cover", $\mathbb R$ is not paracompact (the cover by the intervals $(-n-1,
n+1)$). *Book:* Definition 2.3.4, p. 35 (preprint 2.13, p. 23), with the footnote, new in the 2021
edition, that paracompactness does not include the Hausdorff property; Appendix 2.7.2, p. 72 (and
2017 Appendix 2.6.2, p. 51), states the convention with a locally finite open subcovering. *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the footnote changes nothing for M-polyfolds, whose
Hausdorff property is required separately. The subcover wording of Appendix 2.7.2 does not hold as
we read it for $\mathbb R$; it is read as "refinement" (possible misprint), as in the footnote.

**V2.76 (Lemma 2.3.5 and Lemma 2.7.2; `Polyfold.lemma_2_7_2`,
`Polyfold.exists_isOpen_closure_subset_of_paracompact`, `Polyfold.lemma_2_3_5`).** In a regular
space every open $U \ni x$ contains an open $V \ni x$ with $\mathrm{cl}(V) \subseteq U$. In a Hausdorff
paracompact space, and so in an M-polyfold, every open $W \ni x$ contains such a $V$ inside any given
neighbourhood of $x$. *Book:* Lemma 2.3.5, p. 35, and Lemma 2.7.2, p. 72, new in the 2021 edition;
Lemma 2.7.2 is stated for regular Hausdorff spaces. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):*
Lemma 2.7.2 needs only regularity. *Proof:* Mathlib (regular spaces; Hausdorff paracompact spaces
are normal).

**V2.77 (Propositions 2.3.6 and 2.3.7; `Polyfold.MChart.isLocallyComplete_source`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isLocallyComplete`, `Polyfold.proposition_2_3_6`,
`Polyfold.proposition_2_3_7`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.locallyPathConnectedSpace`).** A chart domain
of an M-polyfold is locally complete. An M-polyfold $X$ is locally complete, with $W(x)$ inside any
given neighbourhood of $x$: there are open $V \subseteq W$ around $x$ with $\mathrm{cl}_X(V) \subseteq
W$ and a metric on $W$ inducing its topology for which $\mathrm{cl}_X(V)$ is complete. An M-polyfold
is locally path-connected. *Book:* Propositions 2.3.6 and 2.3.7, p. 36, new in the 2021 edition.
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Proof:* Proposition 2.3.6 by the open-cover part of V2.70, the cover by
chart domains ($V \cong O$, V2.69 and V2.70 (2)) with condition (b) from V2.76, instead of the
text's direct argument in a chart; Proposition 2.3.7 was already proved for Chapter 7
(`Polyfold.MPolyfold.locallyPathConnectedSpace`).

**V2.78 (Definitions 2.5.18 and 2.5.19, tame sub-M-polyfolds; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasTameInducedStructure`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasReducedComplementAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasReducedComplementAt_self`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.TameSubData`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsTameSubMPolyfold`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsTameSubMPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasTameInducedStructure_univ`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isTameSubMPolyfold_univ`).** For a sub-M-polyfold $Y$ of $X$, the induced
structure is tame if the M-polyfold $Y$ (V2.24) is tame. For a tame $X$, $Y$ is a tame sub-M-polyfold
if every $y \in Y$ lies in an open $V$ with an sc-smooth retraction $r$ of the sub-M-polyfold data
($r(V) = Y \cap V$) such that $d_X(r(x)) = d_X(x)$ on $V$ and, at every smooth $y \in Y \cap V$, in
some chart around $y$ with a presentation of the partial quadrant, the tangent space of the chart
image $Q$ of $Y$ has an sc-complement $A$ in $T_zO$ inside the reduced tangent space $T_zO \cap E_z$
($(T_zO)_m = (T_zQ)_m \oplus A_m$ on every level). A tame sub-M-polyfold is a sub-M-polyfold; in a tame
$X$, $Y = X$ is a tame sub-M-polyfold with tame induced structure. *Book:* Definitions 2.5.18, p. 62,
and 2.5.19, p. 63, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):*
condition (3) is stated in a chart, for some chart around $y$ ($T_yX$ has no linear structure here,
gap G.7); its independence of the chart is V2.99, the remark that a tame sub-M-polyfold is tame
V2.100, and the examples in $[0, \infty)^2 \times \mathbb R$ V2.101 (gap G.77, closed).

**V2.79 (faces of open sets and the corner axioms; `Polyfold.TameBoundary.faceAt`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.IsFaceIn`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.facesThrough`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.LocalPieces`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.IsCornerIndex`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.faceAt_inter_eq`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.faceExt`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.faceExt_unique`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.exists_faceExt_eq`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.isCornerIndex_zero`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_localPieces_chart`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isCornerIndex_degIndex`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isFaceIn_univ_iff`).** For a map $d :
X \to \mathbb N$ on a space $X$ and an open $V$, a face of $V$ is the closure in $V$ of a connected
component of $V \cap \{d = 1\}$; the faces of $X$ itself are those of V2.44. The corner axioms ask
that $d$ be upper semicontinuous and that every $x$ have an open $D$ such that every $y \in D$ has, in
arbitrarily small neighbourhoods, $d(y)$ preconnected pieces of $\{d = 1\}$ accumulating at $y$ and
covering $\{d = 1\}$ near $y$, no preconnected subset of $D \cap \{d = 1\}$ meeting two of them. For
open $U \subseteq V$, a face $\theta$ of $U$ lies in a unique face $\theta'$ of $V$, the one containing
it. The degeneracy index of a tame M-polyfold satisfies the corner axioms; so does $d \equiv 0$.
*Book:* not stated; §2.7.4, pp. 78–82, new in the 2021 edition, uses the faces of open subsets $V$
(Definition 2.5.10 for $V$ with its induced structure, whose degeneracy index is $d_X|V$ by
Proposition 2.4.4) and the local structure of a tame chart. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not
in the book):* all of §2.7.4 is proved from the corner axioms, so that it applies to the object spaces
of tame ep-groupoids (2021 §7.6.5); the local pieces in a tame chart come from the local face
structure of V2.45.

**V2.80 (Proposition 2.7.5; `Polyfold.TameBoundary.exists_nbhd_faces_mem`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.proposition_2_7_5`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.proposition_2_7_5`).** In a tame
M-polyfold (more generally, for $d$ with the corner axioms) every $x$ has an open $V \ni x$ with (1)
$d(y) \le d(x)$ on $V$, (2) every $y \in V$ in exactly $d(y)$ faces of $V$, (3) an open $U(x)$, $x \in
U(x) \subseteq V$, such that every face of $V$ meeting $U(x)$ contains $x$; (3) holds for every open $V
\ni x$. *Book:* Proposition 2.7.5, p. 78, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.

**V2.81 (Definition 2.7.6 and Proposition 2.7.7; `Polyfold.TameBoundary.IsFaceStructuredOpen`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.faceStructuredOpens`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.faceStructuredNbhds`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.faceStructuredNbhdsAt`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.faceStructuredNbhds_eq_iUnion`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.faceStructuredNbhdsAt_nonempty`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.sUnion_faceStructuredNbhds`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.mem_faceStructuredNbhds_of_subset`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.inter_mem_faceStructuredNbhds`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.inter_mem_faceStructuredNbhdsAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.proposition_2_7_7`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.isFaceStructuredOpen_quadrant`).** An open $V$ is face-structured if
every $y \in V$ lies in exactly $d(y)$ faces of $V$; $N_X$ is the set of nonempty face-structured $V$
with $d|V$ bounded, $N_{X,x}$ the set of $V \in N_X$ with $x \in V$ and $d \le d(x)$ on $V$, and $N_X =
\bigcup_x N_{X,x}$. For a tame $X$: every $N_{X,x}$ is nonempty (so $N_X$ covers $X$); a nonempty open
subset of a member of $N_X$ is in $N_X$; nonempty intersections of members of $N_X$ are in $N_X$, and
$N_{X,x}$ is closed under intersections. Every open subset of $[0, \infty)^n \oplus W$ is
face-structured. *Book:* Definition 2.7.6, p. 79, and Proposition 2.7.7, p. 80, new in the 2021
edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.

**V2.82 (Definitions 2.7.8 and 2.7.9, the category $L_X$ and the boundary structure functor;
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.IsMor`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.IsMor.trans`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.LObj`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.boundaryFunctor`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.boundaryFunctor_map_injective`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.boundaryFunctor_map_bijective`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.LocalBoundaryCategory`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.boundaryStructureFunctor`).** The objects of $L_X$ are the pairs $(x, V)$ with $d(x)
\ge 1$ and $V \in N_{X,x}$; there is a morphism $(x, V) \to (y, W)$, and then only one, iff $V
\subseteq W$, $x$ lies in $d(x)$ faces of $W$ and each of them contains $y$; morphisms compose. The
functor $F_X$ sends $(x, V)$ to the set of faces of $V$ through $x$ and a morphism to $\theta \mapsto
\theta'$, the face of $W$ containing $\theta$; $F_X(\varphi)$ is injective, and bijective for a
morphism $(x, V) \to (x, W)$. *Book:* Definitions 2.7.8, p. 80, and 2.7.9, p. 81, new in the 2021
edition, with the text's argument for the composition and the injection (2.43). *Hidden hypotheses:*
none. *Deviation (restated):* $L_X$ is a preorder (a thin category) and $F_X$ takes values in types;
$\theta'$ is defined as the union of the faces of $W$ containing $\theta$, which is the text's "the
face of $W$ through $x$ and $y$ with $\theta \cap \theta'$ open in $\theta$" (`Polyfold.TameBoundary.faceExt_unique`).

**V2.83 (Definition 2.7.10, the set $bX$ and the map $B$; `Polyfold.TameBoundary.BTriple`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.BRel`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.BRel.refl`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.BRel.symm`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.BRel.trans`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.bSetoid`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.BSpace`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.bMap`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.range_bMap`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.encard_bMap_preimage`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.TameBoundarySpace`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.tameBoundaryMap`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.range_tameBoundaryMap`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.encard_tameBoundaryMap_preimage`).** An admissible triple is $(x, V, \theta)$ with
$(x, V)$ an object of $L_X$ and $\theta$ a face of $V$ through $x$; $(x, V, \theta) \sim (x', V',
\theta')$ iff $x = x'$ and some $V'' \in N_{X,x}$, $V'' \subseteq V \cap V'$, has a face $\theta''$
through $x$ sent to $\theta$ and to $\theta'$. This is an equivalence relation; $bX$ is the set of
classes and $B[x, V, \theta] = x$. The image of $B$ is $\partial X = \{d \ge 1\}$, and $B^{-1}(x)$ has
exactly $d(x)$ points. *Book:* Definition 2.7.10, p. 81, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:*
none. *Deviation (stronger):* the fibre count, the set-level content of Theorem 2.7.13 (4).

**V2.84 (Definition 2.7.11 and (2.44), the sets $U(x, V, \theta)$ and the maps $\Phi$;
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.uSet`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.phi`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.phi_injective`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.reach`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.IsCenteredAt`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.isOpen_reach`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.bMap_image_uSet`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.phi_bijective_of_isCenteredAt`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.isCenteredAt_reach`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.reach_mem_faceStructuredNbhdsAt`).**
$U(x, V, \theta)$ is the set of classes with a representative $(y, V', \theta')$ such that $y \in
\theta$, there is a morphism $(y, V') \to (x, V)$, and it sends $\theta'$ to $\theta$; $\Phi_{(x, V,
\theta)} : U(x, V, \theta) \to \theta$ is $[y, V', \theta'] \mapsto y$. $\Phi$ is injective, and its image is
$\theta \cap V^x$, where $V^x = \{y \in V : \text{every face of } V \text{ through } y \text{ contains }
x\}$ is open. If every face of $V$ contains $x$ ($V$ centred at $x$), $\Phi$ is a bijection onto
$\theta$; $V^x$ is centred at $x$, and $V^x \in N_{X,x}$ for $V \in N_{X,x}$. *Book:* Definition 2.7.11
and (2.44), p. 82, new in the 2021 edition: $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ is a canonical bijection onto
$\theta$. *Hidden hypotheses:* that $V$ be small enough; the text says, for the topology of $bX$ (p. 85), that the
main point is to take $V$ sufficiently small. *Deviation (narrower):* the bijection is proved for $V$ centred at $x$; for
every $V \in N_{X,x}$ it does not hold as we read it (V2.85). The centred neighbourhoods are cofinal in
$N_{X,x}$, which is what "$V$ sufficiently small" provides.

**V2.85 ((2.44) for every $V \in N_{X,x}$: an example in $[0, \infty)^3$;
`Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.dq`, `Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.isCornerIndex_dq`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.dq_eq`, `Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.part`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.dq_eq_one_iff`, `Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.subset_part`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.faceAt_subset_coord_eq_zero`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.exists_part_mem_faceAt`, `Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.slab`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.slab_mem_faceStructuredNbhdsAt`, `Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.slabFace`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.counterTriple`, `Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.exists_face_not_mem`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.pt_010_not_mem_image`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.phi_not_surjective`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundaryExample.not_forall_bijective_phi`).** In the tame M-polyfold $X = [0,
\infty)^3 \oplus W$ ($W$ any sc-Banach space), let $x = (0, 0, 1)$, $V = \{p_0 < 1/2,\ 1/2 < p_1 + p_2 <
3/2\}$ (a convex open slab around the segment from $x$ to $(0, 1, 0)$), and $\theta$ the face of $V$
through that segment. Then $V \in N_{X,x}$, $d_X(x) = 2$, $(x, V, \theta)$ is an admissible triple,
$(0, 1, 0) \in \theta$ also lies on the face of $V$ in $\{p_2 = 0\}$, which misses $x$, and so $(0, 1,
0)$ is not in the image of $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$: $\Phi$ is not onto $\theta$, and not every
$\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ is a bijection. *Book:* Definition 2.7.11, (2.44), p. 82, new in the 2021
edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):* the example shows that (2.44) does
not hold as we read it for every $V \in N_{X,x}$, and that some restriction such as "$V$ centred at $x$"
(V2.84) is needed. *Proof:* $d_X(p)$ is the number of vanishing half-line coordinates, a face of an
open $V$ through a point with only $p_k = 0$ lies in $\{p_k = 0\}$.

**V2.86 (Lemma 2.7.15, the topology of $bX$; `Polyfold.TameBoundary.IsBOpen`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.BTriple.exists_shrink`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.BRel.exists_common`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.eq_of_mem_uSet`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.isBOpen_iff`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.bTopology`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.isOpen_iff_isBOpen`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.isOpen_iff_forall_uSet`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.lemma_2_7_15`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_2_7_15`).** A set $\mathcal U \subseteq bX$ is in $T_{bX}$ if every class $p
\in \mathcal U$ has a representative $(x, V, \theta)$ and a set $O \ni p$, $O \subseteq \mathcal U \cap U(x,
V, \theta)$, with $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}(O)$ open in $\theta$; equivalently, if every $p \in \mathcal U$
has a representative with $U(x, V, \theta) \subseteq \mathcal U$. These sets are the open sets of a
topology. *Book:* the description of $T_{bX}$ in §2.7.4.3 and Lemma 2.7.15, p. 85, new in the 2021
edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* $p \in O$, without which $O = \emptyset$ would make every set
open. *Deviation (explicit):* the first description is read with $O$ containing the class. *Proof:*
from the second description and a common refinement of equivalent triples, without the
sc-smoothness of the transition maps that the text's proof of the intersection axiom uses.

**V2.87 (Proposition 2.7.12, topological part; `Polyfold.TameBoundary.isOpen_uSet`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.isTopologicalBasis_uSet`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.continuous_bMap`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.exists_nbhd_faceExt_inter_subset`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.exists_isOpen_bMap_image`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.isOpenEmbedding_phi`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.phiHomeomorph`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.proposition_2_7_12`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.proposition_2_7_12`).** The sets $U(x, V, \theta)$ are open and form a basis of
$T_{bX}$; $B$ is continuous; every $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ is an open embedding into $\theta$, and a
homeomorphism onto $\theta$ for $V$ centred at $x$. For two triples, the image of $U(x, V, \theta) \cap
U(x', V', \theta')$ is open in $\theta$ and in $\theta'$, and the transition map
$\Phi_{(x', V', \theta')} \circ \Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}^{-1}$ is the identity on underlying points of $X$.
*Book:* Proposition 2.7.12, p. 83, new in the 2021 edition: the images are open and the transition
map is an sc-diffeomorphism. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* the sc-diffeomorphism
statement is not part of this item: for representatives with $V$ centred at $x$ it is proved with the
M-polyfold structure of $bX$ (V2.103), and for every representative in V2.104 (gap G.78, closed).

**V2.88 (Proposition 2.7.16; `Polyfold.TameBoundary.tripleOf`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.exists_mem_uSet_tripleOf`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.metrizableSpace_preimage`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.proposition_2_7_16`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.proposition_2_7_16`).** For $d$
with the corner axioms on a Hausdorff $X$, $bX$ is Hausdorff; on a metrizable $X$, $bX$ is metrizable.
For a tame M-polyfold, $T_{bX}$ is Hausdorff and metrizable. *Book:* Proposition 2.7.16, pp. 85–87, new
in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Proof:* not the text's paracompactness argument
(a locally finite refinement built from one of the cover $(V_x)$ of $\partial X$): the pull-back form
of Smirnov's theorem (V2.62) along $B$, each point having an open neighbourhood $B^{-1}(W) \cap
\bigcup_\theta U(x, W, \theta)$ embedded into the metrizable $X \times \mathbb R^{\text{faces}}$ by $B$ and
the indicators of the clopen sets $U(x, W, \theta)$.

**V2.89 (Theorem 2.7.13, topological part, and Definition 2.7.14; `Polyfold.TameBoundary.eq_of_isOpen_uSet`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.theorem_2_7_13_topology`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.theorem_2_7_13`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.tameBoundary`).** For a tame M-polyfold $X$: (1) $bX$ carries the metrizable
topology $T_{bX}$; every $U(x, V, \theta)$ is open and every $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ is an open embedding
into $\theta$; $T_{bX}$ is the only topology in which every $U(x, V, \theta)$ is open and every $\Phi$ maps
open sets to relatively open subsets of $\theta$; $B : bX \to X$ is continuous, with image $\partial X$,
and every $x$ has exactly $d_X(x)$ preimages. The tame boundary is $B$ as a continuous map. *Book:*
Theorem 2.7.13, pp. 83–84, and Definition 2.7.14, p. 84, new in the 2021 edition: (1) the metrizable
topology, (2) a natural tame M-polyfold structure on $bX$, (3) $B$ sc-smooth, (4) $d_X(B(p)) - 1 =
d_{bX}(p)$, characterized by: every $U(x, V, \theta)$ open and every $\Phi$ a homeomorphism and an
sc-diffeomorphism onto $\theta$. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* this item is (1) and the
topological half of the characterization; "homeomorphism onto $\theta$" is proved for $V$ centred at
$x$ (V2.84, V2.87), the open embedding for every $V$. Parts (2)–(4) beyond the fibre count are V2.102
and V2.106; the sc-diffeomorphism half of the characterization is V2.103 for centred representatives and
V2.104 for every representative, with image $\theta \cap V^x$ (V2.105) (gap G.78, closed).

**V2.90 (the tame quadrant as a witness; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.quadrantPolyfold`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.quadrantPolyfold_isTame`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.quadrantPolyfold_encard_preimage`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.quadrantPolyfold_tameBoundarySpace_nonempty`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.quadrantPolyfold_univ`).** The quadrant $[0, \infty)^n \oplus W$ is a tame
M-polyfold; its corner $0$ has exactly $n$ preimages under $B$, so $bX \ne \emptyset$ for $n \ge 1$; and
$Y = X$ has a tame induced structure and is a tame sub-M-polyfold. *Book:* not stated. *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):* satisfiability of the hypotheses of V2.78–V2.89.

**V2.91 (Remark 2.1.6, strictness: the K-topology on $\mathbb R$; `Polyfold.remark_2_1_6_strict`,
`Polyfold.isLocallyCompleteRel_of_forall_isCompletelyMetrizable`,
`Polyfold.isCompletelyMetrizableSpace_of_isEmbedding_compl_range`, `Polyfold.kSeq`, `Polyfold.kTop`,
`Polyfold.RealKTop`, `Polyfold.RealKTop.not_regularSpace`, `Polyfold.RealKTop.not_isLocallyComplete`,
`Polyfold.RealKTop.isLocallyCompleteRel`).** A space in which every point has an open, completely metrizable
neighbourhood satisfies the modified definition of Remark 2.1.6 (with $V = W$). A space embedded in $\mathbb R$ onto
the complement of a sequence is completely metrizable. Let $\mathbb R_K$ be $\mathbb R$ with the K-topology, generated
by the usual open sets and $\mathbb R \setminus K$, $K = \{1/(n+1) : n \in \mathbb N\}$. It is Hausdorff; it satisfies
the modified definition, the points outside $K$ lying in $\mathbb R \setminus K$ and those of $K$ in $\mathbb R
\setminus \{0\}$, both with the usual subspace topology; and it is not regular, so not locally complete (V2.67). So
some Hausdorff space satisfies the modified definition and not Definition 2.1.5. *Book:* Remark 2.1.6, p. 23, new in
the 2021 edition: the modified definition would be weaker. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the
book):* the example; with V2.68 the remark holds as we read it, and "weaker" is strict (gap G.76, closed).
*Proof:* every closed neighbourhood of $0$ in $\mathbb R_K$ meets $K$, through irrational points near $1/(n+1)$.
The complement of a sequence $(a_n)$ embeds as a closed set into $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R^{\mathbb N}$ by $y
\mapsto (y, ((y - a_n)^{-1})_n)$, in place of the theorem that $G_\delta$ subsets of complete metric spaces are
completely metrizable, which Mathlib lacks.

**V2.92 (Definition 2.1.16 (preprint 2.9), bundle retractions and bundle maps;
`Polyfold.ScRetraction.IsBundleRetractionOver`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.tangentRetraction_isBundleRetractionOver`,
`Polyfold.IsBundleMapOn`, `Polyfold.IsBundleMapOn.fst_eq`,
`Polyfold.IsScSmoothRetractMap.retractTangentMap_isBundleMapOn`).** A retraction $R$ of $E \oplus F$ (V2.1) is a
bundle retraction covering the retraction $r$ of $E$ if its domain is $U \oplus F$, $U$ the domain of $r$, and $R(u,
v) = (r(u), \rho(u)v)$ there, with $\rho(u)$ a continuous linear map of $F_0$. A map $\Phi$ from $E \oplus F$ to $E'
\oplus F'$ is a bundle map on $B$ covering $a$ if $\Phi(u, v) = (a(u), \phi(u)v)$ on $B$ with $\phi(u)$ continuous
linear; then $p' \circ \Phi = a \circ p$ on $B$. The tangent retraction $Tr$ is a bundle retraction covering the
level-$1$ retraction $r^1$, and for an sc-smooth $f$ between retracts $Tf$ is a bundle map on $TO$ covering the
level-$1$ map $f^1$. *Book:* Definition 2.1.16, p. 29 (preprint 2.9, p. 22). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(restated):* the definition fixes the shape of the maps; sc-smoothness and $R \circ R = R$ are part of the data (a
retraction of V2.1, an sc-smooth map of V2.6), and $\rho(u)$ is continuous on level $0$, which the text's linear
$\rho(u, \cdot)$ is as a restriction of the continuous $R$. "$p' \circ \Phi = p$" is read as $p' \circ \Phi = a
\circ p$ (possible misprint; Findings, Chapter 2, item 76). The categories $\mathcal R$, $\mathcal{BR}$ and the forgetful functor are not
formalized; they name these objects and maps and state nothing further (gap G.5, formalized since apart from them).

**V2.93 (the levels of $X^1$, gap G.6; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.levelLift_transition`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.levelLift_levelChart`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.shiftLevelMap`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.shiftLevelInv`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.continuous_shiftLevelMap`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.continuous_shiftLevelInv`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.shiftLevelHomeomorph`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.shift_level_eq`).** For every $m$, the identity of
the underlying points of $X$ is a homeomorphism $(X^1)_m \cong X_{m+1}$; in a chart $\varphi$ of $X$, the level-$m$
lift of the level chart $\varphi^1$ of $X^1$ is the level-$(m+1)$ lift of $\varphi$ ($(E^1)_m = E_{m+1}$), and level
lifts in two charts differ by the level map of the transition map. So the iterate $X^m = (X^1)^1 \cdots$ is, for each
$m$, the space $X_m$ with its topology and the charts $(V_m, \varphi, (O_m, C_m, E_m))$, by composing these
homeomorphisms. *Book:* the paragraph after Definition 2.3.8, p. 37 (preprint after Definition 2.14, p. 25): these
charts form an atlas of $X_m$, which with it is the M-polyfold $X^m$. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(restated):* $X^m$ is the iterate, identified with $X_m$ for each fixed $m$; one homeomorphism for the family indexed
by $m$ is not stated. This closes gap G.6 (V2.16).

**V2.94 (Theorem 2.3.16 as a bundle statement; `Polyfold.theorem_2_3_16`, `Polyfold.tangentMap_levelMap_one`,
`Polyfold.toBase_tangentMap_levelMap_one`, `Polyfold.retractTangent_shift_of_isScRetract`,
`Polyfold.toBase_retractTangentMap_shift`).** In a local model, for an sc¹ map $f$ on $U$, the tangent map of $f^1 :
U^1 \to F^1$ is the level-$1$ map of $Tf$ on $T(U^1) = (TU)^1$; $T(O^1) = (TO)^1$ for a retract $O$; and $T(f^1)$
is the level-$1$ map of $Tf$ for an sc-smooth map between retracts. For an M-polyfold $X$: the tangent charts
$T\varphi$ belong to the structure of $TX$; $p : TX \to X^1$ is sc-smooth; in a tangent chart, $p$ is the first
projection onto the level chart $\varphi^1$ of $X^1$; for every retraction $r$ onto a model $O$, the model $(TO, TC,
TE)$ is a bundle retract ($Tr$ covers $r^1$, V2.92); and the transition map of two tangent charts is a bundle map on
$T(\varphi(V \cap V'))$ covering the level-$1$ map of the transition map of the charts. *Book:* Theorem 2.3.16, p.
40 (2017: running text after Proposition 2.5; preprint: after Proposition 2.19, p. 27): the construction $X \mapsto
(p : TX \to X^1)$; the text before it says that $p$ is locally built on the bundle retractions $TO \to O^1$ and that
the transition maps are sc-smooth bundle maps. *Hidden hypotheses:* the paracompactness of $TX$ and $X_1$ (instance
arguments, supplied by V2.20 and V2.17). *Deviation (restated):* "sc-smooth M-polyfold bundle" is read through the
models and the transition maps, with $TX$ the M-polyfold of V2.21; the fibres $T_xX$ carry no linear structure of
their own (gap G.7).

**V2.95 (Proposition 2.3.17 for $i = 1$, $T(X^1) \equiv (TX)^1$; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.someChart`,

TX$, defined in a chosen chart and independent of it, takes values in $(TX)_1$ and gives a bijection $\Phi : T(X^1)
\to (TX)^1$ with: (1) $\Phi$ is an sc-diffeomorphism of the M-polyfolds $T(X^1)$ and $(TX)^1$, in particular a
homeomorphism; (2) $p^1 \circ \Phi = p_{X^1}$, where $p^1 : (TX)^1 \to (X^1)^1$ is the level-$1$ map of $p : TX \to

inclusion of $T(\psi^1)(\alpha)$, so $\Phi$ does not depend on the chart used to define it; (5) in the charts

= T(O^i)$ in a local model, compatible with the tangent charts): natural identifications of $(TX)^i$ with $T(X^i)$
and of the bundles $(TX)^i \to (X^1)^i$ and $T(X^i) \to (X^i)^1$, covering $(X^1)^i \equiv (X^i)^1$. *Hidden

the identification $(X^1)^1 \equiv (X^1)^1$ is the identity.

**V2.96 (Proposition 2.3.17 for $i = 2$, and raising the index of an sc-diffeomorphism;
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.levelOneEquiv`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.levelOneEquiv_isScDiffeoOn`,

of $\Phi^{-1}$ for $X$ gives an sc-diffeomorphism $\Phi_2 : T(X^2) \to (TX)^2$, $X^2 = (X^1)^1$, $(TX)^2 =

p. 42, for $i = 2$. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* $i = 2$; every $i$ is V2.97.

**V2.97 (Proposition 2.3.17 for every $i$; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.ScEquiv`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.ScEquiv.shift`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.ScMap`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentShiftScEquiv`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentProjScMap`,

sc-smooth $f : X \to Y$, from the naturality $\iota \circ T(f^1) = Tf \circ \iota$ of the inclusion $\iota : T(X^1)
\to TX$. A bundled M-polyfold exists (the half-line). *Book:* Proposition 2.3.17, p. 42, with the two towers of p.
41. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "natural identification" is read as (1)–(7) and the
naturality in $X$. Linearity on the fibres is not part of the statement, since $T_xX$ has no linear structure (gap

**V2.98 (Remark 2.4.2, the diagonal half-line in $[0, \infty)^3$; `Polyfold.ScOperator.ofConst`,
`Polyfold.diagonalAverage`, `Polyfold.diagonalRetraction`, `Polyfold.mem_diagonalRetraction_retract_iff`,
`Polyfold.diagonalModel`, `Polyfold.diagonalPolyfold`, `Polyfold.diagonalEmbed`, `Polyfold.diagonalProject`,

`Polyfold.diagonalHalfLineChart`, `Polyfold.diagonalHalfLineChart_spec`, `Polyfold.remark_2_4_2`).** In $C =
[0, \infty)^3 \oplus W$, $W$ any sc-Banach space, replacing the three coordinates by their average is an sc-smooth
retraction onto $\Delta \oplus W$, $\Delta = \{(s, s, s) : s \ge 0\}$. With the M-polyfold structure of this retract:
(1) $(s, w) \mapsto ((s, s, s), w)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism from the half-line M-polyfold $[0, \infty) \oplus W$ onto
$\Delta \oplus W$; (2) $d_C((s, s, s), w)$ is $3$ for $s = 0$ and $0$ otherwise, while $d_\Delta$ is $1$ for $s = 0$
and $0$ otherwise, and in the defining chart (the identity of the retract) the chart index is $d_C$; (3) one chart,
defined on all of $\Delta \oplus W$, has as model the relatively open subset $[0, \infty) \oplus W$ of a partial
quadrant, and in it the chart index is $d_\Delta$. *Book:* Remark 2.4.2, pp. 44–45, new in the 2021 edition, for
$\Delta \subseteq [0, \infty)^3 \subseteq \mathbb R^3$. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* any $W$
($W = 0$ is the text's case); "classically smooth" is read as sc-smooth for the constant sc-structure, and the
retraction, which the text does not give, is the orthogonal projection onto the diagonal. *Proof:* $d_\Delta$ by
Proposition 2.4.4 (preprint 2.24) (V2.28) applied to the sc-diffeomorphism (1).

**V2.99 (Definition 2.5.19 (3) does not depend on the chart; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.mem_smoothSet_iff_of_isChart`,

`Polyfold.MPolyfold.TameSubData.complement_forall_charts`).** A point of an M-polyfold is smooth iff its image
in one chart is a smooth point of the model. Let $Y$ have tame sub-M-polyfold data $(V, r)$ (V2.78), condition (3)
being asked in one chart around each smooth point, for one presentation of its partial quadrant. Then at every smooth
$y \in Y \cap V$ condition (3) holds in every chart $\varphi \ni y$, for every presentation $T$ of the partial
quadrant of $\varphi$ and every level-$1$ representative $z$ of $\varphi(y)$, for the chart image $\varphi(W' \cap
Y)$ of any sub-M-polyfold retraction $r'$ onto $Y$ near $y$, in particular for $r' = r$. *Book:* Definition 2.5.19
(3), p. 63, new in the 2021 edition, stated on $T_yX$. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* (3) remains
a statement in charts, since $T_yX$ has no linear structure here (gap G.7); the chart, the presentation and the
retraction do not matter (gap G.77, closed). *Proof:* by Chapter 4's chart change for the general-position condition
(`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isGeneralPositionRetractAt_chart_change`, V4.45), which is (3) word for word.

**V2.100 (a tame sub-M-polyfold is tame; `Polyfold.ScBanach.levelSub_sup_of_le_of_isScSplitting`,
`Polyfold.ScBanach.isScSplitting_sup_of_complementIn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.TameSubData.isTameRetract_image`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsTameSubMPolyfold.hasTameInducedStructure`).** If $E = M \oplus B$ is an sc-splitting and
$N, A \subseteq M$ are sc-subspaces with $M_m = N_m \oplus A_m$ on every level, then $E = N \oplus (A \oplus B)$ is an
sc-splitting. For tame sub-M-polyfold data $(V, r)$ and a chart $\varphi$ of $X$ with a tame model, the chart image
$\varphi(W \cap Y)$ of $Y$ is a tame retract, of the retraction $(\varphi r \varphi^{-1}) \circ t$ with $t$ the tame
retraction of the model. Hence a tame sub-M-polyfold $Y$ of a tame $X$ has a tame induced structure (Definition
2.5.18): the sub-charts built on tame charts of $X$ have tame models. *Book:* the text after Definition 2.5.19, p. 63,
new in the 2021 edition ("not difficult to see"). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Proof:* the first condition of
tameness from (2) of Definition 2.5.19 and $d_X = d_C \circ \varphi$ in a tame chart; the sc-complement of the tangent
space of $\varphi(W \cap Y)$ inside $E_x$ is $A \oplus B$, with $A$ from (3) in the chart $\varphi$ (V2.99) and $B$
the complement of $T_xO$ given by the tameness of $t$.

**V2.101 (the examples $A$ and $B$ in $[0, \infty)^2 \times \mathbb R$; `Polyfold.TameSubExample.fixSet`,
`Polyfold.TameSubExample.isSubMPolyfold_fixSet`, `Polyfold.TameSubExample.isTameSubMPolyfold_fixSet`,
`Polyfold.TameSubExample.setA`, `Polyfold.TameSubExample.setB`, `Polyfold.TameSubExample.isTameSubMPolyfold_setA`,
`Polyfold.TameSubExample.hasTameInducedStructure_setA`, `Polyfold.TameSubExample.isSubMPolyfold_setB`,
`Polyfold.TameSubExample.not_mem_tameSubData_setB`, `Polyfold.TameSubExample.not_isTameSubMPolyfold_setB`,
`Polyfold.TameSubExample.halfLineToB_isScDiffeoOn`, `Polyfold.TameSubExample.hasTameInducedStructure_setB`,
`Polyfold.TameSubExample.examples_A_B`).** In $X = [0, \infty)^n \oplus W$, $W$ any sc-Banach space, the fixed
set of an idempotent sc-operator $L$ mapping the quadrant into itself is a sub-M-polyfold, and a tame sub-M-polyfold
if $L$ does not change the $\mathbb R^n$-component. For $n = 2$: $A = \{(x, y, 0)\}$ (with $L(a, w) = (a, 0)$) is a
tame sub-M-polyfold with tame induced structure; $B = \{(x, x, 0)\}$ is a sub-M-polyfold, but no retraction onto $B$
with conditions (1) and (2) of Definition 2.5.19 is defined near the corner $0$, so $B$ is not a tame sub-M-polyfold;
$t \mapsto (t, t, 0)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism from the half-line $[0, \infty)$ onto $B$ with its induced structure,
which is tame. For $W = \mathbb R$ these are the text's statements. *Book:* the text after Definition 2.5.19, p. 63,
new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* any $W$. *Proof:* for small $t > 0$ the
point $(t, 0, 0)$ of $V$ has $d_X = 1$, while $d_X$ takes only the values $0$ and $2$ on $B$; (3) is not needed.

**V2.102 (Theorem 2.7.13 (2)–(4), the tame M-polyfold $bX$; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_tame_chart_subset`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_localFace_of_faceIn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.BChartData`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.BChartData.chart`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.BChartData.chart_transition_isScSmooth`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.BChartData.chart_compatible`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_bChartData`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.paracompactSpace_tameBoundarySpace`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.bAtlas`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold_isTame`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.tameBoundaryMap_isScSmooth`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_tameBoundaryMap`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex_tameBoundaryMap_sub_one`).** Let $X$ be tame. A chart datum of $bX$ consists of a triple
$(x, V, \theta)$ with $V$ centred at $x$ (V2.84), a chart $\varphi$ of $X$, an open $V_1 \subseteq \mathrm{dom}\,
\varphi$, an sc-isomorphism $T$ of the model space of $\varphi$ with $\mathbb R^{k+1} \oplus W$ and a coordinate
$i$ vanishing on $T\varphi(\theta \cap V_1)$, such that the image of $\varphi(\theta \cap V_1)$ under the face
projection $\pi$ (Proposition 2.5.15 (preprint 2.43)) is a tame retract of $[0, \infty)^k \oplus W$ and $d_X(y) =
d(\pi\varphi(y)) + 1$ on $\theta \cap V_1$. Its chart is $p \mapsto \pi(\varphi(B(p)))$ on $U(x, V, \theta) \cap
B^{-1}(V_1)$; two such charts are compatible, with transition map $\pi' \circ (\varphi' \circ \varphi^{-1}) \circ
\iota$ ($\iota$ the face inclusion); every point of $\theta$ lies in the $V_1$ of a chart datum with the triple $(x, V,
\theta)$, so the charts cover $bX$. With the topology $T_{bX}$, paracompact by V2.88, they make $bX$ a tame M-polyfold
(2); $B : bX \to X$, which is $\iota$ in these charts, is sc-smooth (3); and $d_X(B(p)) = d_{bX}(p) + 1$, hence
$d_X(B(p)) - 1 = d_{bX}(p)$ (4). *Book:* Theorem 2.7.13 (2)–(4), pp. 83–84, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none. *Proof:* the charts are the charts $\pi \circ \varphi$ of the face $\theta$
composed with $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$; the local faces of $\theta$ in a tame chart inside $V$ are found as in Theorem
2.5.17 (preprint 2.45).

**V2.103 (the characterization after Theorem 2.7.13, and Proposition 2.7.12, for centred representatives;
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.BSpace.exists_centred_rep`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_of_isFaceIn`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.facePolyfold`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.phiTot`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.phi_isScDiffeoOn`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold_unique`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold_satisfies`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.proposition_2_7_12_scDiffeo`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.theorem_2_7_13_structure`).** Let $X$
be tame. Every class of $bX$ has a representative $(x, V, \theta)$ with $V$ centred at $x$. A face $\theta$ of a
face-structured open $V$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $X$ and carries the induced structure. For $V$ centred at $x$,
$\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ is an sc-diffeomorphism of the open set $U(x, V, \theta)$ onto $\theta$, with inverse
$\Phi^{-1}$; an M-polyfold structure on $bX$ (with the topology $T_{bX}$) for which all these $\Phi$ are
sc-diffeomorphisms is equivalent to that of V2.102, which has the property. For two triples with centred
neighbourhoods, the transition map $\Phi_{(x', V', \theta')} \circ \Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}^{-1}$ is an
sc-diffeomorphism between the open subsets $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}(U \cap U')$ of $\theta$ and $\Phi_{(x', V',
\theta')}(U \cap U')$ of $\theta'$, and the identity on points of $X$. One statement collects (2)–(4) with this
characterization and the uniqueness. *Book:* Proposition 2.7.12, p. 83, and the characterization after Theorem
2.7.13, p. 84, new in the 2021 edition: for every class and every representative, $U(x, V, \theta)$ is open and
$\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ a homeomorphism and an sc-diffeomorphism onto $\theta$, with the structure induced from $V$.
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* centred representatives; every representative is V2.104. "The
structure induced from $V$" is read as the sub-M-polyfold structure of $\theta$ in $X$, and "uniquely characterized"
as: every structure with the property has an equivalent atlas.

**V2.104 (Proposition 2.7.12 and the characterization for every representative;
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.BTriple.exists_centred_subset`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.phiInv`,
`Polyfold.TameBoundary.phiInv_spec`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.reachSet`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isOpen_reachSet`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.reachSet_eq_univ_of_isCenteredAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.phiTot_isScSmoothOn`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.phiInv_isScSmoothOn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.phi_isScDiffeoOn_nonCentred`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold_unique_allReps`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold_satisfies_allReps`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.proposition_2_7_12_scDiffeo_nonCentred`).** Every triple $s$ has an equivalent triple $s'$
centred at its point with $U(s') \subseteq U(s)$. For every representative $(x, V, \theta)$, $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$
is sc-smooth on $U(x, V, \theta)$, its inverse is sc-smooth on the image $\theta \cap V^x$, and $\Phi$ is an
sc-diffeomorphism of $U(x, V, \theta)$ onto the open subset $\theta \cap V^x$ of $\theta$, which is $\theta$ when $V$
is centred at $x$. An M-polyfold structure on $bX$ with this property for every representative is equivalent to that
of V2.102, which has it. For every pair of representatives, $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}(U \cap U')$ and $\Phi_{(x', V',
\theta')}(U \cap U')$ are open in $\theta$ and $\theta'$, and the transition map between them is an
sc-diffeomorphism, with inverse $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)} \circ \Phi_{(x', V', \theta')}^{-1}$, the identity on points
of $X$. *Book:* as V2.103. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* Proposition 2.7.12 holds as printed for
all representatives; in the characterization the image of $\Phi$ is $\theta \cap V^x$, and "onto $\theta$" does not
hold as we read it for every representative (V2.105) (gap G.78, closed). *Proof:* near each point, $\Phi^{-1}$ is
$\Phi_{s'}^{-1}$ for a centred refinement $s'$, composed with the inclusion of an open piece of $\theta$ into the face
of $s'$; the sub-M-polyfold calculus (a map into a sub-M-polyfold is sc-smooth if it is sc-smooth into $X$) replaces
the text's open sc-embeddings of faces.

**V2.105 ("$\Phi$ is an sc-diffeomorphism onto $\theta$" for every representative: the slab of V2.85;
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.not_surjOn_phiTot`).** For the triple $(x, V, \theta)$ of V2.85 in $[0, \infty)^3 \oplus W$,
$\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ does not map $U(x, V, \theta)$ onto $\theta$. *Book:* the characterization after Theorem
2.7.13, p. 84, for "any representative". *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):* read for every
representative, the characterization does not hold as we read it; the strongest version that holds is V2.104, onto
$\theta \cap V^x$, which for centred $V$ is the printed statement (V2.103). *Proof:* V2.85.

**V2.106 (Definition 2.7.14 and the iterated boundaries (2.45)–(2.47);
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.TameMPolyfoldBundle`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.TameMPolyfoldBundle.b`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.TameMPolyfoldBundle.iter`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.TameMPolyfoldBundle.iterMap`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.TameMPolyfoldBundle.iterMap_isScSmooth`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.TameMPolyfoldBundle.degIndex_iterMap`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.TameMPolyfoldBundle.range_iterMap`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.definition_2_7_14`).** The tame boundary of a tame $X$ is $bX$ with the tame structure of
V2.102 and the sc-smooth $B$, whose image is $\partial X$. For a tame M-polyfold bundled with its space, $b^0X = X$ and
$b^kX = b(b^{k-1}X)$ are tame M-polyfolds; $B^0 = \mathrm{id}$ and $B^{k+1} = B_X \circ B^k_{bX}$, so $B^k = B_X
\circ B_{bX} \circ \cdots \circ B_{b^{k-1}X}$; $B^k : b^kX \to X$ is sc-smooth, $d_X(B^k(p)) = d_{b^kX}(p) + k$, and
the image of $B^k$ is $\{d_X \ge k\}$. *Book:* Definition 2.7.14 and (2.45)–(2.47), p. 84, new in the 2021 edition.
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the index formula, Theorem 2.7.13 (4) iterated. The bundling makes
$b$ a map that can be iterated.

**V2.107 (witnesses for Theorem 2.7.13 (2)–(4); `Polyfold.MPolyfold.quadrantPolyfold_bChartData_nonempty`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.quadrantPolyfold_degIndex_tameBoundary`).** For the tame quadrant $[0, \infty)^n \oplus W$, $n
\ge 1$, chart data of $bX$ exist, and the $n$ points of $bX$ over the corner $0$ have $d_{bX} = n - 1$. *Book:* not
stated. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):* the hypotheses of V2.102–V2.106 are satisfiable,
and (4) is not vacuous.

**V2.108 (Proposition 2.1.2 (preprint 2.2): the image of a classical smooth retraction is a submanifold;
`Polyfold.GapP1Prop212.proposition_2_1_2`, `Polyfold.GapP1Prop212.isIdempotentElem_fderiv`,
`Polyfold.GapP1Prop212.retractChart`, `Polyfold.GapP1Prop212.retractChart_comp`,
`Polyfold.GapP1Prop212.hasFDerivAt_retractChart`).** `proposition_2_1_2`: for a real Banach space $E$, $U \subseteq E$ open, $r$
$C^\infty$ on $U$ with $r(U) \subseteq U$ and $r \circ r = r$ on $U$, and $x \in r(U)$, there are open $V \ni x$ with $V
\subseteq U$, open $W \ni 0$, closed complementary subspaces $R = \operatorname{range} Dr(x)$ and $N = \ker Dr(x)$, and a
$C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $\psi : V \to W$ ($\psi$ and $\psi^{-1}$ $C^\infty$) with $\psi(x) = 0$ and $\psi(r(U) \cap V) = R
\cap W$. *Book:* §2.1, Proposition 2.1.2 (preprint 2.2), p. 22 (preprint p. 18) (proof §2.7.1 (preprint §2.6.1), preprint pp.
54–55), If $r : U \to U$ is a $C^\infty$ retraction of an open subset of a Banach space $E$, then $O = r(U)$ is a $C^\infty$
submanifold: near each $x \in O$ there are a splitting $E = R \oplus N$ and a diffeomorphism $\psi : V \to W$ with $\psi(O \cap
V) = R \cap W$ (the text prints $\psi(0) = x$ for $\psi(x) = 0$). *Deviation (restated):* The printed normalization $\psi(0) =
x$, for $\psi : V \to W$ with $x \in V$ and $0 \in W$, is read as $\psi(x) = 0$. The proof is not the text's (the estimates of
§2.7.1): $P = Dr(x)$ is idempotent by the chain rule (`isIdempotentElem_fderiv`); $\varphi(y) = P(r(y) - x) + (1 - P)(y - r(y))$
(`retractChart`) has $D\varphi(x) = 1$ (`hasFDerivAt_retractChart`) and conjugates $r$ to $P$, $\varphi \circ r = P \circ
\varphi$ (`retractChart_comp`); Mathlib's inverse function theorem gives $\psi$. $C^\infty$ is `ContDiffOn ℝ ∞` (smooth, not
analytic).

paracompact iff every open cover has a closed locally finite refinement. Proposition 2.7.4 (preprint 2.57): a regular space with

## 4. Chapter 3 (HWZ §§3.1–3.8): partly verified

Chapter 3 of Part I (pp. 89–174 (preprint pp. 61–146)) develops sc-Fredholm theory. §3.1 defines germs, sections
of strong bundles, fillers, basic germs, sc-Fredholm germs and sections, proves local compactness
(Theorem 3.1.13 (preprint 3.12)) and the stability under sc⁺-perturbations (Theorem 3.1.18 (preprint 3.15)), and states the implicit
function theorems (Theorems 3.1.22, 3.1.26 (preprint 3.19, 3.23)), with good position (Definition 3.1.24 (preprint 3.21), Proposition 3.1.25 (preprint 3.22)). §3.2
introduces the tangent germ property and shows that it makes a subset a sub-M-polyfold (Definition
3.2.1 (preprint 3.25), Proposition 3.2.2 (preprint 3.26), Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27)). §3.3 proves the germ implicit function theorem (Definition
3.3.1 (preprint 3.28), Theorems 3.3.2–3.3.7 (preprint 3.29–3.34) and Theorem 3.35 (preprint; not in the 2021 edition)). §3.4 proves that basic germs are stable under sc⁺-perturbations (Theorem
3.4.2 (preprint 3.38)). §3.5 proves local regularity and compactness (Theorem 3.5.1 (preprint 3.40)) and local solvability (Corollary
3.5.3 (preprint 3.41), Theorem 3.5.6 (preprint 3.43), Theorem 3.5.11 (preprint Corollary 3.47)). §3.6 states and proves the implicit function theorem for
sc-Fredholm sections (Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52), Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53), Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), Lemma 3.6.9 (preprint 3.55)) and its global
forms (Theorems 3.6.10, 3.6.11 (preprint 3.56, 3.57)). §3.7 gives a criterion for being conjugate to a basic germ (Theorem
3.7.1 (preprint 3.58), Lemmas 3.7.2–3.7.4 (preprint 3.59–3.61)). The appendix §3.8 proves Proposition 3.1.25 (preprint 3.22), Lemma 3.5.10 (preprint 3.46), Lemma 3.6.9 (preprint 3.55), and
the inverse and implicit function theorems in partial quadrants (Theorems 3.8.15, 3.8.22 (preprint 3.72, 3.78)).

What is verified. **The germ implicit function theorem (Theorem 3.3.6 (preprint 3.33)) holds with the text's
hypotheses**, and so do Corollary 3.3.7 (preprint 3.34) and Theorem 3.35 (preprint; not in the 2021 edition): the solution germ is sc^k on the germ of
neighbourhoods shrunk by $2^k - 1$ levels, and sc-smooth on one diagonal germ, which shrinks fast
with the level (V3.31, V3.32). **The implicit function theorems also hold with the text's
hypotheses, local and global**: Theorems 3.6.8, 3.1.26 and 3.1.22 (preprint 3.54, 3.23 and 3.19) (V3.94, V3.95), Theorem 3.6.11 (preprint 3.57), Corollary
3.1.27 (preprint 3.24) and Theorem 3.6.10 (preprint 3.56) (V3.87, V3.70, V3.86), once three steps of the text's proof are replaced. The
surjectivity of $f'(y)$ at the zeros $y$ near a given zero, which the text derives from Corollary
3.5.3 (preprint 3.41) and which does not follow from it (V3.82; the same step stands in the book's arXiv version), is
proved by a new argument, an implicit function theorem at the nearby zero for a perturbed equation
(V3.93); the regularity of the solution germ away from the centre is proved by re-centring (V3.73,
V3.74); and the relative openness of the set $\Sigma$ in the proof of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27) by the choice of
the good complement (V3.75, V3.77). With them: the dimension of the solution set is the Fredholm
index (V3.96, V3.97), the index is locally constant along the solution set (V3.98; also without good
position, with the text's hypotheses: tame germ data and no bump functions), and so, with the
text's hypotheses, is the index of Definition 6.2.1 (preprint 6.1) (read with the text's locally defined
sc⁺-sections) along sc-smooth paths $\mathbb R \to X$, the text's Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2) for paths on
$\mathbb R$ (V3.98), $\ker f'(y)$ is the tangent space of the solution
set in a chart (V3.99), and good
position is the surjectivity of $f'(y)$ at zeros with $d_X(y) = 0$, so that Theorems 3.1.22 and 3.6.10 (preprint 3.19 and 3.56)
hold with the text's hypothesis "$f'(x)$ surjective" (V3.100, V3.101). The forms first proved under
an added filler condition at the nearby zeros (V3.68, V3.69, V3.82, V3.85) are kept; that condition
follows from good position (V3.102), and with Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4) as stated the text's argument gives the
kernel half of Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54) (V3.81) but not the surjectivity. All these statements are the
repaired ones. They were first proved under the hypothesis that the base retraction of every strong
bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame, which no strong bundle over a nonempty base
satisfies (V3.104, where only the half of the argument that concerns retractions is
machine-checked), so those first statements were vacuous; they now assume what the text's
Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.4 and 3.6.6 (preprint 3.50, 3.51 and 3.53) ask, germ data and good position in a chart whose base retraction is
tame, and conclude good position in such charts (V3.103, V3.107). Also verified: every definition of
§§3.1–3.6 (Definitions 3.1.1–3.1.4, 3.1.6, 3.1.7, 3.1.11, 3.1.16, 3.1.24, 3.2.1, 3.3.1, 3.4.1, 3.6.1, 3.6.3, 3.6.4,
3.6.6 (preprint 3.1–3.4, 3.6, 3.7, 3.11, 3.14, 3.21, 3.25, 3.28, 3.37, 3.48, 3.50, 3.51,
