**V4.52 (sc⁺-retractions in a chart, and Theorem 4.2.11 (4) (preprint 4.22) for one $\sigma$;
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScPlusRetractionOn_of_chart`, `Polyfold.MChart.cornerPreimage`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.theorem_4_2_11_four_of_chart`).** For a chart $\chi$ of $X$ and an sc⁺-retraction $\tau$ of its model with
$\tau(U) \subseteq O$, $\chi^{-1} \circ \tau \circ \chi$ is an sc⁺-retraction on the open set $\chi^{-1}(\tau.U)$ with image $\chi^{-1}(\tau(U))$.
In a tame chart $\psi$ centred at $x$ with the data of V4.49 for the chart retraction of $A$, for every $\sigma$ there are faces
$F_i \ni 0$ and an open $G \ni 0$ such that $\psi^{-1}(G \cap \bigcap_{i \in \sigma}F_i)$ contains $x$, lies in the open set $W$ of the
submanifold chart, and has the properties (4) of V4.50. *Book:* not in the text. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (not in the book).*

**V4.53 (the family $\mathbb R^m \times X$ and stratified regular points; `Polyfold.prod_rn_isTame`, `Polyfold.fibreSet`,
`Polyfold.rnPres`, `Polyfold.IsStratRegularPoint`, `Polyfold.IsStratRegularValue`).** For tame $X$, $\mathbb R^m \times X$ with the
product charts is tame. The fibre of $A \subseteq \mathbb R^m \times X$ over $\lambda$ is $A_\lambda = \{x : (\lambda, x) \in A\}$. A point $z \in A$ is a
*stratified regular point* if, for some data of Definition 4.2.1 (preprint 4.13) at $z$, some $a \in \mathbb R^m$, some chart $\varphi$ of $X$ at $z_2$,
some presentation $T$ of its partial quadrant and the level-$1$ point $y$ over the image of $z$ in the product chart $(r
\mapsto r - a) \times \varphi$, every $\mu \in \mathbb R^m$ is the first component of a tangent vector $v$ of the chart model of $A$ at $y$ with
$v_2 \in E_{\varphi(z_2)}$ (the projection maps $T_zA \cap E_z$, the tangent space of the stratum through $z$, onto $\mathbb R^m$); $\lambda$
is a *stratified regular value* if every $z \in A$ over $\lambda$ is a stratified regular point. *Book:* §4.3, preprint p. 164, and the
proof of Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23), p. 194 (preprint p. 166) ("regular values of $p_\sigma$"). *Hidden hypotheses:* the chart form (gap G.7).
*Deviation (restated):* the chart independence is proved since (V4.93, gap G.36, closed).

**V4.54 (Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23); `Polyfold.theorem_4_3_1_preprint`).** Let $X$ be tame and $A$ a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold of
$\mathbb R^m \times X$ with tame induced structure and compact closure, $\varepsilon > 0$, and suppose (1) for $|\lambda| \le \varepsilon$ ($|\lambda|^2 =
\sum\lambda_i^2$) the set $A \cap \{z_1 = \lambda\}$ is compact and non-empty, (2) $A$ is in general position at every point. Then there is
$\Sigma \subseteq \{|\lambda| < \varepsilon\}$ whose complement in $\{|\lambda| < \varepsilon\}$ is Lebesgue-null, consisting of stratified regular values,
such that for $\lambda \in \Sigma$ the fibre $A_\lambda$ is compact, a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold of $X$, in general position at
each of its points, and its induced structure has a corner structure and is tame. *Book:* Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23), p. 193 (preprint p. 165); proof
pp. 193–194 (preprint pp. 165–166). *Hidden hypotheses:* hypothesis (2), misprinted in the text ("there exists a sc-complement $T_zA$ in $T_zZ$"),
is Definition 4.2.10 (preprint 4.21). *Deviation (stronger):* $\Sigma$ consists of stratified regular values, which are regular values; the
tameness of $A$, the non-emptiness in (1) and $\varepsilon > 0$ are not used, and $A_\lambda$ is moreover tame. With ordinary regular
values the conclusion fails at the value: in $\mathbb R \times [0, \infty)$, $A = \{(x, x) : 0 \le x < 1\} \cup (-1, 1) \times \{5\}$ satisfies
the hypotheses, $Dp$ is onto everywhere, and $A_0 = \{0, 5\}$ meets $\partial X$ (Findings, item 102).

**V4.55 (Remark 4.3.2 (preprint 4.24); `Polyfold.quotDim_le_finrank_of_eq_sup`, `Polyfold.remark_4_3_2_chart`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_4_3_2_codim`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_4_3_2`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_4_3_2_not_mem_boundary`).** For tame $X$ and smooth $x$, in a tame chart at $x$ the reduced tangent
space has codimension $d_X(x)$ in the tangent space. If $A$ is in general position at $a$, then $d_X(a) \le \dim T_aA$ (in any
tame chart at $a$); in particular a submanifold in general position with $T_aA = 0$ does not meet $\partial X$ at $a$. *Book:*
Remark 4.3.2 (preprint 4.24), p. 193 (preprint p. 165). *Hidden hypotheses:* $X$ tame and $x$ smooth for the codimension. *Deviation (hypotheses
explicit):* stated for any submanifold in general position, not only for the $A_\lambda$ of Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23) (to which it applies by
V4.54).

**V4.56 (Sard's theorem, vendored; `Polyfold.MilnorSard.Sard.critSet`, `Polyfold.MilnorSard.Sard.sardStatement`,
`Polyfold.MilnorSard.sard`, `Polyfold.MilnorSard.dense_compl_image_critSet`).** Let $E$, $F$ be finite-dimensional real
normed spaces (in the same universe), $F$ with its Borel σ-algebra and a Haar measure $\mu$, $U \subseteq E$ open and $f$ of class
$C^\infty$ on $U$. Then $\mu(f(\mathrm{Crit})) = 0$, where $\mathrm{Crit}$ is the set of points of $U$ at which $Df$ is not onto, and the
complement of $f(\mathrm{Crit})$ is dense. *Book:* "Sard's theorem", proof of Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23), p. 194 (preprint p. 166), without statement.
*Hidden hypotheses:* Mathlib has only the cases $\dim E \le \dim F$; the general case is Milnor's induction, copied from the
Milnor project (`math_faithful`) with only the namespace changed (Findings, item 100). *Deviation (not in the book).*

**V4.57 (the strata and Sard's theorem on them; `Polyfold.quadC`, `Polyfold.stratSub`, `Polyfold.zeroSetOf`,
`Polyfold.finrank_stratSub`, `Polyfold.stratCritSet`, `Polyfold.measure_image_stratCritSet`).** Let $V$ be finite-dimensional
with linear coordinates $\ell : V \to \mathbb R^n$ and $C = \{\ell \ge 0\}$. The stratum subspace of $\sigma$ is $\{\ell_i = 0, i \in \sigma\}$, of
dimension $\dim V - \#\sigma$ when $\ell$ is onto; $\sigma(v) = \{i : \ell_i(v) = 0\}$. For $f$ of class $C^\infty$ on $U = O \cap C$ ($O$ open)
into a finite-dimensional $F$, the stratified critical points are the $v \in U$ at which $Df(v)$ restricted to the stratum
subspace of $\sigma(v)$ is not onto, and their image is null for every Haar measure. *Book:* proof of Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23), pp. 193–194 (preprint pp. 165–166) ("$A \cap F_\sigma^\circ$ is a smooth manifold ... of dimension $\dim(A) - \#\sigma$"; "Using Sard's theorem we find a subset
$\Sigma_\sigma$ ... having full measure"). *Hidden hypotheses:* the dimension count, which Theorem 4.2.11 (preprint 4.22) does not state (the text
cites "Theorem 4.23" for it). *Deviation (restated):* in the model space $T_0A$ of the chart.

**V4.58 (Theorem 3.8.22 (preprint 3.78) in $C^\infty$ form; `Polyfold.ContractionData.exists_solution_smooth`,
`Polyfold.theorem_3_8_22_smooth`).** Under the hypotheses of Theorem 3.8.22 (preprint 3.78) (V3.63) with $f$ of class $C^\infty$, one solution $\tau$
is $C^\infty$ on $V'$, with the other conclusions of V3.63 (including the uniqueness clause). *Book:* Theorem 3.8.22 (preprint 3.78), p. 169 (preprint p. 141),
states one $j$; the proof of Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23) needs $C^\infty$. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the
contraction radii of Lemmas 3.8.23, 3.8.24 (preprint 3.79, 3.80) and the fixed point do not depend on $j$.

**V4.59 (the kernel at a stratified regular point is in good position; `Polyfold.quadAt`,
`Polyfold.isPartialQuadrant_quadAt`, `Polyfold.exists_goodComplement_stratSub`).** For $\ell$ onto, $\{\ell_i \ge 0, i \in \sigma\}$ is a
partial quadrant. If $K + \{\ell_i = 0, i \in \sigma\} = V$, then $K$ is in good position to $\{\ell_i \ge 0, i \in \sigma\}$ with a closed good
complement inside the stratum subspace. *Book:* not in the text here; the argument of Lemma 5.26 (preprint; not in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:*
none. *Deviation (not in the book).*

**V4.60 (a retraction onto the fibre over a stratified regular point; `Polyfold.exists_fibre_retraction`).** For $\ell$ onto,
$f$ of class $C^\infty$ on $O \cap C$ and $v_0 \in O \cap C$ not stratified-critical, there are an open $O' \ni v_0$, $O' \subseteq O$, and a
map $\rho$, $C^\infty$ on $O' \cap C$, mapping $O' \cap C$ into itself and into $f^{-1}(f(v_0))$, equal to the identity on $O' \cap C
\cap f^{-1}(f(v_0))$, with $D\rho(v_0)$ of range $\ker Df(v_0)$ and equal to the identity there. *Book:* "for $\lambda \in \Sigma$ ... $A_\lambda$ is
a smooth compact manifold with boundary with corners", p. 194 (preprint p. 166), in the model. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not
in the book):* the implicit function theorem at corner points (V4.58 with V4.59).

**V4.61 (the sc⁺-retraction onto $A_\lambda$; `Polyfold.isScSmooth_slice`, `Polyfold.scDeriv_slice`,
`Polyfold.exists_slice_retraction`).** In the model $\mathbb R^m \oplus E$ of a product chart, let $t$ be an sc⁺-retraction
described near a point as the graph $\Gamma : V \to t(U) \cap W$ with inverse $p$ (Proposition 4.1.9 (preprint 4.9)), and $\rho$ a $C^\infty$ retraction of
$O' \cap (\mathbb R^m \times C)$ onto the points $v$ with $\Gamma(v)_1 = c$. Then $\tau(e) = (\Gamma(\rho(p(t(c, e)))))_2$ is an sc⁺-retraction of
$E$ (partial quadrant $C$) onto $\{e : (c, e) \in t(U) \cap W, p(c, e) \in O'\}$; if $D\rho(v_0) = 1$ on $\{h : (D\Gamma(v_0)h)_1 = 0\}$, the
tangent space of its retract at the point over $\Gamma(v_0)_2$ contains $(D\Gamma(v_0)h)_2$ for all such $h$. The slice $e \mapsto (c, e)$
is sc-smooth with derivative $h \mapsto (0, h)$. *Book:* not constructed (Definition 4.2.1 (preprint 4.13) requires it). *Hidden hypotheses:*
none. *Deviation (not in the book).*

**V4.62 (general position of $A_\lambda$; `Polyfold.isGeneralPositionRetractAt_slice`).** In a product chart with $r_X$ tame: if
the chart model of $A$ is in general position at $z = (c, y)$, the projection maps the tangent space of the stratum $T_zA \cap E_z$
onto $\mathbb R^m$, and $\tau$ is an sc⁺-retraction onto $Q \subseteq O$ whose tangent space at the smooth $y$ contains the second components
of the tangent vectors of $A$ at $z$ with first component $0$, then $Q$ is in general position at $y$. *Book:* proof of Theorem
4.3.1 (preprint 4.23), p. 194 (preprint p. 166) ("in view of the assumption (2) ... $T_{z'}(\{\lambda\} \times A_\lambda)$ has a sc-complement in $T^R_{z'}X$"). *Hidden
hypotheses:* stratified regularity at $z$ itself. *Deviation (restated).*

**V4.63 (the local step of Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23); `Polyfold.FibreLocal`, `Polyfold.exists_local_family`).** Let $X$ be tame and $A
\subseteq \mathbb R^m \times X$ a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold in general position at every point. Every $z_0 \in A$ has an open
neighbourhood $U$ and a Lebesgue-null $\mathrm{CV} \subseteq \mathbb R^m$ such that at every $z \in A \cap U$ with $z_1 \notin \mathrm{CV}$: $z$ is a
stratified regular point, $A_{z_1}$ is near $z_2$ the image of an sc⁺-retraction on an open subset of $X$, and $A_{z_1}$ is in
general position and in good position at $z_2$. *Book:* proof of Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23), pp. 193–194 (preprint pp. 165–166), in one $U(z)$. *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* in the product chart of a tame chart of $X$ centred at $z_{0,2}$, through V4.49,
V4.57, V4.60–V4.62.

**V4.64 (the countable cover: Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23) for any parameter set; `Polyfold.theorem_4_3_1_of_subset`).** For $X$ tame, $A \subseteq
\mathbb R^m \times X$ a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold with compact closure, in general position at every point, and any $S \subseteq
\mathbb R^m$, there is $\Sigma \subseteq S$ with $S \setminus \Sigma$ Lebesgue-null such that every $\lambda \in \Sigma$ is a stratified regular value and the
conclusions of V4.63 hold at every point of $A_\lambda$. *Book:* proof of Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23), p. 193 (preprint p. 165) ("We cover the set $\{z \in A : |p(z)|
\le \varepsilon\}$ with the finitely many such neighborhoods"). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* any $S$; the text's
set need not be compact and need not have a finite subcover (in $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R$, $A = (-2\varepsilon, 2\varepsilon) \times \{2\} \cup \{(\varepsilon(1 -
x), x) : 0 < x < 1\}$); $A$ is second countable, its closure being compact in the metrizable $\mathbb R^m \times X$, and countably many
neighbourhoods cover it (Findings, item 103).

**V4.65 (Theorem 4.2.11 (preprint 4.22) in the 2021 form of (1); `Polyfold.MPolyfold.theorem_4_2_11`).** Let $X$ be a
tame M-polyfold, $A \subseteq X$ a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold and $x \in A$ a point at which $A$ is in general
position. There are a tame chart $\psi$ of $X$ with $\psi(x) = 0$, with a tame retraction $R$ onto its model $O$ and a presentation
$T : E \cong \mathbb R^n \oplus W$ of its partial quadrant, and an open $U \ni x$ inside the chart domain, such that: (1) $d_X(x) = n$,
$\psi(x)$ lies in exactly $d_X(x)$ faces of the M-polyfold $O$, and for every $i < n$ there are a face $F_i \ni 0$ of the retract
inside the $i$-th coordinate hyperplane and an open $G \ni 0$ with $x \in \psi^{-1}(G \cap F_i) \subseteq U$; (2)–(4) are those of
V4.50. *Book:* Theorem 4.2.11 (preprint 4.22), p. 190 (preprint p. 162); the 2021 edition asks in (1) that the $d$ local faces in $U$
also contain $x$. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* as in V4.50, the local faces are faces of the chart model,
and their identification with faces of $U$ itself is proved since (V4.50, gap G.35, closed). The count in (1) of V4.50 already counts the
faces through $\psi(x)$, which is the 2021 statement; the germs $\psi^{-1}(G \cap F_i)$ that contain $x$ and lie in $U$ are read off
from (4) for $\sigma = \{i\}$.

**V4.66 (Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23) in the 2021 form; `Polyfold.theorem_4_3_1`).** Let $X$ be tame and $A \subseteq
\mathbb R^m \times X$ a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold with tame induced structure and compact closure, $\varepsilon > 0$, such
that (1) $A \cap \{z_1 = \lambda\}$ is compact for every $\lambda$ with $|\lambda| \le \varepsilon$ (possibly empty), and (2) $A$ is in
general position at every point. Then there is a **measurable** $\Sigma \subseteq \{|\lambda| < \varepsilon\}$ whose complement in
$\{|\lambda| < \varepsilon\}$ is Lebesgue-null, consisting of stratified regular values, such that for $\lambda \in \Sigma$ the fibre
$A_\lambda$ is compact, a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold of $X$ in general position at each of its points, with a corner
structure, and tame. *Book:* Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23), p. 193 (preprint p. 165); the 2021 edition drops "non-empty" from (1)
and asks $\Sigma$ to be measurable. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* stratified regular values, as in V4.54;
the tameness of $A$ and $\varepsilon > 0$ are kept and not used. $\Sigma$ is that of V4.64 for $S = \{|\lambda| < \varepsilon\}$ with a
measurable null hull of its exceptional set removed (Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.toMeasurable`), which keeps every other
conclusion; the compactness of $A_\lambda$ comes from (1). Hypothesis (2) is printed as in the earlier texts and read as general
position (Findings, items 101, 151).

**V4.67 (Definition 4.4.3 in a local model; `Polyfold.IsRetractVectorField`, `Polyfold.isRetractVectorField_zero`,
`Polyfold.IsRetractVectorField.mem_retractTangent`, `Polyfold.IsRetractVectorField.isScSmooth_comp`,
`Polyfold.IsRetractVectorField.scDeriv_apply`).** For a local model $(O, C, E)$, a map $A : E_1 \to E_0$ is (the principal part of)
a vector field on $O$ if $x \mapsto (x, A(x))$ is an sc-smooth map from the retract $(O^1, C^1, E^1)$ to the tangent $(TO, TC,
TE)$. Then $(x, A(x)) \in TO$ for $x \in O_1$; for every sc-smooth retraction $r$ onto $O$ the map $\tilde A = A \circ r^1$ is sc-smooth
on $U^1$; and $Dr(x)A(x) = A(x)$ for $x \in O_1$. The zero map is a vector field on every sc-smooth retract. *Book:* Definition
4.4.3, p. 195, new in the 2021 edition (an sc-smooth section of $p : TX \to X^1$, defined on $X^1$, not on $X$), and formula (4.8),
p. 200. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the definition read in the model of a chart, where the text works in
Appendix 4.5.

**V4.68 (Definition 4.4.3 on an M-polyfold; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScVectorField`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.zeroVectorField`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentChartMap_zeroVectorField`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.continuous_zeroVectorField`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScVectorField_zero`).** An sc-smooth vector field on the M-polyfold $X$ is a map $A : X^1 \to TX$, sc-smooth
for the M-polyfold structures of $X^1$ and of the tangent bundle $TX$ (both paracompact), with $p(A(x)) = x$ for every $x \in
X^1$. The zero section, which reads $(\psi(x), 0)$ in every chart $\psi$, is continuous and an sc-smooth vector field. *Book:*
Definition 4.4.3, p. 195, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.

**V4.69 (Lemma 4.4.4 in a local model, $i = 1$; `Polyfold.retractTangent_shift`, `Polyfold.IsRetractVectorField.shift`).** For an
sc-smooth retraction $r$ onto $O$, the tangent of the retract $(O^1, C^1, E^1)$ is the level-$1$ part of $TO$: $T(O^1) = (TO)^1$.
If $A$ is a vector field on $(O, C, E)$, its level map $A_1 : E_2 \to E_1$ is a vector field on $(O^1, C^1, E^1)$: $x \mapsto (x,
A_1(x))$ is an sc-smooth section of $T(O^1) \to O^2$. *Book:* Lemma 4.4.4, p. 196, new in the 2021 edition, said to be obvious from
the identification of $(TX)^i \to (X^1)^i$ with $T(X^i) \to X^{i+1}$. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* in a local
model and for $i = 1$; larger $i$ follow by iterating the local statement. The lemma on an M-polyfold, with the identification
of $(TX)^1$ and $T(X^1)$ of Proposition 2.3.17 (gap G.6, closed), is V4.78, and for every $i$ V4.79.

**V4.70 (the second derivative and its symmetry; `Polyfold.scSecondDeriv`, `Polyfold.scSecondDeriv_symm`,
`Polyfold.fderivWithin_fderivWithin_eq`, `Polyfold.IsRelOpenInQuadrant.mem_closure_interior_lvlSet`,
`Polyfold.scDeriv_tangentMap_inr`).** For an sc² map $f$ on $U \subseteq E$, $z \in U_2$ and $a, b \in E_1$, $D^2f(z)(a, b)$ is the second
component of $D(Tf)(z, a)(b, 0)$, the derivative of $z \mapsto Df(z)a$ in the direction $b$; and $D(Tf)(z, a)(0, l) = (0, Df(z)l)$. If
$U$ is relatively open in a partial quadrant, $D^2f(z)(a, b) = D^2f(z)(b, a)$. *Book:* §4.5.1, p. 200, new in the 2021 edition
("using the symmetry of the second derivative", for $f = r$). *Hidden hypotheses:* none ($r$ lives on a relatively open subset of
a partial quadrant). *Deviation (restated):* the text does not say what $D^2r(x)(A(x), B(x))$ is when $A(x), B(x)$ lie only in
$E_1$, while $r$ is twice differentiable only as a map $U_2 \to E_0$, in directions of $E_2$; it is defined through the
sc²-structure, the derivative of $Tr$. The
symmetry holds for $a, b \in E_2$ by Mathlib's symmetry of second derivatives within a set (`ContDiffWithinAt.isSymmSndFDerivWithinAt`;
points of a partial quadrant lie in the closure of its interior, also on level $2$), and for $a, b \in E_1$ by density of $E_2$
in $E_1$ and continuity of $D(Tf)$ (Findings, item 154).

**V4.71 (§4.5.1, the Lie bracket in a local model; `Polyfold.retractLieBracket`, `Polyfold.retractLieBracket_antisymm`,
`Polyfold.IsRetractVectorField.diff_identity`, `Polyfold.retractLieBracket_mem_tangent`).** Let $r$ be an sc-smooth retraction
onto $O$ and $A$, $B$ vector fields on $(O, C, E)$. For $x \in E_2$ put $[A, B](x) = D\tilde A(x)B_1(x) - D\tilde B(x)A_1(x)$, with
$\tilde A = A \circ r^1$, $\tilde B = B \circ r^1$ differentiated as maps on $U^1$; $[A, B] = -[B, A]$. For $x \in O_2$ and $b$ with
$Dr^1(x)b = b$: $D^2r(x)(A(x), b) + Dr(x)D\tilde A(x)b = D\tilde A(x)b$. Hence $Dr(x)[A, B](x) = [A, B](x)$ for $x \in O_2$: the bracket is
tangent to $O$. *Book:* §4.5.1, pp. 200–201, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $DA(x)$ is
read as the derivative of $\tilde A = A \circ r^1$, the principal part being defined only on $O^1$; the computation is the
text's, with the symmetry of V4.70 (Findings, item 154).

**V4.72 (Proposition 4.4.5 (preprint 4.26) in a local model; `Polyfold.proposition_4_4_5_local`,
`Polyfold.isScSmooth_scDeriv_apply`, `Polyfold.levelMap_shift_shift_eq`, `Polyfold.levelMap_comp_shift_eq`).** For vector fields
$A$, $B$ on $(O, C, E)$ and an sc-smooth retraction $r$ onto $O$: $(x, [A, B](x)) \in TO$ for every $x \in O_2$, and $x \mapsto (x, [A,
B](x))$ is an sc-smooth map from the retract $(O^2, C^2, E^2)$ to $(TO, TC, TE)$, the local form of "$[A, B]$ is an sc-smooth
section of $TX|X^2 \to X^2$". *Book:* Proposition 4.4.5 (preprint 4.26), p. 196 (preprint p. 167), with the proof in §§4.5.1–4.5.2,
pp. 200–202, new in the 2021 edition (the earlier texts quote it from another paper, as a vector field on $X^1$). *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* in a local model. The statement on an M-polyfold is V4.76, with Lemma 4.5.1
(independence of the chart), whose proof the text leaves to the reader, in V4.74, V4.75 and V4.77 (gap G.38, closed); the
pull-back bundle $TX|X^2 \to X^2$ is built since, with $[A, B]$ an sc-smooth section of it (V4.76; gap G.92, closed). *Proof:* the second component is $x \mapsto D\tilde A(r^2x)(\tilde B)_1(x) -
D\tilde B(r^2x)(\tilde A)_1(x)$ on $U^2$, sc-smooth as the tangent map of $\tilde A$ composed with the sc-smooth pair $(r^2,
(\tilde B)_1)$, and equal to $[A, B] \circ r^2$; the first is V4.71.

**V4.73 (the level of the bracket on pp. 200–201; `Polyfold.lieBracket_level_counterexample`,
`Polyfold.not_forall_lieBracket_mem_level_one`, `Polyfold.BracketLevel.opS`, `Polyfold.BracketLevel.opT`,
`Polyfold.BracketLevel.xPt`, `Polyfold.BracketLevel.bracket_not_mem_level_one`, `Polyfold.isRetractVectorField_scOperator`,
`Polyfold.retractLieBracket_scOperator`).** There are an sc-Banach space $E$, the identity retraction of $E$ onto $O = E$ (with $C
= E$), vector fields $A$, $B$ on $(O, C, E)$ and a point $x \in O_2$ with $[A, B](x) \notin E_1$; so the statement "$[A, B](x) \in E_1$
for every local model, all vector fields $A$, $B$ and all $x \in O_2$" does not hold. Every sc-operator $E^1 \to E$ is a vector field on
$(E, E, E)$, and the bracket of two of them is the commutator $S_0T_1 - T_0S_1$. The example: $E$ the weighted sequence space of
V1.13 ($|x|_m = \sup_k(k + 1)^m|x_k|$), $(Sx)_k = (-1)^k(k + 1)x_k$, $(Tx)_k = (k + 1)x_{k+1}$, $x_k = (k + 1)^{-3}$. *Book:* §4.5.1,
pp. 200–201, new in the 2021 edition: $DA(x)B(x) - DB(x)A(x)$ "belongs to the fiber $(T_xO)_1$ whenever $x \in O_2$" (p. 200), and
for $x \in O_2$ the bracket "belongs to the level 1" (p. 201). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):* both
sentences, read as $[A, B](x) \in E_1$, do not hold as we read them: $[S, T]x = ((-1)^k(k + 1)(2k + 3)x_{k+1})_k$, and for this $x$
the level-$1$ coordinates have absolute value $P^3 + P^2 \ge 1/4$, $P = (k + 1)/(k + 2)$, so they do not tend to $0$ (here $T_xO =
E_0$, so $(T_xO)_1 = E_1$). Read as "a tangent vector at the point $x$ of level $1$ of $X^1$", that is $x \in O_{m+2}$ gives $[A, B](x)
\in E_m$, the sentence is V4.72, and Proposition 4.4.5 is not affected. A first example on a weighted $\ell^2$ space (sketched in
the header of `Polyfold/Chapter4/VectorFields.lean`) is not formalized (Findings, item 156).

**V4.74 (Lemma 4.5.1 in a local model, the computation of §4.5.2; `Polyfold.IsRetractVectorField.diff_related`,
`Polyfold.IsRetractVectorField.related_shift`, `Polyfold.retractLieBracket_natural`, `Polyfold.levelMap_levelMap_comp_eq`,
`Polyfold.IsRetractVectorField.restrict`, `Polyfold.retractLieBracket_restrict`, `Polyfold.retractLieBracket_natural_inter`).**
Let $r$, $r'$ be sc-smooth retractions onto $O$, $O'$, let $f$ be an sc-smooth map from the retract $O$ to the retract $O'$, $g =
f \circ r$ and $Df = Dg$, and let $A$, $B$ be vector fields on $(O, C, E)$ and $A'$, $B'$ on $(O', C', F)$ with $Df(x)A(x) =
A'(f(x))$ and $Df(x)B(x) = B'(f(x))$ for every $x \in O_1$. Then for $x \in O_2$: (a) the relation for $A$ differentiated in a
direction $b$ with $Dr^1(x)b = b$ reads $D^2g(x)(A(x), b) + Dg(x)D\tilde A(x)b = D\tilde A'(g_2(x))Dg^1(x)b$, $\tilde A = A \circ
r^1$, $\tilde A' = A' \circ r'^1$; (b) the relation for $B$ holds on level $1$, $Dg^1(x)B_1(x) = B'_1(g_2(x))$, and $g_2 = f_2$ on
$O_2$; (c) $Df(x)[A, B](x) = [A', B'](f(x))$. A vector field on $O$ is one on the open part $O \cap W$, $W$ open, with the
restricted retraction, and at points of $(O \cap W)_2$ the bracket is the same for both retractions. For $f$ sc-smooth on $O \cap
W$ with $Tf(z, A(z)) = (f(z), A'(f(z)))$ and $Tf(z, B(z)) = (f(z), B'(f(z)))$ on $(O \cap W)_1$, also $Tf(x, [A, B](x)) = (f(x),
[A', B'](f(x)))$ on $(O \cap W)_2$. *Book:* Lemma 4.5.1, p. 201, new in the 2021 edition, whose proof is left to the reader, and
the computation of §4.5.2, pp. 201–202, for a map $\varphi$ with $D\varphi \cdot A = A \circ \varphi$ and $D\varphi \cdot B = B
\circ \varphi$. *Hidden hypotheses:* the relations on an open set of level $1$ (here on all of $O_1$), since the computation
differentiates them at points of $O_2$. *Deviation (restated):* the computation for an sc-smooth $f$ between two local models with
two pairs of vector fields, with $D^2g$ read as in V4.70 and its symmetry; the form on $O \cap W$ is the shape of a transition map
of charts (V4.75). §4.5.2 ends by calling the result "Proposition 4.5.1", a possible misprint for Lemma 4.5.1 (Findings, items
157, 162). *Proof:* the text's: (a) for $A$ with $b = B_1(x)$ and for $B$ with $b = A_1(x)$, both fixed by $Dr^1(x)$ (V4.69), (b)
on both sides, the difference, and the symmetry of $D^2g$.

**V4.75 (principal parts in a chart and the independence of the chart; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentChartMap_change`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartRetraction`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartRetraction_retract`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.principalPart`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentChartMap_eq_principalPart`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScVectorField.isRetractVectorField_principalPart`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScVectorField.principalPart_related`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartLieBracket`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScVectorField.chartLieBracket_spec`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScVectorField.chartLieBracket_change`).**
Let $A$, $B$ be sc-smooth vector fields on the M-polyfold $X$ (V4.68) and $\varphi$, $\psi$ charts of $X$, the model of each with a
chosen sc-smooth retraction. Tangent charts change by $T\psi = T(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1}) \circ T\varphi$ over the overlap (formula
(2.9)). The principal part $A_\varphi$, given on $O_1$ by $T\varphi(A(y)) = (\varphi(y), A_\varphi(\varphi(y)))$ for $y$ of level $1$
in the domain of $\varphi$, is a vector field on the model $(O, C, E)$ (V4.67); the principal parts in $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are
related by the transition map, $T(\psi\varphi^{-1})(z, A_\varphi(z)) = (\psi\varphi^{-1}(z), A_\psi(\psi\varphi^{-1}(z)))$ on level
$1$ of the overlap. The bracket $[A_\varphi, B_\varphi]$ of the principal parts satisfies Proposition 4.4.5 in the model (V4.72), and
the brackets in $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are related by the tangent map of the transition map on level $2$ of the overlap. *Book:* p.
201, new in the 2021 edition: Lemma 4.5.1 shows that the definition of $[A, B]$ does not depend on the local coordinates.
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Proof:* the overlap is $O \cap W$ for an open $W$; V4.74 there, with the relations of the principal
parts.

**V4.76 (Proposition 4.4.5 (preprint 4.26) on an M-polyfold; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.levelLift_levelChart_spec`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.lieBracketPre`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.lieBracket`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentProj_lieBracket`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentChartMap_lieBracket`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentChartMap_lieBracket_eq`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.continuous_lieBracket`, `Polyfold.proposition_4_4_5`).** For sc-smooth vector fields $A$, $B$ on the
M-polyfold $X$, the Lie bracket $[A, B] : X^2 \to TX$, $X^2 = (X^1)^1$, is the tangent vector at $x$ represented by $[A_\varphi,
B_\varphi](\varphi(x))$ in a chart $\varphi$ chosen around $x$. In every chart $\psi$ around $x$, $T\psi([A, B](x)) = (\psi(x), [A_\psi,
B_\psi](\psi(x)))$, so $[A, B]$ depends neither on the chart nor on the retraction chosen for its model; $p([A, B](x)) = x$; and
$[A, B]$ is continuous and sc-smooth from $X^2$ to $TX$. *Book:* Proposition 4.4.5 (preprint 4.26), p. 196 (preprint p. 167), with
the proof in §§4.5.1–4.5.2, pp. 200–202: the bracket, defined in local coordinates by the usual formula, is an sc-smooth section of
$TX|X^2 \to X^2$, the pull-back of $TX \to X^1$ by the inclusion $X^2 \to X^1$ (the preprint and 2017 texts quote it from another
paper, as a vector field on $X^1$). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "an sc-smooth section of $TX|X^2 \to X^2$"
is read as an sc-smooth map $X^2 \to TX$ that covers the inclusion $X^2 \to X^1$; (2026-11-12) the pull-back bundle is built as a
sub-M-polyfold of $X^2 \times TX$ and $[A, B]$ is an sc-smooth section of it (`Polyfold.proposition_4_4_5_section`; gap G.92, closed). The earlier statement, a vector field on $X^1$, would through $\Phi$ (V4.78) put $[A, B](x)$ in $E_1$ for $x \in X_2$,
which the example of V4.73 excludes; as we read it, it does not hold, and the 2021 statement does. With V4.72, V4.75 and V4.77
this closes gap G.38 (Findings, item 161). *Proof:* in the chart $(\psi^1)^1$ of $X^2$ and the
tangent chart $T\psi$, $[A, B]$ reads $z \mapsto (z, [A_\psi, B_\psi](z))$, sc-smooth by V4.72; the chart does not matter by V4.75.

**V4.77 (Lemma 4.5.1 on M-polyfolds; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.liftLevelOneMap`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.levelTwoMap`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.levelMap_coord_levelLift`, `Polyfold.lemma_4_5_1`).** Let $f : X \to Y$ be an sc-smooth map of
M-polyfolds with level maps $f_1 : X^1 \to Y^1$ and $f_2 : X^2 \to Y^2$, $A$, $B$ sc-smooth vector fields on $X$ and $A'$, $B'$ on
$Y$ with $Tf(A(x)) = A'(f_1(x))$ and $Tf(B(x)) = B'(f_1(x))$ for every $x \in X^1$. Then $Tf([A, B](x)) = [A', B'](f_2(x))$ for
every $x \in X^2$. *Book:* Lemma 4.5.1, p. 201, new in the 2021 edition, whose proof is left to the reader: for a local
sc-diffeomorphism $\varphi : X \to X$ and vector fields with $T\varphi(A(x)) = A(\varphi(x))$ and $T\varphi(B(x)) = B(\varphi(x))$ at
points of $X_2$, $T\varphi([A, B](x)) = [A, B](\varphi(x))$ for $x \in X_2$. *Hidden hypotheses:* the relations on an open set of
$X^1$, which the computation of §4.5.2 differentiates. *Deviation (restated):* more general in the map (any sc-smooth $f$, between
two M-polyfolds, with a pair of vector fields on each side); the relations are assumed on all of $X^1$, not only at the points of
$X_2$. A local sc-diffeomorphism between open subsets of $X$ is covered by `Polyfold.lemma_4_5_1_open` (2026-11-12), with the open
subsets as Part I's open sub-M-polyfolds, and on sections of $TX|X^2$ by `Polyfold.lemma_4_5_1_section` (gap G.92, closed)
(Findings, items 162, 163). *Proof:* in charts $\varphi$ around $x$ and $\psi$ around $f(x)$,
$Tf$ reads $T(\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1})$, the principal parts are related by $\psi f \varphi^{-1}$ on the open part of the
model where it is defined, and V4.74 applies there.

**V4.78 (Lemma 4.4.4 on an M-polyfold, $i = 1$; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.vectorFieldLevelOne`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.raiseIndex`,
`Polyfold.lemma_4_4_4`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentShiftEquiv`, `Polyfold.proposition_2_3_17`).** For an sc-smooth
vector field $A$ on $X$, let $A_1 : X^2 \to (TX)^1$ be its level-$1$ map and $\Phi : T(X^1) \to (TX)^1$ the identification of
Proposition 2.3.17 (an sc-diffeomorphism, compatible with the projections to $X^2$). Then $A^{(1)} = \Phi^{-1} \circ A_1$ is an
sc-smooth vector field on the M-polyfold $X^1$, that is, an sc-smooth section of $T(X^1) \to X^2$, and $\Phi(A^{(1)}(x)) = A(x)$ in
$(TX)^1$ for every $x \in X^2$. *Book:* Lemma 4.4.4, p. 196, new in the 2021 edition: through the natural identification of $(TX)^i
\to (X^1)^i$ with $T(X^i) \to X^{i+1}$ the index of $A$ can be raised by every $i \ge 0$. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (narrower):* $i = 1$; every fixed $i$ follows by applying the lemma to $X^1$, $X^2$, …, since $A^{(1)}$ is again an
sc-smooth vector field; the statement for every $i$ is V4.79 (Findings, items 160, 164). The identification $(TX)^i \cong
T(X^i)$ is Proposition 2.3.17 (`Polyfold.proposition_2_3_17`, `Polyfold.proposition_2_3_17_two`, and for every $i$
`Polyfold.proposition_2_3_17_all`; gap G.6, closed). *Proof:* $A_1$ is sc-smooth (the level-$1$ map of an sc-smooth map), $\Phi^{-1}$ is sc-smooth, and $\Phi$ is
compatible with the projections, so $p \circ A^{(1)}$ is the identity of $X^2$.

**V4.79 (Lemma 4.4.4 on an M-polyfold, every $i$; `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.lift`,
`Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.raiseIndexAll`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.tangentIncl_raiseIndexAll`,
`Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.vectorFieldScMap`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.tangentLiftEquiv_raiseIndexAll`,
`Polyfold.lemma_4_4_4_all`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.lemma_4_4_4_all_zero`,
`Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.tangentLiftEquiv`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.shiftLiftEquiv`,
`Polyfold.proposition_2_3_17_all`).** Let $X$ be an M-polyfold, $X^i$ its $i$-th lift ($X^0 = X$, $X^{i+1} = (X^i)^1$), and
$\Phi_i : T(X^i) \to (TX)^i$, $J_i : (X^1)^i \to (X^i)^1$ the sc-diffeomorphisms of Proposition 2.3.17 for every $i$. For an
sc-smooth vector field $A$ on $X$ put $A^{(0)} = A$ and $A^{(i+1)} = (A^{(i)})^{(1)}$, the index raise of V4.78 on $X^i$. Then for
every $i \ge 0$: $A^{(i)}$ is an sc-smooth vector field on $X^i$, a section of $T(X^i) \to X^{i+1}$; it is $A$, in that its image
under the inclusion $T(X^i) \to TX$ at $x \in X^{i+1}$ is $A(x)$; and $\Phi_i \circ A^{(i)} \circ J_i$ is the $i$-th index raise
$(X^1)^i \to (TX)^i$ of $A : X^1 \to TX$. The zero vector field gives a witness for every $i$. *Book:* Lemma 4.4.4, p. 196, new
in the 2021 edition, with the diagram printed before it. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the lifts $X^i$
are bundled with their spaces, so that they form one family indexed by $i$; "the natural identification" is $\Phi_i$ and $J_i$,
and "$A^{(i)}$ is $A$" is read through the inclusions into $TX$ and through the diagram (Findings, item 164). *Proof:*
induction on $i$, with V4.78 on $X^i$; the two identities are checked after the inclusion into $TX$, which is injective and
commutes with $\Phi_i$ (Proposition 2.3.17).

**V4.80 (The Whitney sum $\oplus_kTX$, in the local models; `Polyfold.ScBanach.fiberPow`, `Polyfold.ScBanach.whitney`, `Polyfold.retractWhitney`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.whitney`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.whitney_retract`, `Polyfold.IsScRetract.whitney`, `Polyfold.retractWhitneyMap`, `Polyfold.IsScSmoothRetractMap.whitney`).** `IsScRetract.whitney`: for an sc-retract $(O, C, E)$, $\oplus_kTO = \{(x, h_1, \dots, h_k) : x \in O_1,\ h_i \in T_xO\}$ (`retractWhitney`) is an sc-retract of $E^1 \oplus E^k$ (`ScBanach.whitney`), the image of the retraction $\oplus_kTr$ (`ScRetraction.whitney`). `IsScSmoothRetractMap.whitney`: $\oplus_kTf$ (`retractWhitneyMap`) is sc-smooth for $f$ sc-smooth between retracts, so the charts $\oplus_kT\varphi$ have sc-smooth transitions. *Book:* §4.4, p. 195, before Definition 4.4.1, (New in the 2021 edition.) The tangent bundle $TX \to X^1$ is an sc-smooth bundle, and "it is an easy exercise" that the Whitney sum $TX \oplus \cdots \oplus TX \to X^1$ of $k$ copies is an sc-smooth bundle. *Deviation (restated):* The exercise is done in the local models. $\oplus_kTX$ is not assembled into an M-polyfold bundle: forms are read in its charts $\oplus_kT\varphi$ (V4.81). $E^k$ is an iterated product $E \oplus (E \oplus \cdots)$ (`ScBanach.fiberPow`) (Findings, Chapter 4, item 168).

**V4.81 (Definition 4.4.1 (preprint 4.25): sc-differential $k$-forms; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScForm`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartForm`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartForm_eq`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartForm_transition`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScForm_of_cover`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.scForms`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.constForm_mem_scForms`, `Polyfold.IsRetractScForm`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScForm.isRetractScForm`).** `MPolyfold.IsScForm P k ω`: $\omega$ is a family of alternating $k$-linear maps on the tangent spaces $T_xX$, $x \in X^1$, whose representative `chartForm hφ ω` on $\oplus_kTO$ ($\omega_\varphi(T\varphi\,\alpha) = \omega(x)(\alpha)$, `chartForm_eq`) is sc-smooth in every chart $\varphi$ of the maximal atlas. By `isScForm_of_cover` a covering family of charts suffices (chart change: `chartForm_transition`). `MPolyfold.scForms P k` is the vector space $\Omega^k(X)$; witnesses: $0$ and the constant $0$-forms (`constForm_mem_scForms`). In a local model the notion is `IsRetractScForm`, and `IsScForm.isRetractScForm` says that the representatives are local forms. *Book:* §4.4, Definition 4.4.1 (preprint 4.25), p. 195 (preprint p. 167), An sc-differential $k$-form on $X$ is an sc-smooth map $\omega : \oplus_kTX \to \mathbb R$ which is linear in each argument and skew-symmetric; these forms make up the vector space $\Omega^k(X)$. *Deviation (restated):* "Linear in each argument and skew-symmetric" is built into the type (Mathlib's alternating maps on $T_xX$, a linear space by V2.19). "Sc-smooth on $\oplus_kTX$" is read in the charts $\oplus_kT\varphi$ (V4.80), for every chart of the maximal atlas; a covering family suffices, so the quantifier over all charts is not vacuous. There is no nonzero witness for $k \ge 1$ (a natural one, $df$, is not built) (Findings, Chapter 4, item 168).

**V4.82 (The directed system (4.4) and Definition 4.4.2: $\Omega^k_\infty(X)$, $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.lowerFiberCLM`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.formLower`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.formLower_mem_scForms`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.forms`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsMap`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsMap_comp`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.directedSystem_forms`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInfty`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyOf`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyOf_formsMap`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyGraded`).** `formLower_mem_scForms`: the pull-back by $X^1 \to X$ (fibrewise the inclusion `lowerFiberCLM`, the map $T(X^1) \to TX$ of Proposition 2.3.17) maps $\Omega^k(X)$ to $\Omega^k(X^1)$. `BundledMPolyfold.formsMap` is the directed system $\Omega^k(X^i) \to \Omega^k(X^j)$, $i \le j$ (`formsMap_comp`, `directedSystem_forms`); `formsInfty A k` is its direct limit $\Omega^k_\infty(X)$ (Mathlib's `Module.DirectLimit`), with the classes `formsInftyOf`; `formsInftyGraded A` is $\oplus_k\Omega^k_\infty(X)$. *Book:* §4.4, (4.4) and Definition 4.4.2, p. 195 (preprint p. 167, after Definition 4.25), Pull-back by the inclusions $X^i \to X$ gives the directed system (4.4) $\Omega^k(X) \to \cdots \to \Omega^k(X^i) \to \Omega^k(X^{i+1}) \to \cdots$, whose direct limit $\Omega^k_\infty(X)$ is a real vector space; its elements are the sc-differential $k$-forms on $X_\infty$, and $\Omega^*_\infty(X) = \oplus_k\Omega^k_\infty(X)$. *Deviation (same):* The lifts $X^i$ are the bundled `BundledMPolyfold.lift`, as in V4.79. The preprint writes $\Omega^*_\infty$ both for the limit and for the sum (Findings, Chapter 4, item 124); the 2021 text and the formal version use two names (item 168).

**V4.83 (The formula for $d\omega$ (p. 197) with the bracket of §4.5.1; `Polyfold.bookBracket`, `Polyfold.bookBracket_eq_neg_lieBracket`, `Polyfold.invariantFormula`, `Polyfold.correctSign`, `Polyfold.printedSign`, `Polyfold.item158Sign`, `Polyfold.extDeriv_eq_invariantFormula`, `Polyfold.invariantFormula_printedSign_counterexample`).** `extDeriv_eq_invariantFormula`: on a real normed space, for a $k$-form $\omega$ and fields $V_0, \dots, V_k$ differentiable at $x$, $d\omega(V_0, \dots, V_k)$ (Mathlib's `extDeriv`) equals the formula with the text's bracket $[A, B] = DA\cdot B - DB\cdot A$ (`bookBracket`, $= -$`lieBracket`, `bookBracket_eq_neg_lieBracket`) and the sign $(-1)^{\ell+j+1}$ on the pair $\ell < j$ (`correctSign`). `invariantFormula_printedSign_counterexample`: for $k = 1$, $\omega = dy$ on $\mathbb R^2$, $A_0 = (1, 0)$ and $A_1(p) = (0, p_1)$, the formula with the printed sign $(-1)^{\ell+k}$ (`printedSign`) gives $2$ at $0$, and so does the sign $(-1)^{\ell+j}$ (`item158Sign`), while $d\omega = 0$; with $A_1' = 0$, which equals $A_1$ at $0$, the printed formula gives $0$. *Book:* §4.4, p. 197 (preprint p. 167), the formula for $d\omega$; the bracket: Appendix 4.5.1, p. 200, (2021) $d\omega(A_0^{(1)}, \dots, A_k^{(1)})$ is given by "the familiar formula": the sum over $j$ of $(-1)^jD(\omega(A_0, \dots, \hat A_j, \dots, A_k))\cdot A_j^{(1)}$ (printed with the summation index $i$), plus the sum over $\ell < j$ of $(-1)^{\ell+k}\,\omega([A_\ell, A_j], A_0^{(1)}, \dots, \hat A_\ell^{(1)}, \dots, \hat A_j^{(1)}, \dots, A_k^{(1)})$, where $[A, B] = DA\cdot B - DB\cdot A$ (p. 200). The preprint (p. 167) and the 2017 text print the sign $(-1)^{i+j}$ and give the bracket only as "the usual formula". *Deviation (narrower):* Narrower: with the text's bracket and the printed sign $(-1)^{\ell+k}$ the formula does not hold as we read it (`invariantFormula_printedSign_counterexample`): its right side is $2$ where $d\omega = 0$, and it changes when $A_1$ is changed away from the point, so it is not tensorial. The classical sign $(-1)^{\ell+j}$, which item 158 proposed, fails on the same example, since the text's bracket is the negative of the classical one. With $(-1)^{\ell+j+1}$ the formula is Mathlib's $d$ (`extDeriv_eq_invariantFormula`); the printed sign is possibly a misprint, or the text may intend another bracket convention. The index $i$ of the first sum is read as $j$ (Findings, Chapter 4, items 158, 167). Read in the classical setting, a real normed space, to which the sc formula reduces in a chart. The formal $d$ on M-polyfolds (V4.84, V4.85) is defined by the local formula, so the sign does not enter it.

**V4.84 (The exterior derivative in the local models: the local formula, naturality, independence of the retraction; `Polyfold.ambientD`, `Polyfold.ambientD_apply`, `Polyfold.IsScSmooth.ambientD`, `Polyfold.scDeriv_relation`, `Polyfold.ambientD_whitneyMk`, `Polyfold.IsAmbientScForm`, `Polyfold.IsAmbientScForm.ambientD`, `Polyfold.retractD`, `Polyfold.IsRetractScForm.retractD`, `Polyfold.ambientD_comp_whitneyMap`, `Polyfold.retractD_comp_retractWhitneyMap`, `Polyfold.retractD_eq_of_subset`, `Polyfold.sum_update_symm_eq_zero`).** `ambientD U Ω`$(y, h_0, \dots, h_k) = \sum_j(-1)^jD\Omega(y, h_0, \dots, \hat h_j, \dots, h_k)(h_j, 0)$ (`ambientD_apply`), built from $T\Omega$ and sc-operators. `IsAmbientScForm.ambientD` and `IsRetractScForm.retractD`: $d$ maps sc-forms on $U$ (relatively open in a partial quadrant), and on a retract $O$ (as $d(\omega \circ \oplus_kTr)$), to sc-forms one level up: sc-smooth (`IsScSmooth.ambientD`) and alternating (`ambientD_whitneyMk`, via `scDeriv_relation`). `ambientD_comp_whitneyMap` and `retractD_comp_retractWhitneyMap`: $d(f^*\Omega) = f^*d\Omega$ for sc-smooth $f$. `retractD_eq_of_subset`: $d$ does not depend on the retraction. *Book:* §4.4, pp. 196–197 (preprint p. 167), the definition of $d\omega$, (2021) For an sc-differential $k$-form $\omega$ on $X^i$ and sc-smooth vector fields $A_0, \dots, A_k$ on $X^i$ (sections $X^{i+1} \to T(X^i)$), $d\omega$ on $\oplus_{k+1}T(X^{i+1})$ is defined through the maps $D(\omega(A_0, \dots, \hat A_j, \dots, A_k))$ and the brackets $[A_\ell, A_j]$ by the formula of p. 197. *Deviation (restated):* The text defines $d$ through vector fields. Its formula in a chart is used here: on normed spaces it agrees with the invariant formula with the sign $(-1)^{\ell+j+1}$ (V4.83), and it makes $d$ on an M-polyfold well defined (V4.85). Naturality, and with it the independence of the retraction, uses the symmetry of the second derivative (`scSecondDeriv_symm`), as the bracket does in §4.5.2 (Findings, Chapter 4, item 169).

**V4.85 (The exterior derivative $d : \Omega^k(X^i) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^{i+1})$ on an M-polyfold; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartD`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartD_transition`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.extD`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.extD_apply`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartForm_extD`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.extD_mem_scForms`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.extD_add`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.extD_smul`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.extDₗ`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsD`).** `MPolyfold.extD ω` at $x \in X^2$ is $d(\omega_\varphi)(\varphi(x), T\varphi^1\,\cdot)$ on $T_x(X^1)$, with `chartD` the local $d$ of V4.84 in the chart $\varphi$. `extD_apply`: the same holds in every chart around $x$ (from `chartD_transition`), so $d$ does not depend on the chart. `extD_mem_scForms`: $d\omega \in \Omega^{k+1}(X^1)$ for $\omega \in \Omega^k(X)$, with representative `chartForm_extD` in the level charts. `extD_add`, `extD_smul`, `extDₗ`: $d$ is linear. On the lifts, `BundledMPolyfold.formsD` is $\Omega^k(X^i) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^{i+1})$. *Book:* §4.4, p. 197 (preprint p. 167), (2021) The formula defines the exterior derivative as a linear operator $d : \Omega^k(X^i) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^{i+1})$. (The preprint writes $d : \Omega^k(X^{i+1}) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^i)$.) *Deviation (restated):* $d$ is the local formula in charts (V4.84), not the vector-field formula, which is proved on normed spaces only (V4.83). Domain and target are those of the 2021 text, the direction item 120 proposed for the preprint. On a family that is not an sc-form, `extD` is $0$ by convention (Findings, Chapter 4, item 169).

In the local models `ambientD_ambientD` and `retractD_shift_retractD`, from the symmetry of the second derivative and `sum_removeNth_symm_eq_zero`. **V4.87 ($d$ commutes with $X^{i+1} \to X^i$; $d$ on $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.extD_formLower`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsD_formsStep`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsD_formsMap`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyD`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyD_of`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyGradedD`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.formWedge`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.formWedge_mem_scForms`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.extD_formWedge`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyWedge`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyD_formsInftyWedge`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyWedge_assoc`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyWedge_comm`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyGAlgebra`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyGraded_of_mul_of_comm`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyGradedD_of_mul_of`).** `extD_formLower`: $d(\iota^*\omega) = \iota^*(d\omega)$ for $\iota : X^1 \to X$; `formsD_formsStep` and `formsD_formsMap` give the squares with the maps of (4.4). `formsInftyD A k` $: \Omega^k_\infty(X) \to \Omega^{k+1}_\infty(X)$ is the induced map (`formsInftyD_of`: $d[\omega] = [d\omega]$), and `formsInftyGradedD` the same map on $\oplus_k\Omega^k_\infty(X)$, of degree $+1$. (2026-11-12) The wedge product: `formWedge` is the pointwise $\omega \wedge \tau$, with $\Omega^k(X) \wedge \Omega^l(X) \subseteq \Omega^{k+l}(X)$ (`formWedge_mem_scForms`) and $d(\omega \wedge \tau) = d\omega \wedge \iota^*\tau + (-1)^k\iota^*\omega \wedge d\tau$ (`extD_formWedge`); `formsInftyWedge` is the induced bilinear map on $\Omega^*_\infty(X)$, associative, graded commutative and unital (`formsInftyWedge_assoc`, `formsInftyWedge_comm`, `formsInftyOne`), with $d(a \wedge b) = da \wedge b + (-1)^k a \wedge db$ (`formsInftyD_formsInftyWedge`). $\bigoplus_k\Omega^k_\infty(X)$ is a graded $\mathbb R$-algebra (`formsInftyGAlgebra`, Mathlib's `DirectSum.GAlgebra`), graded commutative (`formsInftyGraded_of_mul_of_comm`), on which $d$ is a derivation of degree $+1$ (`formsInftyGradedD_of_mul_of`) with $d^2 = 0$ (`formsInftyGradedD_comp_self`). *Book:* §4.4, pp. 197–198 (preprint p. 168), $d$ commutes with the inclusion $X^{i+1} \to X^i$ of the directed system (the square from $\Omega^k(X^i) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^{i+1})$ to $\Omega^k(X^{i+1}) \to \Omega^{k+1}(X^{i+2})$); passing to the limit gives $d : \Omega^*_\infty(X) \to \Omega^*_\infty(X)$. *Deviation (same):* "Passing to the limit" is Mathlib's `Module.DirectLimit.lift`. **V4.88 (Definition 4.4.6 (preprint 4.27): the sc-de Rham cohomology $H^*_{sc}(X)$; `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyDRange`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyDRange_le_ker`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.scDeRham`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.scDeRhamMk`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.scDeRhamMk_eq_iff`).** `BundledMPolyfold.scDeRham A k` is $\ker d/\operatorname{im} d$ in degree $k$, a real vector space, with `formsInftyDRange` the image $d(\Omega^{k-1}_\infty(X))$ ($0$ for $k = 0$) and `formsInftyDRange_le_ker`: $\operatorname{im} d \subseteq \ker d$. `scDeRhamMk_eq_iff`: two closed forms have the same class iff they differ by an exact form. *Book:* §4.4, Definition 4.4.6 (preprint 4.27), p. 198 (preprint p. 168), The sc-de Rham cohomology of the M-polyfold $X$ is $H^*_{sc}(X) = \ker(d)/\operatorname{im}(d)$. *Deviation (same):* The text writes $H^*_{sc}(X)$ for the graded space; it is read degree by degree. **V4.89 (The pull-back $f^*$ and $f^*\circ d_Y = d_X\circ f^*$ (p. 198); `Polyfold.MPolyfold.tangentFiberMap`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.formPullback`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartForm_formPullback`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.formPullback_mem_scForms`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.extD_formPullback`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.formPullback_comp`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.formPullback_id`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.formLower_formPullback`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsPullback`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyPullback`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyD_comp_formsInftyPullback`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyPullback_comp`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.scDeRhamPullback`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.formPullback_formWedge`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyPullback_formsInftyWedge`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyPullback_formsInftyOne`).** `formPullback hf ω` is $\omega(f(x))(Tf\,\alpha_1, \dots, Tf\,\alpha_k)$, with $Tf$ on the fibres the continuous linear map `tangentFiberMap` (`tangentMapCLM`). **V4.90 (Forms on $\partial X$ and the pull-back $j^*$ (pp. 198–199); `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsAgreeingOver`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsFaceCompatible`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.bForms`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.extD_mem_bForms`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.le_bForms`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.bFormsInfty`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.jStar`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.formsPullback_mem_bForms`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.jStar_comp_D`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isFaceCompatible_extD`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.bForms_eq_agreeForms`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.mem_bForms_iff`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasCornerCover_bdryMap`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isTangentInjective_bdryMap`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.CornerChart.exists_tangent`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.isAgreeingOver_extD`).** `bForms hP k i` $= \Omega^k(\partial X^i)$: the sc-forms $\tau \in \Omega^k(bX^i)$ on the tame boundary (Theorem 2.7.13) that agree over $B^i$ (`IsFaceCompatible`: $\tau_p(v) = \tau_{p'}(v')$ when $Bp = Bp'$ and $TB\,v_j = TB\,v'_j$); `mem_bForms_iff`, `bForms_eq_agreeForms`. **V4.92 (Theorem 4.4.7 (preprint 4.28) for sc-forms on a finite-dimensional submanifold: Stokes; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.stokes_formsInftyRestrict`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.scFormRestrict`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.scFormRestrict_apply_modelDeriv`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.formsInftyRestrict`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.contMDiffForm_formsInftyRestrict`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.extDeriv_formsInftyRestrict`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.scFormRestrict_formLower`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.subset_smoothSet_of_hasCornerStructureOfDim`, `Polyfold.exists_hasCornerStructureOfDim_of_tame`, `Polyfold.exists_hasCornerStructureOfDim_solutionSet`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.theorem_4_4_7_hyp`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.faceOrientation`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isFaceStructured_of_forall_degIndex_eq_zero`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasCornerStructureOfDim_face`, `Polyfold.sum_integral_restrictForm_eq_boundaryIntegral`, `Polyfold.restrictForm`, `Polyfold.IsInducedOrientation`, `Polyfold.inducedOrientation`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.finite_setOf_isFace`).** `MPolyfold.stokes_formsInftyRestrict`: for a compact sub-M-polyfold $S \subseteq X$ with a corner structure of dimension $n + 1$ (then $S \subseteq X_\infty$, `subset_smoothSet_of_hasCornerStructureOfDim`), a continuous tangent orientation $o$ of the Mathlib manifold $S$ (`cornerChartedSpace`) and $\omega \in \Omega^n_\infty(X)$, $\int_S (d\omega)|_S = \int_{\partial S} \omega|_S$. The restriction $\omega \mapsto \omega|_S$ (`scFormRestrict` on $\Omega^k(X^i)$, `formsInftyRestrict` on $\Omega^k_\infty(X)$) is the pull-back along $S \to X^i$ (V4.89) read on the corner frames of $T_xS = \mathbb R^n$; in a chart of $X$ it is $\omega_\varphi \circ$ `modelDeriv` (`scFormRestrict_apply_modelDeriv`). It is $C^\infty$ (`contMDiffForm_formsInftyRestrict`) and commutes with $d$ (`extDeriv_formsInftyRestrict`) and with the system (4.4) (`scFormRestrict_formLower`). $\int_{\partial S}$ is the boundary integral of the Mathlib manifold $S$. The corner structures exist for every submanifold in good position of a tame $X$ (`exists_hasCornerStructureOfDim_of_tame`), in particular for the solution sets of Theorem 6.6.18 (`exists_hasCornerStructureOfDim_solutionSet`). (2026-11-12) With the faces: `MPolyfold.theorem_4_4_7_hyp`: for a compact sub-M-polyfold $S \subseteq X$ with a corner structure of dimension $n + 1$, face-structured (Definition 2.5.10), a continuous tangent orientation $o$ of the Mathlib manifold $S$ and $\omega \in \Omega^n_\infty(X)$, $\int_S (d\omega)|_S = \sum_F \int_F \omega|_F$, the sum over the finitely many faces $F$ of $S$ (`finite_setOf_isFace`). Each face is a Mathlib manifold modelled on $[0, \infty)^n$ through a corner structure of dimension $n$ (`hasCornerStructureOfDim_face`), oriented by the induced orientation, outward vector first (`faceOrientation`, `IsInducedOrientation`, unique and continuous); $\omega|_F$ is the pull-back of $\omega|_S$ along $F \hookrightarrow S$ (`restrictForm`). The face sum equals the boundary integral of $S$ (`sum_integral_restrictForm_eq_boundaryIntegral`), and `stokes_formsInftyRestrict` gives the rest. *Book:* §4.4, Theorem 4.4.7 (preprint 4.28), p. 199 (preprint p. 168), For an oriented compact tame smooth $n$-dimensional submanifold $N$ whose boundary is a union of faces $F$, and an sc-differential $(n - 1)$-form $\omega$, $\int_N d\omega = \sum_F\int_F\omega$. *Deviation (restated):* The text's $N$ is an oriented compact tame smooth submanifold; here $S$ is a compact sub-M-polyfold with a corner structure of dimension $n + 1$, which every submanifold in good position of a tame $X$ has, with a continuous tangent orientation (as Theorem 6.6.18 gives the solution sets, V6.61). The boundary being a union of faces is read as $S$ face-structured (Definition 2.5.10): every point lies on exactly $d_S(x)$ faces. This is a reading, used through "a face is a coordinate face near each of its points" and "a point of degeneracy index 1 lies on exactly one face"; whether it can be dropped is not examined. It is satisfiable: it holds without boundary (`isFaceStructured_of_forall_degIndex_eq_zero`; then the sum is empty and the theorem says $\int_S d\omega = 0$) and for the quadrants (`isFaceStructured_quadrant`). The faces are manifolds in their own right and the sum is over them, each with the induced orientation (outward vector first, Findings, Chapter 4, item 171; gap G.40, closed). The restriction of $\omega$ to $N$, "clearly" a classical form in the text (p. 199), is the pull-back along the inclusion (items 172, 174, 177). The 2021 text writes $\int_N$, the preprint and 2017 $\int_M$ (item 123).

**V4.93 (Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23): stratified regularity does not depend on the chart; `Polyfold.StratRegCond`, `Polyfold.StratRegCond.transport`, `Polyfold.stratRegCond_chart_change`, `Polyfold.IsStratRegularPoint.stratRegCond`, `Polyfold.isStratRegularPoint_iff_forall`, `Polyfold.isStratRegularValue_iff_forall`).** `StratRegCond` is the chart condition of `IsStratRegularPoint` (every $\mu \in \mathbb R^m$ is $v_1$ for some $v \in T_yQ$ with $v_2$ in the minimal subspace of $C$ at $y_2$); it depends only on the tangent space (`StratRegCond.congr`) and is carried by germs of sc-diffeomorphisms $F$ with $(Fw)_1 = w_1 + c$ that preserve the product partial quadrants (`StratRegCond.transport`). Product-chart transitions have first component $w_1 + a - a'$ (`transition_rnChart_prod_fst`), so their derivatives fix the $\mathbb R^m$-component (`scDeriv_fst_eq_of_fst_eq`), and the condition passes from one product chart, presentation, data and level-1 lift to any other (`stratRegCond_chart_change`). `IsStratRegularPoint.stratRegCond`: a stratified regular point satisfies the condition in every product chart $(r \mapsto r - a') \times \varphi'$, every data of Definition 4.2.1, every presentation and every lift; `isStratRegularPoint_iff_forall`, `isStratRegularValue_iff_forall`: "some chart" $\Leftrightarrow$ "every chart". *Book:* §4.3, proof of Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23), p. 194 (preprint p. 166), Regular values of the maps $p_\sigma : A \cap F_\sigma^\circ \to \mathbb R^m$, intrinsic to $A$ and its strata. *Deviation (restated):* Stratified regularity is read as in V4.53: regularity of $p$ on the stratum through the point, in a product chart (Findings, Chapter 4, items 102, 108). That it is intrinsic to $A$ and its strata, which the proof of Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23) takes for granted, is proved by the transport argument of V4.39 (gap G.36, closed).

**V4.94 (Lemma 4.1.11 (preprint 4.10): the section $u \mapsto (1 - p)(u - t(u))$ is sc-Fredholm; `Polyfold.lemma_4_1_11`, `Polyfold.isConjugateToBasicGerm_qOp`, `Polyfold.exists_splitData`, `Polyfold.isScSubspace_splitW`, `Polyfold.qOp`, `Polyfold.LocalBundle.bundle`, `Polyfold.LocalBundle.sec`, `Polyfold.LocalBundle.isScSmoothSection_sec`, `Polyfold.isFilling2021_of_R_eq_self`).** `lemma_4_1_11`: in the setting of Proposition 4.1.9 (an sc⁺-retraction $t$ onto $O \ni 0$, $N = T_0O$ in good position, $Y$ a good sc-complement (`hsplit : E.IsScSplitting N Y`), $p$ the projection onto $N$ along $Y$), the section $u \mapsto (u, (1 - p)(u - t(u)))$ of the local strong bundle $U \triangleleft Y \to U$ (`LocalBundle.bundle`, `LocalBundle.sec`, one chart with the identity strong bundle retraction) is sc-Fredholm in the sense of 2021 Definition 3.1.16 (`IsScFredholmSection2021`), on all of $U$. Regularizing: $u = (1 - p)(u - tu) + tu + p(u - tu)$. Germ at a smooth $e$: the chart centred at $e$ (`LocalBundle.centred`), whose retraction is pointwise the identity, so the principal part fills itself (`isFilling2021_of_R_eq_self`); $s(v) = (1 - p)(e - t(v + e))$ is the text's $s$, and $g - s = (1 - p)v$ is conjugated to the basic germ $(a + b, w) \mapsto (b, w)$ (`isConjugateToBasicGerm_qOp`), with the splitting $E \cong (T_0O \oplus B) \oplus W$, $B$ smooth, $W = Y \cap \ker L$ (`exists_splitData`, `isScSubspace_splitW`). *Book:* §4.1, Lemma 4.1.11 (preprint 4.10), pp. 179–181 (preprint pp. 151–153), The section $u \mapsto (u, \mathbf f(u))$, $\mathbf f(u) = (1 - p)(u - t(u))$, of the local strong bundle $U \triangleleft Y \to U$ is sc-Fredholm. *Deviation (restated):* The text's "good sc-complement" is the hypothesis `hsplit : E.IsScSplitting N Y` together with the project's `IsGoodComplement`, which keeps only the algebraic splitting; it is a hypothesis of the text, not an added one (satisfiable wherever Proposition 4.1.9 applies, with the closed complement chosen there). No witness of the full data of Proposition 4.1.9 is built. In the proof, $B$ must lie in $Y_\infty$ for $E = (T_0O \oplus B) \oplus W$ to be an sc-splitting; such $B$ exists, since $L(Y \cap E_\infty) = L(Y)$ (`map_le_map_smooth`). The text gets "$C \cap (T_0O \oplus B)$ is a partial quadrant" from good position; here it comes from the corner coordinates on $T_0O \oplus B$, which vanish on $W$. The slips of the printed proof (Findings, item 57) do not enter. Proposition 4.1.9 (preprint 4.9), its only use, is proved directly (V4.20).

**V4.95 (Lemma 4.4.8: the Poincaré lemma for sc-forms (p. 199); `Polyfold.lemma_4_4_8`, `Polyfold.lemma_4_4_8_of_local`, `Polyfold.LocalPoincare`, `Polyfold.localPoincare`, `Polyfold.hasPoincare_lift`, `Polyfold.exists_primitive_of_factor`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasPoincare`, `Polyfold.LocalModel.liftEquiv`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.formRestrict`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.extD_formRestrict`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.openSub`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyResOpen`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyResOpenOpen`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.FormsInftyEqOn`, `Polyfold.BundledMPolyfold.formsInftyEqOn_of_iff`).** `lemma_4_4_8 A x`: there are open $V \subseteq U \ni x$ such that for every $k$ every $a \in \Omega^{k+1}_\infty(U)$ with $da = 0$ has $b \in \Omega^k_\infty(V)$ with $db = a|_V$. $U$, $V$ are Part I's open sub-M-polyfolds (`restrictOpen`, bundled as `BundledMPolyfold.openSub`); forms restrict to open subsets, commuting with $d$ (`formRestrict`, `extD_formRestrict`, `formsInftyResOpen`, `formsInftyResOpenOpen`), and "$[\omega] = [\tau]$ on $V$" of (4.7) is `FormsInftyEqOn` (`formsInftyEqOn_of_iff`). The proof is the text's: a chart $\varphi$ and retraction $r$ with $r(B_\delta \cap C) \subseteq B_\varepsilon$ (`exists_poincareChart`), $V(x) = \varphi^{-1}(B_\delta(\varphi x))$, the M-polyfold $O^m$ as the $m$-th lift (`LocalModel.liftEquiv`), Lemma 4.5.2 on $B_\delta(\varphi x) \cap C$ about a smooth centre on every level (`LocalPoincare`, `hasPoincare_lift`, `localPoincare`), and $d(j^*\tau) = (r \circ j)^*\omega$ on the direct limits (`exists_primitive_of_factor`, `lemma_4_4_8_of_local`). *Book:* §4.4, Lemma 4.4.8, p. 199 (proof §4.5.3, pp. 202–204) (2021), (New in the 2021 edition.) Every $x \in X$ has open neighbourhoods $V(x) \subseteq U(x)$ such that every closed $[\omega] \in \Omega^k_\infty(U(x))$, $k \ge 1$, has $[\tau] \in \Omega^{k-1}_\infty(V(x))$ with $d[\tau] = [\omega]$ on $V(x)$. The proof applies Lemma 4.5.2 in a chart to $B_\delta(x) \cap C$, working with $C^i \subset E^i$ on the levels. *Deviation (restated):* $U(x)$, $V(x)$ are Part I's open sub-M-polyfolds (nonempty, as they contain $x$); "$d[\tau] = [\omega]$ on $V(x)$" is $db = a|_V$; the text's degrees $k \ge 1$, $k - 1$ are $k + 1$, $k$. In the proof Lemma 4.5.2 is applied to the convex set $B_\delta(\varphi(x)) \cap C$, which need not contain $0$, and the remark after Lemma 4.5.2 (a centre $(0, w_0)$) does not cover it; Lemma 4.5.2 is therefore used with the homotopy about any smooth centre, which the same proof gives (V4.96; Findings, Chapter 4, item 177).

**V4.96 (Lemma 4.5.2: the local Poincaré lemma on a convex relatively open set (p. 202); `Polyfold.hasPoincare_relOpen_of_zero_mem`, `Polyfold.hasPoincare_relOpen`, `Polyfold.lemma_4_5_2`, `Polyfold.homotopyForm`, `Polyfold.isScSmooth_homotopyForm`, `Polyfold.ambientD_homotopyForm`, `Polyfold.retractD_eq_ambientD`, `Polyfold.isScSmooth_intervalIntegral`, `Polyfold.isSck_intervalIntegral`, `Polyfold.scDeriv_intervalIntegral`).** `hasPoincare_relOpen_of_zero_mem`: for a local model $M$ with $M.O$ relatively open in the partial quadrant and convex, $0 \in M.O$, and every $k$, every $\sigma \in \Omega^{k+1}(O)$ with $d\sigma = 0$ has $\tau \in \Omega^k(O)$ with $d\tau = \iota^*\sigma$ on $O^1$ (`MPolyfold.HasPoincare`); `hasPoincare_relOpen` is the same about any smooth centre $c \in M.O$. The primitive is the homotopy form $\tau(y)(v) = \int_0^1 t^k\,\omega(c + t(y - c))(y - c, v)\,dt$ (`homotopyForm`, `relOpenForm`), sc-smooth by the sc-smoothness of parametric integrals over $[0, 1]$ (`isScSmooth_intervalIntegral`, `isSck_intervalIntegral`, `scDeriv_intervalIntegral`, by sc-induction through the tangent map) (`isScSmooth_homotopyForm`); `ambientD_homotopyForm` and `lemma_4_5_2` give $d\tau = \omega$ in the chart, with the local $d$ the `deltaFun` of the derivative and the identity $d_r = $ the ambient $d$ on a relatively open set (`retractD_eq_ambientD`). *Book:* Appendix 4.5, Lemma 4.5.2, p. 202 (proof §4.5.3, pp. 202–204) (2021), (New in the 2021 edition.) For $U$ a relatively open convex neighbourhood of $0$ in $[0, \infty)^n \oplus W$ and a closed sc-form $\omega$ on $U$ of degree $k \ge 1$, there is an sc-form $\tau$ on $U$ with $d\tau = \omega$ on $U^1$; $\tau$ is given by the homotopy formula $\tau(y)(v) = \int_0^1 t^{k-1}\omega(ty)(y, v)\,dt$. *Deviation (restated):* The text's degrees $k \ge 1$, $k - 1$ are $k + 1$, $k$; "$d\tau = \omega$ on $U^1$" is $d\tau = \iota^*\omega$ for $\iota : U^1 \to U$, and "closed" is $d\omega = 0$. No hypothesis is added: the hypotheses (convex, relatively open, a smooth centre) are satisfiable, e.g. $D = C = $ the whole space with $c = 0$ (Findings, Chapter 4, item 177).

## 6. Chapter 5 (HWZ §§5.1–5.5 (preprint §§5.1–5.4)): verified except Theorem 5.27 (preprint; not in the 2021 edition) and the Sobolev sc-structure on general bounded domains

Chapter 5 of Part I (pp. 205–236 (preprint pp. 169–199)) is the Fredholm package for M-polyfolds. §5.1 introduces auxiliary norms
on the part $Y_{0,1}$ of biregularity $(0, 1)$ of a strong bundle (Definition 5.1.1 (preprint 5.1), Lemma 5.1.2 (preprint 5.2), Proposition 5.1.3 (preprint 5.3)). §5.2
defines compact solution sets, weakly proper and proper sections (Definition 5.2.1 (preprint 5.4)) and proves that the three agree for
sc-Fredholm sections (Theorem 5.2.2 (preprint 5.5), proof in §5.2 (preprint Appendix 5.4.1)), that solution sets are locally compact on every level
(Theorem 5.2.3 (preprint 5.6)) and compact in $X_\infty$ (Theorem 5.2.4 (preprint 5.7)), and that the shifted sections are sc-Fredholm (Corollary 5.2.5 (preprint 5.8)).
§5.3 builds sc⁺-sections from sc-smooth bump functions (Definition 5.3.1 (preprint 5.9), Proposition 5.3.2 (preprint 5.10), Lemma 5.3.3 (preprint 5.11)), introduces the
allowable sections $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$ (Remark 5.3.4 (preprint 5.12)), and proves the perturbation theorems: transversality when $\partial X =
\emptyset$ (Theorem 5.3.5 (preprint 5.13), Definition 5.3.7 (preprint 5.15)), general position (Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17), Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18)), good position relative to the
boundary (Theorem 5.3.12 (preprint 5.19)), the Morse-type structure of homotopies (Definition 5.3.13 (preprint 5.20), Theorem 5.3.15 (preprint 5.22) with Lemmas 5.3.16, 5.3.17 (preprint 5.23, 5.24)),
perturbation into good position (Theorem 5.25 (preprint; not in the 2021 edition), Lemma 5.26 (preprint; not in the 2021 edition)) and cobordisms (Theorem 5.27 (preprint)). §5.5 (preprint Appendix 5.4.2) discusses
sc-smooth bump functions and partitions of unity (Definitions 5.5.1–5.5.14 (preprint 5.28–5.41), Theorems 5.5.5–5.5.16 (preprint 5.32–5.43), Corollary 5.5.17 (preprint 5.44)).

What is verified. **Theorems 5.2.2, 5.2.3, 5.2.4, 5.3.5, 5.3.10, 5.3.12, 5.5.7, 5.5.10 (preprint 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, 5.13, 5.18, 5.19, 5.34, 5.37) and Theorem 5.25 (preprint) hold**, with the readings recorded
below, and so do Lemmas 5.1.2, 5.3.3, 5.3.16, 5.3.17 (preprint 5.2, 5.11, 5.23, 5.24) and Lemma 5.26 (preprint), Propositions 5.1.3, 5.3.2, 5.5.3, 5.5.8, 5.5.11, 5.5.15 (preprint 5.3, 5.10, 5.30, 5.35, 5.38, 5.42), Remark 5.3.4 (preprint 5.12),
Corollary 5.2.5 (preprint 5.8) (for each fixed $i$) and Corollary 5.5.17 (preprint 5.44) (with no hypothesis since 2026-11-12, V5.63). Every definition of the chapter is formalized:
Definitions 5.1.1 (preprint 5.1; V5.3), 5.2.1 (preprint 5.4; V5.7), 5.3.1 and 5.5.2 (preprint 5.9 and 5.29; V5.16), 5.3.7 (preprint 5.15; V5.23), 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17; V5.31), 5.3.13 (preprint 5.20; V5.41), 5.5.1 (preprint 5.28; V5.47),
5.5.4 (preprint 5.31; V5.50), 5.5.6 (preprint 5.33; V5.51), 5.5.9 (preprint 5.36; V5.54), 5.5.12 (preprint 5.39; V5.59), 5.5.14 (preprint 5.41; V5.60). Corollary 5.2.5 (preprint 5.8) is verified on the shifted strong
bundle $P^1 : Y^1 \to X^1$, which the text uses without defining it, and by iteration for every fixed $i$, with the

Lemma 5.3.3 (preprint 5.11) need no tameness (V5.10–V5.14, V5.20). Several places of the text needed more than a reading. (a) *Tameness.* The §3.6 implicit function
theorems are proved for sections whose germ data lie in a tame strong bundle chart (Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.4 (preprint 3.50, 3.51); Chapter 3,
Findings 190–199); Theorems 5.3.5, 5.3.10, 5.3.12 (preprint 5.13, 5.18, 5.19) and Theorem 5.25 (preprint) take $f$ with tame germ data, the reading of the tame strong bundle
with which §5.3 opens, and nothing else (Findings 74–78). Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) also assumes $X$ tame, which its proof uses
through Theorems 4.2.11 and 4.3.1 (preprint 4.22 and 4.23) (V5.38). (b) *"Generic" and "dense".* The perturbations are $s_0 + \sum\lambda_it_i$ for
$\lambda$ outside a Lebesgue null set of a small ball (V5.29, V5.38), and density is the bound $\rho(s, s') = \sup_x
N(s(x) - s'(x)) \le \varepsilon$ in the metric space of $\rho$ (V5.21, V5.30, V5.39). (c) *Omitted steps proved.* The spanning sections

$W^{1+m,4}(\Omega)$ on bounded domains other than $(0,1) \subset \mathbb R^1$ (see the list at the end of this section). A fourth addendum (2026-11-02: the shifted strong bundle and Corollary 5.2.5 (preprint 5.8), the metric $\rho$, weak against
pointwise bump functions; Findings, items 140–164) updated V5.13, V5.14, V5.16, V5.21, V5.22 and V5.30 in place. A fifth addendum
