E \times \mathbb R \to F$ is Fredholm with $\ker\tilde L = \ker L \times \mathbb R$ and $\operatorname{coker}\tilde L =
\operatorname{coker} L$, and $h \mapsto \tilde h$, $(a_1 \wedge \dots \wedge a_n) \otimes d^* \mapsto ((a_1, 0) \wedge \dots
\wedge (a_n, 0) \wedge e) \otimes d^*$ with $e = (0, 1)$, is an isomorphism $\det(L) \cong \det(\tilde L)$; in local
determinant charts its coordinate is $(-1)^{\dim F/R(P) + \dim\operatorname{coker}L}$ times a continuous nowhere-zero
function, and $(-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker}L}\,h \mapsto \tilde h$ pulls continuous orientations back along $L \mapsto
\tilde L$. In charts: for an sc-Fredholm $f$, an sc⁺-section $S$ of $\pi^*P \to \mathbb R \times X$, $\hat f = \tilde f + S$
with $\tilde f(t, y) = f(y)$, and the product chart point $(t, z)$, the operator $\hat L(\sigma, v) = Lv$ lies in
$\mathrm{Lin}(\hat f, (t, x))$ for every $L \in \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$, and an orientation $o$ of $\mathrm{DET}(f, x)$ gives
exactly one orientation $\hat o$ of $\mathrm{DET}(\hat f, (t, x))$ with $\hat o(\hat L)$ the image of $o(L)$ for **every**
$L$; $o \mapsto \hat o$ is injective. *Book:* Remark 6.6.19 (preprint 6.42), p. 276 (preprint p. 230). *Hidden hypotheses:* $x$ smooth and $\mathrm{Lin}(f,
x)$ nonempty (implied by bump functions, V6.1); only the orientation of $\mathrm{DET}(f, x)$ at the one point is used.
*Deviation (restated):* at a point, as we read it, the literal $h \mapsto \tilde h$ is not continuous in $L$ where the
parity of $\dim\operatorname{coker}L$ changes, so the orientation of $\mathrm{DET}(\hat f, (t, x))$ it defines could
depend on the choice of $L$; the sign $(-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker}L}$ (the sign of V6.40) is used, which agrees with
the text's map when $L$ is onto. $X \times [0, 1]$ is read as $\mathbb R \times X$ (decision D2), with the parameter first,
so $\tilde L(a, b) = La$ is conjugated by the swap of the factors. That $(t, y) \mapsto e \wedge o_y$ is an orientation of $\hat
f$ in the sense of Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40), built from an orientation of $f$, is proved since 2026-11-12 (gap
G.66 closed): `Polyfold.SectionOrientation.prodFirst` ($X$ tame with bump functions, tame germ data, the hypotheses of
`Polyfold.theorem_6_6_18_oriented`); $(t, x) \mapsto e \wedge o_x$ is carried by every push-forward of $\tilde f$
(`Polyfold.isSectionOrientation_prodFirstFun`), since a push-forward datum of $f$ lifts to one of $\tilde f$ and the lifted
push-forward maps $e \wedge o$ to $e \wedge$ (push-forward of $o$) with no sign (`Polyfold.IsPush.prodLift`), and the chart
of $X$ plays no role (`Polyfold.prodOrOf_orTransfer`) (Findings, items 95–97). On a product end the induced orientation
of the solution set is the product orientation, the time vector first (`Polyfold.isEndProductOrientation_cobOr`).

**V6.63 (Appendix 6.8.1 (preprint 6.7.1), the proof of Lemma 6.3.3 (preprint 6.5); `Polyfold.FourTermExact.Choice.exists_smul_source_value`,
`Polyfold.FourTermExact.Choice.wedgeC`).** For two choices of (91) the right-hand sides are related as the sources are: a
change of the basis of $Z$ multiplies both wedges by its determinant, a change of the bases of $A$ and $D$ multiplies both
sides by the same factor, and a change of complements adds to the basis of $Z$ vectors of $\alpha(A)$ and to the
$\gamma$-preimages vectors of $\beta(B)$, which leaves the wedges unchanged. *Book:* §6.8.1 (preprint §6.7.1), preprint pp. 234–235. *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the step "independent of the choices of the basis if and only if $\det(\tau)
= \det(\varepsilon)$" is read as the homogeneity of (91) in the bases of $A$ and $D$, $\tau$ being the $\sigma$ just
introduced; the corrections $p_i$ lie in $\beta(B)$ (written $\beta(C)$) and are combinations of the $\beta$-images,
whose names are exchanged with those of the $\gamma$-preimages in the last step (possible misprints) (Findings, item 1).

**V6.64 (Appendix 6.8.2 (preprint 6.7.2), the proof of Proposition 6.4.11 (preprint 6.12); `Polyfold.mem_span_append_of_ker`,
`Polyfold.gammaProj_wedge_tmul`, `Polyfold.comp_comp_eq_of_projLE`).** For $P \le Q$ in $\Pi_T$: if $Qg = 0$, then $g$ is a
combination of the vectors $d_i$ plus $Tx$ with $x \in \ker(QT)$, so the classes of $d_i$ and $Tb_j$ span what the text
calls $\ker\tilde Q$; the classes $[T\tilde b]$ and $[QT\tilde b]$ in $F/R(P)$ differ by elements of that span, which does
not change the wedge. *Book:* §6.8.2 (preprint §6.7.2), pp. 280–286 (preprint pp. 235–237). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the spanning is
proved directly in $F$; the name $\alpha_q$ in the last part is read as $\alpha^P$ (possible misprint) (Findings, items 6,
7).

**V6.65 (Lemma 6.4.4 (2017: 6.3); `Polyfold.projIntertwiner`, `Polyfold.projIntertwiner_self`, `Polyfold.projIntertwiner_mul`,
`Polyfold.continuous_projIntertwiner`, `Polyfold.lemma_6_4_4`).** Let $E$, $F$ be Banach spaces, $T_0 : E \to F$ Fredholm and
$P_0 \in \Pi_{T_0}$. There is $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every $T$ and every projection $P$ of $F$ with $\|T - T_0\| < \varepsilon$ and
$\|P - P_0\| < \varepsilon$: $T$ is Fredholm, $P \in \Pi_T$, and $\mathrm{ind}(P \circ T) = \mathrm{ind}(T) = \mathrm{ind}(T_0) = \mathrm{ind}(P_0 \circ T_0)$.
For projections $P_0$, $P$ the intertwiner $J(P) = PP_0 + (1 - P)(1 - P_0)$ has $J(P_0) = 1$ and $J(P)P_0 = PJ(P)$, and depends
continuously on $P$. *Book:* Lemma 6.4.4 (2017: 6.3), p. 247 (2017 p. 189); no preprint counterpart; the index equalities are new in
the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (explicit):* $\mathrm{ind}(P \circ T)$ is the index of $P \circ T$ as a map $E \to
F$ (as a map onto $R(P)$ its index would be $\dim\ker(PT)$); $E$ and $F$ are taken in the universe `Type`. The proof is not the
text's: $J(P)$ is invertible near $P_0$ and $P = JP_0J^{-1}$, so $R(P) = JR(P_0)$ has finite codimension, and Lemma 6.5.1 (preprint
6.17) for $J^{-1}T$ near $T_0$ gives $R(PT) = JR(P_0J^{-1}T) = JR(P_0) = R(P)$ (Findings, items 110, 111).

**V6.66 (a common complement; `Polyfold.finrank_sup_span_singleton_of_notMem`, `Polyfold.isCompl_sup_span_singleton`,
`Polyfold.exists_isCompl_isCompl_of_finrank_eq_aux`, `Polyfold.exists_isCompl_isCompl_of_finrank_eq`).** Two finite-dimensional
subspaces $K_1$, $K_2$ of the same dimension of a real vector space have a common algebraic complement $X$. *Book:* the proof of
Proposition 6.4.13 (2017: 6.6), p. 253 (2017 p. 195), takes a closed subspace $X$ complementing both kernels. *Hidden hypotheses:*
none. *Deviation (not in the book):* by induction on $\dim(K_1 + K_2) - \dim K_1$: for $a \in K_2 \setminus K_1$ and $b \in K_1 \setminus K_2$,
$a + b$ lies in neither, and a common complement of $K_1 + \mathbb R(a + b)$ and $K_2 + \mathbb R(a + b)$ plus $\mathbb R(a + b)$ is one of $K_1$ and $K_2$. That
$X$ can be taken closed is V6.69 (Findings, items 112, 116).

**V6.67 (Proposition 6.4.13 (2017: 6.6), the algebraic part; `Polyfold.proposition_6_4_13`).** Let $T : E \to F$ be Fredholm and
$P, Q \in \Pi_T$ with $R(P) = R(Q) = H$. There are linear isomorphisms $A_T : \ker(PT) \to \ker(QT)$ and $B_T : F/R(P) \to F/R(Q)$
with $A_T \circ j_P = j_Q$, $\Phi_Q \circ A_T = B_T \circ \Phi_P$ and $\pi_Q \circ B_T = \pi_P$, for the maps of the exact sequences $E(T, P)$
and $E(T, Q)$ of V6.12. They are the text's: $A_T(e) = e - x(e)$, $x(e) \in X$ with $QTx(e) = QTe$, and $B_T(f + H) = \tilde f + H$ with $Tx +
\tilde f = (1 - P)f$, $x \in X$, $\tilde f \in (1 - Q)F$, for a common complement $X$ of the kernels (V6.66), which exists because
$\dim\ker(PT) = \dim\ker(QT)$ by the indices. *Book:* Proposition 6.4.13 (2017: 6.6), p. 253 (2017 p. 195), proof pp. 253–255; no
preprint counterpart; the 2021 edition makes $\Pi_T \cap \mathcal P_H \ne \emptyset$ a hypothesis. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(narrower):* the last sentence, that $A_T$ and $B_T$ depend continuously on $T$, is not part of this item: it is V6.70, with a
closed $X$ (V6.69) (gap G.81, closed); here $X$ is algebraic, and $F/H$ appears as $F/R(P)$ and $F/R(Q)$ (Findings, items 112, 113,
117).

**V6.68 (Lemmas 6.6.8 and 6.6.9; `Polyfold.lemma_6_6_8`, `Polyfold.lemma_6_6_9`).** For stabilized kernels of the data
$(f, s_1, \dots, s_k)$ along a family, and of the same data with $d$ sections appended, the push-forwards of orientations
between two smooth points agree, both when the appended sections are zero (Lemma 6.6.8: the new parameters $\mu$ enter as dummy
variables) and when they are arbitrary sections $\bar s_1, \dots, \bar s_d$ (Lemma 6.6.9). *Book:* Lemma 6.6.8 (preprint 6.33), p. 267
(preprint p. 224), and Lemma 6.6.9, p. 269, new in the 2021 edition as a separate lemma: the 2021 text splits preprint Lemma 6.33
(2017: 6.15), whose statement is that of Lemma 6.6.9 and whose proof begins with the step of Lemma 6.6.8. *Hidden hypotheses:*
the stabilized kernels of the appended data are given (`IsStabKernels`), as in V6.45. *Deviation (restated):* both are V6.45
(`Polyfold.IsStabKernels.push_append`), Lemma 6.6.8 for $\bar s_j = 0$; the homotopy of the text's proof is not needed (Findings,
item 114).

**V6.69 (a common closed complement; `Polyfold.isCompl_sup_inf_of_isCompl`,
`Polyfold.exists_isClosed_isTopCompl_isTopCompl_of_finrank_eq`).** Two finite-dimensional subspaces $K_1$, $K_2$ of the same
dimension of a real normed space $E$ have a common closed complement $X$, and $E = K_1 \oplus X = K_2 \oplus X$ topologically
(with continuous projections). *Book:* the proof of Proposition 6.4.13 (2017: 6.6), p. 253 (2017 p. 195), takes a closed
subspace $X$ that is a topological complement of both kernels, without argument. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in
the book):* the argument. $X = Z + (X_0 \cap (K_1 + K_2))$, where $X_0$ is the algebraic common complement of V6.66 and $Z$ a
closed complement of the finite-dimensional $K_1 + K_2$; it complements $K_1$ and $K_2$ (if $X_0 \oplus K' = E$, $K' \subseteq K$ and
$K \oplus Z = E$, then $(Z + X_0 \cap K) \oplus K' = E$), it is closed as the sum of a closed and a finite-dimensional subspace, and a
closed complement of a finite-dimensional subspace is a topological one (Findings, items 112, 116).

**V6.70 (Proposition 6.4.13 (2017: 6.6), the last sentence; `Polyfold.projCod`, `Polyfold.solveOp`, `Polyfold.kerTransition`,
`Polyfold.cokerTransition`, `Polyfold.solveOp_mem`, `Polyfold.kerTransition_apply`, `Polyfold.cokerTransition_apply`,
`Polyfold.apply_solveOp_of_projRestrict_eq`, `Polyfold.disjoint_ker_comp_of_projRestrict_eq`,
`Polyfold.isTopCompl_ker_comp_of_projRestrict_eq`, `Polyfold.diagram_of_solveOp`, `Polyfold.continuousAt_solveOp`,
`Polyfold.proposition_6_4_13_continuity`, `Polyfold.proposition_6_4_13_continuity_hyps`).** Let $E$, $F$ be Banach
spaces, $T : E \to F$ Fredholm and $P, Q \in \Pi_T$ with $R(P) = R(Q) = H$. For $S : E \to F$ and a subspace $X$ write $\xi_S = (QS|_X)^{-1}
\circ Q : F \to X$ (the solution $x \in X$ of $QSx = Qg$), $A_S(e) = e - \xi_S(Se)$ on $E$ and $B_S(f) = (1 - P)f - S\xi_S((1 - P)f)$ on $F$.
There are a closed subspace $X \subseteq E$ and $\varepsilon > 0$ such that (a) $S \mapsto A_S$ and $S \mapsto B_S$ are continuous on
$\|S - T\| < \varepsilon$ in the operator norm, and $(S, e) \mapsto A_Se$, $(S, f) \mapsto B_Sf$ are jointly continuous there; (b) for every
such $S$: $P, Q \in \Pi_S$; $E = \ker(PS) \oplus X = \ker(QS) \oplus X$ topologically; $e - A_Se \in X$ and $QSA_Se = 0$ ((6.15), (6.16));
$QB_Sf = 0$ and $Sx + B_Sf = (1 - P)f$ for some $x \in X$ ((6.18), (6.19)); $A_S$ restricts to a linear isomorphism $\ker(PS) \to
\ker(QS)$ and $B_S$ induces a linear isomorphism $F/R(P) \to F/R(Q)$, with $A \circ j_P = j_Q$, $\Phi_Q \circ A = B \circ \Phi_P$ and $\pi_Q \circ
B = \pi_P$ for the exact sequences $E(S, P)$, $E(S, Q)$ (V6.12). The hypotheses are satisfiable ($T = 1$ on $\mathbb R$, $P = Q$). *Book:*
Proposition 6.4.13 (2017: 6.6), p. 253 (2017 p. 195), last sentence: for $T'$ near $T$ with $P, Q \in \Pi_{T'}$ the constructions of
$A_{T'}$ and $B_{T'}$ depend continuously on $T'$; argument pp. 253, 255 (with $X$ fixed, the equation (6.15) for $T'$ has a unique solution
depending continuously on $T'$); no preprint counterpart. *Hidden hypotheses:* none; $P, Q \in \Pi_S$ for $S$ near $T$ follows from
Lemma 6.5.1 (preprint 6.17) (V6.20) and is part of the conclusion. *Deviation (explicit):* "depend continuously" is read as the
continuity of $A_S$ extended to $E$ and of $B_S$ lifted to $F$, which determine the maps $\ker(PS) \to \ker(QS)$ and $F/H \to F/H$
between the varying kernels; the joint continuity says that $(S, e) \mapsto (S, A_Se)$ is continuous on the kernel bundle
$\bigcup_S \{S\} \times \ker(PS)$ of Remark 6.4.5 (V6.21) with its subspace topology. *Proof:* the text's. $X$ is V6.69 for the
kernels of $PT$ and $QT$, of equal dimension by the indices; by Lemma 6.5.1 (preprint 6.17) for $(T, P, X)$ and $(T, Q, X)$, $PS|_X$
and $QS|_X$ are isomorphisms onto $R(P)$, $R(Q)$ near $T$, and inversion is continuous at isomorphisms, so $S \mapsto \xi_S$ is
continuous; the diagram is the construction of the algebraic part (V6.67) for the solution operator $\xi_S$ (Findings, items 113,
117).

**V6.71 (the orientation space and the properties of Theorem 6.6.17; `Polyfold.OrSpace`, `Polyfold.orProj`, `Polyfold.segPath`,
`Polyfold.isScSmoothMap_segPath`, `Polyfold.OrPullback`, `Polyfold.IsContSectionOver`, `Polyfold.IsPropagationContinuous`,
`Polyfold.HasTwoContSections`, `Polyfold.IsOrientationTopology`).** For an sc-Fredholm section $f$ of a strong bundle $P : Y \to X$,
$O_f$ is the set of pairs $(x, o)$ with $x \in X_\infty$ and $o \in \mathrm{Or}^f_x$, an orientation of $\mathrm{DET}(f, x)$ read in the
chosen chart (V6.55), and $\pi_f(x, o) = x$; $X_\infty$ carries the metrizable topology of Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) (V2.17). For
an sc-smooth path $\varphi$ (an sc-smooth map $\mathbb R \to X$), $\varphi^*O_f$ is the subspace $\{(t, p) : \varphi(t) = \pi_f(p)\}$ of
$[0, 1] \times O_f$, and the segment $s \mapsto \varphi(a + s(b - a))$ from $\varphi(a)$ to $\varphi(b)$ is sc-smooth. For a topology on
$O_f$: a continuous section over $U \cap X_\infty$ is a continuous $\sigma : U_\infty \to O_f$ with $\pi_f \circ \sigma = \mathrm{id}$, $U_\infty$
with the topology of $X_\infty$; property (2) asks that every $x \in X_\infty$ have an open $U \ni x$ in $X$ with exactly two continuous
sections over $U \cap X_\infty$; property (3) asks that for every sc-smooth path $\varphi$, every continuous section $\alpha(t) = (t, (\varphi(t),
o_t))$ of $\varphi^*O_f$ and every $t_0 \in [0, 1]$, for all $t$ near $t_0$ an open $U$ with the local propagation property in some chart
contains the segment of $\varphi$ from $t_0$ to $t$, and the push-forward along it in $U$ maps $o_{t_0}$ to $o_t$; an orientation topology is
a Hausdorff topology with (1) $\pi_f$ a local homeomorphism, (2) and (3). *Book:* pp. 274–275, before Theorem 6.6.17, and the three
properties of Theorem 6.6.17, p. 275, new in the 2021 edition (the set $O_f$ appears without a topology in the preprint after
Definition 6.27, p. 219, and in the 2017 text after Definition 6.9, p. 205). *Hidden hypotheses:* the topology of $X_\infty$ ("the
natural metrizable topology"). *Deviation (explicit):* "$o_t$ is the local propagation of $o_{t_0}$" is read as the push-forward
`orPush` (V6.57) along the segment of $\varphi$ in a set with the local propagation property, which does not depend on that set
(`Polyfold.orPush_compat`); paths are the sc-smooth maps $\mathbb R \to X$ of decision D2, restricted to $[0, 1]$ (Findings, item 118).

**V6.72 (sc-smooth paths in $X_\infty$; `Polyfold.rnChart_toBase`, `Polyfold.continuousOn_levelLift_comp`,
`Polyfold.continuous_smoothMk_comp`, `Polyfold.chartSegPath`, `Polyfold.isScSmoothMap_chartSegPath`,
`Polyfold.eventually_exists_scPath_smoothLevel`, `Polyfold.exists_nhds_scPath_of_isOpen`).** An sc-smooth map $\Gamma : \mathbb R^n
\to X$ takes values in $X_\infty$ and is continuous into $X_\infty$, its level-$m$ coordinates in every chart being continuous. For every
neighbourhood $N$ of a smooth point $x$ in $X_\infty$, every $y \in X_\infty$ close enough to $x$ in $X_\infty$ is joined to $x$ by an
sc-smooth path all of whose points lie in $N$: in a chart, $s \mapsto r(u_0 + \kappa(s)(u_1 - u_0))$ with $\kappa$ the smooth transition
function. For an open $W \ni x$ in $X$ there is an open $V$, $x \in V \subseteq W$, whose smooth points are pairwise joined by sc-smooth
paths in $W$. *Book:* not stated; needed for the uniqueness in Theorem 6.6.17, p. 275, whose proof the text leaves to the reader.
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):* tools; the second statement makes small neighbourhoods in $X_\infty$
reachable by paths that stay in them, which is how property (3) controls the topology (Findings, item 119).

**V6.73 (the topology of $O_f$, property (1) and Hausdorffness; `Polyfold.IsContOrOn`, `Polyfold.orSec`, `Polyfold.orBasic`,
`Polyfold.orTopology`, `Polyfold.IsContOrOn.eventually_iff`, `Polyfold.isOpen_orBasic`, `Polyfold.continuousOn_orSec`,
`Polyfold.continuous_orProj`, `Polyfold.eq_orSec_of_mem_orBasic`, `Polyfold.orSec_mem_orBasic`, `Polyfold.exists_isContOrOn`,
`Polyfold.orChartHomeo`, `Polyfold.isLocalHomeomorph_orProj`, `Polyfold.t2Space_orTopology`).** Let $L$ be local transport data
for the sets $\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ (good open sets covering $X_\infty$ with push-forwards, V6.56). A continuous orientation over an open $U$ is a
family $y \mapsto o_y$ carried along by the transport of $L$ along every sc-smooth path in $U$. The topology $\mathcal T_L$ on $O_f$: $W$ is
open iff $\{y \in U_\infty : (y, o_y) \in W\}$ is open in $X_\infty$ for every continuous orientation $o$ over an open $U$. For every $L$: two
continuous orientations agree near a smooth point iff they agree at it; the sets $\{(y, o_y) : y \in U_\infty\}$ are open, $y \mapsto (y,
o_y)$ is continuous on $U_\infty$ and $\pi_f$ is continuous; every point of $O_f$ lies on a continuous orientation over an open set
inside a good set of $L$; $\pi_f$ restricted to $\{(y, o_y) : y \in U_\infty\}$ is a homeomorphism onto $U_\infty$, so (1) $\pi_f$ is a local
homeomorphism; and $\mathcal T_L$ is Hausdorff. *Book:* Theorem 6.6.17, p. 275, new in the 2021 edition: "a uniquely defined
Hausdorff topology" with (1); the text leaves the proof to the reader, in view of Proposition 6.6.3 and Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint
6.28, 6.35). *Hidden hypotheses:* none (every $L$). *Deviation (not in the book):* the construction of the topology. Points over
different smooth points are separated through $\pi_f$ ($X_\infty$ is metrizable); the two points over one $y$ lie on two continuous
orientations that differ at $y$, hence near $y$ (Findings, item 118).

**V6.74 (property (2) under connected smooth neighbourhoods; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasConnectedSmoothNbhds`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasConnectedSmoothNbhds_of_subsingleton`, `Polyfold.rnPolyfold_hasConnectedSmoothNbhds`,
`Polyfold.eq_orSec_or_eq_orSec`, `Polyfold.hasTwoContSections_orTopology`).** $X$ has connected smooth neighbourhoods if every
smooth point $x$ has, inside every open $W \ni x$, an open $U \ni x$ of $X$ with $U \cap X_\infty$ preconnected in $X_\infty$; $\mathbb R^n$ and
every M-polyfold on a subsingleton have them. If every $\mathrm{Or}^f_y$ has exactly two elements and $X$ has connected smooth
neighbourhoods, then for every $L$ the topology $\mathcal T_L$ has property (2): for such a $U$ inside the domain of a continuous
orientation $o$, the continuous sections over $U \cap X_\infty$ are exactly $y \mapsto (y, o_y)$ and $y \mapsto (y, -o_y)$. *Book:* Theorem
6.6.17 (2), p. 275. *Hidden hypotheses:* connected smooth neighbourhoods (`HasConnectedSmoothNbhds`). *Deviation (narrower):* (2) is
proved under this hypothesis only; Part I does not state it, it holds for $\mathbb R^n$ and is open in general (gap G.90). The proofs of §7.4 use that $U \cap X_\infty$ is connected for connected open $U$ (`MPolyfold.SmoothConnected`, gap G.85); as we read it, that fact gives the hypothesis, M-polyfolds being locally path connected (Proposition 2.3.7).
*Proof:* the set where a continuous section equals $(y, o_y)$ is open, and so is the set where it equals $(y, -o_y)$, its complement;
$U_\infty$ is preconnected (Findings, item 120).

**V6.75 (Theorem 6.6.17; `Polyfold.isPropagationContinuous_orTopology`, `Polyfold.eventually_eq_orSec_of_continuousOn`,
`Polyfold.eq_orTopology_of`, `Polyfold.existsUnique_orientationTopology`, `Polyfold.theorem_6_6_17_hyp`).** Let $X$ be a tame
M-polyfold with sc-smooth bump functions, $P : Y \to X$ a strong bundle with sc⁺-sections through every smooth fibre point, $f$
an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (the hypotheses of Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37), V6.57, with its paracompactness
instances for $\mathbb R^n \times X$, $\mathbb R^k \times \mathbb R^n \times X$ and their pull-back bundles), and $\mathcal T$ the topology of V6.73
for the local transport data of $\Gamma_f$. Then $\mathcal T$ has property (3); every topology on $O_f$ with (1) and (3) is $\mathcal T$;
there is exactly one Hausdorff topology on $O_f$ with (1) and (3); and if $X$ has connected smooth neighbourhoods (V6.74), exactly
one Hausdorff topology with (1), (2) and (3). *Book:* Theorem 6.6.17, p. 275, new in the 2021 edition (the preprint and the 2017
text define the set $O_f$, V6.71, but no topology on it): for a strong bundle over a tame $X$ and an sc-Fredholm $f$ there is a uniquely defined Hausdorff
topology on $O_f$ characterized by (1)–(3); "the easy proof is left to the reader". *Hidden hypotheses:* bump functions, tame germ
data and sc⁺-sections through the smooth fibre points (those of V6.57); connected smooth neighbourhoods for (2). *Deviation
(narrower):* existence with (2) needs `HasConnectedSmoothNbhds` (gap G.90); the uniqueness is stronger than stated, from (1) and (3)
alone, without Hausdorffness or (2). The remarks after the theorem (the orientation bundle, orientability iff a global continuous
section, the continuous $\mathbb Z_2$-action, $\det_f = \mathbb R \otimes_{\mathbb Z_2} O_f$) are not formalized (gap G.91). *Proof:* (3): near
$t_0$ a continuous section of $\varphi^*O_f$ stays in one open set $\{(y, o_y)\}$, and $o$ is carried along the segments of $\varphi$ by the
transport, which on a good set is the push-forward. Uniqueness: for a topology with (3), a continuous local section through
$(y_0, o_{y_0})$ equals $y \mapsto (y, o_y)$ near $y_0$, since $y$ is joined to $y_0$ by a small sc-smooth path (V6.72), along which (3) and
the connectedness of $[0, 1]$ carry the equality; the local homeomorphisms of (1) then match the open sets of both topologies
(Findings, items 119, 121).

**V6.76 (Theorem 6.7.1 (preprint 6.43): the invariant $\Psi_{(f,o)}$; `Polyfold.theorem_6_7_1`,

`theorem_6_7_1` (`Chapter6/Theorem671Final2021.lean`): for $X$ tame with sc-smooth bump functions there is $\Psi$ assigning to a
proper tame sc-Fredholm section $f$ with an orientation $o$ a linear map $\Psi_{(f,o)} : H^k_{dR}(X, \partial X) \to \mathbb R$
(`relDeRham`, V4.91) in every degree $k$ with (1): for every auxiliary norm $N$ there are open $U \supseteq S_f$ with
$\mathrm{cl}\{x \in U \mid N(f(x)) \le C\}$ compact for $C > 0$; for each such $U$, $S_{f+s}$ is compact for every allowable
$s$, admissible sections exist (`StrongBundle.IsAdmissible`), and for each admissible $s$, $S_{f+s}$ is the union of its index
parts $S_k$, each a compact oriented Mathlib manifold of dimension $k$ (`SolPartIsOrientedManifold`), with $\Psi([\omega, \tau])
= \int_{S_k}\omega|_S - \int_{\partial S_k}\tau|_{\partial S}$ (`solIntegral`, `solBoundaryIntegral`); and (2):
$\Psi_{(f_0,o_0)} = \Psi_{(f_1,o_1)}$ for a proper oriented homotopy (`IsProperOrientedHomotopyBetween`). $\Psi$ is `psiAt` for
one chosen admissible section; `psiAt` is well defined on classes by Stokes on $S_k$ and on its faces (`psiForms_relD`).
`theorem_6_7_1_of_indep` proves the theorem from (A) `PsiIndepAdmissible` and (B) `PsiIndepHomotopy` with no other hypothesis;
`psiAt_eq_of_admissible_of_orientation` and `psiAt_eq_of_homotopy_of_orientation` prove (A) and (B) from the cobordism identity
`psiAt_eq_of_cobordism_of_orientation` (Stokes on the index-$(k+1)$ part of $S_F$ with a cut-off in time,
`integral_eq_of_cutCobordism`, for the relative form `cobordismRelativeFormsInner`) and the cobordism data
`exists_isCobordismData`, `exists_homotopy_cobordism_data`. On the point $\mathbb R^0$ with $f = 0$, $\Psi([1]) = \pm1$
(`theorem_6_7_1_witness`). In `theorem_6_7_1` these two are applied to `cobordismOrientationHyp`: the cobordism $S_F$ carries
the orientation $e \wedge o_0$ of $F$ (`cobOr`, `SectionOrientation.prodFirst`), which is $e \wedge o_{S_i}$ on its two ends
(`isEndProductOrientation_cobOr`), and the relative form `cobordismRelativeFormsInner`. The earlier form
`theorem_6_7_1_of_orientation` (`Chapter6/CobordismRelativeForms2021b.lean`) took the orientation of $S_F$ as a hypothesis.
*Book:* §6.7 (preprint §6.6), Theorem 6.7.1 (preprint 6.43), p. 277 (preprint p. 231) (proof pp. 277–279 (preprint pp.
231–233)), Over a tame $X$ with sc-smooth bump functions there is a well-defined map associating with a proper oriented
sc-Fredholm section $(f, o)$ a linear map $\Psi_{(f,o)} : H^*_{dR}(X, \partial X) \to \mathbb R$ with (1) for an auxiliary norm
$N$ and $s$ admissible for $(N, U)$, $S_{f+s}$ is an oriented compact manifold with boundary with corners and
$\Psi_{(f,o)}([\omega, \tau]) = \int_{S_{f+s}}\omega - \int_{\partial S_{f+s}}\tau$, the integrals being zero if the dimensions
do not agree; and (2) $\Psi_{(f_0,o_0)} = \Psi_{(f_1,o_1)}$ for a proper oriented homotopy. The proof compares two admissible
sections through the cobordism $S_F$ of Remark 5.3.8, oriented from $o$ and the standard orientation of $[0, 1]$, and gets (2)
by "the same homotopy argument". *Deviation (restated):* (2026-11-12) No hypothesis beyond the text's: the orientation of the
cobordism $S_F$, of product form $e \wedge o_{S_i}$ on its two ends, is proved (`cobordismOrientationHyp`), and the relative
form $p_1^*\omega - d\beta$ on $S_F$ is built on the inner ends $(0, 1/16) \times S_0$ and $(15/16, 1) \times S_1$
(`cobordismRelativeFormsInner`), since the cobordism data give the product structure only for $t \le 1/8$ and $t \ge 7/8$.
Before 2026-11-12 the orientation was a hypothesis (`theorem_6_7_1_of_orientation`; Findings, Chapter 6, items 134, 136). The
proper oriented homotopy of (2), which the text does not define, is read as in R-d: $f_1 = f_0 + S(1, \cdot)$ for an sc⁺-section
$S$ over $\mathbb R^1 \times X$ with $S(0, \cdot) = 0$, compact zeros over $t \in [0, 1]$ and the properness clause on that
slab, and $o_1 = o_0$ transported (`IsProperOrientedHomotopyBetween`; Findings, Chapter 6, item 130). The neighbourhood $U$ of
(1) carries the margin of reading R-b, and (1) holds for every auxiliary norm and every such $U$; the text defines $\Psi$ from
one $N$ (item 128). "Zero if the dimensions do not agree" pairs degree $k$ with the index-$k$ part $S_k$ (R-c, item 129). The
text's $[0, 1] \times X$ is read as $\mathbb R^1 \times X$ (decision D2), and the decomposition $\partial S_F = S_0 \cup S_1
\cup \tilde S$ is replaced by a cut-off in time on the product ends (items 131–133). *Proof:* `psiAt`, for one admissible
section, is well defined on classes by Stokes on $S_k$ and on its faces; two admissible sections, or the two ends of a proper
oriented homotopy, are compared through the cobordism $S_F$ with a cut-off in time: $\int_{S_F} d(gA) = 0$, and on the product
ends $\int_{S_F} d(g_iA) = \int_{S_i} a_i$, for the relative form $A$ built on the inner ends; the orientation $e \wedge o_0$ of
$S_F$ is $e \wedge o_{S_i}$ on the ends, the time vector first and with no sign (Findings, Chapter 6, items 128–134, 136).

**V6.80 (The remark that $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ is not orientable (end of §6.5, p. 262);
`Polyfold.isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_hilbert`, `Polyfold.isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_equiv_hilbert`,
`Polyfold.isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_equiv_prod`, `Polyfold.isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_equiv_ellTwo`,
`Polyfold.isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_ltwo`, `Polyfold.nonempty_lineOrientation_det_iff_of_equiv`,
`Polyfold.isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_equiv`, `Polyfold.isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_ellTwo`,
`Polyfold.isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_complexStructure`, `Polyfold.isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_kernel_loop`,
`Polyfold.isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_prod`, `Polyfold.isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_prod_of_equiv`,
`Polyfold.continuous_kerDetMk`, `Polyfold.isEmpty_lineOrientation_of_loop`,
`Polyfold.exists_two_lineOrientation_det_of_finiteDimensional`, `Polyfold.nonempty_lineOrientation_det_of_finiteDimensional`).**
Non-orientable is `IsEmpty (LineOrientation (DetFiber (E := E) (F := F)))`: $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ over all Fredholm operators has
no orientation in the sense of Proposition 6.6.1 (preprint 6.26). `isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_hilbert`: none for $E = F = H$,
every infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space $H$ (separable or not); `isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_equiv_hilbert`: none when
$E$ and $F$ are isomorphic to such an $H$; `isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_equiv_prod`: none when $E$, $F$ are isomorphic to $H
\times H$ for a Banach space $H$ with a surjective $S : H \to H$ with odd-dimensional kernel, e.g. $H \cong \mathbb R \times H$;
`isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_ellTwo`: $\ell^2 \times \ell^2$. In general, `isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_complexStructure`:
none whenever $E$ and $F$ carry bounded $J$ with $J^2 = -1$ and there is a surjective $T : E \to F$ with kernel of odd finite
dimension; the loop $A_\theta = R'_\theta T R_{-\theta}$, $\theta \in [0, \pi]$, $R_\theta = \cos\theta + \sin\theta J$,
consists of surjective operators, a basis of the kernels $R_\theta(\ker T)$ is a continuous section of $\mathrm{DET}$ in the
chart with $P = 1$ (`continuous_kerDetMk`), and it returns to its negative (`isEmpty_lineOrientation_det_of_kernel_loop`,
`isEmpty_lineOrientation_of_loop`). Orientability depends only on the isomorphism classes of $E$ and $F$
(`nonempty_lineOrientation_det_iff_of_equiv`, through `LineOrientation.conj`). For finite-dimensional $E$, $F$:
`exists_two_lineOrientation_det_of_finiteDimensional`, $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ has exactly two orientations. *Book:* §6.5 (preprint
§6.4), after Lemma 6.5.9 (preprint 6.25), p. 262 (preprint p. 218), The text remarks, with no hypothesis on $E$, $F$ and no
proof or reference, that the line bundle $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ over the Fredholm operators $\mathcal F(E, F)$ (with the topology
of Proposition 6.5.8 (preprint 6.24)) is known to be non-orientable, though orientable over certain subsets. *Deviation
(narrower):* The text gives no hypothesis on $E$, $F$. For finite-dimensional $E$, $F$ the remark does not hold as we read it:
every operator is Fredholm, the base $L(E, F)$ is convex, and $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ has exactly two orientations
(`exists_two_lineOrientation_det_of_finiteDimensional`, on $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ itself) (Findings, Chapter 6, items 26, 135).
Proved under hypotheses: $E$, $F$ isomorphic to one infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, or to $H \times H$ with $H \cong \mathbb
R \times H$, or, in general, complex structures on $E$ and $F$ and a surjective operator with kernel of odd finite dimension.
Non-orientability for infinite-dimensional Banach spaces without such structures is not formalized and not claimed. The remark
presumably intends infinite-dimensional spaces of the kind in the applications. The orientability "over certain subsets" is
Proposition 6.6.1 (preprint 6.26) (V6.30).

**V6.81 (The classical determinant line bundle at the opening of §6.6 (p. 262); `Polyfold.derivFredholm`,

every orientation of one line $\det(Df(x_0))$ extends to exactly one orientation of the bundle. *Book:* §6.6 (preprint §6.5),
the opening paragraph, p. 262 (preprint p. 219), For a classical Fredholm map $f : U \to F$ on an open $U \subseteq E$, the
determinant line bundle of the $Df(x)$ is a smooth line bundle over $U$, with precisely two orientations if $U$ is contractible.
*Deviation (narrower):* $f$ is of class $C^1$, which is weaker than the text's "smooth". The bundle is a topological line
bundle, the pull-back of $\mathrm{DET}(E, F)$ (V6.28); its smoothness, for which smooth frames of Fredholm charts would be
needed, is not formalized (Findings, Chapter 6, item 26).

### What is not verified in this chapter

- preprint p. 201, the facts recalled before Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2): an M-polyfold is locally path connected, and two smooth points in
  one path component are joined by an sc⁺-smooth path. Only the local form inside a chart is formalized (V6.49), and
  "in the same path component" (Definitions 6.6.2, 6.6.14 (preprint 6.27, 6.38)) is read as "joined by an sc-smooth path" (V6.58) (gap G.56;
  Findings, item 42).
- preprint p. 201, the members of $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ as sc-Fredholm operators on every level: they are shown Fredholm on level
  $0$, with the index $\mathrm{ind}(f, x)$, which is what the determinant lines use (V6.1) (gap G.64).
- preprint p. 208, the alternative definition $\det(T) = \lambda(\ker T) \otimes \lambda(\operatorname{coker}(T)^*)$ and its
  identification with Definition 6.4.1 (preprint 6.7). Listed here before 2026-11-12; verified since (V6.78; gap G.57, closed).
- preprint p. 213, the identification (95) and the maps $V \otimes \lambda(\mathbb R^n) \to V$, $V \otimes \lambda^*(\mathbb R^n) \to V$ after

  chapter's statements use only (94) (V6.17, V6.18).

  has no orientation for $E$, $F$ isomorphic to one infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, and under complex structures with a

## 8. Chapter 7 (HWZ, Part II, §§7.1–7.6 (2017 §§7.1–7.5)): verified except the tangent $T\varphi$ of Definition 7.1.4 (2017 Definition 7.4), the remark after Definition 7.1.7 (2017 Definition 7.7) in its 2017 form, and the Hausdorff property of $\mathbf X^R$ in the 2017 Proposition 7.9 and Proposition 7.10 (rewritten in 2021 as Proposition 7.2.10 and Theorem 7.2.14, which assume it)

Chapter 7 (pp. 287–356 (2017 pp. 225–256); Part II has no 2014 preprint, so numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021), with the 2017 text's in parentheses) introduces
ep-groupoids, the sc-smooth version of étale proper Lie groupoids. §7.1 defines groupoids, isotropy groups and
ep-groupoids (Definitions 7.1.1–7.1.3 (2017: 7.1–7.3)), the local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$ and the tangent $T\varphi$ of a morphism
(Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4)), the levels and the degeneracy index of the orbit space (Definition 7.1.5 (2017: 7.5)), tame ep-groupoids (Definition
7.1.6 (2017: 7.6)) and the category $\mathcal{EP}$ (Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7)); it proves the openness of $\pi$, the countable neighbourhood bases
of $|X|$, the local closure relation and the finiteness of the isotropy groups (Propositions 7.1.8–7.1.12 (2017: 7.1–7.4), Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1)), states
the natural representation of $G_x$ (Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1)), discusses the translation groupoid $G_x \ltimes U(x)$ and the map
$\hat\Phi$ (pp. 293–297 (2017 pp. 231–233)), extends the natural representation to finite sets of isomorphic objects (Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5),
Definition 7.1.18 (2017: 7.8)), identifies $|U(x)|$ with $G_x\backslash U(x)$ (Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6)), and defines local uniformizers and
ep-subgroupoids (Definitions 7.1.20, 7.1.21 (2017: 7.9, 7.10), Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7)). §7.2 treats effective ep-groupoids (Definition 7.2.1 (2017: 7.11), Lemmas
7.2.2, 7.2.3 (2017: 7.2, 7.3), Proposition 7.2.4 (2017: 7.8)), the subgroups $T_x$, the reduced morphism space $\mathbf X^R$ and the reduced ep-groupoid
$X_R$ (Definitions 7.2.7, 7.2.15 (2017: 7.12, 7.13), Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017)). §7.3 proves that $|X|$ is locally metrizable, regular and
Hausdorff (Theorem 7.3.1 (2017: 7.2), Lemmas 7.3.2–7.3.5 (2017: 7.4–7.7), Corollaries 7.3.6, 7.3.8 (2017: 7.1, 7.2), Definition 7.3.7 (2017: 7.14)) and lifts ep-groupoids to level $1$
(Propositions 7.3.9, 7.5.3 (2017: 7.11, 7.12)). §7.5 (2017 §7.4) defines paracompact orbit spaces and sc-smooth partitions of unity (Definitions 7.5.1,
7.5.5 (2017: 7.15,
7.16), Remarks 7.5.2, 7.5.6 (2017: 7.1, 7.2)), proves the existence of invariant partitions of unity (Theorems 7.5.4, 7.5.7 (2017: 7.3, 7.4), Corollary 7.6.6 (2017: 7.3)) and
characterizes the closed subsets of $|X|$ (Definition 7.5.8 (2017: 7.17), Propositions 7.5.9, 7.5.10 (2017: 7.13, 7.14)). Appendix 7.6 (2017 7.5) proves Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1)
as Theorem 7.6.1 (2017: 7.5) (Lemmas 7.6.2, 7.6.3 (2017: 7.8, 7.9)) and Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4) as Theorem 7.6.4 (2017: 7.6) (Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10)).

What is verified. **Theorems 7.1.13–7.6.4 (2017: 7.1–7.6) hold**, with the readings recorded below, and so do Propositions 7.1.8–7.2.4, 7.3.9–7.5.10 (2017: 7.1–7.8, 7.11–7.14),
Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017) under the hypothesis that $\mathbf X^R$ is Hausdorff and paracompact, Lemmas 7.1.11–7.6.5 (2017: 7.1–7.10), and
Corollaries 7.3.6–7.6.6 (2017: 7.1–7.3) (Corollary 7.6.6 (2017: 7.3) with the theorem of Godefroy–Troyanski–Whitfield–Zizler as an explicit hypothesis, as
in Part I). Every definition of the chapter is formalized: Definitions 7.1.1 (2017: 7.1; V7.1), 7.1.2 (2017: 7.2; V7.2), 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3; V7.3), 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4; V7.5,
$T\varphi$ as a definition only), 7.1.5 (2017: 7.5; V7.7), 7.1.6 (2017: 7.6; V7.8), 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7; V7.9), 7.1.18 (2017: 7.8; V7.26), 7.1.20 (2017: 7.9; V7.28), 7.1.21 (2017: 7.10; V7.29), 7.2.1 (2017: 7.11; V7.33), 7.2.7 (2017: 7.12; V7.38), 7.2.15 (2017: 7.13; V7.41), 7.3.7 (2017: 7.14; V7.49), 7.5.1 (2017: 7.15; V7.53), 7.5.5 (2017: 7.16; V7.56), 7.5.8 (2017: 7.17; V7.59). Several places of the text
needed more than a reading. (a) *The remark after Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7).* That sc-smoothness of a functor on objects implies
sc-smoothness on morphisms does not hold as we read it (a counterexample on the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action on
$\mathbb R$); it holds for functors continuous on morphisms, which is what the text's argument uses (V7.10). (b) *The
reduced morphism space.* The proof of Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) gives the charts of $\mathbf X^R$ and their sc-smooth transitions,
but, as we read it, neither Hausdorffness nor paracompactness; both are hypotheses of Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017), discharged
for effective ep-groupoids (V7.39, V7.40; gap G.71). (c) *Connectedness.* The natural representation of Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1) is
taken on a connected $U$, which the text chooses on 2017 p. 231 but does not put in the statement; it is what makes $\Phi$ a
homomorphism, $\Gamma$ a functor, and Lemma 7.2.2 (2017: 7.2) true, and the local path connectedness of M-polyfolds that supplies it is
proved (V7.17, V7.18, V7.34). (d) *Tameness of $X^1$.* Proposition 7.3.9's (2017: 7.11) "if $X$ is tame so is $X^1$" needs that the
index lift of a tame retraction is tame, which Part I left open; it is proved (V7.52). (e) *Omitted steps.* The
uniqueness of natural representations behind "adapting restrictions" (V7.24, V7.35), the conjugation $\varphi T_x
\varphi^{-1} = T_y$ needed for $\mathbf X^R$ (V7.37), the passage from compact to component compact sets in Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2)
(V7.51), the support bound that makes the sum in the proof of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4) locally finite (V7.66, V7.67), and Michael's
theorem on unions of closed paracompact sets (V7.50) are proved; Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5) is proved by a construction without
induction (V7.25). Not verified: the properties of $T\varphi$ (Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4)), the set $|X_\infty|$ of the filtration
of $|X|$, the tangent facts (3), (4) recalled before Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7), Hausdorffness and paracompactness of $\mathbf X^R$
for a general ep-groupoid, and the open question of 2017 p. 249 (see the list at the end of this section). An addendum (2026-11-12, the Part II wave; Findings, items 9, 95, 107, 111, 130, 131, 139, 156) verifies the 2021 statements as printed: the remark after Definition 7.1.7 with its continuity on morphisms (V7.10), Proposition 7.2.10 (charts and transitions), Theorem 7.2.14 and Proposition 7.2.16 under $T_R$ Hausdorff (V7.39, V7.40), Corollary 7.6.6 without Theorem 5.5.16 as a hypothesis (V7.68), Theorem 7.6.7 and Corollary 7.6.8 for every $i$ as isomorphisms in $\mathcal{EP}$ (V7.83; gap G.82 closed), and Zhou's example of Appendix 7.6.3 itself, on $L^2(\mathbb R)$ with $E_m = H^{m,\delta_m}(\mathbb R)$, with its exact non-effective part (V7.82, V7.95; gap G.83 closed); Remark 7.5.6 has nothing to formalize (V7.57). Every gap of the chapter is closed.

The setting. Obj and Mor are types with M-polyfold structures `PObj`, `PMor`, Hausdorff and paracompact, as for every
M-polyfold of the project (Definition 2.3.4 (2017: 2.8)). An ep-groupoid is `Polyfold.EpGroupoid`, a `Polyfold.GroupoidStr` (the maps
$s, t, m, u, \iota$ with the groupoid laws on composable pairs; the composition of a non-composable pair is a junk value,
never used) with the conditions (1)–(4) of Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3). Properness is Mathlib's `IsProperMap` of the restriction
$t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X V) \to X$, equivalent to the sequential form the proofs use (V7.4). "An open neighbourhood $U(x)$
equipped with the natural $G_x$-action" is a datum `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep` (V7.17), never a hypothesis "for every
such $U(x)$". $|X|$ carries the quotient topology. Part I results are cited in the same way, by their 2021 numbers with the 2017 numbers in parentheses. Findings referred to
below are those of `Exposition/Findings.md`, "Chapter 7".

**V7.1 (Definition 7.1.1 (2017: 7.1), groupoids and the orbit space; `Polyfold.GroupoidStr`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.src`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.tgt`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.comp`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.unit`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.inv`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.comp_assoc`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.comp_unit`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.unit_comp`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.comp_inv`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.inv_comp`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.mor`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.morOn`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.Isomorphic`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.orbitSetoid`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.OrbitSpace`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.π`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.π_eq_π_iff`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.saturation`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.IsSaturated`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.isSaturated_iff`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.Ob`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.instGroupoid`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.orbitSetoid_eq`).** A groupoid is a set of objects and a set of
invertible morphisms with source, target, an associative composition on composable pairs, units and inverses; $|X|$ is
the quotient by $x \sim y$ iff there is a morphism $x \to y$, with projection $\pi$. *Book:* Definition 7.1.1 (2017: 7.1) and the
paragraph after it, pp. 287–288 (2017 pp. 225–226). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* a structure of maps on types, the
laws required on composable pairs and the composition total with a junk value; the saturation $\pi^{-1}(\pi(A))$ of
Definition 7.1.21 (2017: 7.10) is defined here; the bridge to Mathlib's `CategoryTheory.Groupoid` is added so that "full" and
"faithful" are Mathlib's (Findings, item 1).

**V7.2 (Definition 7.1.2 (2017: 7.2), the isotropy group; `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.Isotropy`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.Isotropy.val_mul`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.Isotropy.val_one`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.Isotropy.val_inv`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.isotropyEquivVertexGroup`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.isotropyEquivAut`).** $G_x$ is the group of
morphisms $x \to x$ under composition. *Book:* Definition 7.1.2 (2017: 7.2), p. 288 (2017 p. 226). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(restated):* the multiplication is $g h = g \circ h$, the text's; Mathlib's vertex group multiplies in the other order
and is identified with the opposite group (Findings, item 2).

**V7.3 (Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3), ep-groupoids; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.PObj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.PMor`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_tgt`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_unit`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_inv`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_isProperMap`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothComp`, `Polyfold.IsScSmoothComp`, `Polyfold.IsScSmoothCompSheet`,
`Polyfold.isScSmoothComp_iff_sheet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothCompSheet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_src`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_tgt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_fibredProduct`).** An ep-groupoid is a
groupoid with M-polyfold structures on objects and morphisms such that (1) $s, t$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms, (2) $u$
and $\iota$ are sc-smooth, (3) every $x$ has an open $V(x)$ with $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X V(x)) \to X$ proper, (4) $m$ is
sc-smooth on the fibred product $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X$; all structure maps are then sc-smooth. *Book:*
Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3), pp. 288 ff. (2017 pp. 226–227). *Hidden hypotheses:* Obj and Mor Hausdorff and paracompact (the project's M-polyfolds).
*Deviation (restated):* (3) existential per point, with Mathlib's proper maps; the universal form "for every open $V
\ni x$" fails (the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$), and every smaller open neighbourhood works. (4) on the sub-M-polyfold of
Part I's Proposition 2.5.20 (2017: 2.15), the book's statement of the text's citation "Lemma 2.8 in [38]" (an external reference, not a
misprint); the proofs use the equivalent sheet form (Findings, items 3, 4, 103).

**V7.4 (properness and its sequential form; `Polyfold.isProperMap_iff_exists_tendsto_subseq`,
`Polyfold.exists_tendsto_subseq_of_isProperMap`, `Polyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_iff`,
`Polyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_iff_of_isClosed`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_iff`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_iff_isCompact_preimage`, `Polyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_closure_mono`,
`Polyfold.isClosed_image_preimage_of_isProperMap_domRestrict`, `Polyfold.isClosed_of_isProperMap_domRestrict`,
`Polyfold.finite_setOf_of_isProperMap_domRestrict`).** For the restriction of $t$ to a closed $s^{-1}(Q)$ between
metrizable spaces, properness is equivalent to: every sequence with convergent targets has a convergent subsequence;
it passes to smaller closures, and proper restrictions have closed images and finite fibres. *Book:* the notion of
Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3), 2017 p. 227, used in sequential form in Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3), Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1) (p. 292 (2017 p. 230)), Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7) (p. 307 (2017 p. 238)),
Proposition 7.3.9 (2017: 7.11) (2017 p. 248), Proposition 7.5.9 (2017: 7.13) (p. 342 (2017 p. 251)) and Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8) (2017 p. 254). *Hidden hypotheses:* metrizability (Theorem
2.3.10 (2017: 2.2)), which M-polyfolds have. *Deviation (not in the book):* the equivalence is used without comment in the text
(Findings, item 3).

**V7.5 (Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4), the local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$ and the tangent $T\varphi$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Sheet`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Sheet.hat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Sheet.isScDiffeoOn_hat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_sheet`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.sheetAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_sheetAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hat`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScDiffeoOn_hat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hat_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentMor`).** For a
morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ there are open $\mathbf U(\varphi)$, $U(x)$, $U(y)$ with $s : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(x)$,
$t : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(y)$ sc-diffeomorphisms, and $\hat\varphi = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1} : U(x) \to
U(y)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism with $\hat\varphi(x) = y$; $T\varphi := T\hat\varphi(x)$. *Book:* 2017 p. 227 (the paragraph
before the definition) and Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4), p. 289 (2017 p. 227). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* $\hat\varphi$ is
verified; $T\varphi$ is a definition only, and that it is a bounded linear isomorphism on level $0$ for $\varphi \in
\mathbf X_1$ and an sc-isomorphism for smooth $\varphi$ is not verified (gaps G.7, G.70). The display reads
"$\hat\varphi = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1} \circ U(x) \to U(y)$", $\circ$ for $:$ (possible misprint), and
"$T\varphi : T_{s(\varphi)}X \to T_{t(\varphi)}$" lacks the $X$ (possible misprint or extraction artefact) (Findings,
items 5, 110).

**V7.6 (the levels of an ep-groupoid and the filtration of $|X|$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_levelSet_src_iff`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_levelSet_tgt_iff`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.maxLevel`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.maxLevel_eq`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.degIndex_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.degIndex_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.degIndex_tgt`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orbitLevel`).** $s$ and $t$ preserve the levels, so $ml(x) = ml(\varphi) = ml(y)$ for $\varphi : x \to
y$; $d_X(s(\varphi)) = d_{\mathbf X}(\varphi) = d_X(t(\varphi))$, so $d_X$ is constant on classes; $|X_k| = \pi(X_k)$.
*Book:* pp. 289–291 (2017 pp. 227–228), with Part I's Proposition 2.4.4 (2017: 2.7). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* the set $|X_\infty|$
and $|X_\infty| = \bigcap_k |X_k|$ are not stated (gap G.72); the density of $X_\infty$ in every $X_k$, stated on 2017 p. 227
without proof, is not formalized and is not in Part I for M-polyfolds (gap G.73; Findings, items 6, 112, 116).

**V7.7 (Definition 7.1.5 (2017: 7.5), the induced degeneracy index; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.degIndexOrbit`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.degIndexOrbit_π`).** $d_{|X|}(|x|) = d_X(x)$ is well defined. *Book:* Definition 7.1.5 (2017: 7.5), p. 290 (2017 p. 228). *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none (Findings, item 6).

**V7.8 (Definition 7.1.6 (2017: 7.6), tame ep-groupoids, and the tameness of $\mathbf X$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsTame`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsTame`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.exists_tame_chart`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isTame`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isTame_iff_of_surjective`).** $X$ is tame if the object M-polyfold is tame; then the
morphism M-polyfold is tame. *Book:* Definition 7.1.6 (2017: 7.6) and the paragraph after it, 2017 p. 228. *Hidden hypotheses:* none; "tame"
is the existence of an equivalent tame atlas (Definition 2.5.7 (2017: 2.19)), satisfiable (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isTame_trivial_rn`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isTame_reflection`); "every chart tame" would be unsatisfiable. *Deviation (restated):* the
tame atlas of $\mathbf X$ is the one transported along $s$ (Findings, items 7, 106).

**V7.9 (Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7), the category $\mathcal{EP}$; `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.mor_inv`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.id`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.comp`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.toFunctor`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isScSmoothMap_obj`,
`Polyfold.EpFunctor.isScSmoothMap_mor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.id`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.comp`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.ext`,
`Polyfold.EP`).** The objects of $\mathcal{EP}$ are the ep-groupoids, its morphisms the functors sc-smooth on objects and
on morphisms. *Book:* Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7), p. 290 (2017 p. 228). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* functors commute with
$s, t, m, u$; the compatibility with $\iota$ is derived (Findings, item 8).

**V7.10 (the remark after Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7): sc-smoothness on objects and continuity on morphisms suffice;
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mor_eq_srcInv_obj_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_mor_of_continuous`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_mor_iff_continuous`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.continuous_mor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.ofContinuous`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.remark_definition_7_1_7_counterexample`).** A functor sc-smooth on objects and continuous (on
level $0$) on morphisms is sc-smooth on morphisms, by $f(\gamma) = (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}(f(s(\gamma)))$ on $\mathbf
U(\varphi)$. *Book:* p. 291 (2017 pp. 228–229); the 2021 text asks the continuity on morphisms. *Hidden hypotheses:* none for
the 2021 text. *Deviation (as in the book, 2021):* the argument needs only a sheet $\mathbf U(\psi)$ at $\psi = f(\varphi)$ and
$\mathbf U(\varphi) = f^{-1}(\mathbf U(\psi))$. The 2017 sentence, without continuity, does not hold as we read it: a functor
of the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action on $\mathbb R$, the identity on objects, is sc-smooth on objects and not continuous on
morphisms (Findings, items 9, 104).

**V7.11 (the quotient topology and Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1), openness of $\pi$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.continuous_π`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_8`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_8_isOpenQuotientMap`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_8_map_nhds`).** $|X|$ carries the quotient topology and $\pi$ is open. *Book:* 2017 p. 229 and
Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1), p. 291 (2017 p. 229). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* proved through the saturation $\pi^{-1}(\pi(U))
= t(s^{-1}(U))$ and the openness of $t$ (Findings, item 10).

**V7.12 (Proposition 7.1.9 (2017: 7.2), countable neighbourhood bases; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_9`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_9_of_hasAntitoneBasis`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_9_firstCountableTopology`).**
Every $z \in |X|$ has a monotone countable basis of open neighbourhoods. *Book:* Proposition 7.1.9 (2017: 7.2), p. 291 (2017 p. 229), with Theorem 2.3.10 (2017: 2.2).
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* Mathlib's `HasAntitoneBasis`, radii $1/(k + 1)$ (Findings, item 10).

**V7.13 (Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3), the local closure relation; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_10`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_10_of_isProperMap`).** Every $x$ has an open $U$ with $\pi(\mathrm{cl}_X A) =
\mathrm{cl}_{|X|}\pi(A)$ for all $A \subseteq U$. *Book:* Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3), pp. 292 ff. (2017 pp. 229–230). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (stronger):* for every $U$ with the properness property and every $A \subseteq \mathrm{cl}_X U$, proved from the
closedness of the proper map instead of sequences (Findings, item 11).

**V7.14 (Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1); `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_1_11`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_1_11_swap`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_1_11_of_isProperMap`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_1_11_swap_of_isProperMap`,
`Polyfold.finite_setOf_mem_of_isProperMap_domRestrict`, `Polyfold.IsProperMap.finite_preimage_singleton_of_isLocallyInjective`).**
If $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X U(x_0)) \to X$ is proper, only finitely many $\psi$ have $s(\psi) = x$ and $t(\psi) \in
U(x_0)$. *Book:* Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1), p. 292 (2017 p. 230). *Hidden hypotheses:* none; the openness of $U(x_0)$ and $x_0 \in U(x_0)$ are not used.
*Deviation (restated):* the proof treats the inverses ($s$ and $t$ exchanged), and both forms are proved; finiteness from a
compact discrete fibre. Possible misprints in the proof: "$t : V(\psi) \to V(y)$" for $V(x)$, "$s(\psi) \in
s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(U(x_0)))$", and unbalanced parentheses in statement and proof (Findings, items 12, 96).

**V7.15 (Proposition 7.1.12 (2017: 7.4), finiteness of the isotropy groups; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_12`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.finite_isotropy_of_isLocalScDiffeo`).** $G_x$ is finite. *Book:* Proposition 7.1.12 (2017: 7.4), p. 293 (2017 p. 230).
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none; from Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1) with $x_0 = x$ (Findings, item 13).

**V7.16 (the identification $G_x \to G_y$, $g \mapsto \varphi \circ g \circ \varphi^{-1}$; `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.isotropyConj`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.isotropyConj_val`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.conjIsotropy`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.conjIsotropy_val`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.nonempty_isotropy_mulEquiv`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.nat_card_isotropy_eq`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isotropyConj_eq_isotropyConj_conj`).** Isomorphic objects have isomorphic isotropy groups, by
conjugation with a chosen $\varphi : x \to y$; there is no canonical identification. *Book:* 2017 p. 230, after Proposition 7.1.12 (2017: 7.4).
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* two choices of $\varphi$ differ by an inner automorphism of $G_x$ (equivalently, of $G_y$)
(Findings, item 13).

**V7.17 (Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1), the natural representation of $G_x$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.U`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpen_U`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isConnected_U`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mem_U`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isScDiffeoOn_Φ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_mul`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isScSmoothOn_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_self`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.src_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.tgt_Γ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.existsUnique_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_one`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mapsTo_Φ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_inv_Φ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.bijOn_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_1_13`).** For every open $V \ni x$ there are an open
$U \subseteq V$ of $x$, a homomorphism $\Phi : G_x \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(U)$ and an sc-smooth $\Gamma : G_x \times U \to
\mathbf X$ with (1) $\Gamma(g, x) = g$, (2) $s(\Gamma(g, y)) = y$, $t(\Gamma(g, y)) = \Phi(g)(y)$, (3) $\Gamma$ a bijection
onto the morphisms between points of $U$. *Book:* Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1), p. 293 (2017 p. 231) (proved as Theorem 7.6.1 (2017: 7.5), V7.62). *Hidden
hypotheses:* $U$ connected, which the text chooses on 2017 p. 231 and the homomorphism property needs. *Deviation
(stronger):* $U$ connected; $\Phi(g)$ an sc-diffeomorphism of $U$ with inverse $\Phi(g^{-1})$; $\Gamma$ sc-smooth on each
slice $\{g\} \times U$, which is sc-smoothness on $G_x \times U$ (V7.20) (Findings, item 20).

**V7.18 (local path connectedness of M-polyfolds; `Polyfold.ScRetraction.exists_ball_joinedIn`,
`Polyfold.IsScRetract.locallyPathConnectedSpace`, `Polyfold.MChart.pathComponentIn_mem_nhds`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.locallyPathConnectedSpace`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.locallyConnectedSpace`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasBasis_isOpen_isConnected`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isOpen_connectedComponent`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isConnected_iff_isPathConnected`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.locallyPathConnectedSpace_quotient`,
`Polyfold.eqOn_sections_of_isPreconnected`).** M-polyfolds and all their quotients are locally path connected; open
connected sets are path connected; two sections of a local homeomorphism agreeing at a point agree on a connected set.
*Book:* used without statement on p. 293 (2017 p. 231) ("the connected open neighborhood $U(x)$"), in Lemma 7.6.3 (2017: 7.9) (p. 345 (2017 p. 254)) and
Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2) (p. 326 (2017 p. 247)). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (not in the book):* the first fact of gap G.56 of Part I,
now formalized (Findings, items 21, 114).

**V7.19 (the splitting $\mathbf U(x) = \bigsqcup_g \mathbf U(g)$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpen_image_Γ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_mem_image`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.pairwise_disjoint_image_Γ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.iUnion_image_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpen_morOn`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isConnected_image_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.connectedComponentIn_morOn`,
