`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.index`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_index`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_6_2`).** The
morphisms between points of $U(x)$ form the disjoint union of the connected open sets $\mathbf U(g) = \Gamma(g, U)$, on
which $s$ and $t$ are sc-diffeomorphisms onto $U(x)$, and $\mathbf U(x)$ can be put into any open neighbourhood of $G_x$.
*Book:* 2017 p. 231. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none; "arbitrarily small" is Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8) for arbitrary open $N_g$
followed by Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1) (Findings, item 22).

**V7.20 (the M-polyfold $G \times U$; `Polyfold.discretePolyfold`, `Polyfold.discreteChart`,
`Polyfold.discreteChart_compatible`, `Polyfold.isScSmoothMap_discrete_iff`, `Polyfold.isScSmoothOn_univ_prod_discrete_iff`,
`Polyfold.isScSmoothMap_prod_discrete_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.objPolyfold`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.morPolyfold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isScSmoothMap_smul`).** $G \times U$ is an
M-polyfold, the finite disjoint union of copies of $U$. *Book:* 2017 p. 232. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(restated):* the product with the discrete M-polyfold on $G$; maps on it are sc-smooth iff they are on each slice
(Findings, item 23).

**V7.21 (the translation groupoid $G_x \ltimes U(x)$ is an ep-groupoid; `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.translation`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translationGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.shearHomeomorph`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translation_isLocalScDiffeo_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translation_isLocalScDiffeo_tgt`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translation_isScSmoothCompSheet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translation_isProperMap`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translationEpGroupoid`).** The category with objects $U$, morphisms $G \times U$,
$s(g, y) = y$, $t(g, y) = \Phi(g)(y)$, $(g, y) \circ (h, z) = (gh, z)$ is an ep-groupoid. *Book:* p. 294 (2017 p. 232) ("using the proof of
Theorem 7.1 one verifies"). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* built from the data $(\Phi, \Gamma)$
alone, with the properness for every open $V$ (Findings, item 22).

**V7.22 (the functor $\Gamma : G_x \ltimes U(x) \to X$ is fully faithful; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_mul`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_one`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_inv`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.functor`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.full`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.faithful`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.epFunctor`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.fullSub`).** $\Gamma$ is a functor, full and faithful by Theorem 7.1.13 (3) (2017: 7.1), with image the full
subcategory on $U(x)$. *Book:* 2017 p. 232. *Hidden hypotheses:* $U$ connected (V7.17), for $\Gamma$ to be a functor.
*Deviation (stronger):* also an ep-functor, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.epFunctor` (Findings, item 22).

**V7.23 (the map $\hat\Phi : G_x \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(\mathbf U(x))$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φhat`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φhat_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φhat_mem_image`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.index_Φhat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.src_Φhat`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.tgt_Φhat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_conj`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φhat_one`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φhat_mul`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isScDiffeoOn_Φhat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.image_Φhat`).**
$\hat\Phi(g)(\varphi) = \Gamma(g h g^{-1}, g \ast s(\varphi))$ for $\varphi \in \mathbf U(h)$ is a homomorphism into the
sc-diffeomorphisms of $\mathbf U(x)$ with $\hat\Phi(g)(\mathbf U(h)) = \mathbf U(g h g^{-1})$ and the two commutative
diagrams with $s$ and $t$. *Book:* pp. 294–297 (2017 pp. 232–233). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none; no possible misprint on pp. 293–297 (2017 pp. 231–233) (Findings, item 22).

**V7.24 (uniqueness and restriction of natural representations; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_eqOn`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_eqOn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mapsTo_Φ_connectedComponentIn`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eventually_Φ_eq_of_actsTrivially`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.restrict`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.restrictInter`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_naturalRep_restrict`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_naturalRep_shrink`).** Two natural representations at $x$ agree on the component of $x$ in
$U \cap U'$, and a natural representation restricts to invariant connected open neighbourhoods. *Book:* used without
statement on pp. 307–311 (2017 pp. 239–241) ("adapting restrictions", "$U(x)$ … can be chosen arbitrarily small"). *Hidden hypotheses:*
none. *Deviation (not in the book):* stated and proved (Findings, item 24).

**V7.25 (Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5), the natural representation of a finite set of isomorphic objects;
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.F`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.isScDiffeoOn_F`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.F_comp`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.F_unit`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.pairwiseDisjoint_U`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.morOn_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.isScDiffeoOn_src`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.isScDiffeoOn_tgt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.F_eq`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.natural`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transportRep`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.exists_star`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.emptyNaturalRepFinite`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_15_2017`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_15_of_mem_nhdsSet`).** For finitely many mutually isomorphic objects $Y$ and a
neighbourhood $V$ of $Y$ there is a functor $f$ assigning disjoint connected open $U(y) \subseteq V$ and sc-diffeomorphisms
$f(\psi) : U(y) \to U(y')$, such that the morphisms between the $U(y)$ split into components $\mathbf U(\psi)$ with (1) the
natural action of $G_y$ on $U(y)$, (2) $s, t : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(y)$ sc-diffeomorphisms, (3) $f(\psi) = t \circ
(s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}$. *Book:* Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5), pp. 297–304 (2017 pp. 233–236). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* proved
by transporting one natural representation along chosen morphisms from a base object, without the text's induction or
shrinking; $V$ a neighbourhood of the set $Y$; $Y = \emptyset$ allowed. Twelve possible misprints in the proof, one possibly
an extraction artefact (Findings,
items 25, 26).

**V7.26 (Definition 7.1.18 (2017: 7.8), the natural representation of $\mathbf Y$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.mono`).** The functor of Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5) with its properties. *Book:* Definition 7.1.18 (2017: 7.8), p. 304 (2017 p. 236). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none (Findings, item 25).

**V7.27 (Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6), $|U(x)| \cong G_x\backslash U(x)$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.π_eq_π_iff_exists_smul`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.orbitQuotientMap`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_orbitQuotientMap`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.range_orbitQuotientMap`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_19`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_19_fullyFaithful`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_19_orbitMap`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.translationOrbitHomeomorph`).** $\tau : G_x\backslash U(x) \to \pi(U(x))$, $G_x \ast y \mapsto |y|$, is a
homeomorphism; the functor $G_x \ltimes U(x) \to X$ is fully faithful and induces a homeomorphism of orbit spaces.
*Book:* Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6), pp. 304 ff. (2017 pp. 236–237). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* $\tau$ is an open embedding into
$|X|$; the openness of $\sigma$ is not needed (Findings, item 27).

**V7.28 (Definition 7.1.20 (2017: 7.9), local uniformizers, and the claims after it; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.rep`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.Ψ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.obj_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.full`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.faithful`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.isEmbedding_orbitMap`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.range_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.toLocalUniformizer`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_localUniformizer`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.injective_obj`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.injective_mor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_functor_obj`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_functor_mor`).** A local uniformizer is a fully faithful embedding
$\Psi_x : G_x \ltimes U(x) \to X$ inducing a homeomorphism onto $\pi(U(x))$; one exists around every object, and it is
injective on objects and morphisms. *Book:* Definition 7.1.20 (2017: 7.9) and the two sentences after it, 2017 p. 237. *Hidden hypotheses:*
none. *Deviation (restated):* "embedding" is derived, not a field; existence inside every open $V \ni x$. "$\Psi_x \circ
G_x \ltimes U(x) \to X$" ($\circ$ for $:$) and "a a local uniformizer" (possible misprints) (Findings, item 28).

**V7.29 (Definition 7.1.21 (2017: 7.10), ep-subgroupoids; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEpSubgroupoid`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEpSubgroupoid.isSubMPolyfold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEpSubgroupoid.isSaturated`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_univ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_of_isOpen`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_saturation`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_trivial`).** An ep-subgroupoid is
the full subcategory of a saturated sub-M-polyfold $A$ of $X$. *Book:* Definition 7.1.21 (2017: 7.10), p. 305 (2017 p. 237). *Hidden hypotheses:*
none; open saturated sets and saturations of open sets are witnesses. *Deviation:* none (Findings, items 40, 105).

**V7.30 (the facts (1)–(4) on the sub-M-polyfold $A$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subObjPolyfold`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_val_subObj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothOn_retractInto_subObj`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.subPolyfold`).** (1) $A \to X$ is sc-smooth and a homeomorphism onto its image, (2) $i^{-1} \circ r$ is
sc-smooth for a retraction onto $A \cap V$, (3), (4) the tangent spaces of $A$ at smooth points. *Book:* 2017 pp. 237–238, from
Part I's Proposition 2.3.19 (2017: 2.6). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* (1) and (2) are used; the tangent facts (3)
and (4) are not restated, as tangent spaces carry no linear structure here (gap G.7) (Findings, item 40).

**V7.31 (the morphism set $\mathbf A$ is a sub-M-polyfold; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.src_mem_of_tgt_mem_of_isSaturated`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.morOn_eq_preimage_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.morOn_eq_preimage_tgt`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isSubMPolyfold_preimage_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isSubMPolyfold_preimage_tgt`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isSubMPolyfold_morOn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subMorPolyfold`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_val_subMor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothOn_retractInto_subMor`).** $\mathbf A =
\{\varphi \mid s(\varphi), t(\varphi) \in A\}$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $\mathbf X$, by the retractions $\mathbf r = (s|\mathbf
U(\varphi))^{-1} \circ r \circ s$. *Book:* 2017 p. 238. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $\mathbf A =
s^{-1}(A)$ for saturated $A$, the preimage of a sub-M-polyfold under a local sc-diffeomorphism. The claim "$t(\mathbf
r(\psi)) \in U(a)$, so that $\mathbf r(\psi) \in \mathbf U(a)$" need not hold and is not used (possible misprint or
extraction artefact) (Findings, item 41).

**V7.32 (Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7), the full subcategory of a saturated sub-M-polyfold is an ep-groupoid;
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_fullSub_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_fullSub_tgt`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_fullSub_unit`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_fullSub_inv`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_isProperMap_fullSub`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothComp_fullSub`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.instParacompactSpaceMorOn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subEpGroupoid`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subEpGroupoid_src_val`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subEpGroupoid_comp_val`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_22`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subEpFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subEpFunctor_full`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.subEpFunctor_faithful`).** For $A$ saturated and a sub-M-polyfold, the full subcategory is an
ep-groupoid with the restricted structure maps, $A$ and $\mathbf A$ sub-M-polyfolds. *Book:* the argument on 2017 p. 238 and
Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7), pp. 307 ff. (2017 pp. 238–239). *Hidden hypotheses:* none; the paracompactness of $A$ and $\mathbf A$, which the project's
M-polyfolds need, is proved. *Deviation (stronger):* the steps the text leaves out (sc-smoothness into the
sub-M-polyfold, the inclusion of fibred products) are proved; any $V(a)$ with the properness property works; the
inclusion is a fully faithful ep-functor (Findings, item 42).

**V7.33 (Definition 7.2.1 (2017: 7.11), effective ep-groupoids, regular objects, and the sentence after it;
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEffective`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.IsRegular`, `Polyfold.GroupoidStr.regularSet`,
`Polyfold.GroupoidStr.isRegular_tgt_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isRegular_tgt_of_isRegular_src`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isSaturated_regularSet`).** $X$ is effective if every open neighbourhood of every $g \in G_x
\setminus \{1_x\}$ contains a $\psi$ with $s(\psi) \neq t(\psi)$; $x$ is regular if $G_x = \{1_x\}$; if $s(\varphi)$ is
regular, so is $t(\varphi)$. *Book:* Definition 7.2.1 (2017: 7.11) and the sentences after it, 2017 p. 239. *Hidden hypotheses:* none;
satisfiable non-vacuously (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isEffective_reflection_nonvacuous`). *Deviation:* none (Findings,
items 50, 101).

**V7.34 (Lemma 7.2.2 (2017: 7.2), $X_{reg}$ is open; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.subset_regularSet`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_2_2`).** The regular part is open. *Book:* Lemma 7.2.2 (2017: 7.2), p. 307 (2017 p. 239). *Hidden hypotheses:* $\Gamma(1, a) =
1_a$, i.e. $U$ connected (V7.17). *Deviation (stronger):* $U(x) \subseteq X_{reg}$ for every natural representation at a
regular $x$ (Findings, item 51).

**V7.35 (Lemma 7.2.3 (2017: 7.3), effectiveness and injective natural representations; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerΦ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.injective_Φ_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerΦ_eq_bot_iff`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEffective.eq_one`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEffective_iff_forall_naturalRep`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_2_3`).** $X$ is effective iff every $x$ has, inside every open $V(x)$, a natural representation
with $\Phi$ injective. *Book:* Lemma 7.2.3 (2017: 7.3), pp. 308–309 (2017 pp. 239–240). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* (1) ⇒ (2) for
every natural representation, without sequences; "adapting restrictions" read through V7.24; injectivity as trivial
kernel (Findings, item 52).

**V7.36 (Proposition 7.2.4 (2017: 7.8), $X_{reg}$ is open and dense for effective $X$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.stabilizerEquivIsotropy`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_4`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEffective_of_dense_regularSet`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEffective_iff_dense_regularSet`).** If $X$ is effective, $X_{reg}$ is open and dense. *Book:*
Proposition 7.2.4 (2017: 7.8), pp. 309 ff. (2017 pp. 240–241). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the minimum of $\#G$ is taken over the
given open set, so $U(x_0)$ is not needed; the converse also holds (Findings, item 53).

**V7.37 (the subgroup $T_x$ of elements acting trivially; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.ActsTrivially`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.trivialSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.one_mem_trivialSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.actsTrivially_iff`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_trivialSet_of_section`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_trivialSet_iff_eventually`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_mem_nhds_trivialSet_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_naturalRep_trivialSet_iff`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_naturalRep_kerΦ_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.trivialSubgroup`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.trivialSubgroup_normal`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEffective_iff_trivialSubgroup_eq_bot`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isotropyConj_mem_trivialSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.map_isotropyConj_trivialSubgroup`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mem_trivialSet_of_val_eq_Γ`).** $g$ acts trivially if $\Phi(g) = 1$ for some natural
representation; for $U(x)$ small the kernel of $\Phi$ is the set $T_x$ of such $g$, a normal subgroup. *Book:* 2017 p. 241.
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* there is a neighbourhood $N$ of $x$ with $\ker\Phi = T_x$ for every
natural representation inside $N$; $g \in T_x$ iff $s = t$ near $g$; $\varphi T_x \varphi^{-1} = T_y$, which Definition
7.2.7 (2017: 7.12) needs and the text does not state. "$\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(U(x)$" (possible misprint or extraction artefact) (Findings,
item 54).

**V7.38 (Definition 7.2.7 (2017: 7.12), the non-effective part $\mathbf X^T$ and the reduced morphisms $\mathbf X^R$;
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.nonEffectivePart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_nonEffectivePart_iff`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.nonEffectivePart_eq_interior`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.ReducedRel`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedRel_iff`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedSetoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedRel_comp_left`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.ReducedMor`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedMor_eq_quotient`).** $\mathbf X^T = \bigcup_x T_x$; $\varphi \sim \varphi'$ iff $s(\varphi) =
s(\varphi') = x$ and $\varphi = \varphi' \circ g$ with $g \in T_x$; $\mathbf X^R$ is the set of classes. *Book:* Definition
7.2.7 (2017: 7.12), p. 310 (2017 p. 241). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $\sim$ is an equivalence since $T_x$ is a subgroup;
$\mathbf X^T$ is the interior of $\{s = t\}$; "the subset $\mathbf X^R$" is a quotient (possible misprint) (Findings,
item 55).

**V7.39 (Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9), the natural charts of $\mathbf X^R$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_10_natural_charts`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedπ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isQuotientMap_reducedπ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isOpenMap_reducedπ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.injOn_reducedπ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedChart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedChart_compatible`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedCharts`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedAtlas`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedPolyfold`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isChart_reducedChart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScDiffeoOn_reducedπ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_reducedπ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_10`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_reducedMor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.t2Space_reducedMor_of_isEffective`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_reducedMor_of_isEffective`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_reducedMor_of_t3`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.exists_not_t2Space_reducedMor`).**
$\mathbf X^R$ with the quotient topology $T_R$ has a natural collection of charts $\psi \circ \sigma \circ s$, which cover it
and have sc-smooth transitions; they form `reducedAtlas`. *Book:* Proposition 7.2.10, p. 313 (2017: 7.9, pp. 242–243).
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (as in the book, 2021):* the quotient map is open and injective on sheets; the
M-polyfold `reducedPolyfold` needs only $T_R$ Hausdorff (paracompactness is an instance, V7.77), which is Proposition 7.2.13
(V7.78). The 2017 Proposition 7.9, a natural M-polyfold structure for every ep-groupoid, does not hold as we read it: for
$\mathbb Z/2$ acting on the dimension-jumping retract of Part I's Remark 4.2.2 (2017: 4.3), $\mathbf X^R$ is not Hausdorff
(`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.exists_not_t2Space_reducedMor`). Four reading points in the 2017 proof (Findings, items 56,
57, 60, 107, 111).

**V7.40 (Theorem 7.2.14 and Proposition 7.2.16 (2017: Proposition 7.10), the reduced ep-groupoid $X_R$;
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_2_14_reduced`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_16`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedSrc`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedTgt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedUnit`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedInv`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedComp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedGroupoidStr`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_reducedSrc`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_reducedTgt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_reducedUnit`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_reducedInv`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_isProperMap_reduced`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothCompSheet_reduced`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedEpGroupoid`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reductionFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEffective_reducedEpGroupoid`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_10_2017`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reductionIso`).** If $T_R$ is Hausdorff, $(X, \mathbf X^R)$
with the induced structure maps is an ep-groupoid $X_R$, effective, with isotropy groups $G_x/T_x$, and $\pi$ is a morphism
$X \to X_R$ of $\mathcal{EP}$. *Book:* Theorem 7.2.14, p. 318, Proposition 7.2.16 and the isotropy sentence, p. 319 (2017
p. 243 and Proposition 7.10, p. 244). *Hidden hypotheses:* none (paracompactness of $T_R$ is an instance, V7.77).
*Deviation (as in the book, 2021):* (3) via the continuous surjection $\mathbf X \to \mathbf X^R$; (4) in sheet form, with a
step the text leaves implicit; effectiveness from the intrinsic form of $T_x$; for effective $X$, $X_R \cong X$. The 2017
Proposition 7.10, for every ep-groupoid, does not hold as we read it, since $\mathbf X^R$ need not be Hausdorff (V7.39)
(Findings, items 58, 60, 107, 111).

**V7.41 (the isotropy groups of $X_R$ and Definition 7.2.15 (2017: 7.13), the effective isotropy group;
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedIsotropyHom`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.surjective_reducedIsotropyHom`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.ker_reducedIsotropyHom`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.quotientTrivialSubgroupEquiv`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.EffIsotropy`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.normalClosure_trivialSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.effIsotropyEquiv`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.effIsotropyEquivReduced`).** The isotropy group of $x$ in $X_R$ is $G_x/T_x$, called the effective
isotropy group $G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$. *Book:* 2017 p. 244 and Definition 7.2.15 (2017: 7.13), p. 319 (2017 p. 244). *Hidden hypotheses:* the isomorphism with
the isotropy of $X_R$ under those of V7.39; $G_x/T_x$ itself needs none. *Deviation:* none; "For and object" (possible
misprint) (Findings, item 59).

**V7.42 (Theorem 7.3.1 (2017: 7.2), basic topological properties of $|X|$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_3_1`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_3_1_metrizable`, `Polyfold.metrizableSpace_of_locally`).** $|X|$ is locally metrizable,
regular and Hausdorff, and metrizable if paracompact. *Book:* Theorem 7.3.1 (2017: 7.2), p. 324 (2017 p. 244). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(restated):* "locally metrizable" as an open metrizable neighbourhood of every point; Smirnov's theorem in Part I's form
(Findings, item 70).

**V7.43 (Lemma 7.3.2 (2017: 7.4), local metrizability; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.metrizableSpace_orbitRel_quotient_naturalRep`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_3_2_naturalRep`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_3_2`).** Every point of $|X|$ has a metrizable
open neighbourhood, $|U(x)|$ for a natural representation. *Book:* Lemma 7.3.2 (2017: 7.4), pp. 324 ff. (2017 pp. 244–245). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (restated):* $\hat\rho$ computed as $\min_h \rho(y, h \ast y')$ (Findings, item 71).

**V7.44 (Lemma 7.3.3 (2017: 7.5), countable neighbourhood bases; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_3_3`).** Every point of $|X|$ has a
monotone countable basis of open neighbourhoods. *Book:* Lemma 7.3.3 (2017: 7.5), p. 324 (2017 p. 245). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:*
none; it is Proposition 7.1.9 (2017: 7.2) (V7.12) (Findings, item 72).

**V7.45 (Lemma 7.3.4 (2017: 7.6), $|X|$ is Hausdorff; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.t1Space_orbitSpace`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_3_4`).**
*Book:* Lemma 7.3.4 (2017: 7.6), pp. 325 ff. (2017 pp. 245–246). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* from Lemma 7.3.5 (2017: 7.7) and the closedness of
points, instead of the text's direct argument (Findings, item 72).

**V7.46 (Lemma 7.3.5 (2017: 7.7), $|X|$ is regular; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_3_5`).** *Book:* Lemma 7.3.5 (2017: 7.7), p. 325 (2017 p. 246). *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* with a closed neighbourhood basis and Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3) (Findings, item 72).

**V7.47 (Corollary 7.3.6 (2017: 7.1), the metrizability criterion; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.corollary_7_3_6`).** If $|X|$ is second countable,
it is metrizable. *Book:* Corollary 7.3.6 (2017: 7.1), p. 326 (2017 p. 247). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none; Urysohn's theorem
(Findings, item 73).

**V7.48 (subsets of $|X|$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_metrizable_nhds_subtype`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.metrizableSpace_of_paracompactSpace_subtype`).** A subset of $|X|$ is again locally metrizable,
regular and Hausdorff; a paracompact one is metrizable. *Book:* 2017 p. 247, before Definition 7.3.7 (2017: 7.14). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation:* none (Findings, item 73).

**V7.49 (Definition 7.3.7 (2017: 7.14), component compact sets; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsComponentCompact`).** $K \subseteq |X|$ meets every
connected component of $|X|$ in a compact set. *Book:* Definition 7.3.7 (2017: 7.14), p. 326 (2017 p. 247). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:*
none (Findings, item 74).

**V7.50 (Michael's theorem and unions of closed paracompact sets; `Polyfold.lemma_2_7_3`, `Polyfold.michael_tfae`,
`Polyfold.proposition_2_7_4`, `Polyfold.paracompactSpace_of_closed_refinement`, `Polyfold.exists_closed_precise_refinement`,
`Polyfold.paracompactSpace_iUnion`, `Polyfold.paracompactSpace_iUnion_of_finite`, `Polyfold.paracompactSpace_biUnion_of_finite`,
`Polyfold.paracompactSpace_union`, `Polyfold.paracompactSpace_of_isClosed_subset`).** A regular space is paracompact iff
every open cover has a closed locally finite refinement; a regular space with a locally finite cover by closed
paracompact subspaces is paracompact. *Book:* Part I, Lemma 2.7.3 (2017: 2.7) and Proposition 2.7.4 (2017: 2.17), used for Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2) (p. 326 (2017 p. 247))
and on the text's route to Proposition 7.5.3 (2017: 7.12) (p. 340 (2017 p. 249)). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the Hausdorff
property assumed by the text is not used; gap G.15 of Part I is now formalized (Findings, items 75, 114).

**V7.51 (Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2), neighbourhoods of component compact sets; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.locallyPathConnectedSpace_orbitSpace`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_isOpen_metrizableSpace_closure`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.corollary_7_3_8_of_isCompact`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.corollary_7_3_8`).** A component compact $K$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with $\mathrm{cl}_{|X|}(U)$
paracompact, hence $\mathrm{cl}(U)$ and $U$ metrizable. *Book:* Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2), p. 326 (2017 p. 247). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (restated):* the reduction to compact $K$ uses open components (local connectedness of $|X|$, V7.18) and a
locally finite union the text does not give; Michael's theorem (V7.50) for the finite union. "$U$" names both $\bigcup
\mathrm{cl}\,U(z_i)$ and $\bigcup U(z_i)$ (possible misprint) (Findings, item 74).

**V7.52 (Proposition 7.3.9 (2017: 7.11), index lifting; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.liftSrc`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.liftTgt`,

`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_liftSrc`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_liftTgt`,

`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothComp_lift`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.liftOne`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsTame.levelOne`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isTame_liftOne`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_3_9`).** $X^1 = (X^1, \mathbf X^1)$ is an
ep-groupoid, tame if $X$ is. *Book:* Proposition 7.3.9 (2017: 7.11), pp. 327–328 (2017 pp. 247–248). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):*
(4) in sheet form, avoiding $(\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X)^1 = \mathbf X^1\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X^1$; (3) with
convergence in $X_1$ for the compact set of the text and without its step (b); the tameness, for which the text gives no
argument and which Part I left open (Chapter 5, item 145), is proved. Display (7.5) has an unbalanced parenthesis
(possible misprint) (Findings, items 80, 81, 96).

**V7.53 (Definition 7.5.1 (2017: 7.15), ep-groupoids with paracompact orbit space, the sentence before Remark 7.5.2 (2017: 7.1), and Remark 7.5.2 (2017: 7.1);
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.HasParacompactOrbitSpace`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_7_5_2`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasParacompactOrbitSpace_of_secondCountableTopology`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasParacompactOrbitSpace_iff_metrizableSpace`).** (5): $|X|$ is paracompact, not required to be

*Book:* Definition 7.5.1 (2017: 7.15), the paragraph after it, and Remark 7.5.2 (2017: 7.1), p. 340 (2017 p. 249). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(restated):* "$X$ second countable" is read for the object space; Remark 7.5.2 (2017: 7.1) has no formal content; "it is presently not
known whether (5) is a consequence of (1)–(4)" is not formalized (Findings, items 82, 113).

**V7.54 (Proposition 7.5.3 (2017: 7.12), paracompactness under lifts, and the map $|X^1| \to |X|$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orbitIncl`,

**V7.55 (Theorem 7.5.4 (2017: 7.3), continuous partitions of unity; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orbitPullback`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orbitPullback_isSubordinate`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_isSaturated_nhds_finite_orbitPullback`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_5_4`).** For paracompact $|X|$, every open cover of $|X|$ has a subordinate partition of unity,
and every saturated open cover of $X$ an invariant continuous one. *Book:* Theorem 7.5.4 (2017: 7.3), p. 341 (2017 p. 250). *Hidden hypotheses:* $|X|$
Hausdorff, from Lemma 7.3.4 (2017: 7.6), for normality. *Deviation:* none (Findings, item 90).

**V7.56 (Definition 7.5.5 (2017: 7.16), ep-groupoids with sc-smooth partitions of unity; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.HasScPartitionsOfUnity`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScSmoothPartitionOfUnity`).** Every saturated open cover of $X$ has a subordinate sc-smooth partition
of unity with (1) saturated neighbourhoods meeting finitely many supports, (2) invariance. *Book:* Definition 7.5.5 (2017: 7.16), pp. 342 ff. (2017 pp. 250–251). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* index types in the universe of $X$, supports as `tsupport`,
(2) as $\beta_\lambda(s\varphi) = \beta_\lambda(t\varphi)$ (Findings, item 91).

**V7.57 (Remark 7.5.6 (2017: 7.2), on sc-smooth partitions of unity).** The remark (the topic is "a zoo" apart from sc-Hilbert spaces)
has no formal content: nothing to formalize. *Book:* Remark 7.5.6 (2017: 7.2), p. 342 (2017 p. 251). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation:* none; the sc-Hilbert case is Corollary 7.6.6 (V7.68), proved with no hypothesis
(`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.corollary_7_6_6_unconditional`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_hilbert_unconditional`)
(Findings, item 91).

**V7.58 (Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4), sc-smooth partitions of unity of an ep-groupoid; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_5_7`).** If $|X|$ is
paracompact and the object M-polyfold admits sc-smooth partitions of unity, $X$ has sc-smooth partitions of unity.
*Book:* Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4), p. 342 (2017 p. 251) (proved as Theorem 7.6.4 (2017: 7.6), V7.65, V7.67). *Hidden hypotheses:* none; satisfiable
(`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_5_7_hypotheses_rn`). *Deviation:* none (Findings, items 94, 105).

**V7.59 (Definition 7.5.8 (2017: 7.17), proper subsets and the properness property; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsProperSubset`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.HasPropernessProperty`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_hasPropernessProperty`,

`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isProperSubset_iff_exists_tendsto_subseq`).** $Q$ is proper if $t : s^{-1}(Q) \to X$ is proper; an
open $U$ has the properness property if $\mathrm{cl}_X(U)$ is proper. *Book:* Definition 7.5.8 (2017: 7.17), p. 342 (2017 p. 251). *Hidden
hypotheses:* none. *Deviation:* none (Findings, item 92).

**V7.60 (Proposition 7.5.9 (2017: 7.13), proper subsets are closed; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_5_9`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsProperSubset.isClosed`).** *Book:* Proposition 7.5.9 (2017: 7.13), p. 342 (2017 p. 251). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation:* none; by the compactness of the preimage (Findings, item 92).

**V7.61 (Proposition 7.5.10 (2017: 7.14), closed subsets of $|X|$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isClosed_saturation_of_isProperSubset`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_5_10_one`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsProperSubset.of_subset`,

the proof starts at $U_0 := V \cap \bigcap_g s(N_g)$ so that $U \subseteq V$; the contractibility of $N^t_g$, $N^s_g$ is

**V7.63 (Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8); `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_6_2`).** There is an open $U_1 \subseteq U_0$ of $x_0$ such that every
morphism between points of $U_1$ lies in some $N_g$. *Book:* Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8), pp. 345 ff. (2017 pp. 253–254). *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (stronger):* for any open $N_g \ni g$ and any neighbourhood $U_0$; "properness assumption of ep-polyfolds"

**V7.67 (the proof of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4); `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_invariant_nhds_of_isOpen`,

**V7.68 (Corollary 7.6.6 (2017: 7.3), sc-Hilbert atlases; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.corollary_7_6_6_unconditional`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_hilbert_unconditional`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.corollary_7_6_6_hypotheses_rn_unconditional`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.corollary_7_6_6`,

(`Polyfold.godefroyTroyanskiWhitfieldZizlerStatement_of_separable`; gap G.53 closed); the form with it as a hypothesis is
kept (Findings, items 95, 106, 114).

### The additions of the 2021 edition (V7.69–V7.104)

The Springer edition (2021) changes the remark after Definition 7.1.7 and Proposition 7.1.15, adds Proposition 7.1.14,
Lemma 7.1.16 and Corollary 7.1.17, rewrites §7.2 from Definition 7.2.5 on (2017 Proposition 7.10 becomes Theorem 7.2.14,
preceded by a Hausdorff criterion for the topology $T_R$ of $\mathbf X^R$), adds §7.4 on the Zhou condition and unique
continuation, and adds Appendices 7.6.3 (Zhou's example), 7.6.4 (the reduced groupoid and index lifts) and 7.6.5 (the
boundary of a tame ep-groupoid). Numbers and pages below are the 2021 text's; items new in the 2021 edition have no 2017
counterpart. Lean files: `Chapter7/Book2021Basic.lean`, `ReducedCriterion.lean`, `Zhou.lean`, `TameBoundaryEp.lean`, and, for
Theorem 7.6.9 in full on top of Part I's Theorem 2.7.13 (2)–(4), `TameBoundaryEpStructure.lean` (V7.99–V7.101), and, for §7.4
on every lift $X^i$, `ZhouLevels.lean` (V7.102–V7.104).

**V7.69 (the remark after Definition 7.1.7, 2021 form; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_definition_7_1_7`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_definition_7_1_7_remarkFunctor`).** Let $F : X \to Y$ be a functor between ep-groupoids which is
sc-smooth on the object M-polyfolds and continuous on the morphism spaces, $\varphi \in \mathbf X$ and $\psi = F(\varphi)$.
There are open sets $U(\varphi) \ni \varphi$, $U(\psi) \ni \psi$, $U(s(\varphi))$, $U(s(\psi))$ with $F(U(s(\varphi)))
\subseteq U(s(\psi))$ and $F(U(\varphi)) \subseteq U(\psi)$ such that $s : U(\varphi) \to U(s(\varphi))$ and $s : U(\psi) \to
U(s(\psi))$ are sc-diffeomorphisms and $F(\gamma) = (s|U(\psi))^{-1}(F(s(\gamma)))$ for $\gamma \in U(\varphi)$; hence $F$ is
sc-smooth on the morphism spaces. The functor of the counterexample of V7.10 (on the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action on
$\mathbb R$) is sc-smooth on objects and not continuous on morphisms. *Book:* the remark after Definition 7.1.7, p. 291
(2017: after Definition 7.7, p. 228), which in 2021 assumes continuity on morphisms. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (restated):* the neighbourhoods are an existential statement; the 2021 hypothesis is the one under which V7.10
proved the 2017 remark, so the counterexample of V7.10 no longer applies (Findings, items 9, 104, 117).

**V7.70 (the data (7.3) and Proposition 7.1.14; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsotropySheetData`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_isotropySheetData`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_14`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_14_of_naturalRep`).** The data (7.3) at an object $x$ are an open $W(x) \ni x$
and, for every $g \in G_x$, open $U^s(g), U^t(g) \ni g$ on which $s$ and $t$ are sc-diffeomorphisms onto $W(x)$, with
inverses $s_g^{-1}$, $t_g^{-1}$; they exist at every object. Let $U(x)$ be an open neighbourhood of $x$, $\Phi(g)$ ($g \in
G_x$) sc-diffeomorphisms of $U(x)$ with inverse $\Phi(g^{-1})$ and $\Phi(gh) = \Phi(g) \circ \Phi(h)$, and $\Gamma(g, \cdot) :
U(x) \to \mathbf X$ sc-smooth with $\Gamma(g, x) = g$, $s(\Gamma(g, y)) = y$, $t(\Gamma(g, y)) = \Phi(g)(y)$. Then there is an
open $\Phi$-invariant $V(x) \ni x$ with $V(x) \subseteq W(x) \cap U(x)$ such that, for $v \in V(x)$ and $g \in G_x$, $\Gamma(g,
v) = s_g^{-1}(v)$, $\Phi(g)(v) = t(s_g^{-1}(v))$ and $\Gamma(g, v) = t_g^{-1}(\Phi(g)(v))$; the same holds for every natural
representation. *Book:* (7.3) and Proposition 7.1.14, p. 296, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (stronger):* property (3) of Theorem 7.1.13 (every morphism between points of $U(x)$ is some $\Gamma(g, y)$) is
assumed as printed but not used; the identity $\Gamma(g, v) = t_g^{-1}(\Phi(g)(v))$ of (7.4), from the proof, is added
(Findings, item 118).

**V7.71 (Proposition 7.1.15 in the 2021 form; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_15`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.src_eq_tgt_of_printed_2017`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.not_printed_2017_reflection`).** For a finite set
$Y$ of mutually isomorphic objects and a neighbourhood $V$ of $Y$ there is a natural representation of $Y$ on disjoint
connected open $U(y) \subseteq V$ (Definition 7.1.18, `NaturalRepFinite`) such that, for every morphism $\psi$ between
points of $Y$: $\psi \in \mathbf U(\psi)$, the connected component of $\psi$ in the set of morphisms between points of
$U = \bigcup_y U(y)$; $s : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(s(\psi))$ and $t : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(t(\psi))$ are sc-diffeomorphisms;
$f(\psi) = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}$ on $U(s(\psi))$; and $t(\psi') = f(\psi)(s(\psi'))$ for $\psi' \in \mathbf
U(\psi)$. The printed 2017 form of (2), $s, t : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(y)$ with one $y$ for both maps, together with the
other requirements forces $s(\psi) = t(\psi)$; for $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$ by reflection and $Y = \{1, -1\}$ the
hypotheses hold and a natural representation in the 2021 form exists, but no data of the printed 2017 form. *Book:*
Proposition 7.1.15, p. 297 (2017: 7.5, p. 233), with (2) printed as $U(s(\psi))$, $U(t(\psi))$ in 2021. *Hidden hypotheses:*
none. *Deviation (same):* none for the 2021 form; the 2017 form of (2) as printed does not hold as we read it, and the
structure `NaturalRepFinite` of V7.25 already had the 2021 form (Findings, items 25, 119).

**V7.72 (Lemma 7.1.16; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.mem_U_of_tendsto`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_1_16`).** In the construction of V7.71, let $\psi \in \mathbf Y$ and $\psi'_k \in \mathbf
U(\psi)$ converge to $\psi' \in \mathbf X$. If $(s(\psi'_k))$ or $(t(\psi'_k))$ converges to a point of $U(s(\psi)) \cup
U(t(\psi))$, then $\psi' \in \mathbf U(\psi)$, $s(\psi'_k) \to s(\psi') \in U(s(\psi))$ and $t(\psi'_k) \to t(\psi') \in
U(t(\psi))$. *Book:* Lemma 7.1.16, p. 300, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; the
step that a limit of points of $U(a)$ lying in $U(b)$ lies in $U(a)$ (the $U(y)$ are open and disjoint) is a separate lemma
(Findings, item 120).

**V7.73 (Corollary 7.1.17 (4)–(7); `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.corollary_7_1_17_4`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.corollary_7_1_17_5`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.corollary_7_1_17_6`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.corollary_7_1_17_7`).** In the construction of V7.71: (4) for $x \in Y$ there is a natural
representation $(\Phi, \Gamma)$ of $G_x$ on $U(x)$ with $\Gamma(g, z) = (s|\mathbf U(g))^{-1}(z)$ and $f(g)(z) = t(\Gamma(g, z)) =
\Phi(g)(z)$; (5) $f(\varphi)$ is equivariant along $\gamma_\varphi(g) = \varphi \circ g \circ \varphi^{-1}$; (6) for
composable $\varphi, \psi$ the multiplication is an sc-diffeomorphism from $\mathbf U(\psi)\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf U(\varphi)$,
an open subset of the fibred product sub-M-polyfold $\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X$, onto $\mathbf U(\psi \circ
\varphi)$; (7) the $U(y)$ can be taken with the properness property. *Book:* Corollary 7.1.17, p. 301, new in the 2021
edition ((1)–(3) are those of Proposition 7.1.15). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* in (6) the domain is
read inside Part I's fibred product sub-M-polyfold (Proposition 2.5.20 (2017: 2.15)) (Findings, item 120).

**V7.74 (Definition 7.2.5 and Lemma 7.2.6; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerOn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mem_kerOn`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerOn_anti`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerOn_normal`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerOn_le_trivialSubgroup`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.definition_7_2_5`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_2_6`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.trivialSubgroupEquiv`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.trivialSubgroupEquiv_apply`).** For a natural representation at $x$ and $V \subseteq X$, $T_x^V$
is the subgroup of the $g$ with $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ on $V \cap U(x)$; it decreases as $V$ grows and is normal for
invariant $V$. For every open $W \ni x$, $T_x^W \subseteq T_x$, and there is an invariant open $V \ni x$ in $U(x)$ with $T_x^W =
T_x$ for every open $x \in W \subseteq V$; so $T_x$, the intrinsic subgroup of V7.37, is the maximal subgroup acting trivially
on a small $W(x)$, for every natural representation. For $\varphi : x \to y$, $g \mapsto \varphi g \varphi^{-1}$ is injective
on $T_x$ with image $T_y$, an isomorphism $T_x \cong T_y$. *Book:* Definition 7.2.5 and Lemma 7.2.6, p. 310 (Definition 7.2.5:
2017 p. 241, before Definition 7.12; Lemma 7.2.6 new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):*
"maximal subgroup acting trivially on some small $W(x)$" is the pair of statements above (Findings, item 121).

**V7.75 (Definition 7.2.7, Remark 7.2.8 and Lemma 7.2.9 in the 2021 form; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_7_2_8`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isOpenQuotientMap_reducedπ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isOpenMap_reducedπ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isOpenEmbedding_domRestrict_reducedπ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedTgt`).** The topology $T_R$ of
$\mathbf X^R$ (the quotient topology) makes $\pi : \mathbf X \to \mathbf X^R$ continuous and is finer than every topology with
this property; $\pi$ is an open quotient map and an open embedding on every sheet of $s$. *Book:* Definition 7.2.7, p. 310
(2017: 7.12), Remark 7.2.8, p. 311, new in the 2021 edition, and Lemma 7.2.9, p. 311. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (restated):* "the finest topology for which $\pi$ is continuous" is the quotient topology. In Definition 7.2.7 the
target map is printed "$s([\varphi]) = t_X(\varphi)$" (possible misprint for $t([\varphi])$; `reducedTgt`); Lemma 7.2.9 is
V7.39's `isOpenMap_reducedπ` and `isOpenEmbedding_domRestrict_reducedπ` (Findings, items 122, 123).

**V7.76 (Lemma 7.2.11; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.finite_reducedπ_preimage`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsReducedEvenlyCovered`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_preimage_reducedπ_subset_of_t2Space`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isReducedEvenlyCovered_of_t2Space`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isClosed_nonEffectivePart_of_isReducedEvenlyCovered`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isReducedEvenlyCovered_iff_t2Space`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_7_2_11`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.JumpingRetract.reducedπ_preimage_one`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.JumpingRetract.not_isReducedEvenlyCovered`).** The class $\pi^{-1}([\varphi_0])$ is finite. If
$T_R$ is Hausdorff, there are open $U(\varphi) \ni \varphi$ for the members $\varphi$ of the class of $\varphi_0$ and an open
$U([\varphi_0]) \ni [\varphi_0]$ such that (1) distinct $U(\varphi)$ have disjoint closures, (2) $\pi(U(\varphi)) =
U([\varphi_0])$ and $\pi$ is an open embedding on $U(\varphi)$, (3) $\pi^{-1}(U([\varphi_0]))$ is covered by the
$U(\varphi)$. Conversely, (1)–(3) at every unit force $\mathbf X^T$ closed; so (1)–(3) hold at every morphism iff $T_R$ is
Hausdorff, and they fail at $(1, o_0)$ for the ep-groupoid of V7.82. *Book:* Lemma 7.2.11, p. 315, new in the 2021 edition,
for every ep-groupoid. *Hidden hypotheses:* $T_R$ Hausdorff; the proof of (3) uses the uniqueness of limits in $T_R$.
*Deviation (explicit):* without the hypothesis the lemma does not hold as we read it; "homeomorphism onto $U([\varphi_0])$"
is read as (2) (Findings, item 124).

**V7.77 (Proposition 7.2.12; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_of_isOpenMap`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.exists_isCompact_preimage_reducedπ_subset`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_reducedMor`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_12`).** For every ep-groupoid, $(\mathbf X^R, T_R)$ is paracompact (every open
cover has a locally finite open refinement; Hausdorffness not included). *Book:* Proposition 7.2.12 and its footnote, p. 317,
new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none in the statement. *Proof:* not the text's,
which uses Lemma 7.2.11 (1)–(3) and so, as we read it, $T_R$ Hausdorff: paracompactness descends along an open continuous
surjection $p : M \to Q$ if every $q$ has a compact $K$ such that every open $N \supseteq K$ contains $p^{-1}(O)$ for an open
$O \ni q$; for $\pi$, $K$ is the set of $\varphi \in s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}\,V)$ with $(s, t)(\varphi) = (s, t)(q)$, by properness
(Findings, items 111, 125).

**V7.78 (Proposition 7.2.13 and Theorem 7.2.14; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_13`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_2_14`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedPolyfold`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedEpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEffective_reducedEpGroupoid`).** The natural charts
(`reducedAtlas`) define an M-polyfold structure on $(\mathbf X^R, T_R)$ — some Hausdorff paracompact M-polyfold structure on
$T_R$ with the natural atlas exists — iff $T_R$ is Hausdorff. If $T_R$ is Hausdorff, $(X, \mathbf X^R)$ is an ep-groupoid
`reducedEpGroupoid` with the groupoid structure of V7.40, the object M-polyfold of $X$, the natural atlas on $\mathbf X^R$, and
an ep-functor $X \to X_R$; it is effective (Proposition 7.2.16, V7.40). *Book:* Proposition 7.2.13, p. 318, new in the 2021
edition, and Theorem 7.2.14, p. 318 (2017: Proposition 7.10, p. 244). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):*
Proposition 7.2.13 is read as the existence of the structure. Theorem 7.2.14 assumes exactly the hypothesis that V7.39 and
V7.40 take, $T_R$ Hausdorff; paracompactness is supplied by V7.77 (gap G.71, changed) (Findings, items 56, 107, 111, 126,
143).

**V7.79 (Proposition 7.2.17; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedπ_eq_iff_comp_inv`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_nonEffectivePart_iff_reducedπ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.continuous_comp_fibredProduct`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.continuousOn_comp_inv`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isClosed_reducedπ_eq_of_isClosed`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isClosed_nonEffectivePart_of_t2Space`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_17`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isClosed_src_eq_tgt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.closure_nonEffectivePart_subset`).** $T_R$ is Hausdorff iff
the non-effective part $\mathbf X^T$ is closed in $\mathbf X$. Also $[\varphi] = [\psi]$ iff $t(\varphi) = t(\psi)$ and
$\psi^{-1} \circ \varphi \in \mathbf X^T$, and $\mathrm{cl}\,\mathbf X^T \subseteq \{s = t\}$. *Book:* Proposition 7.2.17, p. 320,
new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none. *Proof:* the relation $[\varphi] = [\psi]$ is
closed in $\mathbf X \times \mathbf X$ when $\mathbf X^T$ is closed, and a space is Hausdorff iff this relation is closed for
an open quotient map (Mathlib); properness is not used (Findings, item 127).

**V7.80 (Definition 7.2.18 (= Definition 7.4.1), Remarks 7.2.19 and 7.2.20; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.HasLUC`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsLUC`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLUC_iff_forall_naturalRep`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.hasLUC_of_isClosed`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_7_2_20`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.remark_7_2_19`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLUC_trivial`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLUC_of_isEffective`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isClosed_range_unit`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.nonEffectivePart_eq_range_unit_of_isEffective`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isLUC_trivialZ3`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isLUC_reflection`).** $X$ has the local unique continuation property (LUC) if every object $x$
has a natural representation $U(x)$ such that $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ on a nonempty open subset of $U(x)$ forces $\Phi(g) =
\mathrm{id}$ on $U(x)$. Under LUC every natural representation has this property, and there are such inside every open $O
\ni x$. Not every ep-groupoid has LUC (V7.82). LUC holds for the trivial ep-groupoid of every M-polyfold, for every effective
ep-groupoid ($\mathbf X^T$ is then the closed set of units), for $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$ by reflection, and for the
non-effective trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action on $\mathbb R$. *Book:* Definition 7.2.18, Remarks 7.2.19, 7.2.20, p. 321, new in
the 2021 edition; Definition 7.4.1, p. 328, repeats Definition 7.2.18. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* that
the choice of $U(x)$ does not matter is proved (by V7.81, $\mathbf X^T$ is then closed, and a connectedness argument)
(Findings, items 128, 144).

**V7.81 (Proposition 7.2.21, Theorem 7.2.22 and Proposition 7.2.23; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eventually_Φ_eq_of_Γ_mem`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_mem_of_eventually`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isClosed_nonEffectivePart_of_isLUC`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_21`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_2_22`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.t2Space_reducedMor_of_isLUC`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_23`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.nonEffectivePart_trivialZ3`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.t2Space_reducedMor_trivialZ3`).**
$X$ has LUC iff $\mathbf X^T$ is closed. Equivalent are: $T_R$ is Hausdorff; $X$ has LUC; $\mathbf X^T$ is closed in $\mathbf
X$. Under LUC, $T_R$ is Hausdorff and `reducedEpGroupoid` is an effective ep-groupoid with the structure of V7.78 and an
ep-functor $X \to X_R$. For the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action, $\mathbf X^T = \mathbf X$ and $T_R$ is Hausdorff. *Book:*
Proposition 7.2.21, p. 321, Theorem 7.2.22 and Proposition 7.2.23, p. 323, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none.
*Deviation (same):* none. *Proof:* $\Gamma(g, y) \in \mathbf X^T$ iff $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ near $y$; if $\mathbf X^T$ is
closed, the set of such $y$ is open and closed in the connected $U(x)$ (Findings, items 60, 128, 129).

**V7.82 (Appendix 7.6.3, Zhou's example; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.appendix_7_6_3`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.nonEffectivePart_eq`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.closure_nonEffectivePart_diff`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.not_t2Space_reducedMor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.not_isLUC`,

A morphism of level $1$ in $\mathbf X^T$ lies in $(\mathbf X^1)^T$ ((7.24)), and under LUC for $X^1$, $(\mathbf X^1)^T =

and $[\varphi]_1 \mapsto [\varphi]$ on morphisms, is an sc-diffeomorphism and an isomorphism of ep-groupoids; under (SLUC),

text's identifications, and "the identity on objects" is stated for $i = 1$, since for variable $i$ the object types are not
definitionally equal; the case $i$ uses LUC for $X^{i-1}$ and $X^i$ (gap G.82 closed) (Findings, item 131).

**V7.86 (the Part I facts used in §7.4; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.DenseSmooth`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SmoothConnected`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.DenseSmoothTangent`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.TangentDeterminedSmooth`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.TangentDeterminedSmooth.eq_self`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.DenseSmooth.dense`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.DenseSmooth.subset_closure_inter`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.DenseSmooth.exists_smooth`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.eqOn_tangentFiber_of_mem_closure`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SmoothRegular`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.smoothRegular_of_subsingleton`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.smoothRegular_discrete_unit`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.denseSmoothTangent_discrete_unit`).** For an M-polyfold $X$: `DenseSmooth`, $X_\infty$ is dense in every
$X_m$; `SmoothConnected`, $U \cap X_\infty$ is connected in $X_\infty$ for connected open $U$; `DenseSmoothTangent`,
$(T_xX)_\infty$ is dense in $T_xX$ for smooth $x$; `TangentDeterminedSmooth`, two sc-smooth maps agreeing near a smooth $y$ in
$X_\infty$ have the same tangent on $T_yX$. `SmoothRegular` bundles the first, the second, the last and the openness of $p :
TX \to X^1$. Consequences: $X_\infty$ is dense in $X$, and, if $p$ is open, a map continuous on an open $W \subseteq TX$ and the
identity over a set $A \subseteq X_\infty$ is the identity over its closure in $X_\infty$. All hold for M-polyfolds on a
subsingleton with every point smooth. *Book:* used in the proofs of Lemma 7.4.6, Propositions 7.4.8, 7.4.10, 7.4.22 and Lemma
7.4.15, pp. 331–340; the density of $X_\infty$ is stated on p. 289. *Hidden hypotheses:* these Part I facts, not proved in Part
I for M-polyfolds. *Deviation (explicit):* explicit hypotheses of the §7.4 results that use them (gaps G.85, G.73, G.8)
(Findings, item 134).

**V7.87 (the tangent $Tg$ of an isotropy element; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eventually_Φ_eq_Γ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isoΓ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isoΓ_val`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isoΓ_mem_trivialSubgroup_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.tangentMor_Γ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.tangentMor_eq_tΦ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.tΦ_eq_tΦ`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.tangentMor_isoΓ`).** The tangent $T\varphi = Tt \circ (Ts|T_\varphi\mathbf X)^{-1}$ of
Definition 7.1.4 (defined without charts) of the morphism $\Gamma(g, y)$ is the tangent map $T\Phi(g)$ on $T_yX$; in particular
$Tg = T\Phi(g)$ on $T_xX$, the same for every natural representation. For a fixed point $z$ of $\Phi(g)$, $\Gamma(g, z) \in
G_z$, it lies in $T_z$ iff $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ near $z$, and it acts near $z$ as $g$ does. *Book:* p. 331 ("the
linearization $Tg$") and Proposition 8.1.16's "by definition $Tg = T\hat g(x)$", new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:*
none. *Deviation (restated):* $Tg$ is a set map on the fibre $T_xX$; no linear structure is used, since (ZHOU) only asks
that $Tg$ be the identity (gap G.7 not needed) (Findings, item 135).

is an sc-diffeomorphism of $U(x)$ onto $\beta(U(x))$ with $\beta(x) = x$ and $|\beta(y)| = |y|$, then $\beta(U(x)) = U(x)$;

g\}$ and connectedness, instead of paths (Findings, item 138).

points: on the open dense union of the $X_\infty$-interiors of the sets $\{\beta = \hat g\}$, two pieces whose closures meet
have equal tangents at a common smooth point, hence equal $\hat g$ (Findings, item 138).

admissible triples $(y, V, \theta)$ to admissible triples, with a class independent of the chosen $W$. For an index-preserving
local homeomorphism $f$, $[y, V, \theta] \mapsto [f(y), f(V), f(\theta)]$ is a well defined map $bf$ of the tame boundaries,
continuous, open and a local homeomorphism; preimages of compact sets under $B$ are compact. An sc-diffeomorphism between open
sets preserves the degeneracy index. *Book:* §7.6.5.2, pp. 353–355, new in the 2021 edition, where the maps (7.25)–(7.28)
are defined through sc-diffeomorphisms of sheets. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (extra):* a tool of the formalization:
the topological content of those sc-diffeomorphisms (Findings, item 140).

ep-groupoid, $\mathbf X$ is tame. On the tame boundaries $bX$, $b\mathbf X$: $s([\varphi, \mathbf V, \theta]) = [s(\varphi),

\mathbf V^{-1}, \theta^{-1}]$; $u([x, V, \theta]) = [1_x, \mathbf V, \bar\theta]$ with $\bar\theta$ the preimage of $\theta$
under $s|\mathbf V$; and $m(a, b)$ is the unique class over $\psi \circ \varphi$ with source $s(b)$, which is the printed
$[\psi \circ \varphi, \mathbf W\,{}_s{\circ}_t\,\mathbf V, \sigma\,{}_s{\circ}_t\,\theta]$. With these maps $(bX, b\mathbf X)$ is a
groupoid and $B$ a functor $(bX, b\mathbf X) \to (X, \mathbf X)$. *Book:* (7.25)–(7.29), pp. 354–355, new in the 2021 edition.
*Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the sc-diffeomorphisms of the sheets enter through their topological
content (V7.96); (7.28) is read through $u$, an index-preserving homeomorphism onto the open set $u(X)$; off composable pairs
$m$ takes a junk value (Findings, item 140).

**V7.99 (sc-smooth maps of tame boundaries; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScSmoothOn_of_bMap`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_bLift`,
`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isLiftOf_bLift_sheet`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeo_bLift`).** Let $A$, $B$ be tame M-polyfolds with
the tame M-polyfold structures of Part I's Theorem 2.7.13 (2) on $bA$, $bB$ (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold`), and
$f : A \to B$ sc-smooth on an open $U$. A map $g : bA \to bB$, continuous on an open $O \subseteq B^{-1}(U)$ with $B \circ g = f
\circ B$ on $O$, is sc-smooth on $O$; in the charts $p \mapsto \pi(\varphi(B p))$ of $bA$ and $bB$ it reads $\pi' \circ (\varphi' \circ
f \circ \varphi^{-1}) \circ \iota$. Hence the lift $bf$, $[y, V, \theta] \mapsto [f(y), f(V), f(\theta)]$ (V7.96), of an sc-smooth
index-preserving local homeomorphism is sc-smooth, and the lift of a local sc-diffeomorphism is a local sc-diffeomorphism: over a
sheet $f : W \to V$ with inverse $\sigma$, $bf$ maps $B^{-1}(W)$ onto $B^{-1}(V)$, with an inverse that covers $\sigma$ and
undoes $bf$. *Book:* §7.6.5.2, p. 355, new in the 2021 edition: the proof sketch of Theorem 7.6.9, which reads the structure
maps in the charts $\Phi$ as sc-diffeomorphisms $s : \theta \to s(\theta)$ of faces. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation
(extra):* a tool of the formalization; it replaces the sketch's sc-diffeomorphism of faces by the computation in the charts of
$bA$, which needs only that $f$ is sc-smooth (Findings, item 146).

**V7.100 (Theorem 7.6.9 (2), (3), (5): the boundary ep-groupoid, and $B$ an ep-functor; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_bObj`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_bMor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.bPObj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.bPMor`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_bSrc`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_bTgt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_bUnit`,

`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isTame_boundaryEpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryEpFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.phiTot_bSrc`).**
For a tame ep-groupoid $(X, \mathbf X)$, give $bX$ and $b\mathbf X$ the tame M-polyfold structures of Theorem 2.7.13 (2) for the
object and the morphism M-polyfold ($\mathbf X$ is tame, V7.97); both are paracompact. Then $s, t : b\mathbf X \to bX$ of (7.25)
are local sc-diffeomorphisms, $u$ of (7.28) and $\iota$ of (7.27) are sc-smooth, and $m$ of (7.29) is sc-smooth on $b\mathbf
X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,b\mathbf X$; with the properness of V7.98, $(bX, b\mathbf X)$ is an ep-groupoid (Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3)),
the boundary ep-groupoid, and it is tame. Both maps $B$ form an ep-functor $(bX, b\mathbf X) \to (X, \mathbf X)$, a morphism of
the category $\mathcal{EP}$ (Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7)). For a representative $(\varphi, \mathbf V, \theta)$ with $\mathbf V$ in a
sheet of $s$, $s$ maps $U(\varphi, \mathbf V, \theta)$ into $U(x, s(\mathbf V), s(\theta))$ and $\Phi_{(x, s(\mathbf V), s(\theta))} \circ
s = s \circ \Phi_{(\varphi, \mathbf V, \theta)}$ there. *Book:* Theorem 7.6.9 (2), (3), (5), p. 355, new in the 2021 edition, whose
verification is left to the reader, and the diagram of its proof sketch. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the
text asks $B$ to be sc-smooth; it is also a functor (V7.97), so an ep-functor. Condition (4) of Definition 7.1.3, the
sc-smoothness of $m$, is proved in the sheet form of V7.3: near $b$, $b' \mapsto m(\sigma(t b'), b')$ covers $\gamma \mapsto
m(\sigma_1(t\gamma), \gamma)$ for a sheet $\sigma_1$ of $s$ on $\mathbf X$, and V7.99 applies (Findings, items 145, 146).

$(X, \mathbf X)$ (V7.97), so V7.99 applies; tameness is that of Theorem 2.7.13 (2).

`Polyfold.EP.proposition_7_4_18`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.levelConnected_pointEP`,
`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.proposition_7_4_18_pointEP`).** The sets $O \cap X_\infty$, $O$ open in some $X_{N+1}$, form
a neighbourhood basis of $X_\infty$. A natural representation $U(x)$ of $x \in X_1$ with $U(x) \cap X_1$ connected in $X^1$
restricts to a natural representation of $x$ in $X^1$, the isotropy groups of $x$ in $X$ and in $X^1$ being identified; if
every $U(x) \cap X_m$ is connected in $X_m$, so it is for the restriction. Under LUC for $X^{N+1}$, if $\hat g = \mathrm{id}$ on
the smooth points of a nonempty open subset of $U(x) \cap X_{N+1}$, then $\hat g = \mathrm{id}$ on $U(x)$. Hence, if $X_\infty$ is
dense in every $X_m$ and every smooth $x$ has a natural representation with every $U(x) \cap X_m$ connected, (SLUC) implies
(VSLUC); with `SmoothConnected` for every $X^i$ as well, (VSLUC) and (SLUC) are equivalent. Both hold for the point
ep-groupoid, which satisfies the hypotheses. *Book:* Proposition 7.4.18, p. 336, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden
hypotheses:* the density of $X_\infty$ (gap G.73); the natural representations with every $U(x) \cap X_m$ connected, which the
proof takes "by construction" and which are a hypothesis here (gap G.85). *Deviation (explicit):* LUC for $X^N$ is applied to
the restriction of $U(x)$ to $X^N$, built one level at a time; the direction (VSLUC) ⇒ (SLUC) is V7.103 (Findings, item 150).
*Proof:* the text's: an open subset of $V(x) = U(x) \cap X_\infty$ contains $W' \cap X_\infty$ for a nonempty open $W'$ of
some $X_N$, $\hat g = \mathrm{id}$ on $W'$ by density and continuity, and LUC for $X^N$ on the restricted $U(x)$ gives $\hat g
= \mathrm{id}$ on $U(x)$.
