## 10. Chapter 9 (HWZ, Part II, §§9.1–9.5 and §9.6.1 (2017 §§9.1–9.5)): verified for §§9.1–9.4 and §9.6.1 with the readings and hypotheses recorded below, unconditionally for ep-groupoids whose object M-polyfold is $\mathbb R^m$, except the global part of Proposition 9.1.11, Lemma 9.4.3 and, in Figure 9.1, the orientations of the faces of the faces; for §9.5 the sets of measure zero, the σ-algebras and the isotropy factors are verified, branched integration of sc-forms over sheets covered by countably many graph charts, with "oriented, tame" read as a covering by oriented tame structures, the boundary measures and Stokes' theorem as printed for every $n \ge 1$, and Remark 9.5.20 in part (its M-polyfold, the $\mathbb Z_3$-action and the effective isotropy of the boundary points)

Chapter 9 (pp. 401–458 (2017 pp. 291–332); numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021), with the 2017 text's in parentheses) treats branched ep⁺-subgroupoids, the objects that carry the solution sets of perturbed sc-Fredholm problems with symmetries. §9.1 defines them as functors $\Theta : X \to \mathbb Q^+$ that are locally weighted sums of indicator functions of properly embedded finite-dimensional submanifolds (Definition 9.1.2 (2017: 9.1)), proves that $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is locally closed (Lemma 9.1.5 (2017: 9.1)), constructs symmetric local branching structures (Lemma 9.1.7 (2017: 9.2)), defines closed, compact, manifold- and orbifold-type $\Theta$ (Definitions 9.1.6, 9.1.8 (2017: 9.2, 9.3)), and decomposes $\Theta$ by dimension (Propositions 9.1.11 (2017: 9.2) and 9.1.12, the latter new in the 2021 edition). §9.2 introduces the category $\mathrm{Gr}(X)$ of formal sums of tangent spaces and the tangent section $T_\Theta$ (Theorem 9.2.1 (2017: 9.1)), good and bad points (Definitions 9.2.2, 9.2.6, Lemmas 9.2.3–9.2.7 (2017: 9.4, 9.5, 9.3–9.5)), the graph representation near a bad point (Proposition 9.2.8, Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11 (2017: 9.3, 9.6–9.8)), the tangent $T\Theta$ (Definition 9.2.12 (2017: 9.6)), the position of a submanifold relative to $\partial X$ (Lemma 9.2.13, Remark 9.2.14 (2017: 9.9, 9.5)) and the boundary $\partial\Theta$ (Proposition 9.2.15, Definition 9.2.16, Remark 9.2.17 (2017: 9.4, 9.7, 9.6)). §9.3 defines orientations (the category $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$, Definition 9.3.2 (2017: 9.8), Remark 9.3.3, Lemma 9.3.4, Example 9.3.5 (2017: 9.8, 9.10, 9.1)), tame $\Theta$ (Definition 9.3.6 (2017: 9.10), Lemma 9.3.7, new) and boundary orientations ((9.11), Definition 9.3.8, Proposition 9.3.9, Definition 9.3.10 (2017: 9.9, —, 9.11)). §9.4 studies the geometry of local branching structures: essential points, sets of measure zero and the decomposition of an oriented structure (Definitions 9.4.1, 9.4.5, 9.4.7, Lemmas 9.4.2–9.4.8, Propositions 9.4.9, 9.4.10 (2017: Definitions 9.12–9.14, Lemmas 9.11–9.15, Propositions 9.5, 9.6)). §9.5 integrates sc-differential forms over branched ep⁺-subgroupoids and proves Stokes' theorem; verified here are its measure-theoretic part (Definitions 9.5.1, 9.5.3, 9.5.14, Lemma 9.5.2 (2017: Definitions 9.15–9.17, Lemma 9.16)) and the isotropy and set parts of Lemmas 9.5.9–9.5.11 and Proposition 9.5.13 (2017: Lemmas 9.18, 9.19; Lemma 9.5.10 and Proposition 9.5.13 new in the 2021 edition), not the integrals. Appendix §9.6.1 (new in the 2021 edition) proves Proposition 9.1.12 (Lemmas 9.6.1, 9.6.2, 9.6.4, Definition 9.6.3, Proposition 9.6.5); §§9.6.2–9.6.3 discuss open questions and have no formal content.

What is verified. Every definition of §§9.1–9.4, of the measure-theoretic part of §9.5 and of §9.6.1 is formalized: Definitions 9.1.2 (V9.1), 9.1.6 (V9.6), 9.1.8 (V9.8), 9.2.2 (V9.15), 9.2.6 (V9.19), 9.2.12 (V9.23), 9.2.16 (V9.27), 9.3.2 (V9.30), 9.3.6 (V9.34), 9.3.8 (V9.36), 9.3.10 (V9.38), 9.4.1 (V9.39), 9.4.5 (V9.43), 9.4.7 (V9.45), 9.5.1 (V9.49), 9.5.3 (V9.51), 9.5.14 (V9.52) and 9.6.3 (V9.60), with Property (T) (V9.41). **Theorem 9.2.1 (2017: 9.1) holds** for every branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of an ep-groupoid whose object M-polyfold is $\mathbb R^m$, and in general under the graph-chart hypotheses below (V9.13, V9.14); so do Propositions 9.1.12, 9.2.15, 9.3.9, 9.4.9, 9.4.10 and 9.6.5 in the forms stated below, Lemmas 9.1.5, 9.1.7, 9.2.3, 9.2.5, 9.2.7, 9.2.13 (read at points of $\partial X$), 9.3.4 (for $n$-dimensional $\Theta$), 9.3.7, 9.4.2, 9.4.4 (for sheets of one dimension), 9.4.6, 9.4.8, 9.6.1, 9.6.2 and 9.6.4, Remarks 9.1.3 (b), 9.2.4, 9.2.14, 9.2.17 and 9.3.3, and Example 9.3.5 with the corrections recorded in V9.33. In §9.5, Lemma 9.5.2 (2017: 9.16) is verified for structures with sheets of one class (V9.50), the remark after Definition 9.5.3 as the completion by null sets (V9.51), and the parts of Lemmas 9.5.9–9.5.11 and Proposition 9.5.13 that do not involve integrals: the orders of the isotropy groups, (9.23) and the decompositions of the preimages (V9.54–V9.57). Several places of the text needed more than a reading. (a) *Proposition 9.1.11 (2017: 9.2).* The uniqueness of the dimensional decomposition, as stated, does not hold as we read it: on the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^2$ the indicator of the $x$-axis has two decompositions (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.not_proposition_9_1_11_rn`); the local construction is verified, the global gluing is not formalized (V9.9). (b) *Lemma 9.2.13 (2017: 9.9).* As printed, (2) ⇒ (1) does not hold as we read it at interior points (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.not_lemma_9_2_13_two_one`); the lemma is verified for $x \in M \cap \partial X$, the case the text uses, together with $d_M(x) = 0 \Leftrightarrow T_xM \subseteq T^R_xX$ at every $x \in M$ (V9.24). (c) *Definition 9.2.16 (2017: 9.7).* (1) and (2) do not characterize $\partial\Theta$ uniquely as we read them (the zero functor satisfies them; `Polyfold.not_unique_isBoundaryCharacterized_halfLine`); uniqueness holds among functors vanishing off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ (V9.27). (d) *Lemma 9.3.4 (2017: 9.10)* does not hold as we read it without equidimensionality (`Polyfold.lemma_9_3_4_mixed_dim_rn`); it is verified for $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ (V9.32). (e) *Example 9.3.5 (2017: 9.1).* The two orientations also coincide on $\{x < 0\}$, and there are exactly six orientations with weights $1$ (four for each of the two structures, two shared), not four; all orientations form an infinite rational family (`Polyfold.example_9_3_5_classification`) (V9.33). (f) *Lemma 9.4.4 (2017: 9.13)* does not hold as we read it for sheets of different dimensions (`Polyfold.lemma_9_4_4_mixed_dim`) (V9.42), and neither does *Lemma 9.5.2 (2017: 9.16)*: two sheets of different dimensions do not induce the same null sets on their overlap (`Polyfold.isNull_transfer_mixed_dim`) (V9.50). (g) *Omitted steps.* The step of Lemma 9.6.4 "similarly as good points" and the independence of the formula on p. 457 from the structure (V9.61, V9.62), the step "the image is $M$ near $0$" in the converse of Lemma 9.2.13 (V9.24), and the facts on the $TM_i$ needed for Definition 9.2.12 (V9.23) are proved or, where Part I lacks the tools, made explicit hypotheses. (h) *Other routes.* The "measure zero" arguments of Lemmas 9.6.1 and 9.6.2 are replaced by a topological covering lemma (V9.58, V9.59); cones in Proposition 9.2.8 are replaced by rays and slices (V9.22); Proposition 9.4.10 is proved without Property (T) (V9.48). Not verified: the global part of Proposition 9.1.11, Remark 9.1.4, Proposition 9.1.9 and Remark 9.1.10, Lemma 9.4.3, the identification $T_y\partial M = T^R_yM$ with the outward direction and the continuity of $o_{\partial M}$, the classification of all orientations in Example 9.3.5, and in §9.5 the forms, integrals and measures: Theorems 9.5.4, 9.5.5 and 9.5.15–9.5.18 with the measure identities of Lemmas 9.5.7, 9.5.9–9.5.11 and Proposition 9.5.13. An addendum (2026-11-12; Findings, items 114–118) verifies Remark 9.1.4 (V9.63, same), Proposition 9.1.9 with the text's groupoid $\bigsqcup M_x$ and the independence of the choices up to a generalized isomorphism (V9.64, restated) and Remark 9.1.10 for $n$-dimensional $\Theta$, without the composition of the orbifold groupoid in Mathlib's language (V9.65, narrower; gaps G.94, G.95 closed), the classification of all orientations in Example 9.3.5, infinitely many with six of integer weights (V9.33; gap G.101 closed), Lemmas 9.4.4, 9.4.6 and Definition 9.5.1, Lemma 9.5.2 for the sheets of every M-polyfold with null sets read in M-polyfold charts (V9.42, V9.44, V9.49, V9.50 explicit; gaps G.105, G.106 closed), and Theorems 9.5.4, 9.5.5, Lemmas 9.5.7, 9.5.9–9.5.11 and Proposition 9.5.13 (1) for an abstract integration of forms over the oriented sheets, which is not constructed (V9.54–V9.57, V9.66, narrower; gap G.107 in part); Theorems 9.5.15–9.5.18 are proved from their local inputs only (gaps G.108–G.110 in part). A second addendum (2026-11-13; Findings, item 119) constructs the integral of an sc-differential $n$-form over an oriented $n$-dimensional sheet, $n \ge 1$, in graph charts and over sheets covered by countably many of them, as such an integration, which contains the sheets of every oriented tame structure of a compact $n$-dimensional $\Theta$, and verifies with it Theorems 9.5.4, 9.5.5 as printed with "oriented, tame" read as a covering by oriented tame structures, derived when the M-polyfold has no boundary (V9.66, explicit; witness: the unit circle), Lemmas 9.5.9–9.5.11 (V9.54–V9.56, explicit), Proposition 9.5.13 (2) at the level of the integrals (V9.57, restated) and (9.22) as an identity of signed measures (V9.69, explicit; gap G.107 closed); the boundary null sets with the $(n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure (V9.52; gap G.108 closed); the stratum $\{d_M = 1\}$ as an oriented submanifold whose orientation is Part I's face orientation, and Figure 9.1 for face-structured sheets (V9.36, V9.38; gap G.103 closed); and Theorems 9.5.15, 9.5.16 (V9.67) and 9.5.17, 9.5.18 (V9.68) for $n \ge 2$ under an added class condition on the boundary sheets, satisfiable with $\partial S \ne \emptyset$ (the closed upper hemisphere), and open near the corners of the sheets (narrower; gaps G.109, G.110 in part). A third addendum (2026-11-13, wave K; Findings, item 120) verifies Theorems 9.5.15–9.5.18 as printed for every $n \ge 1$, with the text's hypotheses only: the class condition is derived for every oriented tame structure, near the corners of a sheet by an estimate in its corner charts and toward the frontier of $U(x)$ by comparing tangent spaces with other structures; for $n = 1$ the $0$-forms are integrated over the finitely many oriented boundary points (V9.67, V9.68, restated; gap G.109 closed). Witnesses with $\partial S \ne \emptyset$: the closed upper hemisphere ($n = 2$, also with LUC) and the closed half-circle ($n = 1$). Remark 9.5.20 is verified in part: the M-polyfold $X \subseteq \mathbb R \times \mathbb C$ with dimension jumps $0 \to 3 \to 0$, $\partial X = \{(\pm1, 0)\}$, $\mathbb Z_3 \ltimes X$ with LUC, and the effective isotropy of a boundary point, of order $3$ read in $X$ and $1$ read in $\partial X$; $\Theta$ and the integrals are not (gap G.110 in part, for the remark only).

The hypotheses. Part I has no level-0 sc-calculus inside partial quadrants and no linear structure on $T_xX$ (gap G.7), so four facts of the text's §9.2 are taken as hypotheses on a general M-polyfold, each proved for $\mathbb R^m$: the graph representation of the $M_i$ near a point (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasGraphChartAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasGraphChartsAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasGraphBallAt`; Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11), the local constancy of the dimension (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasLocallyConstantDimAt`; Remark 9.1.1), invariance of domain (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasDomainInvarianceAt`; Lemma 9.2.7 (2)) and the level-1 continuity of frame fields (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasContinuousLevelOneOn`; Lemma 9.3.4). Their witnesses are `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasGraphChartAt_rn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasGraphChartsAt_rn`, `Polyfold.hasGraphBallAt_rn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasLocallyConstantDimAt_rn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasDomainInvarianceAt_rn` and `Polyfold.hasContinuousLevelOneOn_rn`. On $\mathbb R^m$ the results that use them are proved without hypotheses: `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_2_7_2_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4_rn`. Definition 9.2.12 keeps, also on $\mathbb R^m$, the hypothesis that the $TM_i$ are smooth submanifolds of $TX$ (gap G.99).

The setting. Ep-groupoids, natural representations of the isotropy groups, the orbit space and paracompact orbit spaces are those of Chapter 7 (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.HasParacompactOrbitSpace`); the tangent ep-groupoid is Chapter 8's (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentEpGroupoid`). Smooth finite-dimensional submanifolds (images of sc⁺-retractions), the smooth set, the boundary and the degeneracy index are Part I's (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.smoothSet`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.boundary`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.degIndex`). A functor $\Theta : X \to \mathbb Q^+$ is a function on objects with $\Theta(s(\varphi)) = \Theta(t(\varphi))$ (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsFunctorial`), with values in $\mathbb Q$ and nonnegativity a separate condition. The tangent space $T_yM$ of a submanifold is a set of tangent vectors (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent`); linear algebra is done in charts (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartTangent`). Witnesses on $\mathbb R^m$ are ep-groupoids with object M-polyfold Part I's $\mathbb R^m$ (`Polyfold.rnPolyfold`), most often the trivial one (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.trivial`). Findings referred to below are those of `Exposition/Findings.md`, "Chapter 9".

**V9.1 (Definition 9.1.2 (2017: 9.1), branched ep⁺-subgroupoids; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsFunctorial`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.supp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orbitSupp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsBranchedEpSubgroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_zero`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.localBranchingStructure_indicator`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_indicator`, `Polyfold.rnPolyfold_isSmoothSubmanifold_singleton`).** A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid is a functor $\Theta \ge 0$ whose support lies in the smooth set, whose orbit support $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is paracompact, and which at every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ has a local branching structure: an open $U(x)$, finitely many smooth submanifolds $M_i \subseteq U(x)$ through $x$ with proper inclusions, weights $\sigma_i > 0$, and $\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ on $U(x)$. The zero functor and the indicator of a smooth point of $\mathbb R^n$ are examples. *Book:* Definition 9.1.2, p. 402 (2017: Definition 9.1, p. 292). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $\Theta$ takes values in $\mathbb Q$ with $\Theta \ge 0$ a field; "the topology induced on $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is paracompact" is a `ParacompactSpace` instance on the subtype; "the inclusion $M_i \to U(x)$ is proper" is `IsProperMap` of the inclusion. The 2017 text's "(ii) and (iii)" in (4) is "(2) and (3)" in 2021 (possible misprint, corrected) (Findings, item 1). *Update (2026-11-12):* by Remark 9.1.4 the paracompactness in (1) holds when $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is component compact (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_of_isComponentCompact`, V9.63; gap G.94 closed).

**V9.2 (Remark 9.1.1 (2017: 9.1) and the last paragraph of Definition 9.1.2, the dimension of a submanifold and $n$-dimensional $\Theta$; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasDimAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.finrank_tangentSpace_chart_change`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasDimAt.finrank_eq`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasDimAt.unique`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold.exists_hasDimAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasDimAt_inter_isOpen_iff`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasDimAt_image_iff`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsSubmanifoldOfDim`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.IsOfDim`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dim_unique`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsNDimensional`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isNDimensional_zero`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasLocallyConstantDimAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasLocallyConstantDimAt_rn`).** A submanifold has dimension $k$ at $a$ if the tangent space of its sub-retract at the chart image of $a$ has dimension $k$; the value does not depend on the data and the chart, is unique, exists at every point, and is invariant under restriction to open sets and under sc-diffeomorphisms. $\Theta$ is $n$-dimensional if at every point of its support some local branching structure has only $n$-dimensional $M_i$; the zero functor is $n$-dimensional for every $n$. The dimensions of the $M_i$ of one structure through $x$ are determined. *Book:* Remark 9.1.1, p. 402 (2017: Remark 9.1, p. 291); Definition 9.1.2, last paragraph and footnote, p. 402. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* the dimension is measured in a chart, since $T_aA$ carries no linear structure (gap G.7). The local constancy of $a \mapsto \dim T_aA$ is not proved in general; it is the hypothesis `HasLocallyConstantDimAt` where it is needed, proved on $\mathbb R^m$ from the trace of $Ds(y)$, and elsewhere the dimensions of the $M_i$ enter as labellings $\mathrm{dim} : I \to \mathbb N$. The footnote ($n$-dimensional $\Theta \ne 0$ is not $m$-dimensional, $m \ne n$) and "locally equidimensional" are not formalized (gap G.93) (Findings, items 2, 3).

**V9.3 (branched ep⁺-subgroupoids of ep-groupoids over $\mathbb R^n$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_orbitSupp_trivial_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.localBranchingStructure_sum_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_sum_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isNDimensional_sum_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.localBranchingStructure_indicator_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_indicator_rn`, `Polyfold.rnPolyfold_isSmoothSubmanifold_range`, `Polyfold.rnPolyfold_hasDimAt_range`, `Polyfold.graph2`, `Polyfold.rnPolyfold_isSubmanifoldOfDim_graph2`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.rnPolyfold_isSubmanifoldOfDim_singleton`).** On the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^n$, finite weighted sums of indicators of closed submanifolds through which the sum is taken, and indicators of locally closed submanifolds, are branched ep⁺-subgroupoids, $n$-dimensional when all submanifolds are. The image of a smooth idempotent $s$ of $\mathbb R^n$ is a closed smooth submanifold of dimension $\mathrm{rank}\,Ds(a)$; graphs of smooth $\beta : \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ in $\mathbb R^2$ are closed $1$-dimensional submanifolds; points are $0$-dimensional. *Book:* not in the book. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (extra):* witnesses for the hypotheses of the chapter (Findings, item 100).

**V9.4 (Remark 9.1.3 (b) (2017: 9.2 (b)), branching structures are not unique; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark913Hyp_expNegInvGlue`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.thetaGraphs`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.thetaGraphs_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.structureβ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.structureγ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.γ₂_pos`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.eq_add_of_thetaGraphs_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_9_1_3_b`).** For smooth $\beta_1, \beta_2 : \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ with the sign conditions of the text (satisfiable, from `expNegInvGlue`), $\Theta(p) = \#\{i \mid p \in \mathrm{graph}\,\beta_i\}$ is a $1$-dimensional branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^2$, equal to the one given by the graphs of $0$ and $\beta_1 + \beta_2$, and no submanifold of the one structure agrees with a submanifold of the other on any neighbourhood of the origin. *Book:* Remark 9.1.3 (b), p. 403 (2017: Remark 9.2 (b), p. 292). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the text gives $\gamma_2$ only by $\gamma_2(s) > 0$ for $s \ne 0$; describing the same $\Theta$ forces $\gamma_2 = \beta_1 + \beta_2$; "not unique, even close to $x$" is read as the last conjunct (Findings, item 4).

**V9.5 (Lemma 9.1.5 (2017: 9.1), $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is locally closed; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.preimage_π_orbitSupp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.mem_supp_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isClosed_preimage_val_supp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLocallyClosed_supp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_1_5`).** For a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\Theta$, $\pi^{-1}(|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|) = \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$, $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \cap U(x) = \bigcup_i M_i$ is closed in $U(x)$, $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ is locally closed in $X$ and $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is locally closed in $|X|$. *Book:* Lemma 9.1.5, p. 403 (2017: Lemma 9.1, p. 293). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the openness of $\pi$ (Chapter 7) replaces the text's neighbourhood with the properness property (Findings, item 5).

**V9.6 (Definition 9.1.6 (2017: 9.2), closed and compact $\Theta$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsClosedBranched`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsCompactBranched`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isCompactBranched_indicator`).** $\Theta$ is closed if $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is closed in $|X|$, compact if it is compact; the indicator of a point of $\mathbb R^n$ is compact. *Book:* Definition 9.1.6, p. 404 (2017: Definition 9.2, p. 293). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 7).

**V9.7 (the restriction of a local branching structure, and Lemma 9.1.7 (2017: 9.2), symmetric structures; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.restrict`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isClosed_M`, `Polyfold.isProperMap_inclusion_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.SymmetricBranchingStructure`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsFunctorial.apply_Φ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.symmetrize`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_1_7`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_1_7'`).** A local branching structure at $x$ restricts to every open $V \subseteq U(x)$ containing $x$. For a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid and $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ there is, inside every open $V \ni x$, a symmetric local branching structure: the domain of a natural representation $(\Phi, \Gamma)$ of $G_x$, a $G_x$-action on the index set with $\Phi(g)(M_i) = M_{g \cdot i}$ and $\sigma_{g\cdot i} = \sigma_i$, and $\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ there; it is obtained with $J = I \times G_x$, $M_{(i,g)} = \Phi(g)(M_i \cap U)$ and $\sigma_{(i,g)} = \sigma_i / |G_x|$. *Book:* the remark before Lemma 9.1.7, p. 404, and Lemma 9.1.7, p. 405 (2017: Lemma 9.2, p. 294). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the symmetric structure lies inside any given $V$. The restriction remark is formalized at $x$ itself, not at a point $x_0$ of $V(x_0) \subseteq U(x)$, where the $N_i$ may miss $x_0$ (reading). That $\Phi(g)(M_i \cap U)$ is a submanifold properly embedded in $U$ through $x$, used without statement in the text, is proved (Findings, items 5, 6).

**V9.8 (Definition 9.1.8 (2017: 9.3), manifold- and orbifold-type; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsOrbifoldType`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsManifoldType`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isManifoldType_indicator`).** $\Theta$ is of orbifold type if it takes only the values $0$ and $1$, of manifold type if moreover between two objects of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ there is at most one morphism; the indicator of a point of $\mathbb R^n$ is of manifold type. *Book:* Definition 9.1.8, p. 405 (2017: Definition 9.3, p. 294). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; Proposition 9.1.9 and Remark 9.1.10, which build on it, were not formalized (gap G.95) (Findings, item 7). *Update (2026-11-12):* Proposition 9.1.9 and Remark 9.1.10 are formalized (V9.64, V9.65; gap G.95 closed; Findings, item 114).

**V9.9 (Proposition 9.1.11 (2017: 9.2), the dimensional decomposition; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartStructure`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartStructure_isOfDim`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.eq_sum_dimPart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart_eq_zero`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart_eq_of_isOfDim`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.SymmetricBranchingStructure.dim_smul`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.SymmetricBranchingStructure.dimPart_Φ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsDimDecomposition`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsLocallyFiniteFamily`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Proposition_9_1_11`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.axis2`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.decompA`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.decompB`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.decompA_isDimDecomposition`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.decompB_isDimDecomposition`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.not_proposition_9_1_11_rn`).** For a local branching structure with dimension labelling, $\Theta_k(y) = \sum_{\dim M_i = k,\, y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ is represented on $U(x)$ by the $k$-dimensional structure $(M_i)_{\dim M_i = k}$, $\Theta = \sum_k \Theta_k$ on $U(x)$, and for a symmetric structure $G_x$ preserves dimension and $\Theta_k$ is $G_x$-invariant. The statement of the proposition, "a unique family $(\Theta_k)$ of branched ep⁺-subgroupoids, $\Theta_k$ $k$-dimensional, with $\Theta = \sum_k \Theta_k$ pointwise, and every such family locally finite", is `Proposition_9_1_11`; on the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^2$ it does not hold as we read it: for the indicator $\Theta$ of the $x$-axis $L$, both $\Theta_0 = 1_{\{0\}}$, $\Theta_1 = 1_{L \setminus \{0\}}$ and $\Theta_0 = 0$, $\Theta_1 = 1_L$ are such families. *Book:* Proposition 9.1.11, pp. 407–408 (2017: Proposition 9.2, p. 297). *Hidden hypotheses:* the dimension labellings of V9.2. *Deviation (narrower):* only the local construction is verified; the gluing of the local $\Theta_k$ into functors on $X$ (compatibility across morphisms, paracompactness of $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta_k)|$, local finiteness) and a uniqueness statement under an extra condition (for instance that each $\Theta_k$ be represented near every point by a subfamily of a local branching structure of $\Theta$) are not formalized (gap G.96) (Findings, item 8).

**V9.10 (Proposition 9.1.12, the decomposition does not depend on the structure; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.DimPartsAgreeNear`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.DimPartsAgreeNear.exists_naturalRep`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Proposition_9_1_12`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartsAgreeNear_of_isOfDim`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartsAgreeNear_of_topMultiplicity`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12_of_topMultiplicity`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartsAgreeNear_of_hasGraphChartAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12_of_hasGraphChartAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12_rn`, `Polyfold.proposition_9_1_12_rn_zero`, `Polyfold.proposition_9_1_12_rn_one`, `Polyfold.exists_mixed_rn_one`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.exists_mixed_rn_two`).** For two local branching structures of $\Theta$ at $x$ with dimension labellings there is an open $V \ni x$ in both domains on which their dimensional decompositions agree, and $V$ can be taken to be the domain of a natural representation of $G_x$. This holds for equidimensional structures without hypothesis, for every M-polyfold with `TopMultiplicity` in every dimension or with `HasGraphChartAt` at every point, and, without hypothesis, for every ep-groupoid whose object M-polyfold is $\mathbb R^m$. Structures with sheets of different dimensions exist on $\mathbb R^1$ and $\mathbb R^2$. *Book:* Proposition 9.1.12, p. 408, proof in §9.6.1, pp. 452–457, new in the 2021 edition (the 2017 proof of Proposition 9.2 calls the uniqueness obvious). *Hidden hypotheses:* the graph representation `HasGraphChartAt` (Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11) on a general M-polyfold. *Deviation (explicit):* "open, $G_x$-invariant, with the usual properties" is any open $V$ in both domains, shrunk to a natural representation by `exists_naturalRep`; the hypothesis is discharged on $\mathbb R^m$ (gap G.97 in general) (Findings, items 9, 90–93).

**V9.11 (the category $\mathrm{Gr}(X)$, p. 409; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentMor_unit_of_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentMor_injOn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentMor_eq_tangentMapOn_hat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Gr`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grPush`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grPush_mem`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grPush_comp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grPush_unit`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.GrObj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.SmoothCat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grProj`).** $\mathrm{Gr}(x)$ is the set of finite formal sums $\sum_L \sigma_L L$, $\sigma_L \in \mathbb Q$, of subsets $L$ of $T_xX$; a morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ of $X^\infty$ pushes them forward by the tangent $T\varphi$ of Chapter 7, functorially; the objects $(x, a)$, $a \in \mathrm{Gr}(x)$, and the pairs $(a, \varphi)$ form a category with the projection functor $\pi$ to the full subcategory $X^\infty$ of smooth objects. *Book:* §9.2, p. 409 (2017 pp. 297–298). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the generators are subsets of $T_xX$ rather than linear subspaces, since $T_xX$ carries no linear structure (gap G.7); in a chart the tangent spaces of submanifolds are linear subspaces (V9.12) (Findings, item 20).

**V9.12 (the tangent space $T_yM$ of a submanifold, set form and chart form; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.mem_submanifoldTangent_iff`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent_subset_tangentFiber`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent_inter_isOpen`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent_image`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartTangent`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartTangent_eq`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_submodule_chartTangent`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.finrank_chartTangent`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartTangent_chart_change`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_linearEquiv_chartTangent`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.exists_submodule_of_mem_support`).** $T_yM$ is the set of tangent vectors at $y$ fixed by the tangent of the sc⁺-retraction that presents $M$; it does not depend on the retraction, is local, and is carried by sc-diffeomorphisms. In a chart its image is a linear subspace of the dimension of $M$ at $y$, carried linearly by chart changes; the generators $T_xM_i$ of $T_\Theta(x)$ are linear subspaces in charts. *Book:* §9.2, the tangent spaces $T_xM_i$ before Theorem 9.2.1, p. 409 (2017 p. 298), with Part I's Remark 4.2.2 (preprint: 4.14). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* sets instead of subspaces (gap G.7) (Findings, item 20).

**V9.13 (Theorem 9.2.1 (2017: 9.1), the tangent section $T_\Theta$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.tangentSum`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.transport`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.tangentSum_transport`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.HasIndependentTangentSums`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentValue`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentValue_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grPush_tangentValue`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentSection`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_9_2_1`).** If the sums $\sum_i \sigma_i\, T_xM_i$ of any two local branching structures of $\Theta$ at $x$ agree (`HasIndependentTangentSums`), there is a functor $T_\Theta : X^\infty \to \mathrm{Gr}(X)$ with $\pi \circ T_\Theta = \mathrm{Id}$, $T_\Theta(x) = \sum_i \sigma_i\, T_xM_i$ for every local branching structure at $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$, $T_\Theta(x) = 0$ off the support, and $T_\Theta(\varphi) = (T_\Theta(s(\varphi)), \varphi)$. *Book:* Theorem 9.2.1, p. 409 (2017: Theorem 9.1, p. 298), proved on pp. 412–418 (2017 pp. 301–306). *Hidden hypotheses:* the independence, which the text proves through Proposition 9.2.8 (V9.14). *Deviation (explicit):* the functoriality on morphisms uses the transport of structures along $\hat\varphi$ and $\Theta \circ \hat\varphi = \Theta$ (Findings, items 21, 22).

**V9.14 (Theorem 9.2.1 (2017: 9.1), the independence of the local branching structure; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.tangentSum_eq_of_isGoodPoint`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_of_subset_goodSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_of_isOfDim`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_of_dimPartsAgreeNear`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_of_isOfDim_of_hasGraphChartsAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_of_hasGraphChartAt_of_hasLocallyConstantDimAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.tangentSum_structureβ_eq_structureγ`, `Polyfold.hasIndependentTangentSums_indicator`).** The sums are independent at good points without hypothesis; for equidimensional structures under the slice hypothesis `HasTangentSlicesAt`, which follows from `HasGraphChartsAt`; in general under `HasGraphChartAt` and `HasLocallyConstantDimAt` on the support; and for every $\Theta$ on an ep-groupoid whose object M-polyfold is $\mathbb R^m$, without hypothesis. In the example of Remark 9.1.3 (b) the two structures have the same tangent sum at the bad point $0$. *Book:* Theorem 9.2.1, p. 409 (2017: Theorem 9.1, p. 298), the proof on pp. 412–418 (2017 pp. 301–306). *Hidden hypotheses:* the graph representation and the local constancy of the dimension on a general M-polyfold. *Deviation (explicit):* the text reduces to the equidimensional case by Proposition 9.1.11; the formalization does the same through Proposition 9.1.12 (V9.10) with dimension labellings (gaps G.93, G.97) (Findings, items 21, 25, 100).

**V9.15 (Definition 9.2.2 (2017: 9.4), good points; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.MU`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.IsGoodPoint`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isGoodPoint_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.nbhdAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.eq_iff_of_mem_nbhdAt`).** $y \in M_U = \bigcup_i M_i$ is good for a local branching structure if near $y$ all $M_i$ through $y$ coincide; equivalently, $y \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ and $\Theta$ is constant on $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ near $y$. *Book:* Definition 9.2.2, p. 410 (2017: Definition 9.4, p. 299). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* stated for every $\Theta$ with a local branching structure, not only equidimensional ones; the intrinsic form is the argument of the proof of Lemma 9.2.3 (Findings, item 23).

**V9.16 (Lemma 9.2.3 (2017: 9.3), being good does not depend on the structure; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.lemma_9_2_3`).** If $y$ lies in the domains of two local branching structures of $\Theta$, at possibly different points, and is good for one, it is good for the other. *Book:* Lemma 9.2.3, p. 410 (2017: Lemma 9.3, p. 299). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* any two structures whose domains contain $y$, any $\Theta$; in the proof $Q(z)$ is presumably $Q(y)$ (possible misprint) (Findings, item 23).

**V9.17 (Remark 9.2.4 (2017: 9.4); `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_9_2_4_a`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_goodSet_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_9_2_4_b`).** (a) A point good for some structure is good for every structure whose domain contains it. (b) Near a good point $y$, $\Theta = \Theta(y) \cdot 1_M$ for one submanifold $M$ properly embedded in an open $V \ni y$. *Book:* Remark 9.2.4, p. 411 (2017: Remark 9.4, p. 300). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* (b) with $M = M_i \cap V(y)$ for any $i$ with $y \in M_i$ (Findings, item 23).

**V9.18 (Lemma 9.2.5 (2017: 9.4), good points are preserved by morphisms; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Sheet.apply_hat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.src_mem_goodSet_of_tgt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_2_5`).** For every morphism $\varphi$, $s(\varphi)$ is good iff $t(\varphi)$ is. *Book:* Lemma 9.2.5, p. 411 (2017: Lemma 9.4, p. 300). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* for every branched ep⁺-subgroupoid, not only equidimensional ones; the transport of structures is replaced by $\Theta \circ \hat\varphi = \Theta$ on the sheet of $\varphi$ (Findings, item 23).

**V9.20 (Lemma 9.2.7 (1) (2017: 9.5 (1)), the good set is open and dense; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_2_7_1`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.dense_goodSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isNowhereDense_badSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_2_7_1_dense`).** In $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ the good set is open and dense and the bad set is closed and nowhere dense. *Book:* Lemma 9.2.7 (1), p. 412 (2017: Lemma 9.5 (1), p. 300). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* for every branched ep⁺-subgroupoid, without equidimensionality and without (2), from a topological covering argument (Findings, item 24).

**V9.21 (Lemma 9.2.7 (2) (2017: 9.5 (2)), good points accumulate on every sheet; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasDomainInvarianceAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasDomainInvarianceAt_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_2_7_2`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_2_7_2_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.zero_mem_badSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.exists_seq_goodSet_structureβ`).** For an $n$-dimensional local branching structure at $x$ and every $i$ there is a sequence of good points in $M_i$ converging to $x$, under invariance of domain for $n$-dimensional submanifolds on $U(x)$, which holds on $\mathbb R^m$; on $\mathbb R^m$ the statement has no hypothesis. In Remark 9.1.3 (b) the origin is bad and is approached by good points of the graph of $\beta_1$. *Book:* Lemma 9.2.7 (2), p. 412 (2017: Lemma 9.5 (2), p. 301). *Hidden hypotheses:* invariance of domain (`HasDomainInvarianceAt`) on a general M-polyfold. *Deviation (explicit):* the statement holds at every $x$, not only at bad points (gap G.98) (Findings, item 24).

**V9.22 (Proposition 9.2.8 and Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11 (2017: Proposition 9.3, Lemmas 9.6–9.8), the graph representation and tangent slices; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasTangentSlicesAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsGraphChartAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasGraphChartsAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasTangentSlicesAt_of_hasGraphChartsAt`, `Polyfold.exists_mem_graph_of_hasStrictFDerivAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isGraphChartAt_rn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasGraphChartsAt_rn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasTangentSlicesAt_rn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasGraphChartAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasGraphChartAt_rn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_slice_of_isGraphChartAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_generic_slice`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsGraphBallAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasGraphBallAt`, `Polyfold.hasGraphBallAt_rn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasOrientedGoodPointsAt_of_hasGraphBallAt`).** If near $x$ every $n$-dimensional submanifold through $x$ is, in one chart, a graph over a ray (or ball) in its tangent space (`IsGraphChartAt`, `HasGraphChartAt` for all dimensions at once, `HasGraphBallAt`), then for every class $\Xi$ of sheets with one tangent space $L$ at $x$ and every neighbourhood $W$ of $x$ there is a finite slice of points in $W$ meeting each $M_i$, $i \in \Xi$, once and missing the other $M_i$, so that $\sum_{i \in \Xi} \sigma_i = \sum_{y \in F} \Theta(y)$ (`HasTangentSlicesAt`), and the slice can be chosen generic.
