**V9.23 (Definition 9.2.12 (2017: 9.6), the tangent $T\Theta$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentSubmanifold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentTheta`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentTheta_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.sum_tangent_eq_sum_tangent`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentTheta_nonneg`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isFunctorial_tangentTheta`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.TangentBranchingHyp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isClosed_tangentSubmanifold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_orbitSupp_tangentTheta`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentBranchingHyp_of_isSmoothSubmanifold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta_of_isSmoothSubmanifold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isSubMPolyfold_tangentSubmanifold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangentBranchingHyp_zero`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta_zero`).** Under the independence of V9.13, $T\Theta(h) = \sum_{h \in TM_i} \sigma_i$ for $h$ over $U(x)$, and $0$ over the complement of the support, is well defined, nonnegative and a functor on the tangent ep-groupoid; it is a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of $TX$ if the $TM_i$ are smooth submanifolds of $TX$ (closedness and the paracompactness of $|\mathrm{supp}(T\Theta)|$ for paracompact $|X|$ are proved), and on $\mathbb R^m$ the $TM_i$ are sub-M-polyfolds of $TX$, retracts of $Ts$. *Book:* Definition 9.2.12, p. 418 (2017: Definition 9.6, p. 306). *Hidden hypotheses:* that the $TM_i$ are smooth submanifolds of $TX$ (the tangent of the sc⁺-retraction is sc⁺ on $TX$), and the paracompactness of $|X|$, neither discussed in the text. *Deviation (explicit):* $h \in TM_i$ is read as $h \in T_{p(h)}M_i$; only the zero functor is a witness of the full hypothesis (gap G.99) (Findings, item 26). *Update (2026-11-12):* our Proposition 9.1.9 does not use the paracompactness of $|X|$ (V9.64).

**V9.24 (Lemma 9.2.13 (2017: 9.9), $d_M(x) = 0$ and reduced tangent position; `Polyfold.IsReducedTangentAt`, `Polyfold.isReducedTangentAt_iff_subset_reduced`, `Polyfold.isReducedTangentAt_iff_subset_partialCone`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.subDegIndex`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.subDegIndex_le`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsTangentReducedAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isReducedTangentAt_chart_change`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isTangentReducedAt_iff_forall`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_9_2_13_chart`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_9_2_13`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_9_2_13_two_one`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_9_2_13_iff`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.subDegIndex_eq_zero_iff`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.IsScPlus.exists_injOn_proj`, `Polyfold.ScRetraction.IsScPlus.exists_flat`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.not_lemma_9_2_13_two_one`).** For a smooth submanifold $M$ and $x \in M \cap \partial X$: $d_M(x) = 0$ iff $T_xM \subseteq T^R_xX$ (in every chart, the chart image of $T_xM$ lies in the reduced tangent space). For every $x \in M$: $d_M(x) = 0$ iff $T_xM \subseteq T^R_xX$. As printed, with "$x \in \partial X$" in (1), (2) ⇒ (1) does not hold as we read it at a point $p$ of $\mathbb R^n$, which satisfies (2) and lies off $\partial\mathbb R^n$. *Book:* Lemma 9.2.13, p. 419 (2017: Lemma 9.9, p. 307). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* read with $x \in M \cap \partial X$ as the standing assumption, which is where the text uses it, and proved at every $x \in M$ in the form `subDegIndex_eq_zero_iff`. The converse needs a chart of $M$ without boundary near $x$: by the inverse function theorem on $T_xM$ and the step that the projection is injective on $M$ near $x$ ("the image is $M$ near $0$"), which the text does not spell out; the text's complement $Y$ and map $F$ are not needed (Findings, items 40, 41).

**V9.25 (Remark 9.2.14 (2017: 9.5), $\partial M$; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_9_2_14`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_9_2_14_mem_boundary`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.mem_boundary_subPolyfold_iff`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_9_2_14_not_isTangentReducedAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_9_2_14_iff`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.remark_9_2_14_not_mem_boundary_iff`).** $x \in \partial M$ iff $x \in \partial X$ and $T_xM \not\subseteq T^R_xX$; in particular $\partial M \subseteq \partial X$, and $d_M(x) \ge 1$ at such points. *Book:* Remark 9.2.14, p. 419 (2017: Remark 9.5, p. 307). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $\partial M$ is the boundary of the induced M-polyfold structure; the text's "not contained in $C_xX$" is equivalent to the reduced-tangent form (`isReducedTangentAt_iff_subset_partialQuadrant`) (Findings, item 42).

**V9.26 (Proposition 9.2.15 (2017: 9.4), the boundary weights; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.submanifoldBoundary`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.mem_submanifoldBoundary_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryPart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryTheta`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryTheta_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_2_15_1`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_2_15_2`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isFunctorial_boundaryTheta`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_2_15_3`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.filter_tangentValue_eq`).** (1) Under the independence of V9.13, $\sum_{y \in \partial M_i} \sigma_i$ is the same for any two local branching structures whose domains contain $y$. (2) At $y$ with $d_X(y) = 0$ this sum and the corresponding formal sum of tangent spaces vanish, for every structure. (3) $\partial\Theta$, the part of $T_\Theta(y)$ on tangent spaces not contained in $T^R_yX$, is a functor, nonnegative, supported in $\partial X$, and equal to $\sum_{y \in \partial M_i} \sigma_i$ on every structure. *Book:* Proposition 9.2.15, p. 420 (2017: Proposition 9.4, p. 308). *Hidden hypotheses:* the independence of Theorem 9.2.1 for (1) and (3). *Deviation (explicit):* (1) and (2) need neither $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \cap \partial X$ nor that $\Theta$ be branched, and (2) needs no independence (Findings, item 43).

**V9.27 (Definition 9.2.16 (2017: 9.7), the boundary $\partial\Theta$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsBoundaryCharacterized`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBoundaryCharacterized_boundaryTheta`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBoundaryCharacterized_zero`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.eq_boundaryTheta`, `Polyfold.not_unique_isBoundaryCharacterized_halfLine`).** $\partial\Theta$ satisfies the text's (1) $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta) \subseteq \partial X$ and (2) the local formula at points of $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$; a functor that vanishes off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ and satisfies (2) at the points of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ equals $\partial\Theta$. As stated, (1) and (2) do not characterize $\partial\Theta$ uniquely as we read them: the zero functor satisfies them for every $\Theta$, and for $\Theta = 1$ on $[0, \infty)$ both $0$ and $\partial\Theta \ne 0$ do. *Book:* Definition 9.2.16, p. 421 (2017: Definition 9.7, p. 309). *Hidden hypotheses:* the independence of Theorem 9.2.1. *Deviation (narrower):* "uniquely characterized" is verified with (2) asked on $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$. "In view of Proposition 9.2.13" before the definition (2017: "Proposition 9.9") is presumably Proposition 9.2.15, and "branched ep⁺-groupoid" is "ep⁺-subgroupoid" (possible misprints) (Findings, items 44, 45). *Update (2026-11-12):* read as "the solution of (1), (2) with the largest support", the characterization is unique: among the functions $F \ge 0$ vanishing off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ with (1) and (2), $\partial\Theta$ is the one with the largest support (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.definition_9_2_16_existsUnique`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsBoundaryCharacterized.eq_boundaryTheta_iff`), and every such $F$ equals $\partial\Theta$ on $U(x)$ for $x \in \mathrm{supp}(F)$ (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsBoundaryCharacterized.eq_boundaryTheta_on`); the independence of Theorem 9.2.1 is a theorem, so there is no hidden hypothesis (Findings, item 44).

**V9.28 (Remark 9.2.17 (2017: 9.6); `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryTheta_le`, `Polyfold.boundaryTheta_halfLineCorner`, `Polyfold.boundaryTheta_halfLine_one`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryTheta_indicator_of_mem`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_one`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryTheta_one`).** $\partial\Theta \le \Theta$; $\partial\Theta$ is in general not the restriction of $\Theta$ to $\partial X$: for the indicator of the corner $0$ of $[0, \infty)$, $\Theta(0) = 1$ and $\partial\Theta(0) = 0$, while for $\Theta = 1$ on $[0, \infty)$, $\partial\Theta(0) = 1$. *Book:* Remark 9.2.17, p. 421 (2017: Remark 9.6, p. 310). *Hidden hypotheses:* the independence of Theorem 9.2.1, which the witnesses satisfy. *Deviation (restated):* the forward reference "In Section 9.5, Definition 9.3.6" is to §9.3 (possible misprint, also in 2017) (Findings, items 45, 46).

**V9.29 (the category $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ and oriented tangent spaces, p. 422; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartVec`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.OrTangent`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.chartFrames`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsChartOrientation`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsOrientedAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsOrientedAt.isChartOrientation`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isOrientedAt_iff_forall`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_two_orientations`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.OrTangent.push`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsOrientedAt.push_tangentMapOn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isOrientedAt_push_tangentMor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.GrHat`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grHatPush`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.GrHatObj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grHatProj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grForget`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grForgetFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.grForgetFunctor_comp_grProj`).** An oriented tangent space at $y$ is a subset $L \subseteq T_yX$ with a set of positive frames, oriented in a chart and then in every chart; every finite-dimensional tangent space has exactly two orientations; morphisms push oriented tangent spaces forward. $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ is the category of formal sums of oriented tangent spaces over $X^\infty$, with the forgetful functor to $\mathrm{Gr}(X)$ over $X^\infty$. *Book:* §9.3, p. 422 (2017 p. 310), with Remark 9.3.1 (2017: 9.7), which is historical. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* frames instead of orientations of vector spaces (gap G.7) (Findings, item 50).

**V9.30 (Definition 9.3.2 (2017: 9.8), orientations of $\Theta$; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure.orientedSum`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure.grForget_orientedSum`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsOrientation`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsOrientable`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsOrientation.mk'`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orientedSection`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orientedSection_comp_grHatProj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orientedSection_comp_grForgetFunctor_obj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isOrientation_zero`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isOrientation_sum_rn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isOrientation_sum_trivial_rn`).** An orientation of $\Theta$ is a natural assignment $\hat T_\Theta$ of formal sums of oriented tangent spaces at smooth points, lifting $T_\Theta$, which near every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ is $\sum_i \sigma_i\, T_y(M_i, o_i)$ for an oriented local branching structure (continuous orientations $o_i$ of the $M_i$); it defines a section functor of $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ over $X^\infty$. The zero functor and finite sums of oriented closed submanifolds of $\mathbb R^n$ are oriented. *Book:* Definition 9.3.2, p. 423 (2017: Definition 9.8, p. 311). *Hidden hypotheses:* the lift condition uses $T_\Theta$, hence the independence of Theorem 9.2.1, discharged on $\mathbb R^m$. *Deviation (restated):* the continuity of $o_i$ is the local constancy of the chart frames (Findings, item 51).

**V9.31 (Remark 9.3.3 (2017: 9.8), orientations are not unique; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_9_3_3`).** The indicator of a point of $\mathbb R^n$ has infinitely many orientations, pairwise distinct, $T_q$ for $q \in (0, 1) \cap \mathbb Q$. *Book:* Remark 9.3.3, p. 423 (2017: Remark 9.8, p. 311). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* infinitely many, not only more than one (Findings, item 52).

**V9.32 (Lemma 9.3.4 (2017: 9.10), orientations are determined by good points; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsOrientationOfDim`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasOrientedGoodPointsAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4`, `Polyfold.hasOrientedGoodPointsAt_rn_zero`, `Polyfold.hasOrientedGoodPointsAt_rn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasContinuousLevelOneOn`, `Polyfold.hasContinuousLevelOneOn_rn`, `Polyfold.frameDet`, `Polyfold.orientation_eq_iff_frameDet`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation.exists_isOpen_tangent_eq_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4_of_hasGraphBallAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4_rn`, `Polyfold.mixedTheta`, `Polyfold.lemma_9_3_4_mixed_dim`, `Polyfold.lemma_9_3_4_mixed_dim_rn`).** Two orientations of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ that agree at the good points agree at every smooth point, under `HasOrientedGoodPointsAt` on the support, which follows from the ball graph representation `HasGraphBallAt` and the level-1 continuity `HasContinuousLevelOneOn`; on $\mathbb R^m$ without hypothesis. Without equidimensionality the lemma does not hold as we read it: for $\Theta = 1_{\mathbb R \times 0} + 1_{(0,0)}$ on $\mathbb R^2$ two orientations agree at all good points and differ at the origin. *Book:* Lemma 9.3.4, p. 423 (2017: Lemma 9.10, p. 311). *Hidden hypotheses:* $n$-dimensional $\Theta$; on a general M-polyfold the graph representation and the continuity of frame fields on level 1. *Deviation (narrower):* the proof compares the two structures on one family of slices, applying Proposition 9.2.8 to both families together, and compares frames of different sheets by level-1 continuity; the text takes the good-point sequences from the first structure only, a step that needs an argument it does not give (gaps G.97, G.100) (Findings, item 53). *Update (2026-11-12):* for an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ the lemma holds for any two orientations, with no hypothesis that they are $n$-dimensional: every orientation of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ has $n$-dimensional local representations (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsOrientation.isOrientationOfDim`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4_of_isNDimensional`), since every local branching structure of $\Theta$ has $n$-dimensional sheets (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isOfDim_of_isNDimensional`).

**V9.33 (Example 9.3.5 (2017: 9.1); `Polyfold.betaPP`, `Polyfold.betaMM`, `Polyfold.betaPM`, `Polyfold.betaMP`, `Polyfold.example935Theta`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5_count`, `Polyfold.example935Theta_isBranched`, `Polyfold.exampleT1`, `Polyfold.exampleT2`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5_rn`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5_eq_origin`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5_ne_of_pos`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5_cannot_coincide`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5_eq_of_neg`, `Polyfold.orientedLift1_injective`, `Polyfold.exampleT2_ne_orientedLift1`, `Polyfold.exists_goodSet_exampleT1_ne_exampleT2`).** For $\beta^{++} = e(s) + e(-s)$ ($e$ = `expNegInvGlue`), $\beta^{--} = -\beta^{++}$ and the two mixed functions, the graphs define a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\Theta$ of the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^2$ by two structures; the orientations $\hat T^1$, $\hat T^2$ given by $\pm(1, \beta')$ coincide at the origin, differ at $(s, \beta^{++}(s))$ for $s > 0$, and no sign choice for the second structure reproduces $\hat T^1$ near the origin. They also coincide wherever $x < 0$, and the four sign choices of the first structure give four different orientations, none equal to $\hat T^2$. *Book:* Example 9.3.5, p. 425 (2017: Example 9.1, p. 313). *Hidden hypotheses:* none on $\mathbb R^2$. *Deviation (narrower):* "otherwise different" and "four different possibilities" do not hold as we read them (at least five orientations with weights $1$); the classification of all orientations of $\Theta$ is not formalized (gap G.101) (Findings, item 54). *Update (2026-11-12):* the orientations of $\Theta$ are classified (`Polyfold.example_9_3_5_classification`; gap G.101 closed): coefficients $a(s, b) \in [0,1] \cap \mathbb Q$ on the four open arcs, constant along each, with $a(+,\uparrow) + a(+,\downarrow) = a(-,\uparrow) + a(-,\downarrow) = A$ and weights $A$, $2 - A$ on $\pm(1,0)$ at the origin. There are infinitely many (`Polyfold.example_9_3_5_infinite`); the sign choices on the two structures give exactly six (`Polyfold.ncard_signOrientations`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5_six`), and these are the orientations with integer weights (`Polyfold.example_9_3_5_integral`, `Polyfold.example_9_3_5_integral_ncard`). "Four different possibilities" holds for each structure; for $\Theta$ it does not hold as we read it, so the row stays narrower (Findings, items 54, 115).

**V9.34 (Definition 9.3.6 (2017: 9.10), tame $\Theta$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.TameBranchingStructure`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsTameBranched`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isTameBranched_zero`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isTameBranched_indicator`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasTameInducedStructure_of_degIndex_eq_zero`).** $\Theta$ is tame if at every point of its support there is a local branching structure on a domain with the natural $G_x$-action and the properness property all of whose $M_i$ have a tame induced structure; the zero functor and the indicator of a point of $\mathbb R^n$ are tame. *Book:* Definition 9.3.6, p. 425 (2017: Definition 9.10, p. 314). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "an equivalent tame structure" is Part I's tame induced structure (Definition 2.5.18); the consequence "in particular every $M_i$ is a manifold with boundary with corners" is not formalized (gap G.102) (Findings, item 55).

**V9.35 (Lemma 9.3.7, equal tangent spaces have equal degeneracy; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.subDegIndex_eq_quotDim_of_hasTameInducedStructure`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.subDegIndex_eq_of_tangentSpace_eq`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_9_3_7`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.subDegIndex_eq_of_submanifoldTangent_eq`).** For submanifolds $M_1$, $M_2$ with tame induced structures and $y \in M_1 \cap M_2$, $T_yM_1 = T_yM_2$ implies $d_{M_1}(y) = d_{M_2}(y)$. *Book:* Lemma 9.3.7, p. 426, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* neither "$Y$ tame" nor "of the same dimension" is needed; in the proof "$T_0O \cap C = T^R_0O$" is read through the linearity of the chart image of $T_0M$ (Findings, item 56).

**V9.36 (Definition 9.3.8 (2017: 9.9), the boundary orientation of an oriented $M$; `Polyfold.exists_basis_orientation_iff_det_pos`, `Polyfold.exists_boundary_orientation`, `Polyfold.det_cons_smul_add`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.boundaryFrames`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isOrientedAt_boundaryFrames`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.boundaryFrames_eq`, `Polyfold.exists_boundaryFrames_graph`).** For an oriented $(M, o)$, a hyperplane $K$ of $T_yM$ and $e \notin K$, the frames $(a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1})$ of $K$ with $(e, a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1})$ positive orient $K$, and the orientation is unchanged under $e \mapsto ce + k$, $c > 0$, $k \in K$; both orientations occur. *Book:* Definition 9.3.8, p. 427 (2017: Definition 9.9, p. 313). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (explicit since 2026-11-13; narrower before):* $T_y\partial M$ and the outward vector enter as data $K$, $e$; that $T_y\partial M = T^R_yM$ and the outward half-space are determined by $M$ (through the cones $C_yM$) is not formalized (gap G.103) (Findings, item 57). *Update (2026-11-12):* for a tame sheet the stratum $\{d_M = 1\}$ is open and dense in $\partial M$ (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_isOpen_boundaryStratum_eq`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.submanifoldBoundary_subset_closure_boundaryStratum`); it is not built as a submanifold of its own (gap G.103 in part; Findings, item 110). *Update (2026-11-13):* for a tame sheet the stratum $\{d_M = 1\}$ is a smooth $(n-1)$-dimensional submanifold of $X$ with tangent spaces $T^R_yM$ (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isSubmanifoldOfDim_stratumOne`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent_stratumOne`), oriented by $o_{\partial M}$ in the sense of Definition 9.3.3 (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation.stratumOrientation`); in corner coordinates the convention is "outward normal first" (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.incFrame_mem_boundaryFramesAt_iff`), and for a face-structured sheet Part I's face orientation is $o_{\partial M}$ at the points with $d_M = 1$ (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.faceOrientation_eq_iff_mem_stratumOrientation`). The outward direction is read as "in $T_yM$, not in $C_yM$" in a presented chart (gap G.103 closed; Findings, items 110, 119).

**V9.37 ((9.11) and Proposition 9.3.9, the boundary orientation does not depend on the structure; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasSubDegree`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation.hasSubDegree_tangent_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.degreePart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.degreePart_orientedSum`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.eq_9_11`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_3_9`).** For two oriented local branching structures with tame $M_i$ and the same oriented sum at $y$, the parts of degree $\ell = d_{M_i}(y)$ agree for every $\ell$ (9.11); hence (9.12) gives the same value for every structure, and vanishes at smooth points off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$. *Book:* (9.11), p. 427, and Proposition 9.3.9, p. 428, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* the boundary operation $T_y(M, o) \mapsto T_y(\partial M, o_{\partial M})$ is a function `bd` of the oriented tangent space, which is what "the discussion preceding it" provides, given G.103 (Findings, item 58).

**V9.38 (Definition 9.3.10 (2017: 9.11), the oriented boundary $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryLift`).** $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}(y) = 0$ off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ and $\sum_{d_{M_i}(y) = 1} \sigma_i\, T_y(\partial M_i, o_{\partial M_i})$ on a structure (9.12). *Book:* Definition 9.3.10, p. 428 (2017: Definition 9.11, p. 314, with (9.12) numbered (9.11) there). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated since 2026-11-09; narrower before):* with `bd` as in V9.37; the continuity of $o_{\partial M}$ along $\partial M$ and its extension to the faces (Figure 9.1) are not formalized (gap G.103); Remark 9.3.11 has no formal content (Findings, item 58). *Update (2026-11-12):* the closed faces with their orientations exist in the corner-chart reading for face-structured sheets; their identification with $o_{\partial M}$ is not formalized (gap G.103 in part). Remark 9.3.11 is a comment, with nothing to formalize. *Update (2026-11-13):* for a face-structured tame sheet, read as a manifold with corners, the orientation of the open face $\{d_{M_i} = 1\}$ extends to exactly one continuous orientation of the closed face, Part I's `faceOrientation` (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.figure_9_1_existsUnique_faceOrientation`, through `Polyfold.MPolyfold.faceOrientation_eq_iff_mem_stratumOrientation` and `Polyfold.MPolyfold.dense_faceStratum`). The orientations of the faces of the faces are not formalized (gap G.103 closed; Findings, items 110, 119).

**V9.39 (Definition 9.4.1 (2017: 9.12), the relative tangent space and essential points; `Polyfold.chartImage`, `Polyfold.relTangent`, `Polyfold.span_tangentConeAt_chartImage_eq_map`, `Polyfold.relTangent_eq_map`, `Polyfold.relTangent_eq_top_iff`, `Polyfold.essentialSet`, `Polyfold.essentialSet_eq`, `Polyfold.crossLines`, `Polyfold.essentialSet_crossLines`, `Polyfold.nonEssential_crossLines`).** For a subset $K$ of a finite-dimensional manifold with corners, $T^K_zM$ is the span of the limits of unit directions $\varphi(z_k)/|\varphi(z_k)|$, $z_k \to z$ in $K \setminus \{z\}$, in a chart centred at $z$, independent of the chart; $z \in K$ is essential if it is a limit of $z_k \in K$ with $T^K_{z_k}M = T_{z_k}M$. For two crossing lines in $\mathbb R^2$ the essential set is $\{0\}$. *Book:* Definition 9.4.1, p. 429 (2017: Definition 9.12, p. 315). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* on Mathlib manifolds with corners, the span of Mathlib's tangent cone in a chart (Findings, item 70). *Update (2026-11-12):* in M-polyfold charts the condition $T^K_zM = T_zM$ is independent of the chart (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isRelTangentFull_of_chart`): chart changes are differentiable along a finite-dimensional submanifold for the level-$0$ norms (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_hasFDerivWithinAt_transition`; Findings, item 116).

**V9.40 (Lemma 9.4.2 (2017: 9.11), the essential set is closed; `Polyfold.lemma_9_4_2`, `Polyfold.lemma_9_4_2_open`).** $K^e$ is closed in $K$ and $K \setminus K^e$ is open in $K$. *Book:* Lemma 9.4.2, p. 430 (2017: Lemma 9.11, p. 315). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 70).

**V9.41 (Property (T) (2017 p. 316); `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure.PropertyT`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.OrTangent.eq_or_eq_or_eq_of_isOrientedAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.exists_ne_isOrientedAt`, `Polyfold.propertyT_example935B1`).** An oriented local branching structure has Property (T) on $V$ if, whenever two sheets have the same tangent space at a point of $V$ and their orientations there are related by $\varepsilon$, they are related by $\varepsilon$ at every point of $V$ where their tangent spaces agree; the first structure of Example 9.3.5 has it. *Book:* Property (T), p. 430 (2017 p. 316). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* Lemma 9.4.3, that (T) holds after shrinking $U(x)$, is not formalized (gap G.104) (Findings, item 71).

**V9.42 (Lemma 9.4.4 (2017: 9.13), essential in $M_i$ iff essential in $M_{i'}$; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry`, `Polyfold.graphSheets`, `Polyfold.graphSheetGeometry`, `Polyfold.lemma_9_4_4_mixed_dim`).** For sheets of one dimension the essential points of $K(i, i') = M_i \cap M_{i'}$ do not depend on the reference sheet; this is the field `ess_comm` of a sheet geometry, which exists for smooth graphs in $\mathbb R^2$. For sheets of different dimensions the lemma does not hold as we read it: $\mathbb R \times 0$ is essential in itself as a subset of $\mathbb R$ and has no essential point as a subset of $\mathbb R^2$. *Book:* Lemma 9.4.4, p. 431 (2017: Lemma 9.13, p. 317). *Hidden hypotheses:* sheets of one dimension. *Deviation (narrower):* for M-polyfold sheets, which carry no Mathlib manifold structure, Lemmas 9.4.4 and 9.4.6 are the fields of `SheetGeometry` (gap G.105); the note in Definition 9.4.7 ($i \sim_y i'$ implies $T_yM_i = T_yM_{i'}$) is its field `submanifoldTangent_eq` (Findings, item 72). *Update (2026-11-12):* for the sheets of every M-polyfold, read in M-polyfold charts, Lemmas 9.4.4 and 9.4.6 are theorems and `SheetGeometry` is built with no hypothesis (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_9_4_4_chart`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_9_4_6_chart`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.sheetGeometry`); every local branching structure of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ has $n$-dimensional sheets, so the lemma holds for them (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.lemma_9_4_4_of_isNDimensional`; gap G.105 closed). The verdict stays narrower for sheets of different dimensions (Findings, items 72, 113, 116).

**V9.43 (Definition 9.4.5 (2017: 9.13), sets of measure zero; `Polyfold.IsMeasureZero`, `Polyfold.isMeasureZero_iUnion`, `Polyfold.isMeasureZero_of_forall_mem`, `Polyfold.not_isMeasureZero_univ`).** $K \subseteq M$ has measure zero if its image in every chart has Lebesgue measure zero; measure zero is monotone and closed under countable unions, can be checked on a cover by charts, and $\mathbb R^2$ itself does not have it. *Book:* Definition 9.4.5, p. 431 (2017: Definition 9.13, p. 317). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* for Mathlib manifolds with corners (Findings, item 70). *Update (2026-11-12):* for submanifolds of an M-polyfold the null sets are `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsHNull` (the $n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the chart image, for the level-$0$ norm, is $0$), checked in one chart near each point (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isHNull_of_forall_exists_chart`) and equal to Lebesgue measure zero in the smooth charts of a tame sheet (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isHNull_iff_isMeasureZero_sheet`; Findings, item 116).

**V9.44 (Lemma 9.4.6 (2017: 9.14), non-essential points form a null set; `Polyfold.unitDirections`, `Polyfold.span_unitDirections`, `Polyfold.exists_pos_measure_cone_lt`, `Polyfold.addHaar_setOf_span_tangentConeAt_ne_top`, `Polyfold.isMeasureZero_setOf_relTangent_ne_top`, `Polyfold.lemma_9_4_6`).** For every subset $K$ of a finite-dimensional manifold, $K \setminus K^e$ has measure zero, by a Lebesgue density argument at points where the relative tangent space is not everything. *Book:* Lemma 9.4.6, p. 431 (2017: Lemma 9.14, p. 317). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* any $K$, not only $K(i, i')$; for M-polyfold sheets it is the field `isNull_diff_ess` of `SheetGeometry` (gap G.105) (Findings, items 70, 72). *Update (2026-11-12):* for every subset $K$ of an $n$-dimensional submanifold of an M-polyfold, $K \setminus K^e$ is null (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.lemma_9_4_6_chart`; gap G.105 closed).

**V9.45 (Definition 9.4.7 (2017: 9.14), $y$-equivalence; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.IsLink`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.YEquiv`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.equivalence_yEquiv`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.ySetoid`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.submanifoldTangent_eq_of_yEquiv`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.numClasses`).** $i \sim_y i'$ if a chain of sheets through $y$ links them with $y$ essential in each consecutive intersection; it is an equivalence relation on $I_y$, $y$-equivalent sheets have the same tangent space at $y$, and $\#P_y$ is the number of classes. *Book:* Definition 9.4.7, p. 432 (2017: Definition 9.14, p. 318). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* none (Findings, item 72).

**V9.46 (Lemma 9.4.8 (2017: 9.15), points with two classes form a null set; `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.IsNullIn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.lemma_9_4_8`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.MStar`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.isNullIn_diff_MStar`).** $\{y \in M_U \mid \#P_y \ge 2\}$ is null in the sheets, and $M_U \setminus M^*_U$ is null. *Book:* Lemma 9.4.8, p. 432 (2017: Lemma 9.15, p. 318). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "measure zero" in $M_U$ is null in every sheet through the point; the last step of the proof uses $K(i, j)^{ne}$ inside $M_i$, while $K(j, j')^{ne}$ is null only in $M_j$ and $M_{j'}$ (reading) (Findings, item 73). *Update (2026-11-12):* for an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ the sheet geometry is `Polyfold.MPolyfold.sheetGeometry n` (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_4_8_of_isNDimensional`).

**V9.47 (Proposition 9.4.9 (2017: 9.5), the decomposition of $M^*_U$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.tangentValue_eq_sum`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.MStarPart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_4_9`).** For an oriented local branching structure with Property (T), the independence of Theorem 9.2.1 and sheets in a sheet geometry: $M_U \setminus M^*_U$ is null, $M^*_U$ is the disjoint union of the $M^J_U = \{y \in M^*_U \mid I_y = J\}$, and on $M^J_U$: $\Theta = \sigma_J$, $T_\Theta = \sigma_J\, T^J$, $\hat T_\Theta = a_J (T^J, o^a_J) + b_J (T^J, o^b_J)$ with $a_J + b_J = \sigma_J$ and $o^a_J = -o^b_J$. *Book:* Proposition 9.4.9, p. 434 (2017: Proposition 9.5, p. 319). *Hidden hypotheses:* the independence of Theorem 9.2.1; the sheet geometry. *Deviation (explicit):* the footnote's "Lemma 9.5.2" is a forward reference (Findings, items 72, 74). *Update (2026-11-12):* for an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ the sheet geometry is `Polyfold.MPolyfold.sheetGeometry n` and the independence is a theorem; Property (T) remains (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_4_9_of_isNDimensional`).

**V9.48 (Proposition 9.4.10 (2017: 9.6), comparing two oriented structures; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_4_10`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tangent_eq_iff_of_mem_ess`, `Polyfold.example935B1`, `Polyfold.example935B2`, `Polyfold.example935_two_le_numClasses`, `Polyfold.example935_hypotheses_9_4_10`, `Polyfold.example935_MU_eq`).** For two oriented local branching structures on the same $U(x)$ with (a) the same weights and (b) the same oriented sums at every point, $M_U = M'_U$ and there are $M^\dagger_U \subseteq M_U$ with null complement in both families and a finite partition $A_1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup A_\ell$ of $M^\dagger_U$ with (2)–(5) of the text. The two structures of Example 9.3.5 satisfy (a) and (b), and the origin has two classes. *Book:* Proposition 9.4.10, p. 435 (2017: Proposition 9.6, p. 321). *Hidden hypotheses:* the sheet geometry. *Deviation (stronger):* Property (T) is not needed (Findings, item 74). *Update (2026-11-12):* for an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ there is no sheet-geometry hypothesis (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_9_4_10_of_isNDimensional`).

**V9.49 (Definition 9.5.1 (2017: 9.15), sets of measure zero in $S = |\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$; `Polyfold.SheetNullSets`, `Polyfold.SheetNullSets.isNull_union`, `Polyfold.SheetNullSets.isNull_iUnion_countable`, `Polyfold.SheetNullSets.isNull_of_cover`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetMeasureGeometry`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.SheetMeasureGeometry.toSheetNullSets`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.HasNullPreimages`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.hasNullPreimages_iff_isNullIn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.HasTameSheetsIn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroSupp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroSuppAny`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroSuppAll`).** For a system of null sets in the sheets of a class $\mathcal S$ of submanifolds (a σ-ideal in every sheet, local, the same on the overlap of two sheets of $\mathcal S$, a nonempty sheet not null in itself), $A \subseteq |X|$ has measure zero if at every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ some tame local branching structure (Definition 9.3.6) with sheets in $\mathcal S$ has preimages $M_i \cap \pi^{-1}(A)$ null in $M_i$; the variants ask this of some local branching structure, or of every structure with sheets in $\mathcal S$. A `SheetMeasureGeometry` is a §9.4 sheet geometry whose null sets are such a system. *Book:* Definition 9.5.1, p. 437 (2017: Definition 9.15, p. 322). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "measure zero in $M_i$" is the abstract system `SheetNullSets`, satisfiable by Lebesgue null sets of graphs in $\mathbb R^2$ and of open subsets of $\mathbb R^2$ (V9.53); "a suitable $U(x)$" is a tame structure; compactness and orientation of $\Theta$ are not used (gap G.106) (Findings, item 80). *Update (2026-11-12):* with the null sets `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsHNull` of the sheets of a general M-polyfold, Definition 9.5.1 is `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroH`, and the abstract system is instantiated by `Polyfold.MPolyfold.sheetNullSets` (gap G.106 closed; Findings, items 80, 116).

**V9.50 (Lemma 9.5.2 (2017: 9.16), measure zero does not depend on the choice; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isMeasureZeroSuppAll_of_any`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isMeasureZeroSuppAny_of_isMeasureZeroSupp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_5_2`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isSigmaIdeal_isMeasureZeroSupp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isSigmaIdeal_isMeasureZeroSuppAll`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.not_isMeasureZeroSuppAny_orbitSupp`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.not_isMeasureZeroSupp_orbitSupp`, `Polyfold.isNull_transfer_mixed_dim`).** If every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ has a tame local branching structure with sheets in $\mathcal S$, then "null preimages for a choice of tame structures", "for a choice of structures" and "for every structure with sheets in $\mathcal S$" agree; the sets of measure zero form a σ-ideal, and $S \ne \emptyset$ does not have measure zero. The axis $\mathbb R \times 0$ is null in the sheet $\mathbb R^2$ and not null in itself. *Book:* Lemma 9.5.2, p. 437 (2017: Lemma 9.16, p. 322), cited from the literature without proof. *Hidden hypotheses:* the sheets of all structures compared lie in one class $\mathcal S$ on which two sheets induce the same null sets on their overlap. *Deviation (explicit since 2026-11-12; narrower before):* this transfer property holds for sheets of one dimension and does not hold across dimensions (`Polyfold.isNull_transfer_mixed_dim`), so the lemma is proved for structures with sheets in one class, as for the $n$-dimensional structures of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$; for every structure of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ it would need Proposition 9.1.12 in general (gaps G.97, G.106) (Findings, item 81). *Update (2026-11-12):* for an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ (the standing assumption of §9.5) every local branching structure has $n$-dimensional sheets, and with the null sets `IsHNull` the lemma holds as stated: if at every point some local branching structure has null preimages of $A$, then every local branching structure has (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_5_2_of_isNDimensional`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lemma_9_5_2_tame`). The verdict is explicit: the one hidden hypothesis is the standing one; across dimensions the transfer still does not hold (`Polyfold.isHNull_mixed_dim`) (gap G.106 closed; Findings, items 81, 116).

**V9.51 (Definition 9.5.3 (2017: 9.16) and the remark after it, the σ-algebra $L(S)$; `Polyfold.borelNullSigma`, `Polyfold.IsSigmaIdeal`, `Polyfold.borel_le_borelNullSigma`, `Polyfold.measurableSet_borelNullSigma_of_mem`, `Polyfold.borelNullCompletion`, `Polyfold.measurableSet_borelNullSigma_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.measureZeroSets`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lebesgueSigma`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isSigmaIdeal_measureZeroSets`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_9_5_3`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.measurableSet_lebesgueSigma_of_isMeasureZeroSupp`).** $L(S)$ is the smallest σ-algebra on the subspace $S$ containing the Borel sets and the subsets of measure zero; for a σ-ideal $\mathcal N$ the σ-algebra generated by the Borel sets and $\mathcal N$ is $\{A \mid A \,\Delta\, B \in \mathcal N$ for a Borel $B\}$, so, under the standing assumption of V9.50, $K \in L(S)$ iff $K \,\Delta\, B$ has measure zero for some Borel $B$. *Book:* Definition 9.5.3 and the remark after it, p. 438 (2017: Definition 9.16, p. 323). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the remark that $L(S)$ is obtained by adding the sets of measure zero is read as the completion $K \,\Delta\, B$ null; the form $B \cup N$ would need Borel null hulls (Findings, item 82). *Update (2026-11-12):* with the null sets `IsHNull`: `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lebesgueSigmaH`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.remark_9_5_3_H`, equal to the earlier σ-algebra for tame $\Theta$ (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lebesgueSigmaH_eq`).

**V9.52 (Definition 9.5.14 (2017: 9.17) and measure zero in $\partial S$, p. 448; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroBoundary`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroBoundaryAll`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isMeasureZeroBoundaryAll_of`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.boundaryMeasureZeroSets`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lebesgueSigmaBoundary`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orbitSupp_boundaryTheta_subset`).** For a second null-set system on a class of boundaries $\partial M_i$, $K \subseteq |X|$ has measure zero in $\partial S = |\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)|$ if at every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$ a tame structure has boundary preimages $\partial M_i \cap \pi^{-1}(K)$ null in $\partial M_i$; then every structure with boundaries in the class has; $\partial S \subseteq S$; $L(\partial S)$ is the σ-algebra generated by the Borel sets of $\partial S$ and these sets. *Book:* p. 448 and Definition 9.5.14, p. 448 (2017: Definition 9.17, p. 327). *Hidden hypotheses:* the independence of Theorem 9.2.1 (through which $\partial\Theta$ is defined). *Deviation (explicit):* $(n-1)$-dimensional measure zero in $\partial M_i$ is an abstract system; its description face by face is not formalized, and no witness with $\partial S \ne \emptyset$ is given (gap G.108) (Findings, item 83). *Update (2026-11-12):* face by face, for face-structured tame sheets (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsFaceNull`, a proper σ-ideal), and as a system for $n = 1$ (`Polyfold.SheetNullSets.point`), with the witness $\Theta = 1$ on $[0, \infty)$, $\partial S \ne \emptyset$ (V9.53); for $n \ge 2$ on a general M-polyfold the boundary null sets are not built (gap G.108 in part; Findings, items 83, 117). *Update (2026-11-13):* the $(n-1)$-dimensional null sets of the boundaries are the Hausdorff null sets in the ambient charts (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsHNull`), a null-set system on the boundaries of tame sheets with no hypothesis (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.boundaryNullSets`; a nonempty $\partial M$ is not null, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.not_isHNull_submanifoldBoundary`), and Definition 9.5.14 is `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.lebesgueSigmaBoundaryH`, independent of the tame structures (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isMeasureZeroBoundary_boundaryNullSets_iff`) (gap G.108 closed; Findings, items 117, 119).

**V9.53 (witnesses for §9.5 (not in the book); `Polyfold.isMeasureZero_image_of_local`, `Polyfold.isMeasureZero_of_subsingleton`, `Polyfold.isMeasureZero_rn2_iff`, `Polyfold.exists_tameBranchingStructure_trivial_rn`, `Polyfold.hasTameSheetsIn_trivial_rn`, `Polyfold.injective_π_trivial_rn`, `Polyfold.graphSheetMeasureGeometry`, `Polyfold.graphNull`, `Polyfold.theta935`, `Polyfold.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_theta935`, `Polyfold.hasTameSheetsIn_theta935`, `Polyfold.zero_mem_supp_theta935`, `Polyfold.isMeasureZeroSupp_theta935_zero`, `Polyfold.not_isMeasureZeroSupp_theta935`, `Polyfold.lebesgueSigma_theta935`, `Polyfold.planeSheets`, `Polyfold.planeNull`, `Polyfold.planeSheet`, `Polyfold.thetaPlane`, `Polyfold.isSmoothSubmanifold_univ_rn2`, `Polyfold.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_thetaPlane`, `Polyfold.mem_supp_thetaPlane`, `Polyfold.hasTameSheetsIn_thetaPlane`, `Polyfold.exists_mem_lebesgueSigma_not_borel_thetaPlane`).** On the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^n$ every local branching structure restricts to a tame one. The graph sheets of §9.4 carry a `SheetMeasureGeometry`; for the $\Theta$ of the two graphs $G^{++}$, $G^{--}$ of Example 9.3.5 the touching point $|0|$ is a nonempty set of measure zero, $S$ is not null and $S \in L(S)$; for $\Theta = 1$ on $\mathbb R^2$ with the Lebesgue null sets there is a member of $L(S)$ that is not Borel. *Book:* not in the book. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (extra):* the hypotheses of V9.49–V9.51 are satisfiable, and $L(S)$ is strictly larger than the Borel σ-algebra (Findings, item 82). *Update (2026-11-12):* for $\partial S$: $\Theta = 1$ on the half-line has a tame structure at every point (`Polyfold.halfLineTame`), $\partial S \ne \emptyset$ (`Polyfold.halfLine_orbitSupp_boundary_nonempty`), $\partial S$ is not null and $L(\partial S)$ is the Borel σ-algebra (`Polyfold.halfLine_lebesgueSigmaBoundary`).

**V9.62 (Proposition 9.6.5 and the formula on p. 457; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.IsTopSlice`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.proposition_9_6_5`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.sum_class_eq_sum_of_isTopSlice`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart_topDim_eq_sum_slices`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.sum_class_eq_of_hasGraphChartAt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart_topDim_eq_of_hasGraphChartAt`).** Under `HasGraphChartAt` at $x$, for every class of top-dimensional sheets with one tangent space at $x$ and every neighbourhood $W$ of $x$ there is a finite top slice in $W$; the top-dimensional part is $\Theta_k(x) = \sum_{\text{classes}} \sum_{y \in \text{slice}} \Theta(y)$, and the class sums agree for any two structures. *Book:* Proposition 9.6.5, p. 456, and the formula on p. 457, new in the 2021 edition. *Hidden hypotheses:* the graph representation on a general M-polyfold. *Deviation (narrower):* slices replace the subsets $I^e$ and the sequences of top-good points; the independence of the right-hand side from the structure, which the text does not show, is proved with one slice for the sheets of both structures. the local measures (9.21) (`localMeasure`, `localMeasureEff`); Lemma 9.5.7 (`lemma_9_5_7`); `theorem_9_5_4`: for $\Theta$ branched, compact, with an orientation $T$ and, at every point of the support, an oriented tame structure of dimension $n$ with sheets in $S$ describing $T$ (`hcov`), there is exactly one linear map $\Omega \to$ signed measures on $(S, L(S))$ given on measurable $K \subseteq |U(x)|$ by the local formula with $1/\#G_x$, for all such structures; `theorem_9_5_5`: the same with $1/\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$ and structures with LUC; Definition 9.5.6 (`branchedIntegral`, `branchedIntegralEff`). The gluing is `existsUnique_linearMap_signedMeasure_of_openCover`. The structure is satisfiable in dimension $0$ for every ep-groupoid (`pointIntegration`). (2026-11-13) For the integrals of sc-forms over sheets covered by countably many graph charts (`FormEval.msheetIntegration`, $n \ge 1$; gap G.107): `theorem_9_5_4_full`, `theorem_9_5_5_full`. There is exactly one linear map with the local formula for every oriented tame structure describing $\hat T_\Theta$ (no class condition: the sheets of every oriented tame structure of a compact $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ have finite $\int|\omega|$, `msheets_of_orientedTameStructure`), under the printed hypotheses with "oriented, tame" read as `hloc`; Definition 9.5.6: `multiBranchedIntegral`, `multiBranchedIntegralEff`. Without boundary, `hloc` comes from $n$-dimensionality and the orientation (`theorem_9_5_4_full_of_degIndex_eq_zero`). Witness with nonempty compact support: the unit circle in $\mathbb R^2$ (`circle_theorem_9_5_4_full`). *Book:* §9.5, Theorem 9.5.4, p. 438 (2017: Theorem 9.2, p. 323), Theorem 9.5.5, p. 438 (new in the 2021 edition), Definition 9.5.6, (9.21), Lemma 9.5.7, pp. 439–441. *Hidden hypotheses:* the text's "oriented, tame" is read as `hloc`: at every point of the support an oriented tame structure describes $\hat T_\Theta$. It follows from $n$-dimensionality and the orientation when the M-polyfold has no boundary (`hloc_of_degIndex_eq_zero`, `theorem_9_5_4_full_of_degIndex_eq_zero`, where the theorem is the text's); with boundary, that the oriented local structures can be taken with tame sheets is the reading of "tame". *Deviation (explicit since 2026-11-13; narrower before):* The abstract theorems are stated for a `SheetIntegration` with forms in a real vector space $\Omega$; since 2026-11-13 it is realized for $\Omega^n_{ep}(X)$ and $\Omega^n_{ep,\infty}(X)$, $n \ge 1$, by the integrals over sheets covered by countably many graph charts (`FormEval.msheetIntegration`), and the local formula holds for every oriented tame structure describing $\hat T_\Theta$ (`theorem_9_5_4_full`, `theorem_9_5_5_full`); the hypotheses hold for the unit circle (`circle_theorem_9_5_4_full`). Dimension $0$ is the abstract `pointIntegration` (gap G.107, closed) (Findings, Chapter 9, items 85, 118, 119).

- pp. 449–452, Theorems 9.5.17 and 9.5.18 (2017: Theorem 9.4 and new), Stokes' theorem: verified since 2026-11-13 (wave K) as printed for every $n \ge 1$, with the text's hypotheses only (V9.68); witnesses with $\partial S \ne \emptyset$: the closed upper hemisphere (also with LUC) and the closed half-circle (no corners, no branching). Remark 9.5.20 is verified in part: its M-polyfold $X$, $\partial X$, $\mathbb Z_3 \ltimes X$ with LUC and the effective isotropy of the boundary points in $X$ and in $\partial X$. Not verified: $\Theta(t, z) = \delta_0(z)$, $\oint_{\hat\Theta} df$ and the two boundary integrals of the remark, and that $\partial X$ is a smooth submanifold (gap G.110 in part; Findings, items 85, 117, 119, 120). Remarks 9.5.12 (history and open questions) and 9.5.19 (on the partition-of-unity hypothesis) have no formal content.

- Witnesses: every hypothesis of the chapter is satisfiable, and those of §9.2 and §9.6.1 hold on every ep-groupoid over $\mathbb R^m$; the hypothesis of Definition 9.2.12 has only the zero functor as a witness, and no witness of Lemma 9.2.13 at a boundary point is constructed (Findings, items 100–102).

## 11. Chapter 10 (HWZ, Part II, §§10.1–10.5 and Appendix §§10.6.1–10.6.3 (2017 §§10.1–10.5)): verified for equivalences, natural equivalences, the weak fibred product, the localization $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ with its universal property, strong bundle equivalences and generalized strong bundle maps, Remark 10.1.8 with Zhou's example, and Propositions 10.4.6, 10.4.7 and 10.5.6 with Definition 8.4.2 read for local strong bundle isomorphisms, with the readings recorded below; Theorems 10.3.19 and 10.5.7 do not hold as we read them, and Theorem 10.3.19 holds for an effective target

Chapter 10 (pp. 461–520 (2017 pp. 333–374); numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021), with the 2017 text's in parentheses) treats equivalences of ep-groupoids, the sc-smooth form of equivalences of categories, and prepares their inversion. §10.1 defines equivalences (Definition 10.1.1 (2017: 10.1)), characterizes them (Lemma 10.1.2 (2017: 10.1)), refines an ep-groupoid along an open covering (Proposition 10.1.3 (2017: 10.1)), recalls natural equivalences (Definition 10.1.4 (2017: 10.2)) and shows that they and compositions respect equivalences (Propositions 10.1.5, 10.1.6 (2017: 10.2, 10.3)), that the tangent of an equivalence is one (Theorem 10.1.7 (2017: 10.1)), and, mostly new in the 2021 edition, which properties of Chapter 7 are invariant under equivalences: the local regularity property (Propositions 10.1.9, 10.1.10 (2017: 10.4), Remark 10.1.11 (2017: 10.1)), the non-effective part and the reduced ep-groupoid (Remark 10.1.12, Propositions 10.1.13, 10.1.14 (2017: 10.5), Example 10.1.15 (2017: 10.1)), (LUC), (ZHOU), (SLUC) and (SLR) (Propositions 10.1.16–10.1.19). §10.2 builds the weak fibred product $X \times_Y Z$ (Definition 10.2.1 (2017: 10.3)) and shows that it is an ep-groupoid with an equivalence to $Z$ when $F$ is an equivalence (Theorem 10.2.2 (2017: 10.2), Remark 10.2.3 (2017: 10.2)). §10.3 inverts the equivalences: diagrams $X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y$ with $F$ an equivalence, their refinements and equivalence (Definitions 10.3.1, 10.3.3, 10.3.5, Lemmas 10.3.2, 10.3.4 (2017: Definitions 10.4–10.6, Lemmas 10.3, 10.4)), the induced maps of orbit spaces (Lemma 10.3.6, Definition 10.3.7 (2017: 10.5, 10.7)), the composition of classes (Theorem 10.3.8 (2017: 10.3), proved in Appendix §10.6.1), generalized maps and isomorphisms (Definition 10.3.9, Theorem 10.3.10 (2017: 10.8, 10.4), the latter proved in Appendix §10.6.2), the category $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ with the functors $i : \mathcal{EP} \to \mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ and $|\cdot| : \mathcal{EP}(E^{-1}) \to \mathrm{TOP}$ (Proposition 10.3.11, Definition 10.3.12, Theorems 10.3.14, 10.3.15 (2017: Proposition 10.6, Definition 10.9, Theorems 10.5, 10.6)), and, mostly new in 2021, the invariance of the properties of Chapter 7 under generalized isomorphisms (Propositions 10.3.16, 10.3.17, Remark 10.3.18 (2017: 10.3), Theorem 10.3.19 (2017: 10.7), Definition 10.3.20, Theorem 10.3.21). §10.4 defines strong bundle equivalences (Definition 10.4.1 (2017: 10.10)), the pull-back and push-forward of section functors and their properties (Propositions 10.4.2–10.4.4 (2017: 10.7–10.9), Theorem 10.4.5 (2017: 10.8)), natural equivalences of strong bundle functors (Definitions 10.4.8, 10.4.10, Remark 10.4.9 (2017: Definitions 10.11, 10.12, Remark 10.4)) and the category $\mathcal{SEP}$ (Definition 10.4.11 (2017: 10.13)). §10.5 repeats the localization for strong bundles: diagrams $W \xleftarrow{\Phi} W'' \xrightarrow{\Psi} W'$ with $\Phi$ a strong bundle equivalence, their classes, the generalized strong bundle maps, with the maps $[d]$ and $|[D]|$, the square $|\mathscr D|$ and the homomorphisms $\gamma$ (pp. 504–506 (2017 pp. 364–366, with Remark 10.5)), the category $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ and the generalized strong bundle isomorphisms (Definitions 10.5.1, 10.5.2 (2017: 10.14, 10.15), Remark 10.5.3), the push-forward of section functors along them (Theorem 10.5.4 (2017: 10.9), Remark 10.5.5), and the local regularity property under them (Proposition 10.5.6, new in the 2021 edition, and Theorem 10.5.7 (2017: 10.10), whose local regularity hypothesis is new in the 2021 edition).

What is verified. Every definition of §§10.1, 10.2 and 10.4 is formalized: Definitions 10.1.1 (V10.1), 10.1.4 (V10.4), 10.2.1 (V10.17), 10.4.1 (V10.22), 10.4.8 (V10.28), 10.4.10 (V10.30) and 10.4.11 (V10.31), with the class $E$ of equivalences, the refinement $X_{\mathcal U}$ (V10.3) and the pull-back and push-forward of section functors (V10.23). Lemma 10.1.2, Propositions 10.1.3, 10.1.5, 10.1.6, 10.1.13, 10.1.14, 10.1.16, 10.1.17 and 10.1.18, Theorem 10.1.7, Remark 10.1.12 and Remark 10.2.3 hold as stated; Remark 10.1.11 and Example 10.1.15 hold in stronger forms (V10.8, V10.12); Theorem 10.2.2 holds in all its claims, its first claim under the weaker hypothesis that $F$ or $G$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects (V10.18–V10.20); Propositions 10.4.2–10.4.4 hold for all section functors, without sc-smoothness (V10.24–V10.26); Theorem 10.4.5 holds without its Fred part (V10.27); Remark 10.4.9 and the equivalence of Definitions 10.4.8 and 10.4.10 hold for strong bundle functors (V10.29, V10.30). Propositions 10.1.9 and 10.1.19 hold as stated, and Proposition 10.1.10 holds with (LR) on one side only (V10.62, V10.16, V10.63). In §10.3 every definition is formalized (V10.33, V10.35, V10.37, V10.39, V10.41, V10.44, V10.49); the properties (E1)–(E3), Lemmas 10.3.2, 10.3.4, 10.3.6, Theorems 10.3.8, 10.3.10, 10.3.14, 10.3.15, Propositions 10.3.11 and 10.3.17 hold as stated, with the proofs of Appendix §§10.6.1–10.6.2 (V10.32–V10.47); Remark 10.3.18 is verified, its non-uniqueness claim through the example of Remark 10.5.5 (V10.48, V10.60), Proposition 10.3.16 and Theorem 10.3.21 hold as stated (V10.64, V10.50); Theorem 10.3.19 does not hold as we read it, and holds when the target is effective (V10.65, V10.66). In §10.5 the diagrams of strong bundles, their refinements, the maps $[d]$ and $|[D]|$, the square $|\mathscr D|$ and the homomorphisms $\gamma$ are formalized (V10.51–V10.54); Definition 10.5.2 and Remark 10.5.5 hold as stated, the latter with an example the text does not give (V10.56, V10.60); the weak fibred product of strong bundles, which the text leaves to the reader, is constructed, with the strong bundle versions of Theorem 10.2.2, Lemma 10.3.4 and Theorem 10.3.8 (V10.68–V10.70), and Definition 10.5.1 holds, $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ being a category with a localization functor (V10.55); Remark 10.5.3 is verified for the base and total spaces and, read as "generalized strong bundle isomorphisms are isomorphisms", as one direction of the strong bundle Theorem 10.3.10 (V10.57, V10.71); Theorem 10.5.4 holds without its Fred part (V10.58, V10.59); Proposition 10.5.6 is reduced to Proposition 10.4.6 (V10.61); and Theorem 10.5.7 does not hold as we read it (V10.67). Several places of the text needed more than a reading. (a) *Proposition 10.1.6 (2017: 10.3).* The argument on objects covers only the points $F(x)$; the transport to every $y$ along a morphism $F(x) \to y$ is supplied (V10.6). (b) *Theorem 10.1.7 (2017: 10.1).* Fullness and faithfulness of $TF$, left to the reader, are proved (V10.7); Proposition 10.1.5, quoted from the literature, is proved (V10.5). (c) *Propositions 10.1.13 and 10.1.16.* The closedness of $\mathbf X^T$ passes along equivalences by a closure argument with a conjugation by a local inverse of $t$ in place of sequences (V10.10, V10.13). (d) *Theorem 10.2.2 (2017: 10.2).* The ep-groupoid structure of $X \times_Y Z$ needs of $F$ only that it is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, its properness holds for any $F$ and $G$, and its M-polyfold structures are read as iterated sub-M-polyfolds of Part I's fibred products (V10.18); the composite in the fullness step is read with the ends it must have (V10.19). (e) *Definition 10.4.1 (2017: 10.10).* $W[1]$ is not an ep-groupoid in the project; clause (1) at level $[1]$ is read as "$|\Phi| : |W[1]| \to |W'[1]|$ is a homeomorphism", the rest of it being a consequence of (2) (V10.22). (f) *Theorem 10.4.5 (2017: 10.8).* The sc-smoothness of $\Phi_*f$, "easily verified" in the text, and the preservation of $\mathrm{sc}^+$-sections are proved (V10.27). (g) *Theorem 10.3.8 (2017: 10.3), Appendix §10.6.1.* The functor $L$ between weak fibred products is shown to be an equivalence by two out of three, and the text's identification of the two iterated weak fibred products ("the same space") is a reassociation functor, an equivalence (V10.40). (h) *Theorem 10.3.10 (2017: 10.4), Appendix §10.6.2.* In claim (C2) the text uses that a map $\Gamma'$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, which, as we read it, already needs the other half of (C2); the local sc-diffeomorphism property of $\Phi$ is proved instead from a local sc-smooth right inverse and local injectivity (V10.42). (i) *Theorem 10.3.14 (2017: 10.5).* With Definition 10.3.1 as stated, it is the composite diagram (10.13) that refines $d_{\Psi \circ \Phi}$, not the reverse; the equality of classes is unchanged (V10.45). (j) *§10.5.* The weak fibred product of strong bundles, which the text uses "following our earlier construction" (p. 504) without constructing it, is the pull-back of $W''$ along $\pi_Z$, so that the squares in the proofs of the composition commute strictly, by the fibrewise injectivity of strong bundle equivalences (V10.68, V10.70); the classes, taken for the generated equivalence relation, are the text's by the transitivity (V10.51, V10.69), and the independence of $[D]_*$ of the representative is proved through the orbit spaces, for any two representatives with the same $|D|$ (V10.58). (k) *Proposition 10.1.9.* That $Q(U(x))$ carries a natural representation of $G_y$, which the text takes for granted, is proved by restricting one at $y$ (V10.62). (l) *Theorem 10.3.19 (2017: 10.7).* The proof's step on p. 494 uses the families $\alpha_a$ of Proposition 10.1.10 (1) as a natural transformation; on $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ with the trivial action, which has (LR), there is no natural transformation $1 \to \mathrm{Inv}$, and the statement and its strong bundle version, Theorem 10.5.7, do not hold as we read them (V10.65, V10.67); over an effective target the families are unique and glue (V10.66). Possible misprints are recorded in V10.3, V10.6, V10.9, V10.14, V10.15, V10.17, V10.19, V10.24, V10.27, V10.40, V10.42, V10.53 and V10.62; V10.61 records a reading point. Not verified: the subcategory $\mathcal{EP}_{lreg}$, Remark 10.1.8 with its example in Appendix §10.6.3, the agreement of the M-polyfold structure of $X \times_Y Z$ with one induced from the triple products, the universal property of the localization, the Fred part of Theorem 10.4.5, Propositions 10.4.6 and 10.4.7, the converse half of the strong bundle version of Theorem 10.3.10, the symbolic diagram (10.24) made precise with the local expressions $q$, $Q$ of (10.25), the Fred part of Theorem 10.5.4 and Proposition 10.5.6 itself (gaps G.111–G.127; G.113, G.114, G.115, G.118 and G.119 are closed since, by V10.62, V10.63, V10.16, V10.64 with V10.50, and V10.60, G.123 is closed since by V10.68–V10.71 except the converse half of the strong bundle Theorem 10.3.10, and G.120 and G.127 are settled since by the counterexamples V10.65 and V10.67). Since 2026-11-12 every gap of the chapter is closed: the subcategory $\mathcal{EP}_{lreg}$ (V10.74), Remark 10.1.8 with Appendix §10.6.3 as printed, on the appendix's weighted Sobolev scale with its projections (V10.75), the triple-product structures of Theorem 10.2.2 (V10.18), the universal property of the localization (V10.45), Propositions 10.4.6 and 10.4.7 (V10.72, V10.73) and Proposition 10.5.6 (V10.61), with Definition 8.4.2 read for local strong bundle isomorphisms, (10.24) with generalized vertical maps and the local expressions $q$, $Q$ of (10.25) (V10.53, V10.54), and the converse half of the strong bundle Theorem 10.3.10 (V10.71) (gaps G.111, G.112, G.116, G.117, G.122, G.124, G.126 closed, and G.123 in full).

The hypotheses. No hypothesis beyond the text's is taken on a general ep-groupoid, apart from two technical ones, each with a witness: the object set is nonempty in Proposition 10.1.3 (the open-subset M-polyfold structure of Part I needs a nonempty set; the trivial covering of any nonempty ep-groupoid and a two-set covering of $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$ are witnesses); the weak fibred product is given its ep-groupoid structure under `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Admissible` ($F$ or $G$ a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects), which every equivalence supplies (`Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Admissible.of_isEquivalence_left`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Admissible.of_isEquivalence_right`). The reduction of Proposition 10.1.19 took Proposition 10.1.9 for the lifts as a hypothesis (satisfied when the two ep-groupoids agree, `Polyfold.EP.isLR_iff_lift_self`); since Proposition 10.1.9 is proved (V10.62), Proposition 10.1.19 holds without it (V10.16). Theorem 10.3.19 is proved under the added hypothesis that the target is effective (V10.66), without which it does not hold as we read it (V10.65). Proposition 10.1.14 keeps the text's hypothesis that both reduced morphism spaces are Hausdorff. In §10.3 no hypothesis is added; a diagram is a structure one universe above the object and morphism types of the ep-groupoids, so that the classes of diagrams are sets and $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ is a large category like $\mathcal{EP}$. In §10.5 no hypothesis is added; the classes of diagrams of strong bundles are taken for the equivalence relation generated by having a common refinement, which is that relation itself (V10.51, V10.69). Propositions 10.4.6, 10.4.7 and 10.5.6 (since 2026-11-12) add no hypothesis; they read Definition 8.4.2 as `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsLRLocal`, with local strong bundle isomorphisms of $W|U(x)$ (witness `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isLRLocal_trivial`), the reading already used for Theorem 10.5.7 (Findings, items 72, 74), and Proposition 10.4.7 uses (LR) of the target only.

The setting. Ep-groupoids, sc-smooth functors, the orbit spaces with their quotient topologies, the category $\mathcal{EP}$ (with Mathlib's composition order: $f ≫ g$ is the text's $g \circ f$, and so is $d.\mathrm{comp}\,e$ for diagrams) and the lifts $X^i$ are those of Chapter 7 (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor`, `Polyfold.EP`, `Polyfold.EP.lift`); (LUC), (ZHOU), (LR), (SLUC) and (SLR) are Chapter 7's `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsLUC`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsZhou`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsLR`, `Polyfold.EP.IsSLUC`, `Polyfold.EP.IsSLR`, and the reduced ep-groupoid is `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.reducedEpGroupoid`. Natural transformations, natural equivalence and the tangent functor are Chapter 8's (`Polyfold.EpNatTrans`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.tangent`), and so are strong bundles over ep-groupoids, strong bundle functors and local strong bundle isomorphisms (`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleFunctor`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleIsoOn`). "Full", "faithful", "essentially surjective" and "equivalence of categories" are Mathlib's notions for the underlying functor of the groupoids. The category $\mathcal{SEP}$ and its class $F$ of strong bundle equivalences are §10.4's (`Polyfold.SEP`, `Polyfold.SEP.equivalences`). Findings referred to below are those of `Exposition/Findings.md`, "Chapter 10".

**V10.1 (Definition 10.1.1 (2017: 10.1), equivalences and the class $E$; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence`, `Polyfold.EP.equivalences`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.full_iff`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.faithful_iff`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.essSurj_iff`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.essSurj`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.exists_iso`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.exists_mor_eq`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.mor_injective`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.id`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.pairToPoint`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isEquivalence_pairToPoint`).** An equivalence $F : X \to Y$ of ep-groupoids is an sc-smooth functor which is full and faithful (every $\psi : F(x) \to F(x')$ is $F(\varphi)$ for some $\varphi : x \to x'$, and $F$ is injective on each set of morphisms $x \to x'$), induces a homeomorphism $|F| : |X| \to |Y|$ of the orbit spaces, and is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects. The equivalences form a class $E$ of morphisms of $\mathcal{EP}$ containing the identities and closed under composition. An equivalence is essentially surjective: every $y$ is the target of a morphism from some $F(x)$. The identity and the functor from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ to the point are equivalences. *Book:* Definition 10.1.1, p. 461 (2017: Definition 10.1, p. 333), with the category notions recalled on pp. 461–462. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 1).

**V10.2 (Lemma 10.1.2 (2017: 10.1) and the remarks around it; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.lemma_10_1_2`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isEquivalence_iff`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isEquivalence_toFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.comp`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.injective_orbitMap_of_full`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.surjective_orbitMap_iff`, `Polyfold.GroupoidFunctor.bijective_orbitMap_of_isEquivalence`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.continuous_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isOpenMap_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.not_exists_leftInverse_pairToPoint`).** An sc-smooth functor which is an equivalence of categories and a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects is an equivalence, and conversely every equivalence is both. For a functor of groupoids, $|F|$ is injective if $F$ is full, surjective if and only if $F$ is essentially surjective, and bijective for an equivalence of categories; $|F|$ is continuous, and open if $F$ is open on objects. The composite of two equivalences is an equivalence, and the equivalence from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ to the point has no left inverse on objects. *Book:* Lemma 10.1.2, p. 462 (2017: Lemma 10.1, p. 334), and the remarks on pp. 461–462. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the lemma is stated with its converse; "not invertible as a functor" gets a witness.

**V10.3 (Proposition 10.1.3 (2017: 10.1), the refinement $X_{\mathcal U}$; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.univ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.objSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.morSet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.groupoidStr`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.objPolyfold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.morPolyfold`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.isLocalScDiffeo_src`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.isLocalScDiffeo_tgt`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.exists_isProperMap`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.isScSmoothCompSheet`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.epGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.functor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.OpenCover.proposition_10_1_3`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.reflectionCover`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isEquivalence_reflectionCover`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.not_injective_reflectionCover_obj`).** For a covering of the object M-polyfold of $X$ by open sets $U_i$, $i \in \iota$, the refinement $X_{\mathcal U}$ has as objects the pairs $(i, x)$ with $x \in U_i$, an open subset of $\iota \times X$ with $\iota$ discrete, and as morphisms the triples $(i, \varphi, j)$ with $s(\varphi) \in U_i$, $t(\varphi) \in U_j$, an open subset of $(\iota \times \iota) \times \mathbf X$, with $s(i, \varphi, j) = (i, s(\varphi))$, $t(i, \varphi, j) = (j, t(\varphi))$, $(j, \psi, k) \circ (i, \varphi, j) = (i, \psi \circ \varphi, k)$, units $(i, 1_x, i)$ and inverses $(j, \varphi^{-1}, i)$. If $X$ has an object, $X_{\mathcal U}$ is an ep-groupoid and $F : X_{\mathcal U} \to X$, $(i, x) \mapsto x$, $(i, \varphi, j) \mapsto \varphi$, is an equivalence. For the covering $\{x > -1\}$, $\{x < 1\}$ of $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$ this $F$ is an equivalence which is not injective on objects. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.3, p. 462 (2017: Proposition 10.1, p. 334), with the construction of $X_{\mathcal U}$ on p. 462. *Hidden hypotheses:* the object set is nonempty (the open-subset M-polyfold structure needs a nonempty set; for an empty $X$ the statement is trivial). *Deviation (explicit):* the covering is indexed by a type, the text's index set being the covering itself; "induced from $X$ and $\mathbf X$" is read as open subsets of products with a discrete factor; the printed $(U, \varphi, v)$ in the formula for $F$ is read $(U, \varphi, V)$ (possible misprint) (Findings, item 2). *Proof:* the properness at $(i, x)$ takes a closed neighbourhood of $x$ inside $U_i$ and a neighbourhood with the properness property of $X$, and is proved with ultrafilters instead of sequences.

**V10.4 (Definition 10.1.4 (2017: 10.2), natural equivalence; `Polyfold.definition_10_1_4`, `Polyfold.EpNatTrans`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.naturallyEquivalent_equivalence`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent.comp_left`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent.comp_right`, `Polyfold.EpNatTrans.toNatIso`).** A natural transformation $\tau : F \to G$ of sc-smooth functors $X \to Y$ is an sc-smooth map $\tau : X \to \mathbf Y$ with $\tau(x) : F(x) \to G(x)$ and $\tau(x') \circ F(\varphi) = G(\varphi) \circ \tau(x)$ for $\varphi : x \to x'$; $F \simeq G$ if one exists. $\simeq$ is an equivalence relation, and $F \simeq G$ implies $F \circ \Psi \simeq G \circ \Psi$ and $\Phi \circ F \simeq \Phi \circ G$. A natural transformation is a natural isomorphism of the underlying functors. *Book:* Definition 10.1.4, p. 463 (2017: Definition 10.2, p. 335), and the claims after it, p. 464. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; the definition is Definition 8.1.13 (Findings, item 3).

**V10.5 (Proposition 10.1.5 (2017: 10.2), natural equivalence preserves equivalences; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_5`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.of_natTrans`, `Polyfold.EpNatTrans.continuous_app`, `Polyfold.EpNatTrans.isLocalScDiffeo_app`, `Polyfold.EpNatTrans.isLocalScDiffeo_obj`).** If $F \simeq G$, then $F$ is an equivalence if and only if $G$ is. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.5, p. 464 (2017: Proposition 10.2, p. 336), quoted from the literature without proof. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none. *Proof:* $s \circ \tau = F$ makes $\tau$ a local sc-diffeomorphism, so $G = t \circ \tau$ is one on objects; the underlying functors are naturally isomorphic, so $G$ is an equivalence of categories, and Lemma 10.1.2 applies (Findings, item 4).

**V10.6 (Proposition 10.1.6 (2017: 10.3), the two-out-of-three property; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_6`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt.comp`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt.congr`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt.of_comp_left`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt.of_comp_right`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isLocalScDiffeoAt_mor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isLocalScDiffeo_mor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isLocalScDiffeoAt_obj_tgt`).** If $F : X \to Y$ and $\Phi \circ F : X \to Z$ are equivalences and $\Phi : Y \to Z$ is sc-smooth, then $\Phi$ is an equivalence. A functor which is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects at $s(\varphi)$ is one at $t(\varphi)$, and one on morphisms at $\varphi$. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.6, p. 464 (2017: Proposition 10.3, p. 336). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the text's argument on objects gives the local sc-diffeomorphism property of $\Phi$ only at the points $F(x)$; the transport along a morphism $F(x) \to y$ is added. The proof writes $|\Phi| : |X| \to |Y|$ for $|\Phi| : |Y| \to |Z|$ (possible misprint) (Findings, item 5). *Proof:* $\Phi$ is an equivalence of categories since $F$ and $\Phi \circ F$ are, and Lemma 10.1.2 applies.

**V10.7 (Theorem 10.1.7 (2017: 10.1), the tangent of an equivalence; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.theorem_10_1_7`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.tangent`).** If $F$ is an equivalence, its tangent $TF : TX \to TY$ is an equivalence of the tangent ep-groupoids. *Book:* Theorem 10.1.7, p. 465 (2017: Theorem 10.1, p. 337). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; fullness and faithfulness of $TF$, left to the reader, are proved (Findings, item 6). *Proof:* by Lemma 10.1.2; a tangent morphism is determined by its base morphism and its source vector, so faithfulness comes from that of $F$; fullness lifts the base morphism given by fullness of $F$ and uses the injectivity of $TF$ on tangent fibres; essential surjectivity lifts $\psi^{-1}$ for $\psi : F(x) \to y$ and uses that $TF$ maps $T_xX$ onto $T_{F(x)}Y$.

**V10.8 (Remark 10.1.11 (2017: 10.1), $\alpha_x$ cannot be prescribed; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.pointReflectionEpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.negFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isEquivalence_negFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.orbitMap_id_eq_negFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.remark_10_1_11_family`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.remark_10_1_11`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.remark_10_1_11_scSmooth`).** On the translation groupoid of $\mathbb Z/2$ acting on $\mathbb R^2$ by $z \mapsto -z$, with $F = \mathrm{id}$ and $G = -\mathrm{id}$ (both equivalences, $|F| = |G|$), $\alpha_z = (-1, z) : F(z) \to G(z)$ is an sc-smooth family, but no family $\alpha_z : F(z) \to G(z)$ defined near $0$ with $\alpha_0 = 1_0$ is continuous at $0$, and none is sc-smooth on an open neighbourhood of $0$. *Book:* Remark 10.1.11, p. 470 (2017: Remark 10.1, p. 340). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* "not in an sc-smooth local family" is proved in the form "not in a family continuous at $0$"; that the conclusion of Proposition 10.1.10 (1) holds in the example is added (Findings, item 8).

**V10.9 (Remark 10.1.12, isotropy groups under equivalences; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isotropyHom`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isotropyHom_mem_trivialSet_iff`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.bijective_isotropyHom`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.remark_10_1_12`).** For a functor which is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, $g \mapsto F(g)$, $G_x \to G_{F(x)}$, maps $g$ into $T_{F(x)}$ if and only if $g \in T_x$; for an equivalence it is bijective, and for $\psi : F(x) \to y$ there is a group isomorphism $G_x \to G_y$, $g \mapsto \psi \circ F(g) \circ \psi^{-1}$, mapping $T_x$ onto $T_y$. *Book:* Remark 10.1.12, p. 472 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the printed $G_x \to Y_y$ is read $G_x \to G_y$ (possible misprint) (Findings, item 9).

**V10.10 (Proposition 10.1.13, the reduced morphism spaces; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.mor_mem_nonEffectivePart`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.mem_nonEffectivePart_of_mor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.nonEffectivePart_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.continuousAt_comp`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isClosed_nonEffectivePart_iff`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.reducedMap`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.continuous_reducedMap`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isOpenMap_reducedMap`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_13`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.theorem_7_2_22`).** For a functor which is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, $\mathbf X^T = F^{-1}(\mathbf Y^T) \cap \{s = t\}$ and $F_R : \mathbf X^R \to \mathbf Y^R$, $[\varphi] \mapsto [F(\varphi)]$, is well defined, continuous and open. For an equivalence $F$, $\mathbf X^T$ is closed if and only if $\mathbf Y^T$ is, and $\mathbf X^R$ is Hausdorff if and only if $\mathbf Y^R$ is. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.13, p. 472 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* (1) is proved for any functor which is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects (Findings, item 10). *Proof:* (2) through Theorem 7.2.22 ($T_R$ Hausdorff if and only if $\mathbf X^T$ closed), as in the text; the closedness passes from $\mathbf X^T$ to $\mathbf Y^T$ by conjugating with a local inverse of $t$ at a morphism $\sigma : F(x) \to y$, with closures in place of sequences.

**V10.11 (Proposition 10.1.14 (2017: 10.5), the reduced functor; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.reducedGroupoidFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.reduced`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.reducedπ_eq_of_mor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_14`).** If $F$ is an equivalence and the reduced morphism spaces $\mathbf X^R$, $\mathbf Y^R$ are Hausdorff, then $F_R = F$ on objects, $F_R([\varphi]) = [F(\varphi)]$ is a well-defined sc-smooth functor $X_R \to Y_R$ of the reduced ep-groupoids and an equivalence. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.14, p. 473 (2017: Proposition 10.5, p. 341). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; by Proposition 10.1.13 (2) one Hausdorff hypothesis would suffice (Findings, item 11).

**V10.12 (Example 10.1.15 (2017: 10.1), a functor that does not pass to the reduced groupoids; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015X`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015Y`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015Functor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015X_two_mem_nonEffectivePart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015Y_two_not_mem_nonEffectivePart`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015X_reducedπ_one_eq_three`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015Y_reducedπ_one_ne_three`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example_10_1_15`).** For $X = \mathbb Z/4 \ltimes \mathbb R$ ($1$ and $3$ acting by $x \mapsto -x$, $2$ trivially), $Y = \mathbb Z/4 \ltimes \mathbb R^2$ (rotations by multiples of $90°$) and the sc-smooth functor $\Phi(x) = 0$, $\Phi(i, x) = (i, 0)$: $(2, x) \in \mathbf X^T$, $(2, 0) \notin \mathbf Y^T$, $[(1, x)] = [(3, x)]$ in $\mathbf X^R$ and $[(1, 0)] \ne [(3, 0)]$ in $\mathbf Y^R$, so no map $f : \mathbf X^R \to \mathbf Y^R$ satisfies $f([\varphi]) = [\Phi(\varphi)]$. *Book:* Example 10.1.15, p. 474 (2017: Example 10.1, p. 341). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* no Hausdorff hypothesis and no topology on the reduced spaces is involved; no map at all is compatible with $\Phi$ (Findings, item 12).

**V10.13 (Proposition 10.1.16, (LUC) under equivalences; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_16`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isClosed_nonEffectivePart_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_21`).** If $F : X \to Y$ is an equivalence, $X$ has the local unique continuation property if and only if $Y$ has it. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.16, p. 474 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 10). *Proof:* (LUC) holds if and only if $\mathbf X^T$ is closed (Proposition 7.2.21, a part of Theorem 7.2.22), and the closedness passes along equivalences (V10.10).

**V10.14 (Proposition 10.1.17, the Zhou condition under equivalences; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_smoothSet_src_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.mem_smoothSet_tgt_iff`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.tangentMor_mor`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isZhou_of_isZhou`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isZhou_of_isZhou_right`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_17`).** If $F : X \to Y$ is an equivalence, $X$ satisfies the Zhou condition (for smooth $x$ and $g \in G_x$, $Tg = \mathrm{id}$ on $T_xX$ implies $g \in T_x$) if and only if $Y$ does. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.17, p. 475 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the proof uses the naturality $T(F(\varphi)) \circ TF = TF \circ T\varphi$, the composition rule for $T$ and the bijectivity of $TF$ on tangent fibres instead of the natural representations; the text's $U(F(y))$ and "$x \in U(x)$" in (b) are read $U(F(x))$ and $a \in U(x)$ (possible misprints) (Findings, item 13).
