**V10.15 (Proposition 10.1.18, (SLUC) under equivalences; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.liftOne`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.liftOne`, `Polyfold.EP.exists_isEquivalence_lift`, `Polyfold.EP.proposition_10_1_18`).** The restriction $F^1 : X^1 \to Y^1$ of an sc-smooth functor to level $1$ is an sc-smooth functor, and an equivalence if $F$ is; hence for every $i$ there is an equivalence $X^i \to Y^i$, and $X$ satisfies (SLUC) if and only if $Y$ does. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.18, p. 476 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the proof cites Proposition 10.1.9 for the step (LUC) along $F^i$, which is Proposition 10.1.16 (possible misprint) (Findings, item 14).

**V10.16 (Proposition 10.1.19, (SLR) under equivalences; `Polyfold.EP.proposition_10_1_19`, `Polyfold.EP.isSLR_iff_of_isLR_iff`, `Polyfold.EP.isLR_iff_lift_self`).** If $F : X \to Y$ is an equivalence, $X$ satisfies (SLR) if and only if $Y$ does. The reduction: if, for every $i$, every equivalence $X^i \to Y^i$ carries (LR) in both directions, then (SLR) passes along $F$; Proposition 10.1.9 (V10.62) supplies the hypothesis for the lifts $F^i$. *Book:* Proposition 10.1.19, p. 477 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the text's proof, Proposition 10.1.9 for the lifts (gap G.115, closed since: V10.16, through V10.62; Findings, items 15, 16).

**V10.17 (Definition 10.2.1 (2017: 10.3), the weak fibred product as a groupoid; `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.objRight`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.objSet`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Obj`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.morRight`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.morSet`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Mor`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.conj`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.conj_comp_mor`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.conj_recover`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.src`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.tgt`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.unit`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.inv`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.comp`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.src_eq_tgt_iff`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.groupoid`).** For sc-smooth functors $F : X \to Y$ and $G : Z \to Y$, the objects of $X \times_Y Z$ are the triples $(x, \phi, z)$ with $\phi : F(x) \to G(z)$, the morphisms the triples $(h, \phi, k)$ with $\phi : F(s(h)) \to G(s(k))$; $s(h, \phi, k) = (s(h), \phi, s(k))$, $t(h, \phi, k) = (t(h), G(k) \circ \phi \circ F(h)^{-1}, t(k))$, the unit at $(x, \phi, z)$ is $(1_x, \phi, 1_z)$, the inverse is $(h^{-1}, G(k) \circ \phi \circ F(h)^{-1}, k^{-1})$ and the product of a composable pair is $(h \circ h', \phi', k \circ k')$. This is a groupoid. *Book:* Definition 10.2.1, p. 477 (2017: Definition 10.3, p. 342). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* objects and morphisms are elements of iterated fibred products, $X \,{}_F\!\times_s (\mathbf Y \,{}_t\!\times_G Z)$ and $\mathbf X \,{}_{F \circ s}\!\times_s (\mathbf Y \,{}_t\!\times_{G \circ s} \mathbf Z)$; the multiplication is a total map whose value off composable pairs is not used; the printed inverse $\iota(h, \psi, k) = (h^{-1}, G(k) \circ \phi \circ F(h)^{-1}, k^{-1})$ is read with $\psi = \phi$ (possible misprint) (Findings, item 20).

**V10.18 (Theorem 10.2.2 (2017: 10.2), first claim: $X \times_Y Z$ is an ep-groupoid; `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Admissible`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Admissible.of_isEquivalence_left`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Admissible.of_isEquivalence_right`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.PA`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.PB`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.PObj`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.PMor`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isSubMPolyfold_objSet`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isSubMPolyfold_morSet`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_z`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_k`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_x`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_h`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_src`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_tgt`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothMap_unit`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothMap_inv`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothComp`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.exists_isProperMap`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.epGroupoid`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.of_comm`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeo_snd_fibredProduct`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeo_fst_fibredProduct`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isScSmoothOn_comp_of`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.tendsto_comp`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.theorem_10_2_2_triple`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isSubMPolyfold_objSetTriple`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isSubMPolyfold_morSetTriple`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_image_of_isScDiffeoOn`).** If $F$ or $G$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, in particular if one of them is an equivalence, the groupoid of Definition 10.2.1 with the object M-polyfold $X \,{}_F\!\times_s (\mathbf Y \,{}_t\!\times_G Z)$ and the morphism M-polyfold $\mathbf X \,{}_{F \circ s}\!\times_s (\mathbf Y \,{}_t\!\times_{G \circ s} \mathbf Z)$, iterated sub-M-polyfolds of products, is an ep-groupoid. For $F$ a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, $(x, \phi, z) \mapsto z$ and $(h, \phi, k) \mapsto k$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms ((10.9), (10.10)); for $G$ one, $(x, \phi, z) \mapsto x$ and $(h, \phi, k) \mapsto h$ are. The properness of Definition 7.1.3 (3) holds for any $F$ and $G$. *Book:* Theorem 10.2.2, p. 477 (2017: Theorem 10.2, p. 343), first claim, and its proof, pp. 478–481 (2017 pp. 343–346). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* of $F$ the construction uses only that it is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects. The text's "sub-M-polyfolds of $X \times \mathbf Y \times Z$ and $\mathbf X \times \mathbf Y \times \mathbf Z$" is read as the iterated sub-M-polyfold structures of Part I's fibred products (Proposition 2.5.20); they agree with the structures induced directly from the triple products: $L$ and $\mathbf L$ are sub-M-polyfolds of $X \times \mathbf Y \times Z$ and $\mathbf X \times \mathbf Y \times \mathbf Z$, sc-diffeomorphic to the iterated structures, by the transitivity of sub-M-polyfolds (`Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.theorem_10_2_2_triple`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_image_of_isScDiffeoOn`; gap G.116 closed); the text's "$t : s^{-1}(U) \to X$ proper" is read with $\mathrm{cl}(U)$, as in Definition 7.1.3 (3) (Findings, items 21, 22). *Proof:* $s$ and $t$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms by the diagrams $\pi_Z \circ s = s_Z \circ \pi_{\mathbf Z}$ and $\pi_Z \circ t = t_Z \circ \pi_{\mathbf Z}$; the properness is the text's sequential argument, with $\phi_n = G(k_n)^{-1} \circ (G(k_n) \circ \phi_n \circ F(h_n)^{-1}) \circ F(h_n)$.

**V10.19 (Theorem 10.2.2 (2017: 10.2), the case $F$ an equivalence; `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.projLeft`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.projRight`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.natTrans`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.natTrans_app`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.naturallyEquivalent`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isEquivalence_projRight`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.degIndex_eq_z`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.theorem_10_2_2`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.degIndex_obj`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isTame_of_isTame`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.hasParacompactOrbitSpace`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Examples.theorem_10_2_2_pairToPoint`).** The projections $\pi_X$ and $\pi_Z$ are sc-smooth functors and $\sigma(x, \phi, z) = \phi$ is a natural transformation $F \circ \pi_X \to G \circ \pi_Z$ whenever $X \times_Y Z$ is defined. If $F$ is an equivalence and $G$ is sc-smooth, then $\pi_Z$ is an equivalence, $F \circ \pi_X \simeq G \circ \pi_Z$, $d_{X \times_Y Z}(x, \phi, z) = d_Z(z)$, and if $Z$ is tame, or has a paracompact orbit space, so has $X \times_Y Z$. An equivalence preserves the degeneracy index and pulls back tameness and the paracompactness of the orbit space. The weak fibred product of the equivalence from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ to the point with the identity of the point is a nonempty ep-groupoid whose projection to the point is an equivalence. *Book:* Theorem 10.2.2, pp. 477–478 (2017: Theorem 10.2, p. 343), with the paragraph after it, p. 478, and its proof, pp. 481–482. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* in the fullness step the printed $\phi' \circ G(k) \circ \phi^{-1}$, which does not compose, is read $\phi'^{-1} \circ G(k) \circ \phi : F(x) \to F(x')$ (possible misprint); essential surjectivity is taken from that of $F$ (Findings, item 23). *Proof:* $\pi_Z$ is full and faithful because the unique morphism over $k : z \to z'$ is $(h, \phi, k)$ with $F(h) = \phi'^{-1} \circ G(k) \circ \phi$, essentially surjective because every $G(z)$ receives a morphism from some $F(x)$, and Lemma 10.1.2 applies.

**V10.20 (Theorem 10.2.2 (2017: 10.2), the cases $G$ an equivalence and both; `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isEquivalence_projLeft`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.degIndex_eq_x`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.theorem_10_2_2_right`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.theorem_10_2_2_both`).** If $G$ is an equivalence, $\pi_X$ is an equivalence, $F \circ \pi_X \simeq G \circ \pi_Z$, $d_{X \times_Y Z}(x, \phi, z) = d_X(x)$, and tameness and a paracompact orbit space pass from $X$ to $X \times_Y Z$; if both are, $d_X(x) = d_{X \times_Y Z}(x, \phi, z) = d_Z(z)$. Since the admissibility is a proposition, the two cases give the same ep-groupoid. *Book:* Theorem 10.2.2, p. 478 (2017: Theorem 10.2, p. 343). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* for $G$ an equivalence the text states only that $\pi_X$ is an equivalence and the degeneracy index; the natural equivalence and the transfer of tameness and paracompactness are added (Findings, item 24).

**V10.21 (Remark 10.2.3 (2017: 10.2), two equivalences; `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.remark_10_2_3`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Examples.remark_10_2_3_negFunctor`).** For equivalences $F : X \to Y$ and $G : Z \to Y$, both projections of $X \times_Y Z$ are equivalences and $\tau(x, \phi, z) = \phi$ is a natural transformation $F \circ \pi_X \to G \circ \pi_Z$. For the identity and $-\mathrm{id}$ of $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R^2$ the weak fibred product is nonempty and both projections are equivalences. *Book:* Remark 10.2.3, pp. 482–483 (2017: Remark 10.2, p. 347). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; the closing sentences on "smaller models" have no formal content (Findings, item 25).

**V10.22 (Definition 10.4.1 (2017: 10.10), strong bundle equivalences; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.OneOrbitSpace`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.oneOrbitMap`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleFunctor.comp`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.covers`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.fiberEquiv`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.eq_of_obj_eq`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isLocalScDiffeo_obj`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isLocalScDiffeo_one`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isStrongBundleEquivalence_id`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.comp`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isStrongBundleEquivalence_of_inverse`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleEquivalenceExamples.isStrongBundleEquivalence_pullbackProj'`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleEquivalenceExamples.trivialNeg_obj_ne_id`).** A strong bundle equivalence $\Phi : (P : W \to X, \mu) \to (P' : W' \to X', \mu')$ is a strong bundle functor $\Phi : (W, \mathbf W) \to (W', \mathbf W')$ (linear on fibres, satisfying (10.14)) covering an equivalence $\phi : X \to X'$, with (1) $\Phi : W[0] \to W'[0]$ an equivalence of ep-groupoids and $|\Phi| : |W[1]| \to |W'[1]|$ a homeomorphism, and (2) every point of $X$, and every morphism of $\mathbf X$, having an open neighbourhood over which $\Phi$ on objects, respectively on morphisms, is a strong bundle isomorphism covering $\phi$. The fibre maps $W_x \to W'_{\phi(x)}$ are then topological linear isomorphisms and $\Phi : W[1] \to W'[1]$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism. The identity and composites of strong bundle equivalences are strong bundle equivalences, and so is every isomorphism of strong bundles over ep-groupoids; the projection $(-\mathrm{id})^*(\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k) \to \mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k$ over $-\mathrm{id}$ is one, not over the identity for $n \ge 1$. *Book:* Definition 10.4.1, p. 496 (2017: Definition 10.10, p. 357). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $W[1]$ is not built as an ep-groupoid in the project; (1) at level $[1]$ is read as the homeomorphism of $|W[1]|$, the quotient of $W_{0,1}$ by the orbit relation of $W$; the local sc-diffeomorphism property at level $[1]$ follows from (2), and fullness and faithfulness at level $[1]$ are those at level $[0]$ restricted (Findings, item 40).

**V10.23 (the pull-back and the push-forward of section functors, (10.15)–(10.17) and (10.22); `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pullback`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.obj_pullback`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pullback_eq`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isFunctorialSection_pullback`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.preObj`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.preMor`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pushforward`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pushforward_eq`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isFunctorialSection_pushforward`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pullback_pushforward`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pushforward_pullback`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.μ_injective_snd`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.exists_μ_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.orbitMap_eq_of_forall_exists`).** For a strong bundle equivalence $\Phi$ covering $\phi$, $\Phi^*(f')(x) = \Phi_x^{-1}(f'(\phi(x)))$ is the unique $w \in W_x$ with $\Phi(w) = f'(\phi(x))$, and $(\Phi_*f)(x') = \mu'(\sigma, \Phi(f(x)))$ for a chosen $x$ and $\sigma : \phi(x) \to x'$. For a section functor $f$ the value does not depend on the choice: $(\Phi_*f)(x') = \mu'(\sigma', \Phi(f(y)))$ for every $y$ and $\sigma' : \phi(y) \to x'$ ((10.22)). Pull-backs and push-forwards of section functors are section functors, and $\Phi^*\Phi_*f = f$, $\Phi_*\Phi^*f' = f'$. $|\Phi| = |\Psi|$ if and only if every $\Phi(w)$ is connected to $\Psi(w)$ by a morphism $(\sigma, \Phi(w))$ with $\mu'(\sigma, \Phi(w)) = \Psi(w)$ ((10.15)). *Book:* §10.4, pp. 496–498 (2017 pp. 357–360). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $\Phi^*$ and $\Phi_*$ are defined on all maps, by the zero of the fibre where the value is not in the right fibre (never for sections), and the choice of $x$ and $\sigma$ is made once for all (Findings, item 41).

**V10.24 (Proposition 10.4.2 (2017: 10.7), pull-backs along $|\Phi| = |\Psi|$; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_2`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pullback_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`).** If $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are strong bundle equivalences $(P, \mu) \to (P', \mu')$ covering $\phi$ and $\psi$ with $|\Phi| = |\Psi|$, then $\Phi^*(f') = \Psi^*(f')$ for every section functor $f'$ of $(P', \mu')$, sc-smooth or not. *Book:* Proposition 10.4.2, p. 497 (2017: Proposition 10.7, p. 358). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* sc-smoothness of $f'$ is not used; the printed "$f' : W' \to X'$" is read $f' : X' \to W'$ (possible misprint) (Findings, item 42). *Proof:* with $g = \Psi^*f'$ and a morphism $(\sigma, \Phi(g(x)))$ with $\mu'(\sigma, \Phi(g(x))) = \Psi(g(x))$, functoriality of $f'$ gives $\mu'(\sigma, \Phi(g(x))) = \mu'(\sigma, \Phi(\Phi^*f'(x)))$; $\mu'(\sigma, \cdot)$ and $\Phi_x$ are injective.

**V10.25 (Proposition 10.4.3 (2017: 10.8), push-forwards along $|\Phi| = |\Psi|$; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_3`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pushforward_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`).** Under the hypotheses of Proposition 10.4.2, $\Phi_*f = \Psi_*f$ for every section functor $f$ of $(P, \mu)$, sc-smooth or not. *Book:* Proposition 10.4.3, p. 499 (2017: Proposition 10.8, p. 360). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* sc-smoothness of $f$ is not used (Findings, item 43).

**V10.26 (Proposition 10.4.4 (2017: 10.9), functoriality; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_4`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.comp`).** For strong bundle equivalences $\Phi : (P, \mu) \to (P', \mu')$ and $\Psi : (P', \mu') \to (P'', \mu'')$, $(\Psi \circ \Phi)^* = \Phi^* \circ \Psi^*$ on all sections of $P''$ and $(\Psi \circ \Phi)_* = \Psi_* \circ \Phi_*$ on all section functors of $(P, \mu)$. *Book:* Proposition 10.4.4, p. 499 (2017: Proposition 10.9, p. 360). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the pull-back identity holds for all sections and the push-forward identity for all section functors, without sc-smoothness (Findings, item 43).

**V10.27 (Theorem 10.4.5 (2017: 10.8), without the Fred part; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.theorem_10_4_5`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.eqOn_pullback`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isScSmoothSection_pullback`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isScPlusSection_pullback`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.exists_pushforward_local`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isScSmoothSection_pushforward`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isScPlusSection_pushforward`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.isScSmoothOn_to_pullback_one`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScSmoothOn_of_forall_charts`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleIsoOn.restrict`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleIsoOn.comp`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsStrongBundleIsoOn.exists_comp`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleEquivalenceExamples.bijOn_pushforward_example`).** For a strong bundle equivalence $\Phi$ covering $\phi$, $\Phi_* : \Gamma(P, \mu) \to \Gamma(P', \mu')$ and $\Phi^* : \Gamma(P', \mu') \to \Gamma(P, \mu)$ are mutually inverse bijections of the sc-smooth section functors; if $\Psi$ is another strong bundle equivalence with $|\Phi| = |\Psi|$, then $\Phi_* = \Psi_*$ and $\Phi^* = \Psi^*$ on them; and $\Phi_*$, $\Phi^*$ map $\mathrm{sc}^+$-section functors to $\mathrm{sc}^+$-section functors. For the projection $(-\mathrm{id})^*(\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k) \to \mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k$ the push-forward is a bijection of the section functors. *Book:* Theorem 10.4.5, pp. 500–501 (2017: Theorem 10.8, p. 362), with the paragraph before it, p. 500. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* the preservation of sc-Fredholm section functors is not formalized (gap G.121); the second display's $\Phi^* : \Gamma(P', \mu') \to \Gamma(P, \mu)$ is read with $\Gamma^+$ (possible misprint) (Findings, item 44). *Proof:* the sc-smoothness of $\Phi_*f$, called easily verified in the text, comes from the local form $\Phi_*f = \mu' \circ (\tau, \Phi \circ f \circ g_1 \circ s' \circ \tau)$ near $x'_0$, with $\tau$ a local inverse of $t'$ and $g_1$ one of $\phi$; at level $[1]$ through the universal property of the pull-back on an open set.

**V10.28 (Definition 10.4.8 (2017: 10.11), natural equivalence of strong bundle functors; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatEquiv`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.refl`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleEquivalenceExamples.strongBundleNatEquiv_example`).** A natural transformation between strong bundle functors $\Phi, \Psi : (W, \mathbf W) \to (W', \mathbf W')$ covering $\phi, \psi$ is a map $T$ assigning to each $w$ a morphism $T(w) : \Phi(w) \to \Psi(w)$ of $(W', \mathbf W')$ with $T(w') \circ \Phi(h) = \Psi(h) \circ T(w)$ for $h : w \to w'$, together with a natural transformation $\tau : \phi \to \psi$ with $\tau(P(w)) = P'(T(w))$; $\Phi \simeq \Psi$ if one exists. Every strong bundle functor is naturally equivalent to itself. *Book:* Definition 10.4.8, p. 502 (2017: Definition 10.11, p. 362). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $T$ is data without smoothness, as in the text, and $\tau$ is sc-smooth (Definition 10.1.4) (Findings, item 46).

**V10.29 (Remark 10.4.9 (2017: 10.4) and (10.23); `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.T_val`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.T_eq`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.obj_eq`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.unique`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.unique_functor`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.isStrongBundleMap_T`).** For a natural transformation $(T, \tau)$ from $\Phi$ to $\Psi$: $T(w) = (\tau(P(w)), \Phi(w))$ and $\Psi(w) = \mu'(\tau(P(w)), \Phi(w))$; $\Psi$ on objects and $T$ are determined by $\Phi$ and $\tau$, and so is $\Psi$ itself among strong bundle functors covering $\psi$; for a strong bundle functor $\Phi$, $T : W \to \mathbf X' \,{}_s\!\times_{P'} W'$ is a strong bundle map covering $\tau$. *Book:* Remark 10.4.9, pp. 502–503 (2017: Remark 10.4, p. 363). *Hidden hypotheses:* that $\Psi$ is a strong bundle functor, for the determination of $\Psi$ as a functor. *Deviation (explicit):* the second line of (10.23), printed with $\mu$, is read with $\mu'$ (Findings, item 46).

**V10.30 (Definition 10.4.10 (2017: 10.12) and its equivalence with Definition 10.4.8; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleNatTransMap`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.isStrongBundleNatTransMap`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleNatTransMap.toNatTrans`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatTrans.orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.StrongBundleNatEquiv.orbitMap_eq`).** A natural transformation in the sense of Definition 10.4.10 is a strong bundle map $T : W \to \mathbf X' \,{}_s\!\times_{P'} W'$ covering a natural transformation $\tau : \phi \to \psi$, with $T(w) = (\tau(P(w)), \Phi(w))$ and $\Psi(w) = \mu'(\tau(P(w)), \Phi(w))$. For strong bundle functors $\Phi$, $\Psi$ the two definitions agree; $\Phi \simeq \Psi$ implies $|\Phi| = |\Psi|$. *Book:* Definition 10.4.10 and the sentence after it, p. 503 (2017: Definition 10.12, p. 363). *Hidden hypotheses:* that $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are strong bundle functors, for Definition 10.4.10 ⇒ Definition 10.4.8. *Deviation (explicit):* none beyond the hypothesis (Findings, item 46).

**V10.31 (Definition 10.4.11 (2017: 10.13), the category $\mathcal{SEP}$; `Polyfold.SEP`, `Polyfold.SEP.Hom`, `Polyfold.SEP.equivalences`, `Polyfold.SEP.toEP`, `Polyfold.SEP.toEP_map_mem_equivalences`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleEquivalenceExamples.negSEPHom`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleEquivalenceExamples.negSEPHom_mem_equivalences`).** $\mathcal{SEP}$ is a category whose objects are the strong bundles over ep-groupoids and whose morphisms are the strong bundle functors $(\phi, \Phi)$; the strong bundle equivalences form a class $F$ containing the identities and closed under composition; the forgetful functor $\mathcal{SEP} \to \mathcal{EP}$ maps $F$ into $E$. The projection $(-\mathrm{id})^*(\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k) \to \mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k$ is a morphism in $F$. *Book:* Definition 10.4.11, p. 503 (2017: Definition 10.13, p. 364). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* a morphism carries both $\phi$ and $\Phi$, since $\Phi$ determines $\phi$ only on the image of $P$ (Findings, item 47).

**V10.32 (the properties (E1)–(E3) of the class $E$; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.isEquivalence_of_isIso`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.comp`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_5`).** Every isomorphism of the category $\mathcal{EP}$ is an equivalence; the composite of two equivalences is an equivalence; a functor naturally equivalent to an equivalence is an equivalence. *Book:* §10.3, (E1)–(E3), p. 483 (2017 p. 347). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 30).

**V10.33 (Definition 10.3.1 (2017: 10.4), diagrams and refinements; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.refl`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.precomp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_precomp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_of_naturallyEquivalent`).** A diagram $d : X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y$ consists of an ep-groupoid $A$, an equivalence $F : A \to X$ and an sc-smooth functor $\Phi : A \to Y$. A diagram $d' : X \xleftarrow{F'} A' \xrightarrow{\Phi'} Y$ is a refinement of $d$ if there is an equivalence $H : A' \to A$ with $F \circ H \simeq F'$ and $\Phi \circ H \simeq \Phi'$. Every diagram refines itself; for an equivalence $H : A' \to A$, $X \xleftarrow{F \circ H} A' \xrightarrow{\Phi \circ H} Y$ refines $d$; for $G \simeq F$ (an equivalence) and $\Psi \simeq \Phi$, $X \xleftarrow{G} A \xrightarrow{\Psi} Y$ refines $d$. *Book:* Definition 10.3.1, p. 484 (2017: Definition 10.4, p. 348), with the diagrams of p. 483 and the two examples after the definition. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the middle ep-groupoid is an object of $\mathcal{EP}$, so a diagram is a structure one universe above the types of objects and morphisms (Findings, item 30).

**V10.34 (Lemma 10.3.2 (2017: 10.3), refinements compose; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.lemma_10_3_2`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.trans`).** A refinement of a refinement of $d$ is a refinement of $d$. *Book:* Lemma 10.3.2, p. 484 (2017: Lemma 10.3, p. 348). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 31).

**V10.35 (Definition 10.3.3 (2017: 10.5), common refinements; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsCommonRefinement`).** $d''$ is a common refinement of $(d, d')$ if it refines both. *Book:* Definition 10.3.3, p. 485 (2017: Definition 10.5, p. 349). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 31).

**V10.36 (Lemma 10.3.4 (2017: 10.4), transitivity; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.lemma_10_3_4`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.trans`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.equiv`).** If $(d, d')$ and $(d', d'')$ have common refinements, so has $(d, d'')$: for $W$ refining $d$ by $H$ and $d'$ by $H'$, and $W'$ refining $d'$ by $K$ and $d''$ by $K'$, the diagram (10.11) $X \leftarrow W \times_{A'} W' \to Y$, formed with the weak fibred product of $H'$ and $K$, refines $d$ by $H \circ \pi_W$ and $d''$ by $K' \circ \pi_{W'}$. A refinement is equivalent to the refined diagram. *Book:* Lemma 10.3.4, p. 485 (2017: Lemma 10.4, p. 349), with (10.11), p. 486. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 31).

**V10.37 (Definition 10.3.5 (2017: 10.6), equivalence of diagrams; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.refl`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.symm`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.setoid`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.equiv_iff`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Examples.equiv_pairToPoint_id`).** Two diagrams are equivalent if they have a common refinement; this is an equivalence relation on the diagrams $X \to Y$. The diagram $\mathrm{pt} \leftarrow \mathbb Z\text{-pair} \to \mathrm{pt}$ with both legs the equivalence from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ is equivalent to $1_{\mathrm{pt}}$. *Book:* Definition 10.3.5, p. 486 (2017: Definition 10.6, p. 350). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the equivalence relation is a setoid on the type of diagrams; its quotient lives in the universe of the objects of $\mathcal{EP}$ (Findings, item 31).

**V10.38 (Lemma 10.3.6 (2017: 10.5), the map of orbit spaces of a diagram; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.continuous_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.orbitMap_orbitMap_F`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.lemma_10_3_6`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent.orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.orbitMap_comp`).** For a diagram $d$, $|d| = |\Phi| \circ |F|^{-1} : |X| \to |Y|$ is continuous; naturally equivalent functors induce the same map of orbit spaces; if $d'$ refines $d$, then $|d| = |d'|$, and equivalent diagrams have the same map. *Book:* Lemma 10.3.6, p. 488 (2017: Lemma 10.5, p. 351), with $|d|$ on p. 487. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 32).

**V10.39 (Definition 10.3.7 (2017: 10.7), the map $|[d]|$; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.orbitMapQ`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.orbitMapQ_mk`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isHomeomorph_orbitMap`).** $|[d]| : |X| \to |Y|$ is $|\Phi| \circ |F|^{-1}$ for any representative; if $\Phi$ is an equivalence too, it is a homeomorphism. *Book:* Definition 10.3.7 and the remark after it, p. 488 (2017: Definition 10.7, p. 351). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 32).

**V10.40 (Theorem 10.3.8 (2017: 10.3), the composition of classes, with its proof in Appendix §10.6.1; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.theorem_10_3_8`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.id`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.admissible`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.wfp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.wfpMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.projLeft_comp_wfpMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.projRight_comp_wfpMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.isEquivalence_wfpMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.assocFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.isEquivalence_assocFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_assoc`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.equiv_assoc`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_id_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_comp_id`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.of_comp_left`).** For $d : X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y$ and $e : Y \xleftarrow{G} B \xrightarrow{\Psi} Z$, the composite $X \xleftarrow{F \circ \pi_A} A \times_Y B \xrightarrow{\Psi \circ \pi_B} Z$, with the weak fibred product of $\Phi$ and $G$, is a diagram whose class depends only on the classes of $d$ and $e$; the composition of classes is associative, and the classes of $1_X = X \xleftarrow{1} X \xrightarrow{1} X$ are units. If $d'$ refines $d$ by $H$ and $e'$ refines $e$ by $K$, the composite of $d'$ and $e'$ refines that of $d$ and $e$ by the functor $L(a', \phi, b') = (H(a'), \tau_{B'}(b') \circ \phi \circ \tau_{A'}(a')^{-1}, K(b'))$, an equivalence. If $G$ and $G \circ L$ are equivalences, so is $L$. *Book:* Theorem 10.3.8, p. 488 (2017: Theorem 10.3, p. 352), proved in Appendix §10.6.1, pp. 509–515. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* $d.\mathrm{comp}\,e$ is the text's $[e] \circ [d]$; the two iterated weak fibred products of the associativity are related by a reassociation functor, an equivalence, where the text identifies them; $L$ is shown to be an equivalence by two out of three ($\pi_A \circ L = H \circ \pi_{A'}$); in the proof, $\tau_A$ in the naturality of $\tau_{B'}$, "$(\Phi \circ \pi_B) \circ L$", $[1_X] \circ [d]$ and $\tau(a, \phi, a)$ are read $\tau_{B'}$, $(\Psi \circ \pi_B) \circ L$, $[d] \circ [1_X]$ and $\tau(x, \phi, a)$ (possible misprints) (Findings, items 33, 60).

**V10.41 (Definition 10.3.9 (2017: 10.8), generalized maps and isomorphisms; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.homMk`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.IsGeneralizedIso`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isGeneralizedIso_iff_isIso`).** A generalized map $X \to Y$ is a class $[d]$ of diagrams; it is a generalized isomorphism if some generalized map $g : Y \to X$ composes with it to the units on both sides. The generalized isomorphisms are the isomorphisms of $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$. *Book:* Definition 10.3.9, p. 489 (2017: Definition 10.8, p. 352). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 34).

**V10.42 (Theorem 10.3.10 (2017: 10.4), generalized isomorphisms, with its proof in Appendix §10.6.2; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_10_3_10`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.symm`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.diagFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.isEquivalence_diagFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_comp_symm`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_id`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.equiv_comp_symm`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.equiv_symm_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isEquivalence_Φ_of_equiv_id`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.isEquivalence_toFunctor_of_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.isLocalScDiffeo_obj_of_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isEquivalence_Φ_of_equiv`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isIso_homMk_iff`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isIso_homMk`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.inv_homMk`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeoAt_of_injOn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt.exists_injOn`).** (1) $[X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y]$ is a generalized isomorphism if and only if $\Phi$ is an equivalence; (2) every inverse is then $[Y \xleftarrow{\Phi} A \xrightarrow{F} X]$. An sc-smooth map injective near $x$ with an sc-smooth local right inverse through $x$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism at $x$. *Book:* Theorem 10.3.10, p. 489 (2017: Theorem 10.4, p. 353), proved in Appendix §10.6.2, pp. 515–519. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* in (C1) the text's $A \times_X B$, $\mathrm{mor}_Y(\Psi(a), \Psi(a'))$ and "$x$" are read $A \times_Y B$, $\mathrm{mor}_X(\Psi(b), \Psi(b'))$ and "$y$", and in (C2) $(s|U)^{-1}(b')$ is read $(s|U)^{-1}(\Psi(b'))$ (possible misprints); the step of (C2) that $\Gamma'$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism does not hold as we read it without the other half of (C2), and the local sc-diffeomorphism property of $\Phi$ is proved from a local right inverse obtained from the equivalence $\Phi \circ \pi_{A'}$ and from local injectivity (Findings, items 34, 61).

**V10.43 (Proposition 10.3.11 (2017: 10.6), orbit maps compose; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitMap_homMk`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.continuous_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitMap_id`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.orbitMap_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.proposition_10_3_11`).** For generalized maps $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$, $|g \circ f| = |g| \circ |f|$; $|f|$ is continuous and $|1_X| = \mathrm{id}$. *Book:* Proposition 10.3.11, p. 490 (2017: Proposition 10.6, p. 353), with the computation before it. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 35).

**V10.44 (Definition 10.3.12 (2017: 10.9), the category $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.toEP_of`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.of_toEP`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.homMk_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.id_eq`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.homMk_eq_homMk_iff`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.homMk_surjective`).** $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ is a category with the ep-groupoids as objects and the generalized maps as morphisms, composed by Theorem 10.3.8, with units $[1_X]$; $[d] = [d']$ if and only if $d$ and $d'$ are equivalent, and every morphism is some $[d]$. *Book:* Definition 10.3.12, p. 490 (2017: Definition 10.9, p. 354). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the objects are a copy of those of $\mathcal{EP}$ (a one-field structure), and $[d] ≫ [e] = [d.\mathrm{comp}\,e]$ is the text's $[e] \circ [d]$ (Findings, item 35).

**V10.45 (Theorem 10.3.14 (2017: 10.5), the localization functor; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.ofFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_ofFunctor_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.localizationFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.localizationFunctor_obj`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.localizationFunctor_map`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_10_3_14`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isInvertedBy_localizationFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.inv_localizationFunctor_map`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.homMk_eq`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Examples.pairToPointEP`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Examples.not_isIso_pairToPointEP`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Examples.isGeneralizedIso_pairToPoint`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Examples.inv_localizationFunctor_map_pairToPoint`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isLocalization`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.universal_property`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.map_eq_of_naturallyEquivalent`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.secFunctor`).** There is a functor $i : \mathcal{EP} \to \mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$, the identity on objects, with $i(\Phi) = [X \xleftarrow{1} X \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y]$; for an equivalence $F$, $i(F)$ is a generalized isomorphism and every inverse is $[Y \xleftarrow{F} X \xrightarrow{1} X]$. $i$ inverts the class $E$ in the sense of Mathlib, and every generalized map is $i(\Phi) \circ i(F)^{-1}$. The equivalence from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ to the point is not an isomorphism of $\mathcal{EP}$, but its image under $i$ is invertible. *Book:* Theorem 10.3.14, p. 491 (2017: Theorem 10.5, p. 354), with p. 487 for $[d] = i(\Phi) \circ i(F)^{-1}$. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* in the proof, the text calls $d_{\Psi \circ \Phi}$ a refinement of (10.13) by $\pi_X$; with Definition 10.3.1 it is (10.13) that refines $d_{\Psi \circ \Phi}$, which is what is proved; the universal property of the localization, mentioned on p. 483, is proved: a functor inverting $E$ identifies naturally equivalent functors, through the section $x \mapsto (x, \tau(x), F'(x))$ of $X \times_Y Y \to X$ (`Polyfold.EPLocalization.map_eq_of_naturallyEquivalent`), so every such functor factors uniquely through $i$ (`Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.universal_property`) and $i$ is a localization in Mathlib's sense (`Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isLocalization`; gap G.117 closed) (Findings, item 36).

**V10.46 (Theorem 10.3.15 (2017: 10.6), the orbit space functor; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_10_3_15`).** There is a functor $|\cdot| : \mathcal{EP}(E^{-1}) \to \mathrm{TOP}$ taking $X$ to $|X|$ and $[X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y]$ to $|\Phi| \circ |F|^{-1}$. *Book:* Theorem 10.3.15, p. 492 (2017: Theorem 10.6, p. 355). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* TOP is Mathlib's `TopCat` (Findings, item 35).

**V10.47 (Proposition 10.3.17, (LUC) under generalized isomorphisms; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.exists_diagram_of_isGeneralizedIso`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.iff_of_isGeneralizedIso`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.proposition_10_3_17`).** A generalized isomorphism is represented by a diagram whose two legs are equivalences; hence a property of ep-groupoids invariant under equivalences is invariant under generalized isomorphisms, and for a generalized isomorphism $X \to Y$, $X$ has (LUC) if and only if $Y$ has it. *Book:* Proposition 10.3.17, p. 492 (new in the 2021 edition), with the argument before Proposition 10.3.16. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* "if one has it, so has the other" is stated as an equivalence (Findings, item 38).

**V10.48 (Remark 10.3.18 (2017: 10.3), equivalence of pairs $(X, \beta)$; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.OrbitChart`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.OrbitChart.Rel`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.OrbitChart.Rel.refl`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.OrbitChart.Rel.symm`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.OrbitChart.Rel.trans`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.OrbitChart.setoid`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.OrbitChart.rel_pairEP_pointEP`).** For a space $Z$, pairs $(X, \beta)$ with $\beta : |X| \to Z$ a homeomorphism, with $(X', \beta')$ equivalent to $(X, \beta)$ if some generalized isomorphism $f : X \to X'$ has $\beta' \circ |f| = \beta$, form a set with an equivalence relation. The pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ with the orbit map of its equivalence to the point, and the point with the identity, are equivalent pairs. *Book:* Remark 10.3.18, pp. 492–493 (2017: Remark 10.3, p. 355). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* the claim that $f$ is in general not unique is not formalized here (gap G.119, closed since: V10.60, by the base classes of the example of Remark 10.5.5); the metrizability of $Z$ plays no role in the relation and is not assumed (Findings, item 39).

**V10.49 (Definition 10.3.20, the subcategories of ep-groupoids with (LR); `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPreg`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLocReg`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Examples.pointReg`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Examples.pointLocReg`).** $\mathcal{EP}_{reg}$ and $\mathcal{EP}_{reg}(E^{-1})$ are the full subcategories of $\mathcal{EP}$ and $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ on the ep-groupoids with the local regularity property; the point ep-groupoid is an object of both. *Book:* Definition 10.3.20, p. 494 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 39).

**V10.50 (Theorem 10.3.21, invariance under generalized isomorphisms; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_10_3_21`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_10_3_21_all`).** For a generalized isomorphism $X \to Y$, $X$ has (LR), (LUC), (SLR), (SLUC), respectively (ZHOU), if and only if $Y$ has it. *Book:* Theorem 10.3.21, p. 495 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the proof, left to the reader in the text, applies Propositions 10.1.9, 10.1.16, 10.1.17, 10.1.18 and 10.1.19 to the two legs of a representing diagram; the parts (LR) and (SLR) were not formalized in the first edition of this page (gap G.118, closed since: V10.50, V10.64; Findings, items 16, 38).

**V10.51 (the diagrams of strong bundles, their refinements and equivalence; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.IsRefinement`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.precomp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.isRefinement_precomp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.isRefinement_of_natEquiv`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.IsRefinement.refl`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.IsRefinement.trans`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.IsCommonRefinement`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.Equiv`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.Equiv.refl`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.Equiv.symm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.IsRefinement.equiv`, `Polyfold.SEP.NatEquiv`, `Polyfold.SEP.NatEquiv.comp_left`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.cls`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.cls_eq_cls_of_equiv`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.cls_eq_cls_iff`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.foldDiagram`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.isRefinement_foldDiagram`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.cls_foldDiagram`).** A diagram $D : W \xleftarrow{\Phi} W'' \xrightarrow{\Psi} W'$ between strong bundles $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ and $(P' : W' \to X', \mu')$ over ep-groupoids consists of a strong bundle $(P'' : W'' \to X'', \mu'')$ over an ep-groupoid, a strong bundle equivalence $\Phi$ and a strong bundle functor $\Psi$ (morphisms of $\mathcal{SEP}$). $D'$ refines $D$ if a strong bundle equivalence $H : W''' \to W''$ has $\Phi \circ H \simeq \Phi'$ and $\Psi \circ H \simeq \Psi'$ (natural equivalence of strong bundle functors, Definition 10.4.8); every diagram refines itself, composing both legs with a strong bundle equivalence or replacing them by naturally equivalent ones gives a refinement, and a refinement of a refinement is one. Two diagrams are equivalent if they have a common refinement, an equivalence relation (V10.69); a generalized strong bundle map $[D] : W \to W'$ is the class of $D$, and $[D] = [D']$ iff $D$ and $D'$ have a common refinement. For $W' = \mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^n$, $W' \xleftarrow{P'} (-\mathrm{id})^*W' \xrightarrow{P'} W'$ refines $1_{W'}$, so its class is $[1_{W'}]$. *Book:* §10.5, p. 504 (2017 p. 364), "following our earlier construction". *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; the classes are formed for the generated equivalence relation, which is having a common refinement by the transitivity, the strong bundle version of Lemma 10.3.4 (V10.69) (gap G.123, closed since; Findings, items 18, 50).

**V10.52 ($[D]$ covers $[d]$, and the map $|[D]|$; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.base`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.total`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.IsRefinement.base`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.Equiv.base`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.Equiv.total`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.base`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.total`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.orbitMap`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.continuous_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.Equiv.orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.orbitMap`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.orbitMap_eq_total`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.continuous_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.SEP.baseEP`, `Polyfold.SEP.totalEP`).** A diagram $D$ covers the diagram $d : X \xleftarrow{\phi} X'' \xrightarrow{\psi} X'$ of the underlying ep-groupoids, and refinements and equivalent diagrams cover refinements and equivalent diagrams; so $[D]$ covers a generalized map $[d] : X \to X'$ (Definition 10.3.9), and it induces a generalized map $(W, \mathbf W) \to (W', \mathbf W')$ of the total-space ep-groupoids as well. $|[D]| = |\Psi| \circ |\Phi|^{-1} : |W| \to |W'|$ is continuous and does not depend on the representative. *Book:* §10.5, p. 504 (2017 pp. 364–365). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* $|\Phi|$ is a homeomorphism by Definition 10.4.1 (1), and $|[D]|$ is the orbit map of the diagram of total spaces (Lemma 10.3.6) (Findings, item 51).

**V10.53 (the symbolic diagram (10.24) and the commutative square $|\mathscr D|$; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.orbitMap_square`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.orbitMap_square`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.orbitMap_orbitMap_Φ`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.square_10_24`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.square_10_24`, `Polyfold.SEP.projEP`).** $|P'| \circ |[D]| = |[d]| \circ |P|$ as maps $|W| \to |X'|$, for diagrams and for their classes. *Book:* §10.5, pp. 504–505 (2017: Remark 10.5, p. 365). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the symbolic diagram (10.24) itself has no formal content; its version with the generalized maps $i(P) = [W \xleftarrow{1} W \xrightarrow{P} X]$, $i(P')$ as vertical arrows, left to the reader, commutes in $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ (`Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.square_10_24`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.square_10_24`; gap G.124 closed); the bottom arrow $|[d]|$ is printed $|X| \to |X|$, as are the bottom arrows of (10.24) and of the diagram after Remark 10.5.3, in both editions; we read $X'$ (possible misprint) (Findings, item 51).

**V10.54 (the homomorphism $\gamma : G_x \to G'_{x'}$; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isotropyHom`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isotropyHom_spec`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.bijective_isotropyHom`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.exists_isotropyData`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.exists_germ_q`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isotropyHom_conj`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.exists_lift_Q`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsLocalMap₂`).** For a diagram $d : X \xleftarrow{\phi} X'' \xrightarrow{\psi} X'$ of ep-groupoids and $x, x'$ with $|[d]|(|x|) = |x'|$ there are $x''$ and morphisms $a : \phi(x'') \to x$, $b : \psi(x'') \to x'$. For such data, $\gamma$, the composite of $g \mapsto a^{-1} \circ g \circ a$, of the inverse of $\phi : G_{x''} \to G_{\phi(x'')}$, of $\psi : G_{x''} \to G_{\psi(x'')}$ and of $\ell \mapsto b \circ \ell \circ b^{-1}$, is a group homomorphism with $\gamma(g) = b \circ \psi(k) \circ b^{-1}$ for the $k$ with $\phi(k) = a^{-1} \circ g \circ a$, and it is a group isomorphism when $\psi$ is an equivalence. *Book:* §10.5, p. 505 (2017 p. 365). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* stated for every diagram of ep-groupoids (for $D$ it is applied to $d$), with the bijectivity for $\psi$ an equivalence added; the 2021 first step $a^{-1} \circ g \circ a$ is used (the 2017 text has $a \circ g \circ a^{-1}$); the equivariant germ $q = Q_b \circ \psi \circ Q_a^{-1}$ on a natural representation, sc-smooth with $q(x) = x'$ and $q(g * z) = \gamma(g) * q(z)$, and its lift $Q = H_b \circ \Psi \circ H_a^{-1}$, a local strong bundle map with $P' \circ Q = q \circ P$, (10.25), equivariant on the natural lifts, are stated for each choice of the data, since they depend on the representative (`Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.exists_germ_q`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.exists_lift_Q`; gap G.124 closed; Findings, item 52).

**V10.55 (Definition 10.5.1 (2017: 10.14), the category $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.idHom`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.localizationPrefunctor`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.localizationPrefunctor_map_id`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.id`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.ofHom`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.category`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.homMk`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.homMk_comp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.id_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.homMk_eq_homMk_iff`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.homMk_surjective`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.localizationFunctor`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.localizationFunctor_toPrefunctor`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.isInvertedBy_localizationFunctor`).** The objects of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ are the strong bundles over ep-groupoids and its morphisms $W \to W'$ the generalized strong bundle maps; with the composition of V10.70 and the identities $[1_W]$ they form a category, every morphism is a class $[D]$, and $[D] = [D']$ iff $D$ and $D'$ have a common refinement. $\Psi \mapsto [W \xleftarrow{1} W \xrightarrow{\Psi} W']$, which maps $1_W$ to $[1_W]$, is a functor $\mathcal{SEP} \to \mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ (the strong bundle analogue of Theorem 10.3.14) that inverts the strong bundle equivalences. *Book:* Definition 10.5.1, p. 506 (2017: Definition 10.14, p. 366). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (explicit):* the composition, which the text does not spell out, is that of V10.70; until it was constructed, $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ was formalized as a quiver (gap G.123, closed since; Findings, items 18, 53).

**V10.56 (Definition 10.5.2 (2017: 10.15), generalized strong bundle isomorphisms; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.IsGeneralizedIso`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.symm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.isGeneralizedIso_symm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.isGeneralizedIso_ofHom`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.negDiagram`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.isGeneralizedIso_negDiagram`).** A generalized strong bundle map is a generalized strong bundle isomorphism if it is the class of a diagram $W \xleftarrow{\Phi} W'' \xrightarrow{\Psi} W'$ in which both $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are strong bundle equivalences. The reversed diagram of such a representative, and $[W \xleftarrow{1} W \xrightarrow{\Psi} W']$ for a strong bundle equivalence $\Psi$, give generalized strong bundle isomorphisms; for $W' = \mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^n$ and the projection $P' : (-\mathrm{id})^*W' \to W'$ over $-\mathrm{id}$, $[(-\mathrm{id})^*W' \xleftarrow{1} (-\mathrm{id})^*W' \xrightarrow{P'} W']$ is one. *Book:* Definition 10.5.2, p. 506 (2017: Definition 10.15, p. 366). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, items 53, 59).

**V10.57 (Remark 10.5.3, the comparison with Theorem 10.3.10; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.remark_10_5_3`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.isIso_of_isGeneralizedIso`).** A generalized strong bundle isomorphism $[D] : W \to W'$ covers a generalized isomorphism $[d] : X \to X'$ of the base ep-groupoids, induces a generalized isomorphism of the total-space ep-groupoids, $|[D]|$ is a homeomorphism, and $[D]$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$. *Book:* Remark 10.5.3, p. 506 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the remark says that a result similar to Theorem 10.3.10 can be proved in the strong bundle case and that it is built into Definition 10.5.2; we read this as "generalized strong bundle isomorphisms are isomorphisms of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$", which is proved (V10.71); the converse half of the similar result, that every isomorphism of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ is one, is proved for the base functor only (V10.71); the consequences for the base and the total spaces are proved through Theorem 10.3.10 (gap G.123, closed since except the converse half; Findings, items 19, 53).

**V10.58 (the push-forward and pull-back along a diagram, and their independence of the representative; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pushforward`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pullback`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pushforward_eq_of_isRefinement`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.π_μ`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.π_eq_π_of_isFunctorialSection`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.eq_of_forall_π_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.π_pushforward`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.base_orbitMap_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pushforward_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pullback_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`).** For a diagram $D$ with both legs strong bundle equivalences, $D_*f = \Psi_*\Phi^*f$ and $D^*g = \Phi_*\Psi^*g$, the push-forward along the reversed diagram. If $D'$ refines $D$, both with second legs strong bundle equivalences, then $\Psi'_*\Phi'^*f = \Psi_*\Phi^*f$ for every section functor $f$, by the text's computation through Propositions 10.4.2–10.4.4. A section functor $g$ is determined by the orbits $|g(x')|$ in $|W'|$, and $|(D_*f)(x')| = |[D]|(|f(x)|)$ whenever $|[d]|(|x|) = |x'|$; hence any two such diagrams with the same map $|D|$ have the same push-forward and the same pull-back on section functors. *Book:* §10.5, p. 507 (2017 p. 367), the paragraph before Theorem 10.5.4. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the independence is proved for any two diagrams with the same map of orbit spaces, not only along refinements; the text's own step is proved as printed (Findings, item 54).

**V10.59 (Theorem 10.5.4 (2017: 10.9), without the Fred part; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.rep`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pushforward`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pullback`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pushforward_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pullback_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.theorem_10_5_4`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.invOn_pullback_pushforward`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.bijOn_pushforward`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.bijOn_pushforward_plus`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.bijOn_pushforward_negDiagram`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.pushforward_foldDiagram`).** For a generalized strong bundle isomorphism $[D] : (P, \mu) \to (P', \mu')$: $[D]_*f = \Psi_*\Phi^*f$ and $[D]^*g = \Phi_*\Psi^*g$ for every representative with both legs strong bundle equivalences; $[D]_* : \Gamma(P, \mu) \to \Gamma(P', \mu')$ and $[D]^*$ are mutually inverse bijections of the sc-smooth section functors; the push-forward along the reversed diagram is $[D]^*$; the same holds for $\mathrm{sc}^+$-section functors; and $|[D]| = |[D']|$ implies $[D]_* = [D']_*$ and $[D]^* = [D']^*$. For the example of V10.56 $[D]_*$ is a bijection, and the push-forward along $W' \xleftarrow{P'} (-\mathrm{id})^*W' \xrightarrow{P'} W'$ is the identity of $\Gamma(W')$. *Book:* Theorem 10.5.4, pp. 507–508 (2017: Theorem 10.9, p. 367). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* the preservation of sc-Fredholm section functors is not formalized, as for Theorem 10.4.5 (gap G.125); "isomorphism" of the vector spaces $\Gamma$ is read as mutually inverse bijections, $\Gamma(P, \mu)$ having no vector space structure in the project (Findings, item 55).

**V10.60 (Remark 10.5.5, $|[D]| = |[D']|$ does not give $[D] = [D']$; `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.remark_10_5_5`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.pushforward_inv_eq_pushforward_id`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.z3EpBundle`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.z3InvHom`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.z3InvHom_mem_equivalences`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.orbitMap_ofHom_z3InvHom`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.base_orbitMap_ofHom_z3InvHom`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsotropyRel`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isotropyRel_isotropyHom`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.isotropyRel_iff`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.isotropyRel_iff`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.isotropyRel_id`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationExamples.not_isotropyRel_inv`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.remark_10_5_3`).** For the strong bundle $W = \mathbb R \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R$ over $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ (trivial action, $\mu((g, x), w) = w$) and the strong bundle equivalence $\mathrm{Inv}$ covering $(g, x) \mapsto (g^{-1}, x)$, $[1_W]$ and $[W \xleftarrow{1} W \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Inv}} W]$ are generalized strong bundle isomorphisms with $|[\mathrm{Inv}]| = |[1_W]|$ and with the same map of base orbit spaces, but $[\mathrm{Inv}] \neq [1_W]$, and already their base classes differ; nevertheless $[\mathrm{Inv}]_* = [1_W]_*$ on section functors. The classes are separated by the relation of the homomorphisms $\gamma$ (the union of their graphs over all choices), which is invariant under refinement and equivalence of diagrams of ep-groupoids: for $[1]$ the generator of $G_0 = \mathbb Z/3$ is related to itself, for $[\mathrm{Inv}]$ only to its inverse. *Book:* Remark 10.5.5, p. 508 (new in the 2021 edition), with the paragraph before it. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the text gives no example; the positive half is the last assertion of Theorem 10.5.4 (V10.59). The base classes are two distinct generalized isomorphisms of $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ (Remark 10.5.3) with the same orbit map, an instance of the non-uniqueness claimed in Remark 10.3.18 (gap G.119, closed since: V10.60); the example has the local regularity property, so Theorems 10.3.19 and 10.5.7, and the 2017 Theorems 10.7 and 10.10, do not hold as we read them (V10.65, V10.67; Findings, items 56, 58).

**V10.62 (Proposition 10.1.9, (LR) under equivalences; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_9`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.TransportChart`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.exists_transportChart`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.TransportChart.conj`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.TransportChart.bijective_conj`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.TransportChart.Q_Φ`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.TransportChart.exists_naturalRep_push`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.TransportChart.exists_naturalRep_pull`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.HasLR`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isLR_iff_hasLR`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.hasLR_iff_of_equivariant`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eqOn_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eqOn_Φ`, `Polyfold.EquivalenceLRExamples.nonempty_transportChart_pointEP`).** If $F : X \to Y$ is an equivalence, $X$ has the local regularity property (Definition 7.4.19) if and only if $Y$ has it. **V10.65 (Theorem 10.3.19 (2017: 10.7) does not hold as we read it; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.Theorem_10_3_19`, `Polyfold.LocalizationLRCounterexample.not_theorem_10_3_19`, `Polyfold.LocalizationLRCounterexample.theorem_10_3_19_counterexample`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isLR_trivialZ3`, `Polyfold.LocalizationLRCounterexample.not_naturallyEquivalent_id_inv`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.not_isEffective_trivialZ3`).** The statement "if one of $X$, $Y$ has (LR), generalized isomorphisms $f, f' : X \to Y$ with $|f| = |f'|$ are equal" is false: $X = \mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ with the trivial action has (LR), its orbits being points, and $[X \xleftarrow{1} X \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Inv}} X]$ and $[1_X]$, $\mathrm{Inv}(g, x) = (g^{-1}, x)$, are generalized isomorphisms with the same orbit map that differ (the base part of V10.60). **V10.66 (Theorem 10.3.19 for an effective target; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_10_3_19_of_isEffective`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.naturallyEquivalent_of_isEffective`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.eqOn_of_isEffective`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.eqOn_unit_of_isEffective`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_10_3_19_of_isEffective_hypotheses`, `Polyfold.EquivalenceLREffectiveExamples.naturallyEquivalent_of_isEffective_hypotheses`).** If one of $X$, $Y$ has (LR) and $Y$ is effective, generalized isomorphisms $f, f' : X \to Y$ with $|f| = |f'|$ are equal. On the way: in an effective ep-groupoid a continuous family $v \mapsto k(v) \in G_v$ on an open set of objects is the family of units; over an effective target two continuous families $\alpha_z, \alpha'_z : H(z) \to H'(z)$ on an open set agree when $H$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects; and equivalences $H, H' : X \to Y$ with $|H| = |H'|$, $X$ with (LR) and $Y$ effective are naturally equivalent, by an sc-smooth natural transformation on all of $X$. **V10.68 (Theorem 10.2.2 (2017: 10.2) for strong bundles, the weak fibred product of strong bundles; `Polyfold.SBWeakFibredProduct.wfpSEP`, `Polyfold.SBWeakFibredProduct.projX`, `Polyfold.SBWeakFibredProduct.projZ`, `Polyfold.SBWeakFibredProduct.theorem_10_2_2`, `Polyfold.SBWeakFibredProduct.theorem_10_2_2_right`, `Polyfold.SBWeakFibredProduct.nonempty_wfpSEP`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.pullbackAlong`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isStrongBundleEquivalence_pullbackProjFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.transportFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.invLiftFunctor`, `Polyfold.SEP.pullbackAlong`, `Polyfold.SEP.coneHom`, `Polyfold.SEP.natEquiv_cone`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleWeakFibredProductExamples.theorem_10_2_2_negSEPHom`).** For a strong bundle equivalence $\Phi : W \to W'$ covering $\phi : X \to X'$ and a strong bundle functor $\Psi : W'' \to W'$ covering $\psi : X'' \to X'$, the weak fibred product $W \times_{W'} W''$ is the pull-back $\pi_Z^*W''$ over the weak fibred product $X \times_{X'} X''$ of $\phi$ and $\psi$, with $\Pi_Z((x, \varphi, z), w'') = w''$ covering $\pi_Z$ and $\Pi_X((x, \varphi, z), w'') = \Phi_x^{-1}(\mu'(\varphi^{-1}, \Psi(w'')))$ covering $\pi_X$, where $\Phi_x$ is the fibrewise isomorphism of Proposition 10.4.4. $\Pi_Z$ is a strong bundle equivalence, $\Phi \circ \Pi_X \simeq \Psi \circ \Pi_Z$ (Definition 10.4.8), $\Pi_X$ is a strong bundle equivalence when $\Psi$ is one, and $W \times_{W'} W''$ is nonempty when $W''$ is. **V10.69 (Lemma 10.3.4 (2017: 10.4) for strong bundles, transitivity; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.lemma_10_3_4`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.Equiv.trans`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.equivalence_equiv`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.cls_eq_cls_iff`).** The equivalence of diagrams of strong bundles is transitive: if $w$ refines $D$ by $H$ and $D'$ by $H'$, and $w'$ refines $D'$ by $K$ and $D''$ by $K'$, the diagram on the weak fibred product of $H'$ and $K$ (V10.68) refines $D$ by $H \circ \Pi_X$ and $D''$ by $K' \circ \Pi_Z$. **V10.71 (Theorem 10.3.10 (2017: 10.4) for strong bundles; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.theorem_10_3_10`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.isIso_of_isGeneralizedIso`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.inv_homMk`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.equiv_comp_symm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.equiv_symm_comp`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.baseFunctor`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.isEquivalence_base_of_isIso`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.equivalences_Ψ_of_isIso`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.isIso_homMk_iff`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SEPLoc.isIso_iff_isGeneralizedIso`, `Polyfold.SEP.equivalences_of_natEquiv_comp`, `Polyfold.SEP.exists_isStrongBundleIsoOn`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.fibInj_Ψ_of_equiv`, `Polyfold.StrongBundleLocalizationCategoryExamples.isIso_homMk_negDiagram`).** $[W \xleftarrow{\Phi} W'' \xrightarrow{\Psi} W']$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ if and only if $\Psi$ is a strong bundle equivalence (Definition 10.4.1 in full), and then every inverse of it is $[W' \xleftarrow{\Psi} W'' \xrightarrow{\Phi} W]$; so the isomorphisms of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ are exactly the generalized strong bundle isomorphisms of Definition 10.5.2. **V10.72 (Proposition 10.4.6, (LR) under strong bundle equivalences; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_6`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.exists_transport`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.transport_Γ`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.hasLRLocal_iff_of_equivariant`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.HasLRLocal`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isLRLocal_iff_hasLRLocal`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsLocalIso₂`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsLocalIso₂.comp`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsLocalIso₂.symm`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.IsLocalIsoOn.exists_isLocalIso₂`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isLocalIso₂_lrAct`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsLRLocal`).** For strong bundles $(P : V \to X, \mu)$, $(Q : W \to Y, \nu)$ over ep-groupoids and a strong bundle equivalence $\Phi : V \to W$ covering $\phi$, $V$ has the local regularity property for strong bundles (Definition 8.4.2, with local strong bundle isomorphisms of $W|U(x)$) iff $W$ has. **V10.73 (Proposition 10.4.7, natural families for strong bundle equivalences; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_7`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.proposition_10_4_7'`, `Polyfold.GapP2_GBundleFamilyExamples.proposition_10_4_7_hypotheses`, `Polyfold.SEP.exists_family_of_isLRLocal`).** For strong bundle equivalences $\Phi, \Psi$ covering $\phi, \psi$ with $|\Phi| = |\Psi|$, the target bundle having the local regularity property (`IsLRLocal`), every $x$ and every open $O \ni x$ have a natural representation $U(x) \subseteq O$ and an sc-smooth $z \mapsto \alpha_z : \phi(z) \to \psi(z)$ on $U(x)$ with $\nu(\alpha_z, \Phi(v)) = \Psi(v)$ whenever $P(v) = z$. **V10.74 (the full subcategory $\mathcal{EP}_{lreg}$; `Polyfold.EP.lreg`, `Polyfold.EP.Lreg`, `Polyfold.EP.fullyFaithful_ι_lreg`, `Polyfold.EP.lreg_iff_of_isEquivalence`, `Polyfold.EP.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_lreg`, `Polyfold.EP.lreg_pointEP`, `Polyfold.EP.Lreg.point`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.lreg`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.lreg_A_of_lreg`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isClosedUnderIsomorphisms_lreg`).** The ep-groupoids with the local regularity property (Definition 7.4.19) form a full subcategory $\mathcal{EP}_{lreg}$ of $\mathcal{EP}$ (Mathlib's full subcategory of an object property; the inclusion is fully faithful). The property passes along equivalences, so it is closed under the isomorphisms of $\mathcal{EP}$ and of $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$, and the middle of a diagram out of an object of $\mathcal{EP}_{lreg}$ has it; the point ep-groupoid is an object. *Book:* §10.1, p. 461 (new in the 2021 edition), the subcategory generated by the ep-groupoids with the local regularity property. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; "generated by" is the full subcategory on these objects (gap G.111 closed; Findings, item 7).

The appendix's side remark that $Y$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb R^2 \setminus \{(0,t) \mid t \neq 0\}$ is not formalized; Remark 10.1.8 does not use it. A variant with the moving projections of Remark 4.1.3 and the opposite sign convention for $\eta$ is kept (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouSigma.remark_10_1_8`) (gap G.112 closed; Findings, item 7).

### What is not verified in this chapter

- p. 461, the full subcategory $\mathcal{EP}_{lreg}$ of ep-groupoids with the local regularity property: not formalized, not a numbered item (gap G.111; Findings, item 7); closed since: V10.74, the full subcategory, closed under the isomorphisms of $\mathcal{EP}$ and $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$.
- p. 467, Remark 10.1.8 and Appendix §10.6.3, p. 519 (Zhou's example of a $\beta$ with $|\beta(y)| = |y|$ not given by the group): it needs the weighted Sobolev sc-structure and the sc-retraction of the appendix (gap G.112; Findings, item 7); closed since: V10.75, as printed, on the appendix's scale with its projections. Not verified: the appendix's side remark that $Y$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb R^2 \setminus \{(0,t) \mid t \neq 0\}$, which Remark 10.1.8 does not use.

- p. 470, Proposition 10.1.10 (2017: 10.4): sc-smooth families $\alpha_z : F(z) \to G(z)$ for $|F| = |G|$, and $|TF| = |TG|$; it assumes (LR) and uses Proposition 10.1.9; the example of Remark 10.1.11 satisfies (1) (V10.8) (gap G.114; Findings, items 7, 8); closed since: V10.63, with (LR) on one side only (Findings, item 16).
