## 12. Chapter 11 (HWZ, Part II, §§11.1–11.6 (2017 §§11.1–11.6)): verified for the tangent functor and faces up to equivalence, sc-differential forms up to equivalence, push-forwards and pull-backs of branched ep⁺-subgroupoids with their tangents, boundaries and orientations, auxiliary norms and multisection functors under generalized strong bundle isomorphisms, proper coverings and proper strong bundle coverings up to equivalence with their localizations, and the canonical measures and boundary measures under generalized isomorphisms, with the readings recorded below (the intersection clause of Proposition 11.1.6 does not hold as we read it), except the boundary operations of Theorem 11.3.9 along equivalences; Theorems 11.4.4 and 11.4.5 are verified with the text's hypotheses for every $n \ge 1$

Chapter 11 (pp. 521–566 (2017 pp. 375–416); numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021), with the 2017 text's in parentheses) studies how the notions of Chapters 8 and 9 behave under equivalences and generalized maps. §11.1 extends the tangent functor to $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ (Theorem 11.1.1 (2017: 11.1)), shows that generalized isomorphisms preserve the degeneracy index (Proposition 11.1.2 (2017: 11.1)), defines faces in the ep-groupoid sense (Definition 11.1.3 (2017: 11.1), Example 11.1.4 (2017: 11.1)) and shows that equivalences and generalized isomorphisms induce bijections of faces (Remark 11.1.5, Proposition 11.1.6, Remark 11.1.7, Proposition 11.1.8 (2017: Remark 11.1, Proposition 11.2, Remark 11.2, Proposition 11.3)). §11.2 carries sc-differential forms along equivalences and generalized maps (Theorem 11.2.1, Lemmas 11.2.2, 11.2.4–11.2.6, Definitions 11.2.3, 11.2.7, Propositions 11.2.8, 11.2.9 (2017: Theorem 11.2, Lemmas 11.1–11.4, Definitions 11.2, 11.3, Propositions 11.4, 11.5)). §11.3 defines the pull-back and the push-forward of functors $\Theta : X \to \mathbb Q^+$ along equivalences (Definition 11.3.1, Lemma 11.3.2 (2017: Definition 11.4, Lemma 11.5)) and along generalized isomorphisms (pp. 536–537), shows that they preserve branched ep⁺-subgroupoids and their properties (Theorem 11.3.3 (2017: 11.3)), and continues with section functors of the bundles of oriented tangent sets, orientations, tangents and boundaries (Lemma 11.3.4 to Theorem 11.3.9 (2017: Lemma 11.6 to Theorem 11.7)). §11.4 transforms the canonical measures and boundary measures (Theorems 11.4.1, 11.4.4 (2017: 11.8, 11.9), Remark 11.4.3 (2017: 11.3), and the effective versions, Theorems 11.4.2 and 11.4.5, new in the 2021 edition). §11.5 carries auxiliary norms and sc⁺-multisections along generalized strong bundle isomorphisms (Proposition 11.5.1, Lemma 11.5.2, Proposition 11.5.3 (2017: Proposition 11.6, Lemma 11.7, Proposition 11.7)). §11.6 studies proper covering functors up to equivalence: their morphism maps (Lemma 11.6.1, new in the 2021 edition), the fibres as translation groupoids (Lemmas 11.6.2, 11.6.3 (2017: 11.8, 11.9)), functors, equivalences and natural transformations between proper coverings (Definitions 11.6.4, 11.6.5 (2017: 11.6, 11.7)), the weak fibred product (Theorem 11.6.6 (2017: 11.10)), diagrams and their common refinements (Definition 11.6.7, Proposition 11.6.8 (2017: Definition 11.8, Proposition 11.8)), the localization $\mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$ (pp. 561–563) and, in Remark 11.6.9 (2017: 11.4), proper strong bundle coverings.

What is verified. In §11.1 Theorem 11.1.1, Proposition 11.1.2, Remark 11.1.7 and Definition 11.1.3 are verified as stated, the last with faces recorded by their object sets (V11.1–V11.3, V11.7); Example 11.1.4 holds for $[0, \infty)^2 \oplus W$ with any sc-Banach space $W$ (V11.4); the bijections of faces of Remark 11.1.5, quoted there from the literature, are proved (V11.5); Proposition 11.1.6 is verified for the bijection $[d]_*$, the faces as tame ep-groupoids and the generalized isomorphisms $[d]_F$, with the intersection clause in a corrected form, and Proposition 11.1.8 as stated (V11.6, V11.8). §11.2 is verified as stated, with $F_*$ defined as the inverse of $F^*$ (V11.9–V11.13). In §11.3 Definition 11.3.1, Lemma 11.3.2 in a stronger form, the push-forward and pull-back along generalized maps with their functorial properties, and Theorem 11.3.3, with (6) read as below, are verified (V11.14–V11.19); so are Lemma 11.3.4 with (11.8) and (11.9), Theorem 11.3.5, Definition 11.3.6 with (11.10), and Theorems 11.3.7 and 11.3.8, under Chapter 9's hypothesis that the tangent sums of Theorem 9.2.1 are independent, and Theorem 11.3.9 for a representative under a boundary-transfer hypothesis (V11.20–V11.26). In §11.4 Theorems 11.4.1 and 11.4.2 and Remark 11.4.3 are verified as stated, for the canonical measures of Theorems 9.5.4 and 9.5.5 built from Chapter 9's sheet integrals (V11.27, V11.28), and Theorems 11.4.4 and 11.4.5 for the boundary measures of Theorems 9.5.15 and 9.5.16 under their class hypothesis, for $n \ge 2$ (V11.29). In §11.5 Proposition 11.5.1, Lemma 11.5.2 and Proposition 11.5.3 are verified, the last two for sc⁺-multisections (V11.30–V11.32; gaps G.132, G.133 closed on 2026-11-09). In §11.6 Lemmas 11.6.1–11.6.3, Definitions 11.6.4, 11.6.5, 11.6.7, Theorem 11.6.6 in all its claims and Proposition 11.6.8 are verified (V11.33–V11.41), and so are the localization $\mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$ with $I$ (V11.43) and Remark 11.6.9, the strong bundle version (V11.42). Several places of the text needed more than a reading. (a) *Theorem 11.1.1 (2017: 11.1).* The text checks that $T$ respects refinements; that $T$ preserves composition needs a comparison functor $T(A \times_Y B) \to TA \times_{TY} TB$, an equivalence by two out of three (V11.1). (b) *Proposition 11.1.6 (2017: 11.2).* The clause that two faces meet in a face of each does not hold as we read it: two faces of a face structured open subset of $[0, \infty)^3 \oplus W$ meet in two pieces of an edge; what holds, and is proved, is that the intersection is a union of faces of each (V11.6). (c) *Theorem 11.3.3 (2017: 11.3).* The paracompactness of $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$, which 2021 Definition 9.1.2 (1) asks for, is proved for push-forwards and pull-backs, though the text's proof does not mention it, and the sheets of a local branching structure are first restricted to the domain of the local sc-diffeomorphism (V11.17); the uniqueness part of Proposition 9.1.11 does not hold as we read it (Chapter 9), so (6) is read as "every dimensional decomposition is mapped to one" (V11.18). (d) *Lemma 11.3.2 (2017: 11.5).* The well-definedness of $F_*$ needs only fullness, (2) only essential surjectivity (V11.15). (e) *Definition 11.6.4 (2017: 11.6).* For proper covering functors the fibre condition of (2) follows from the other two conditions (V11.36). (f) *Theorem 11.6.6 (2017: 11.10).* Step (C) is proved through the properness of $H$ on objects instead of sequences (V11.38). (g) *Theorems 11.3.7 and 11.3.8 (2017: 11.5, 11.6).* Their proofs, left to the reader, need Chapter 9's tangent, orientation and boundary notions carried by sc-diffeomorphisms between different M-polyfolds; the independence of the tangent sums, assumed for $\Theta$, is carried to $f_*\Theta$ and $f^*\Theta'$ (V11.23, V11.24). (h) *Theorem 11.3.9 (2017: 11.7).* Chapter 9's boundary orientation depends on a boundary operation taken as data, so the theorem is stated for a representative and boundary operations corresponding under the transfer maps (V11.25). (i) *Proposition 11.6.8 (2017: 11.8).* The displayed chain for the functors $\varepsilon$ stops one step short; the last step uses the fourth assumption (V11.41). Reading points on the printed text are recorded in V11.2, V11.14, V11.17, V11.34 and V11.38. Not verified: that the boundary operations of Definition 9.3.8 satisfy the boundary-transfer hypothesis along equivalences, and so a form of Theorem 11.3.9 independent of the representative; Theorems 11.4.4 and 11.4.5 without the class hypothesis near the corners of the sheets, and for $n = 1$ (gap G.131 in part). Conditions (1) and (2) of Definition 8.3.5 in Proposition 11.5.1 and the local section structures of sc⁺-multisections are verified since 2026-11-09 (gaps G.132, G.133 closed). Addendum (2026-11-12): the Part II wave closed gaps G.128, G.129, G.134 and G.135 (faces as ep-groupoids with $[d]_F$ and the intersection clause settled by a counterexample and a corrected form, §11.2 in full, the localization $\mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$, and Remark 11.6.9 with Theorem 11.6.6 and the diagram calculus for strong bundles), with no hypothesis added; §11.4 remains open. Addendum (2026-11-13): the second integration of the Part II wave formalizes §11.4 (gap G.131 in part): Theorems 11.4.1, 11.4.2 and Remark 11.4.3 as stated, Theorems 11.4.4 and 11.4.5 under the class hypothesis `hcov` inherited from Theorems 9.5.15 and 9.5.16 (Lean), which a closed hemisphere with nonempty boundary satisfies; the text's tacit step that $|f|$ preserves the σ-algebras $L$ and $L(\partial S)$ is proved. Addendum (2026-11-13, wave K): Theorems 11.4.4 and 11.4.5 hold with the text's hypotheses only, for every $n \ge 1$, the class hypothesis being derived in Chapter 9 (gap G.109) and the $n = 1$ boundary measures transported along equivalences, spans and generalized isomorphisms (V11.29, restated; gap G.131 closed).

The hypotheses. Two hypotheses beyond the text's statements are taken, both in §11.3. Chapter 9's `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.HasIndependentTangentSums`, the independence part of Theorem 9.2.1, which Chapter 9's formalization assumes and proves on $\mathbb R^n$ (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_rn`), is assumed for the branched ep⁺-subgroupoid being moved in Theorems 11.3.5, 11.3.7–11.3.9 and Definition 11.3.6, and proved for its push-forward and pull-back. `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsBoundaryTransfer`, a pointwise condition on the given transfer maps and boundary operations, is assumed in Theorem 11.3.9; it holds along the identity (`Polyfold.MPolyfold.isBoundaryTransfer_id`). The branched statements of §11.3 take $X$ and $Y$ in one universe; generalized isomorphisms relate objects of one $\mathcal{EP}$ anyway. The tangent functor on $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ is defined on the ep-groupoids of the universe that Chapter 8's tangent functor uses ($\max(u, 1)$). Several statements need less than the text assumes: Lemma 11.3.2 (V11.15), Proposition 11.1.6, whose bijection of faces holds for every generalized isomorphism and whose other claims need only $X$ face structured (V11.6, V11.8), Theorem 11.6.6 (1) (V11.38), and Theorem 11.2.1 (4), which needs the local regularity property of $Y$ only (V11.9). The sc-differential forms of §11.2 and the localizations of §11.6 take no hypothesis beyond the text's; nor do Theorems 11.4.1, 11.4.2 and Remark 11.4.3 (the independence of the tangent sums holds for every $\Theta$, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums`), while Theorems 11.4.4 and 11.4.5 inherit the class hypothesis `hcov` of Theorems 9.5.15 and 9.5.16 (Lean; nonempty boundary sheets in the class of integrated sheets), proved for the transported subgroupoid and satisfiable with $\partial S \ne \emptyset$ (`Polyfold.E8W.e8w_hcov` with `Polyfold.EP.hcovB_of_hcovS`) (V11.29); Remark 11.6.9 does not define the equivalences of proper strong bundle coverings nor their natural transformations, and both are read (V11.42).

The setting. Ep-groupoids, sc-smooth functors, orbit spaces, the degeneracy index $d_X$ and the induced index $d_{|X|}$ on $|X|$ are those of Chapter 7 (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.degIndexOrbit`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsTame`); the tangent functor, strong bundles over ep-groupoids, auxiliary norms and proper covering functors are Chapter 8's (`Polyfold.EpFunctor.tangent`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsAuxNorm`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering`); branched ep⁺-subgroupoids, local branching structures and their properties are Chapter 9's (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsFunctorial`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsBranchedEpSubgroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsDimDecomposition`); equivalences, the weak fibred product, the localization $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ with its diagrams, refinements and generalized isomorphisms, strong bundle equivalences and generalized strong bundle isomorphisms are Chapter 10's (`Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.Admissible`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.IsGeneralizedIso`, `Polyfold.SEP.equivalences`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.IsGeneralizedIso`). Compositions in $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ are in Mathlib's order, $f ≫ g$ for the text's $g \circ f$. $\mathbb Q^+$ is $\mathbb Q_{\ge 0}$; functors $X \to \mathbb Q$ are maps on objects constant along morphisms. Findings referred to below are those of `Exposition/Findings.md`, "Chapter 11".

**V11.1 (Theorem 11.1.1 (2017: 11.1), the tangent functor on $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_11_1_1`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.tangentFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.tangentFunctor_obj`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.tangentFunctor_map_homMk`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.tangentFunctor_map_localizationFunctor`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isGeneralizedIso_tangent`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.tangent`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.tangent`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.tangent`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_tangent_id`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_tangent_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.wfpLift`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.projLeft_comp_wfpLift`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.projRight_comp_wfpLift`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.tangent_comp`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.tangent_id`).** The assignment $X \mapsto TX$, $[X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y] \mapsto [TX \xleftarrow{TF} TA \xrightarrow{T\Phi} TY]$ is a functor $T : \mathcal{EP}(E^{-1}) \to \mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$: a refinement $H : d' \to d$ gives the refinement $TH : Td' \to Td$, equivalent diagrams have equivalent tangent diagrams, $T$ preserves identities and composition, and $T(i(\Phi)) = i(T\Phi)$ for the localization functor $i : \mathcal{EP} \to \mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$. $T$ maps generalized isomorphisms to generalized isomorphisms. For functors $P : C \to X$, $Q : C \to Z$ and a natural transformation $\tau : \Phi \circ P \to G \circ Q$, $c \mapsto (P(c), \tau(c), Q(c))$ is a functor $C \to X \times_Y Z$ with $\pi_X$ and $\pi_Z$ composites $P$ and $Q$. *Book:* Theorem 11.1.1, p. 521 (2017: Theorem 11.1, p. 375), with its proof, pp. 521–522. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the text checks refinements and leaves "the remaining argument" to the reader; that $T$ preserves composition needs the comparison $T(A \times_Y B) \to TA \times_{TY} TB$, $v \mapsto (T\pi_A(v), T\sigma(v), T\pi_B(v))$, an equivalence by two out of three, through which $T(d \circ e)$ refines $Td \circ Te$; $T$ is defined on the ep-groupoids of Chapter 8's tangent universe (Findings, item 1). *Proof:* $TF$ is an equivalence (Theorem 10.1.7); a natural transformation $\sigma : G \to F \circ H$ gives $T\sigma : TG \to TF \circ TH$ (Proposition 8.1.14).

**V11.2 (Proposition 11.1.2 (2017: 11.1), the degeneracy index under generalized isomorphisms; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.proposition_11_1_2`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.degIndexOrbit_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.degIndexOrbit_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.degIndexOrbit_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.degIndexOrbit`).** If $f : X \to Y$ is a generalized isomorphism and $|f|(|x|) = |y|$, then $d_X(x_0) = d_Y(y_0)$ for all $x_0$ with $|x_0| = |x|$ and $y_0$ with $|y_0| = |y|$, and $d_{|X|}(|x|) = d_{|Y|}(|y|)$. *Book:* Proposition 11.1.2, p. 522 (2017: Proposition 11.1, p. 376), with its proof, pp. 522–523. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; the proof cites "Proposition 10.3.10" for Theorem 10.3.10 (possible misprint) (Findings, item 2). *Proof:* a representative with both legs equivalences (Theorem 10.3.10); equivalences are local sc-diffeomorphisms on objects and preserve $d$.

**V11.3 (Definition 11.1.3 (2017: 11.1), faces in the ep-groupoid sense; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsOrbitFace`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.faceObj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.faceMor`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEpFace`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orbitFacesThrough`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEpFaceStructured`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsWeaklyFaceStructured`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.faceMor_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isSaturated_faceObj`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isOrbitFace_iff_isFaceIn`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.orbitFacesThrough_eq`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isEpFaceStructured_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.faceEpGroupoid`).** A face of $|X|$ is the closure in $|X|$ of the connected component, in $\{z \in |X| \mid d_{|X|}(z) = 1\}$, of a point of that set; for $\theta \subseteq |X|$, $X_\theta$ is the full subcategory on the objects $x$ with $|x| \in \theta$, recorded by its object set $\pi^{-1}(\theta)$, a saturated set, and its morphisms are those with source in it; a face of $X$ is $X_\theta$ for a face $\theta$ of $|X|$. $X$ is face structured if it is tame and every $z \in |X|$ lies in exactly $d_{|X|}(z)$ faces of $|X|$ (counted in $\mathbb N \cup \{\infty\}$), and weakly face structured if it is tame and its object M-polyfold is face structured (Definition 2.5.10). The faces of $|X|$ are Chapter 2's faces for the index $d_{|X|}$ on the open set $|X|$. *Book:* Definition 11.1.3, p. 523 (2017: Definition 11.1, p. 377). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* a face of $X$ is recorded by its object set; its sub-M-polyfold and ep-groupoid structure is Proposition 11.1.6 (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.faceEpGroupoid`, V11.6) (Findings, item 3).

**V11.4 (Example 11.1.4 (2017: 11.1); `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.example_11_1_4`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.swapEpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isFaceStructured_quadrant`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isHomeomorph_π_trivial`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.setOf_degIndexOrbit_eq_one_swap`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isOrbitFace_swap_iff`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.not_isEpFaceStructured_swap`).** For $C = [0, \infty)^2 \oplus W$ with any sc-Banach space $W$: $C$ with only identities is a face structured ep-groupoid; $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes C$, with $-1$ exchanging the two coordinates, is weakly face structured and not face structured, since $\{d_{|X|} = 1\}$ is connected, so that $|X|$ has exactly one face and $|0|$, with $d_{|X|}(|0|) = 2$, lies in one face only. *Book:* Example 11.1.4, p. 523 (2017: Example 11.1, p. 377). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the text has $W = 0$; the reason for "not face structured", not given in the text, is proved (Findings, item 4).

**V11.5 (Remark 11.1.5 (2017: 11.1), the bijections of faces; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.remark_11_1_5`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.saturation_image_faceObj`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.preimage_faceObj`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.bijOn_faces`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.faceMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.faceComap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.faceMap_homMk`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.faceComap_homMk`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.bijOn_faceMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isHomeomorph_orbitMap`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.isDHomeoOn_univ`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.isFaceIn_univ_image`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.exists_isFaceIn_univ_preimage`, `Polyfold.TameBoundary.isFaceStructuredOpen_univ_iff`).** For an equivalence $\Phi : X \to Y$, $\theta \mapsto |\Phi|(\theta)$ is a bijection of the faces of $|X|$ onto those of $|Y|$ with inverse $\theta' \mapsto |\Phi|^{-1}(\theta')$, and $\Phi_*(X_\theta) = \mathrm{saturation}(\Phi(X_\theta)) = Y_{|\Phi|(\theta)}$, $\Phi^*(Y_{\theta'}) = \Phi^{-1}(Y_{\theta'}) = X_{|\Phi|^{-1}(\theta')}$. For a generalized isomorphism $[d] = [X \xleftarrow{\Phi} A \xrightarrow{\Psi} Y]$, $[d]_*$ and $[d]^*$ on faces are $\theta \mapsto |[d]|(\theta)$ and $\theta' \mapsto |[d]|^{-1}(\theta')$, equal to $\Psi_* \circ \Phi^*$ and $\Phi_* \circ \Psi^*$, and mutually inverse bijections. The general fact behind it: a homeomorphism preserving the index maps faces to faces and preserves face-structuredness. *Book:* Remark 11.1.5, p. 524 (2017: Remark 11.1, p. 378), quoting [56, Proposition 3.15]. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the quoted result is proved; the ordered face structures of the remark's first paragraph have no formal content (Findings, item 5).

**V11.6 (Proposition 11.1.6 (2017: 11.2), faces up to generalized isomorphisms; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.proposition_11_1_6`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isOrbitFace_faceMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isOrbitFace_faceComap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.faceComap_faceMap`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.faceMap_faceComap`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEpFaceStructured.isWeaklyFaceStructured`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEpFaceStructured.exists_nhds_eq_face`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.faceEpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isTame_faceEpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.degIndex_faceEpGroupoid`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.proposition_11_1_6_faces`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.restrictSub`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.faceEP`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.faceIso`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isGeneralizedIso_faceIso`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitMap_faceIso`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.proposition_11_1_6_faceIso`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.FacesMeetInFaces`, `Polyfold.FaceMeetExample.isEpFaceStructured_XV`, `Polyfold.FaceMeetExample.not_facesMeetInFaces`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.mem_closure_inter_faces`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEpFaceStructured.faceObj_inter_eq_sUnion`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.FacesMeetInUnionsOfFaces`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEpFaceStructured.facesMeetInUnions`).** A generalized isomorphism $[d] : X \to Y$ induces the bijection $[d]_*$ of the faces of $|X|$ onto those of $|Y|$, with inverse $[d]^*$; $[d]_*(X_\theta) = Y_{|[d]|(\theta)}$; and for every $\theta$, $|[d]|$ restricts to a homeomorphism $\theta \to [d]_*\theta$. If $X$ is face structured (Definition 11.1.3), its object M-polyfold is weakly face structured, each $X_\theta$ agrees near each of its points with one face of the object M-polyfold, and so $X_\theta$ is a closed saturated sub-M-polyfold with a tame induced structure, its morphisms form a sub-M-polyfold with a tame structure, and the full subcategory is a tame ep-groupoid with $d_X = d_{X_\theta} + 1$; $[d]$ restricts to a generalized isomorphism $[d]_F : X_\theta \to Y_{[d]_*\theta}$, independent of the representative, whose orbit map is the restriction of $|[d]|$. For distinct faces $\theta \ne \theta'$ with $X_\theta \cap X_{\theta'} \ne \emptyset$, the intersection is the union of the faces of $X_\theta$ it contains, and of the faces of $X_{\theta'}$ it contains. The printed clause, that it is one face of each, is stated (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.FacesMeetInFaces`) and negated for the trivial ep-groupoid of $([0, \infty)^3 \oplus W) \setminus K$, $K = \{p_0 + p_1 \le 1/4,\ 1 \le p_2 \le 2\}$, which is tame and face structured. *Book:* Proposition 11.1.6, p. 524 (2017: Proposition 11.2, p. 378), with its proof, pp. 524–525. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* the clause that two faces meet in a face of each does not hold as we read it: the faces $\{p_0 = 0\}$ and $\{p_1 = 0\}$ of the example meet in the two pieces $p_2 < 1$ and $p_2 > 2$ of the edge, and a face of $X_\theta$ is the closure of one connected component of the index-$1$ set (`Polyfold.FaceMeetExample.not_facesMeetInFaces`); the union form is proved for every face structured $X$ (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsEpFaceStructured.facesMeetInUnions`, from `Polyfold.MPolyfold.mem_closure_inter_faces`: in a tame M-polyfold a point on two distinct faces is a limit of points of index $2$ on both). Only $X$ is assumed face structured; $Y$ then is (Remark 11.1.7). The bijection needs no face structure (gap G.128 closed; Findings, items 6, 9).

**V11.7 (Remark 11.1.7 (2017: 11.2), face structure under generalized isomorphisms; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.remark_11_1_7`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isTame_of_isTame_left`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isTame_iff`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isTame_of_isTame`).** If $f : X \to Y$ is a generalized isomorphism, $X$ is tame and face structured if and only if $Y$ is. If $F : X \to Y$ is an equivalence, $X$ is tame if and only if $Y$ is. *Book:* Remark 11.1.7, p. 525 (2017: Remark 11.2, p. 379). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the forward transfer of tameness along an equivalence, needed for the remark and not in Chapter 10, is proved through the weak fibred product $X \times_Y Y$ (Findings, item 7).

**V11.8 (Proposition 11.1.8 (2017: 11.3), generalized isomorphisms with the same orbit map; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.proposition_11_1_8`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.faceIso`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.proposition_11_1_8_faceIso`).** For generalized isomorphisms $f, g : X \to Y$ with $|f| = |g|$: $f_* = g_*$ and $f^* = g^*$ on faces, and, for face structured $X$, the generalized isomorphisms $f_F, g_F : X_\theta \to Y_{f_*\theta}$ of (11.1) have the same orbit map, the restriction of $|f| = |g|$. *Book:* Proposition 11.1.8, p. 526 (2017: Proposition 11.3, p. 380). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* $Y$ need not be assumed face structured; it is, by Remark 11.1.7 (Findings, item 8).

**V11.9 (Theorem 11.2.1 (2017: Theorem 11.2), sc-differential forms under generalized maps; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.formsPullback`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.formsPush`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.formsPullback_homMk`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.formsPush_homMk`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_11_2_1_one`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_11_2_1_two`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_11_2_1_three`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.formsPullback_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_11_2_1_four`).** $d \circ d = 0$ on $\Omega^*_{ep,\infty}(X)$. A generalized map $f : X \to Y$ (a morphism of $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$) has a pull-back $f^*$ with $d_X \circ f^* = f^* \circ d_Y$, equal to $F_* \circ \Phi^*$ for every diagram $X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y$ representing $f$. A generalized isomorphism $h$ has a push-forward $h_*$, equal to $\Phi_* \circ F^*$ for every representing diagram, with $h_* \circ d_X = d_Y \circ h_*$, $h_* \circ h^* = 1$ and $h^* \circ h_* = 1$. If $X$ and $Y$ have the local regularity property and $|h| = |k|$, then $h_* = k_*$ and $h^* = k^*$. *Book:* Theorem 11.2.1, p. 526 (2017: Theorem 11.2, p. 380). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* $h_*$ is defined as the pull-back by the inverse generalized map, which is the text's $G_* \circ F^*$ on every representative (Theorem 10.3.10); beyond the text, $(g \circ f)^* = f^* \circ g^*$, and (4) holds with the local regularity property of $Y$ only (Findings, items 20, 22).

**V11.10 (Lemma 11.2.2 and Definition 11.2.3 (2017: Lemma 11.1, Definition 11.2), the push-forward of forms along an equivalence; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.bijective_formPullback`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.formPush`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.definition_11_2_3`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.exists_lift_tangent`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.lemma_11_2_2`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.exists_epForms_formPullback_eq_of_surjective`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.isScForm_of_formPullback`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.formDescend`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.formPullback_formDescend`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.formPullback_injective_of_isLocalScDiffeo`, `Polyfold.EP.epFormsInftyPush`, `Polyfold.EP.epFormsInftyD_comp_epFormsInftyPush`).** For an equivalence $F : X \to Y$ the pull-back $F^* : \Omega^k_{ep}(Y) \to \Omega^k_{ep}(X)$ is a bijection, and $F_*$ is its inverse. For $x \in X_1$, $\psi : F(x) \to y$ in $\mathbf Y_1$ and $l_j \in T_xX$, $(F_*\omega)_y(T\psi(TF(x)l_1), \ldots, T\psi(TF(x)l_k)) = \omega_x(l_1, \ldots, l_k)$; every $h_1, \ldots, h_k \in T_yY$ is of this form, and the value does not depend on the choices (Lemma 11.2.2). On $\Omega^*_{ep,\infty}$, $F_*[\omega] = [(F^i)_*\omega]$ and $d_Y \circ F_* = F_* \circ d_X$ ((11.5)). *Book:* Lemma 11.2.2, p. 527 (2017: Lemma 11.1, p. 380); Definition 11.2.3, p. 528 (2017: Definition 11.2, p. 382). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the text defines $F_*\omega$ by the formula and proves it well defined and sc-smooth ((11.4)); here $F_*$ is the inverse of $F^*$, whose bijectivity is proved by descent along $\pi_Y : X \times_Y Y \to Y$, the weak fibred product of $F$ and $1_Y$, whose objects are the triples $(x, \psi, y)$ of the definition; the formula and Lemma 11.2.2 are theorems, and sc-smoothness is the text's argument (11.4). Reading point: before Definition 11.2.3 the text writes $F_*\omega \in \Omega_{ep,\infty}(X)$; we read $\Omega_{ep,\infty}(Y)$ (Findings, items 21, 22).

**V11.11 (Lemmas 11.2.4–11.2.6 (2017: Lemmas 11.2–11.4), composition, natural equivalence and refinement; `Polyfold.EP.lemma_11_2_4_two`, `Polyfold.EP.epFormsInftyPush_comp_epFormsInftyPullback`, `Polyfold.EP.epFormsInftyPullback_comp_epFormsInftyPush`, `Polyfold.EP.lemma_11_2_5_push`, `Polyfold.EP.lemma_11_2_6`, `Polyfold.EP.lemma_11_2_6_push`, `Polyfold.EP.epFormsInftyPush_eq_of_comp_eq_id`).** Push-forwards and pull-backs of forms along equivalences compose and are mutually inverse; naturally equivalent equivalences have the same push-forwards, and naturally equivalent sc-smooth functors the same pull-backs; refinements of diagrams do not change $F_* \circ G^*$ and $G_* \circ F^*$. *Book:* Lemma 11.2.4, p. 528 (2017: Lemma 11.2, p. 382); Lemma 11.2.5, p. 529 (2017: Lemma 11.3, p. 383); Lemma 11.2.6, p. 531 (2017: Lemma 11.4, p. 385). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the proofs are formal from $F_* = (F^*)^{-1}$. Reading point: the proof of Lemma 11.2.6 cites Lemmas 11.2.2 and 11.2.3 for what it uses; we read Lemmas 11.2.4 and 11.2.5 (Findings, item 21).

**V11.12 (Definition 11.2.7 (2017: Definition 11.3), pull-back and push-forward of forms by generalized maps; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.formsPullback`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.formsPush`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.formsPullback_eq_of_equiv`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.formsPush_eq_of_equiv`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.formsPullback`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.formsPush`).** For $[d] = [X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{G} Y]$, $[d]^*\omega' = F_* \circ G^*\omega'$, and for a generalized isomorphism $[d]_*\omega = G_* \circ F^*\omega$; both are independent of the representing diagram. *Book:* Definition 11.2.7, p. 532 (2017: Definition 11.3, p. 386). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none.

**V11.13 (Propositions 11.2.8 and 11.2.9 (2017: Propositions 11.4, 11.5), forms under maps with the same orbit map; `Polyfold.EP.proposition_11_2_8`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.proposition_11_2_9`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.HasLocalNatIso`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.HasLocalNatIso.formPullback_eq`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.hasLocalNatIso_of_orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.EP.epFormsInftyPullback_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.formsPullback_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`).** If $X$ and $Y$ have the local regularity property, equivalences $F, G : X \to Y$ with $|F| = |G|$ have $F_* = G_*$ and $F^* = G^*$ on $\Omega^*_{ep,\infty}$, and generalized isomorphisms $f, g$ with $|f| = |g|$ have $f_* = g_*$ and $f^* = g^*$. *Book:* Proposition 11.2.8, p. 532 (2017: Proposition 11.4, p. 386); Proposition 11.2.9, p. 534 (2017: Proposition 11.5, p. 388). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the text takes from Proposition 10.1.10 a morphism $\psi : F(x) \to G(x)$ with $T\psi \circ TF(x) = TG(x)$; the proof uses the local sc-smooth families $\alpha_z : F(z) \to G(z)$ of Proposition 10.1.10 (1), restricted to the index lifts $X^i$, so that no local regularity of the lifts is needed; the statements also hold with the local regularity property of one of $X$, $Y$ only. The hypothesis is satisfiable (`Polyfold.EpGroupoid.Examples.isLR_trivialZ3`, `Polyfold.EP.lreg_pointEP`) (Findings, item 22).

**V11.14 (Definition 11.3.1 (2017: 11.4), pull-back and push-forward of functors along a functor; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.pullbackTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.pushforwardTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.pullbackTheta_apply`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.pushforwardTheta_of_not_exists`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.exists_isomorphic_of_pushforwardTheta_ne_zero`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.pushforwardTheta_nonneg`).** For an sc-smooth functor $F : X \to Y$ and maps $\Theta : X \to \mathbb Q$, $\Theta' : Y \to \mathbb Q$ on objects, $F^*\Theta' = \Theta' \circ F$ and $(F_*\Theta)(y) = \Theta(x)$ for a chosen $x$ with a morphism $F(x) \to y$, and $0$ if there is none; $F_*$ preserves nonnegativity. *Book:* Definition 11.3.1, p. 535 (2017: Definition 11.4, p. 389). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* both are defined for every sc-smooth functor and every map, the choice made once; for an equivalence a morphism $F(x) \to y$ always exists and the value does not depend on the choice (V11.15). The push-forward is printed as a map $X' \to \mathbb Q^+$, also in 2017; we read $Y \to \mathbb Q^+$ (possible misprint) (Findings, item 30).

**V11.15 (Lemma 11.3.2 (2017: 11.5), in a stronger form; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.pushforwardTheta_eq`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.pushforwardTheta_obj`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.pushforwardTheta_eq_of_isomorphic`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isFunctorial_pushforwardTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isFunctorial_pullbackTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.pullbackTheta_pushforwardTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.pushforwardTheta_pullbackTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.pushforwardTheta_eq_of_naturallyEquivalent`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.pullbackTheta_eq_of_naturallyEquivalent`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.pullbackTheta_comp`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.pushforwardTheta_comp`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.pushforwardTheta_id`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsFunctorial.eq_of_isomorphic`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isomorphic_obj`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isomorphic_of_full`).** (1) If $F$ is full and $\Theta$ is a functor, then $(F_*\Theta)(y) = \Theta(x)$ for every $x$ with a morphism $F(x) \to y$, $F_*\Theta$ is a functor and $F^*F_*\Theta = \Theta$; (2) if $F$ is essentially surjective and $\Theta'$ is a functor, $F_*F^*\Theta' = \Theta'$; (3) naturally equivalent full functors $F \simeq G$ have $F_*\Theta = G_*\Theta$, and naturally equivalent functors have $F^*\Theta' = G^*\Theta'$. Moreover $F^*$ of a functor is a functor, $(G \circ F)^* = F^* \circ G^*$, $(G \circ F)_* = G_* \circ F_*$ for full $F$, $G$, $G \circ F$, and $1_*\Theta = \Theta$. *Book:* Lemma 11.3.2, p. 536 (2017: Lemma 11.5, p. 389). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the text assumes equivalences throughout; (1) needs only fullness, (2) only essential surjectivity, (3) fullness for push-forwards and nothing for pull-backs; the composition rules are added (Findings, item 31). *Proof:* for $\psi : F(x) \to y$, $\psi' : F(x') \to y$, fullness lifts $\psi^{-1} \circ \psi'$ to $\sigma : x' \to x$, as in the text.

**V11.16 (the push-forward and pull-back along generalized maps, pp. 536–537; `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.pushTheta`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.pullTheta`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.isEquivalence_Φ_iff`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.pushTheta_eq_of_isRefinement`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.pullTheta_eq_of_isRefinement`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.pushTheta_eq_of_equiv`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.Diagram.pullTheta_eq_of_equiv`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.rep`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.homMk_rep`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.equiv_rep_homMk`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isEquivalence_rep_Φ`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.pushTheta`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.pullTheta`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.pushTheta_homMk`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.pullTheta_homMk`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isFunctorial_pushTheta`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.isFunctorial_pullTheta`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.pushTheta_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.pullTheta_comp`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.pushTheta_inv`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.pullTheta_pushTheta`, `Polyfold.EPLocalization.EPLoc.pushTheta_pullTheta`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.pushforwardTheta_projRight_pullbackTheta`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.pushforwardTheta_projLeft_pullbackTheta`).** For a diagram $d : X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y$, $d_*\Theta = \Phi_*F^*\Theta$ and $d^*\Theta' = F_*\Phi^*\Theta'$; a refinement does not change $d^*\Theta'$, nor $d_*\Theta$ when $\Phi$ is an equivalence, so equivalent diagrams have the same pull-backs, and the same push-forwards when $\Phi$ is an equivalence. Hence $f^*$ is well defined for every generalized map and $f_*$ for every generalized isomorphism, computed on any representative (with $\Phi$ an equivalence for $f_*$); both map functors to functors; $(f ≫ g)^* = f^* \circ g^*$ for all generalized maps, $(f ≫ g)_* = g_* \circ f_*$ and $(f^{-1})_* = f^*$ for generalized isomorphisms, and $f^*f_*\Theta = \Theta$, $f_*f^*\Theta' = \Theta'$. In a weak fibred product $X \times_Y Z$, $(\pi_Z)_*(\pi_X)^*\Theta = G^*F_*\Theta$ for an equivalence $F$, and $(\pi_X)_*(\pi_Z)^*\Theta = F^*G_*\Theta$ for an equivalence $G$. *Book:* §11.3, pp. 536–537 (2017 pp. 389–390), not a numbered statement. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the text defines $f^*$ for generalized isomorphisms; it is well defined, and contravariantly functorial, for all generalized maps. The composition rules, "easily verified" in the text, go through the base change in the weak fibred product that represents the composite (Theorem 10.3.8); nothing uses Theorem 10.3.19, which does not hold as we read it (Chapter 10, V10.65) (Findings, item 32).

**V11.17 (Theorem 11.3.3 (2017: 11.3), the proof's step for an equivalence; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_pullbackTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_pushforwardTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.exists_localBranchingStructure_pushforwardTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.exists_mem_supp_of_mem_supp_pushforwardTheta`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.mapDiffeo`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.mapU`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.mem_image_iff_of_mem_mapU`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isOfDim_mapDiffeo`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.orbitSupp_pullbackTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.orbitSupp_pushforwardTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isClosedBranched_pushforwardTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isClosedBranched_pullbackTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isCompactBranched_pushforwardTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isCompactBranched_pullbackTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isOrbifoldType_pushforwardTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isOrbifoldType_pullbackTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isManifoldType_pushforwardTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isManifoldType_pullbackTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isNDimensional_pullbackTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isNDimensional_pushforwardTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.exists_pushforwardTheta_eq_apply`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isDimDecomposition_pushforwardTheta`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isDimDecomposition_pullbackTheta`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.HasDimAt.of_image`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.hasDimAt_image_iff_of_isScDiffeoOn`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsSubmanifoldOfDim.image_isScDiffeoOn`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.TransportChart`).** For an equivalence $F : X \to Y$: $F^*\Theta'$ and $F_*\Theta$ of branched ep⁺-subgroupoids are branched ep⁺-subgroupoids; The text uses without comment that $|f|$ maps $\mathcal L$ onto $\mathcal L$; it is proved through Lemma 9.5.2 (`Polyfold.EpFunctor.measurable_suppMap`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.measurable_suppInv`) (gap G.131, closed since 2026-11-13; Findings, item 50).

**V11.30 (Proposition 11.5.1 (2017: 11.6), auxiliary norms under generalized strong bundle isomorphisms, without conditions (1) and (2) of Definition 8.3.5; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.proposition_11_5_1`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pullNorm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pushNorm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pullNorm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pushNorm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pullNorm_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pullNorm_eq_Ψ`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.isOneInvariant_pullNorm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pullNorm_eq_lift`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.continuous_pullNorm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pushNorm_pullNorm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pullNorm_pushNorm`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pullNorm_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pushNorm_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.oneOrbitMap`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.continuous_oneOrbitMap`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.oneOrbitMap_oneMap`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.oneToOrbit_oneOrbitMap`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.oneOrbitMap_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.oneToOrbit`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.oneToOrbit_injective`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.oneMap`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.continuous_oneMap`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.oneToOrbit_oneMap`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsOneInvariant`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isOneInvariant_const`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isOneInvariant_iff`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.isOneInvariant`).** For a generalized strong bundle isomorphism $[D] : W \to W'$ and functions $N'$ on $W'_{0,1}$, $N$ on $W_{0,1}$: $[D]^*N'(e) = N'(e')$ for a representative $e'$ of $|D|(|e|) \in |W'[1]|$, and $[D]_*N$ is the pull-back along the reversed diagram; **V11.31 (the pull-back and push-forward of multisection functors along a strong bundle equivalence, and Lemma 11.5.2 (2017: 11.7); `Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsWFunctor`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.isWFunctor_const`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsWFunctor.eq_of_π_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.pullMult`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.IsWFunctor.pullMult`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.pushMult`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.π_obj_choose`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.pushMult_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.lemma_11_5_2`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.pullMult_pushMult`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.pushMult_pullMult`).** A functor $\Lambda : W \to \alpha$ on the total ep-groupoid of a strong bundle is a map constant along morphisms, $\Lambda(\mu(\varphi, w)) = \Lambda(w)$. For a strong bundle functor $\Psi$, $\Psi^*\Lambda' = \Lambda' \circ \Psi$ of a functor is a functor; for a strong bundle equivalence $\Phi$, $\Phi_*\Lambda(w') = \Lambda(w)$ for a chosen $w$ and morphism $\Phi(w) \to w'$, equal to $\Lambda(w)$ for every $w$ with $\Phi(w) \cong w'$; $\Phi_*\Lambda$ is a functor (Lemma 11.5.2), and $\Phi^*\Phi_*\Lambda = \Lambda$, $\Phi_*\Phi^*\Lambda' = \Lambda'$. *Book:* §11.5, pp. 547–548 (2017 pp. 399–400), and Lemma 11.5.2, p. 548 (2017: Lemma 11.7, p. 400). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* only the functor $\Lambda : W \to \mathbb Q^+$ underlying an sc⁺-multisection is treated; its local section structures (2021 Definition 13.2.1) and their transport along $\Phi$ are not formalized (gap G.133) (Findings, item 61).

**V11.32 (Proposition 11.5.3 (2017: 11.7), multisection functors under generalized strong bundle isomorphisms; `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.proposition_11_5_3`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pushMult`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.GenSBMap.pullMult`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pushMult`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pullMult`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pushMult_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pullMult_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.isWFunctor_pushMult`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.isWFunctor_pullMult`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pullMult_pushMult`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pushMult_pullMult`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pushMult_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`, `Polyfold.SBLocalization.SDiagram.pullMult_eq_of_orbitMap_eq`).** For a generalized strong bundle isomorphism $[D]$ and functors $\Lambda : W \to \mathbb Q_{\ge 0}$, $\Lambda' : W' \to \mathbb Q_{\ge 0}$: $[D]_*\Lambda = \Psi_*\Phi^*\Lambda$ and $[D]^*\Lambda' = \Phi_*\Psi^*\Lambda'$ do not depend on the representative $W \xleftarrow{\Phi} W'' \xrightarrow{\Psi} W'$ (both legs strong bundle equivalences); they map functors to functors and are mutually inverse; and if $[D']$ is a generalized strong bundle isomorphism with $|[D]| = |[D']|$, the push-forwards and the pull-backs agree. *Book:* Proposition 11.5.3, p. 548 (2017: Proposition 11.7, p. 401). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (narrower):* for the functors underlying sc⁺-multisections, without their local section structures (gap G.133); the text's "generalized strong bundle maps" with $|[D]| = |[D']|$ is read as generalized strong bundle isomorphisms, for which the push-forward is defined (Findings, item 61). *Proof:* $[D]_*\Lambda(w') = \Lambda(w)$ whenever $|D|(|w|) = |w'|$, so everything depends only on $|D|$.

**V11.33 (Lemma 11.6.1, the morphism map of a proper covering functor; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.lemma_11_6_1`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.lift`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.mor_lift`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.src_lift`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.eq_lift`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.obj_tgt_lift`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.existsUnique_lift_tgt`).** For a proper covering functor $F : Y \to X$, $F$ on morphisms is a surjective local sc-diffeomorphism. The inverse $\alpha^{-1}(\varphi, y)$ of $\alpha : \psi \mapsto (F(\psi), s(\psi))$ is the unique $\psi$ with $F(\psi) = \varphi$, $s(\psi) = y$; it has $F(t(\psi)) = t(\varphi)$, and lifts with prescribed target are unique too. *Book:* Lemma 11.6.1, p. 549 (new in the 2021 edition). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none; the local sc-diffeomorphism half is also Chapter 10's `Polyfold.EpFunctor.isLocalScDiffeo_mor` (Findings, item 70).

**V11.34 (Lemma 11.6.2 (2017: 11.8), the fibre as a translation groupoid; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.lemma_11_6_2`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.Fiber`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.Fiber.val`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.Fiber.mk`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.fiberSMul`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.fiberSMul_val_of`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.instMulActionFiber`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.smul_val_of`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.FiberFull`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.Translation`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.toTranslation`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.bijective_toTranslation_obj`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.full_toTranslation`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.faithful_toTranslation`).** For a proper covering functor $F : Y \to X$ and an object $x$, $g * y = t(\alpha^{-1}(g, y))$ is an action of the isotropy group $G_x$ on $Y_x = F^{-1}(x)$ ((11.15)); the functor from the full subcategory $Y(x)$ on $Y_x$ to the translation groupoid $G_x \ltimes Y_x$ which is the identity on objects and $\psi \mapsto (F(\psi), s(\psi))$ on morphisms is bijective on objects, full and faithful, hence an isomorphism of categories and an equivalence. *Book:* the action, p. 550, and Lemma 11.6.2, p. 551 (2017: Lemma 11.8, p. 402). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* "naturally identified" is read as this functor, an isomorphism of categories, as the text says before the lemma; the topology of $Y(x)$ plays no part. In the computation of $\alpha(\psi_2 \circ \psi_1)$ on p. 550 the second factor is printed $(F(\psi_2), s(\psi_1))$; we read $(F(\psi_1), s(\psi_1))$ (possible misprint) (Findings, item 71).

**V11.35 (Lemma 11.6.3 (2017: 11.9), transport of fibres along a morphism; `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.lemma_11_6_3`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.transportFiber`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.transportFiber_val_of`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.transportFiber_inv_transportFiber`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.bijective_transportFiber`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.transportFiber_smul`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.translationMap`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.conjIsotropy`).** A morphism $\varphi : x \to x'$ of $X$ induces the bijection $B_\varphi : Y_x \to Y_{x'}$, $B_\varphi(y) = t(\psi)$ for $F(\psi) = \varphi$, $s(\psi) = y$, with inverse $B_{\varphi^{-1}}$, equivariant along $\gamma_\varphi(g) = \varphi \circ g \circ \varphi^{-1}$ ((11.16)); and $\tilde\varphi : G_x \ltimes Y_x \to G_{x'} \ltimes Y_{x'}$, $(g, y) \mapsto (\varphi \circ g \circ \varphi^{-1}, B_\varphi(y))$, is a functor bijective on objects, full and faithful, an equivalence. *Book:* Lemma 11.6.3, p. 551 (2017: Lemma 11.9, p. 403), with its proof, pp. 551–552. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none (Findings, item 71).

**V11.36 (Definition 11.6.4 (2017: 11.6), functors and equivalences between proper coverings; `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.ext`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.mapsTo_fiber`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.id`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.comp`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.IsFiberBijective`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.IsEquivalence`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.IsEquivalence.id`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.IsEquivalence.comp`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.isFiberBijective_of_isEquivalence`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.isEquivalence_iff`, `Polyfold.CoveringEquivalence.Examples.pairToPointCovering`, `Polyfold.CoveringEquivalence.Examples.isEquivalence_pairToPointCovering`).** (1) An sc-smooth functor $(\Psi, \Phi) : F \to F'$ between functors $F : Y \to X$, $F' : Y' \to X'$ is a pair of sc-smooth functors $\Psi : Y \to Y'$, $\Phi : X \to X'$ with $\Phi \circ F = F' \circ \Psi$ on objects and on morphisms; $\Psi$ then maps $Y_x$ into $Y'_{\Phi(x)}$; identities and composites are such pairs. (2) It is an equivalence if $\Psi$ and $\Phi$ are equivalences and $\Psi$ maps $Y_x$ bijectively onto $Y'_{\Phi(x)}$ for every $x$; identities and composites of equivalences are equivalences. If $F$ and $F'$ are proper covering functors, the fibre condition follows from the other two, so that $(\Psi, \Phi)$ is an equivalence if and only if $\Psi$ and $\Phi$ are. The pair $(\mathbb Z\text{-pair} \to \mathrm{pt}, \mathbb Z\text{-pair} \to \mathrm{pt})$ between the identity coverings is an equivalence, though it has no inverse functor. *Book:* Definition 11.6.4, p. 553 (2017: Definition 11.6, p. 404). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* the redundancy of the fibre condition for proper coverings is added; the text's remark after the definition treats the fibre bijection as defining a subclass of the functors of (1) (Findings, item 72). *Proof:* injectivity from the faithfulness of $\Phi$ and unique lifting along $F$; surjectivity from the essential surjectivity of $\Psi$, the fullness of $\Phi$ and unique lifting along $F'$.

**V11.37 (Definition 11.6.5 (2017: 11.7), natural transformations between functors of proper coverings; `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.NatTrans`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.NaturallyEquivalent`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.NatTrans.naturality_F`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.NatTrans.refl`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.NatTrans.symm`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.NatTrans.trans`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.NatTrans.whiskerLeft`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.NatTrans.whiskerRight`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.naturallyEquivalent_equivalence`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.NaturallyEquivalent.comp_left`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.NaturallyEquivalent.comp_right`, `Polyfold.CoveringEquivalence.Examples.naturallyEquivalent_pairToPointCovering`).** A natural transformation $(\zeta, \xi) \to (\zeta', \xi')$ is a pair of natural transformations $\tau_Y : \zeta \to \zeta'$, $\tau_X : \xi \to \xi'$ of ep-groupoids with $\tau_X(F(y)) = F'(\tau_Y(y))$ for every $y$ ((11.20)); then $\tau_X(x_2) \circ \xi(F(\psi)) = \xi'(F(\psi)) \circ \tau_X(x_1)$ for $\psi : y_1 \to y_2$, $x_i = F(y_i)$ (the diagram after the definition). Natural equivalence, the existence of one, is an equivalence relation compatible with composition on both sides. *Book:* Definition 11.6.5, p. 554 (2017: Definition 11.7, p. 405), and the diagram on p. 555. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* $\tau_X \circ F = F' \circ \tau_Y$ is read objectwise (Findings, item 73).

**V11.38 (Theorem 11.6.6 (2017: 11.10) (1), $H$ is a proper covering functor, with steps (A)–(C); `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.hFunctor`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.hObj`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.hMor`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.mor_conj`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.hMor_src`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.hMor_tgt`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.surjective_hObj`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.isLocalScDiffeo_hObj`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.isScDiffeo_fibredMap_hFunctor`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.finite_fiber_hObj`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.isProperMap_hObj`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.isProperCovering_hFunctor_of`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.restrictTarget`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.evenlyCovered_of_isProperMap`, `Polyfold.EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.isProperMap`).** For proper covering functors $F : Y \to X$, $F' : Y' \to X'$, $F'' : Y'' \to X''$, functors $\Gamma = (\Psi, \Phi) : F \to F'$, $(\zeta, \xi) : F'' \to F'$ and admissible weak fibred products $P = Y \times_{Y'} Y''$, $Q = X \times_{X'} X''$, the maps $H(y, \psi', y'') = (F(y), F'(\psi'), F''(y''))$ and $H(h, \psi', h'') = (F(h), F'(\psi'), F''(h''))$ ((11.18), (11.19)) form a functor $H : P \to Q$; if $\Psi$ and $\Phi$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms on objects and $\Psi$ maps each $Y_x$ onto $Y'_{\Phi(x)}$, then $H$ is a proper covering functor: (A) surjective and a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, (B) its map $\alpha$ an sc-diffeomorphism onto the fibred product, (C) with finite fibres and proper on objects, hence evenly covered. A proper covering functor is a proper map on objects, and a proper local sc-diffeomorphism with a finite fibre is evenly covered near it. *Book:* Theorem 11.6.6 (1), p. 555 (2017: Theorem 11.10, p. 405), and steps (A)–(C) of its proof, pp. 556–560. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (stronger):* (1) is proved under the weaker hypotheses stated; step (C) is proved through properness instead of the text's argument with sequences. The heading of step (A) has the two weak fibred products in the reverse order, "maps $X \times_{X'} X''$ onto $Y \times_{Y'} Y''$"; we read $Y \times_{Y'} Y''$ onto $X \times_{X'} X''$ (possible misprint) (Findings, item 74).

**V11.39 (Theorem 11.6.6 (2017: 11.10), the weak fibred product of proper coverings; `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.theorem_11_6_6`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.projLeftHom`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.projRightHom`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.natTransProj`, `Polyfold.CoveringEquivalence.Examples.theorem_11_6_6_pairToPoint`, `Polyfold.CoveringEquivalence.Examples.nonempty_fiber_id`, `Polyfold.WeakFibredProduct.isEquivalence_projRight`, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isTame`).** Let $F$, $F'$, $F''$ be proper covering functors, $\Gamma = (\Psi, \Phi) : F \to F'$ an equivalence and $(\zeta, \xi) : F'' \to F'$ an sc-smooth functor between them, with $P$, $Q$, $H$ as in V11.38. Then (1) $H$ is a proper covering functor; (2) $(\pi_{Y''}, \pi_{X''}) : H \to F''$ is an equivalence; (3) $(\Psi \circ \pi_Y, \Phi \circ \pi_X)$ and $(\zeta \circ \pi_{Y''}, \xi \circ \pi_{X''})$ are naturally equivalent, through $\tau_P(y, \psi', y'') = \psi'$, $\tau_Q(x, \varphi', x'') = \varphi'$; if $X''$ is tame, $P$ and $Q$ are tame; if $(\zeta, \xi)$ is an equivalence, so is $(\pi_Y, \pi_X) : H \to F$. Witness: the equivalence $\mathbb Z\text{-pair} \to \mathrm{pt}$ of identity coverings and the identity of the identity covering of the point satisfy the hypotheses, with $P$ nonempty. *Book:* Theorem 11.6.6, p. 555 (2017: Theorem 11.10, p. 405), with steps (D)–(F) of its proof, pp. 560–561. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* in (D) the fibre bijection of $\pi_{Y''}$ comes from V11.36 instead of a direct check; the tameness of $Y''$, "trivial" in the text, is that of a surjective local sc-diffeomorphism onto a tame M-polyfold (Findings, item 74).

**V11.40 (the category $\mathcal{PC}$ and Definition 11.6.7 (2017: 11.8), diagrams and common refinements; `Polyfold.PC`, `Polyfold.PC.equivalences`, `Polyfold.ProperCoveringHom.comp_assoc`, `Polyfold.PC.fibred`, `Polyfold.PC.fibredFst`, `Polyfold.PC.fibredSnd`, `Polyfold.PC.Diagram`, `Polyfold.PC.Diagram.CommonRefinement`, `Polyfold.PC.Diagram.HasCommonRefinement`, `Polyfold.PC.Examples.pair`, `Polyfold.PC.Examples.point`, `Polyfold.PC.Examples.equivalences_pairToPoint`, `Polyfold.PC.Examples.diagram`, `Polyfold.PC.Examples.fibredPair`, `Polyfold.PC.Examples.isEquivalence_fibredFst`, `Polyfold.PC.Examples.diagram'`).** Proper covering functors (in one universe) and the functors of Definition 11.6.4 (1) form a category $\mathcal{PC}$, with composition associative on the nose and a multiplicative class $E_{\mathcal{PC}}$ of equivalences; Theorem 11.6.6 (1) gives the weak fibred product as an object of $\mathcal{PC}$ with its two projections. A diagram $d : F \to F'$ is $F \xleftarrow{\Gamma} A \xrightarrow{\varepsilon} F'$ with $\Gamma$ an equivalence of proper coverings; a common refinement of $d$, $d'$ consists of equivalences $H : A'' \to A$, $H' : A'' \to A'$ with $\Gamma \circ H \simeq \Gamma' \circ H'$ and $\varepsilon \circ H \simeq \varepsilon' \circ H'$. Witnesses: $\mathrm{pair} \leftarrow \mathrm{pair} \to \mathrm{point}$ and $\mathrm{pair} \leftarrow \mathrm{pair} \times_{\mathrm{point}} \mathrm{pair} \to \mathrm{point}$. *Book:* the category $\mathcal{PC}$ and its diagrams, p. 561, and Definition 11.6.7, p. 561 (2017: Definition 11.8, p. 410). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* all proper coverings of $\mathcal{PC}$ are in one universe, so that weak fibred products stay in $\mathcal{PC}$ (Findings, item 75).

**V11.41 (Proposition 11.6.8 (2017: 11.8), common refinements are transitive; `Polyfold.PC.proposition_11_6_8`, `Polyfold.PC.Diagram.hasCommonRefinement_equivalence`, `Polyfold.PC.Examples.hasCommonRefinement_diagram`, `Polyfold.PC.Examples.hasCommonRefinement_diagram_diagram`).** If $d, d'$ and $d', d''$ have common refinements, so have $d, d''$; having a common refinement is an equivalence relation on diagrams $F \to F'$. The two witness diagrams of V11.40 have a common refinement, built from Theorem 11.6.6 (3). *Book:* Proposition 11.6.8, p. 562 (2017: Proposition 11.8, p. 411), and the sentence before it, p. 561. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the displayed chain for the $\varepsilon$'s ends at $\varepsilon' \circ K \circ \pi_{B''}$; the last step to $\varepsilon'' \circ K' \circ \pi_{B''}$ uses the assumption $\varepsilon' \circ K \simeq \varepsilon'' \circ K'$, as in the chain for the $\Gamma$'s, and is added (Findings, item 75). *Proof:* the weak fibred product $A'' \times_{A'} B''$ of $H'$ and $K$ with the equivalences $H \circ \pi_{A''}$ and $K' \circ \pi_{B''}$ (Theorem 11.6.6).

**V11.42 (Remark 11.6.9 (2017: 11.4), proper strong bundle coverings up to equivalence; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsProperStrongBundleCovering2021`, `Polyfold.SBPC`, `Polyfold.SBPC.Hom`, `Polyfold.SBPC.forget`, `Polyfold.SBPC.equivalences`, `Polyfold.SBPC.Loc`, `Polyfold.SBPC.Q`, `Polyfold.SBPC.isLocalization_Q`, `Polyfold.SBPC.lift`, `Polyfold.SBPC.uniq`, `Polyfold.SBPC.toPCLoc`, `Polyfold.SBPC.toPCLoc_fac`, `Polyfold.SBPC.toSEPLocW`, `Polyfold.SBPC.toSEPLocV`, `Polyfold.SBPC.ofSEP`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isStrongBundleIso_fibredLift_of_isProperCovering`, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.evenlyCovered_of_isStrongBundleIsoOn`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isProperStrongBundleCovering2021_of`, `Polyfold.SEP.pullbackCovering`, `Polyfold.SEP.isProperStrongBundleCovering2021_pullbackCovering`, `Polyfold.SEP.isProperStrongBundleCovering2021_pullbackCovering_of_isEquivalence`, `Polyfold.SBPC.equivalences_iff`, `Polyfold.SBPC.NatTrans`, `Polyfold.SBPC.NaturallyEquivalent`, `Polyfold.SBPC.fibred`, `Polyfold.SBPC.fibredFst`, `Polyfold.SBPC.fibredSnd`, `Polyfold.SBPC.fibredNatTrans`, `Polyfold.SBPC.theorem_11_6_6`, `Polyfold.SBPC.fibredLift`, `Polyfold.SBPC.Diagram`, `Polyfold.SBPC.Diagram.CommonRefinement`, `Polyfold.SBPC.proposition_11_6_8`, `Polyfold.SBPC.Diagram.comp`, `Polyfold.SBPC.Diagram.hasCommonRefinement_comp`, `Polyfold.SBPCLoc`, `Polyfold.SBPCLoc.I`, `Polyfold.SBPCLoc.isIso_I_map`, `Polyfold.SBPCLoc.homMk_eq`, `Polyfold.SBPCLoc.inv_homMk`, `Polyfold.SBPCLoc.fromLoc`, `Polyfold.SBPC.Examples.theorem_11_6_6_ep`).** The category SBPC: objects are strong bundle functors $A$ over a functor $F$ satisfying Definition 8.5.9 (proper strong bundle coverings, Chapter 8's `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsProperStrongBundleCovering2021`), morphisms commutative cubes of strong bundle functors; the class $E_{SBPC}$ of morphisms whose two strong bundle components are strong bundle equivalences; the localization $SBPC[E^{-1}]$ with its universal property, and the functors it induces to $\mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$ and to the localization of strong bundles. Theorem 11.6.6 for SBPC: for $\Lambda \in E_{SBPC}$ the weak fibred product of the strong bundles is a proper strong bundle covering over the weak fibred product of the bases, its second projection lies in $E_{SBPC}$, and the square commutes up to natural equivalence. $SBPC[E^{-1}]$ is described by diagrams under common refinement (Definition 11.6.7 and Proposition 11.6.8 for SBPC), $I$ inverts $E_{SBPC}$, every morphism is $I(\Gamma)^{-1} \circ I(\varepsilon)$, and the comparison functor from the universal localization commutes with $I$. Witness: the identity of $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^n$. *Book:* Remark 11.6.9, pp. 563–566 (2017: Remark 11.4, pp. 412–413). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* the text leaves the details to the reader and defines neither $E_{SBPC}$ nor natural transformations of SBPC morphisms; they are read as above and as strong bundle natural transformations on both levels whose bases satisfy (11.20). Along the way, conditions (2) and (3) of Definition 8.5.9 follow from (0) and (1) when the base functor is a proper covering (`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isProperStrongBundleCovering2021_of`) (gap G.135 closed; Findings, items 76–78).

**V11.43 (the localization $\mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$ and $I : \mathcal{PC} \to \mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$; `Polyfold.PC.fibredLift`, `Polyfold.PC.isEquivalence_fibredLift`, `Polyfold.PC.IsEquivalence.of_comp_left`, `Polyfold.PC.Diagram.comp`, `Polyfold.PC.Diagram.hasCommonRefinement_comp`, `Polyfold.PC.Diagram.hasCommonRefinement_assoc`, `Polyfold.PCLoc`, `Polyfold.PCLoc.I`, `Polyfold.PCLoc.isIso_I_map`, `Polyfold.PCLoc.homMk_eq`, `Polyfold.PCLoc.isIso_homMk`, `Polyfold.PCLoc.inv_homMk`, `Polyfold.PCLoc.Examples.not_isIso_pairToPoint_isIso_I_map`).** Classes of diagrams $F \xleftarrow{\Gamma} A \xrightarrow{\varepsilon} F'$ under common refinement are the morphisms of a category $\mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$, composed through the weak fibred products of Theorem 11.6.6; the class of the composite does not depend on the representatives, and the composition is associative and unital. $I(\varepsilon) = [F \xleftarrow{1} F \xrightarrow{\varepsilon} F']$ defines a functor $I : \mathcal{PC} \to \mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$ mapping equivalences to isomorphisms, every morphism is $I(\Gamma)^{-1} \circ I(\varepsilon)$, and a diagram whose legs are both equivalences is invertible, with inverse $[F' \xleftarrow{\varepsilon} A \xrightarrow{\Gamma} F]$. The functor from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ to the point is not an isomorphism of $\mathcal{PC}$, and its image under $I$ is one. *Book:* pp. 561–563 (2017 pp. 410–412), after Proposition 11.6.8. *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (restated):* the text leaves the well-definedness of the composition to the reader; it is proved with the common refinement of Definition 11.6.7 directly, through maps into weak fibred products built from natural transformations, which are equivalences by two out of three. The middle of the composite is $A' \times_{F'} A$, the text's $A \times_{F'} A'$ with the factors exchanged, because Theorem 11.6.6 is formalized with the equivalence on the left (gap G.134 closed; Findings, items 76, 78).

### What is not verified in this chapter

- pp. 524–525, Proposition 11.1.6 (2017: 11.2): the clause that two faces meet in a face of each does not hold as we read it; a counterexample and the corrected form, a union of faces of each, are proved instead (V11.6) (gap G.128 closed; Findings, items 6, 9).
- p. 524, Remark 11.1.5, the ordered face structures: no formal content (Findings, item 5).
- p. 542, Theorem 11.3.9 (2017: 11.7): that the boundary operations of Definition 9.3.8 satisfy `Polyfold.MPolyfold.IsBoundaryTransfer` along equivalences (it needs sc-diffeomorphisms between different M-polyfolds to preserve tame induced structures, $d_M$ and outward vectors; Chapter 9 takes the boundary operation as data, the partial cones of submanifolds not being formalized), and hence a form of the theorem independent of the representative (V11.25) (gap G.130; Findings, item 45).
- pp. 545–546, Theorems 11.4.4 and 11.4.5: listed here before 2026-11-13 (wave K) without the class hypothesis of Theorems 9.5.15 and 9.5.16 near the corners of the sheets and for $n = 1$; verified since with the text's hypotheses for every $n \ge 1$ (V11.29; gap G.131 closed; Findings, item 50). Theorems 11.4.1, 11.4.2 and Remark 11.4.3 are verified as stated since 2026-11-13 (V11.27, V11.28).
- Readings, not claims of the text: the class $E_{SBPC}$ and the natural transformations of SBPC morphisms of Remark 11.6.9, which the text does not define (V11.42; Findings, item 77).
- Witnesses: every hypothesis taken is satisfiable, and every definition has a witness (Findings, item 80).

## 13. Chapter 12 (HWZ, Part III, §§12.1–12.5 (2017 §§12.1–12.5)): begun 2026-11-13 (Part III wave 1), verified for sc-Fredholm section functors, auxiliary norms and their existence, continuous partitions of unity, the good neighbourhood theorem, bump functions and sc⁺-section functors (Theorems 12.3.2 (2) and 12.3.3 with the pointwise reading of bump functions), the local and equivariant extension from the boundary, the three compactness notions and Lemma 12.4.4, and the orientation bundle with Part I's hypotheses, except the local step of Theorem 12.2.7, the last clause of Theorem 12.5.3 and the continuity in Proposition 12.5.6 (⇐); the reflexive auxiliary norms (Definition 12.2.8 to Theorem 12.2.13), Theorem 12.3.9, Definition 12.4.3 to Theorem 12.4.6 and Theorem 12.5.7 are not yet begun

Chapter 12 (pp. 569–598; numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021), with the 2017 text's numbers in parentheses) is the Fredholm theory of Part I carried to strong bundles over ep-groupoids. §12.1 defines sc-Fredholm section functors (Definition 12.1.1 (2017: 12.1)). §12.2 defines auxiliary norms (Definition 12.2.1 (2017: 12.2)) and proves their existence (Theorem 12.2.2 (2017: 12.1)), with continuous partitions of unity (Definitions 12.2.3, 12.2.4, Proposition 12.2.5 (2017: Definitions 12.3, 12.4, Proposition 12.1)), the good neighbourhood theorem (Theorem 12.2.6 (2017: 12.2)) and the extension from the boundary (Theorem 12.2.7 (2017: 12.3)). §12.3 treats bump functions and sc⁺-section functors (Definition 12.3.1, Theorems 12.3.2, 12.3.3, Remarks 12.3.4, 12.3.5 (2017: Definition 12.7, Theorems 12.6, 12.7, Remarks 12.3, 12.4)) and the extension of sc⁺-sections from the boundary (Definition 12.3.6, Proposition 12.3.7, Corollary 12.3.8 (2017: Definition 12.8, Proposition 12.2, Corollary 12.1)). §12.4 compares compactness notions (Definition 12.4.1, Theorem 12.4.2, Lemma 12.4.4 (2017: Definition 12.9, Theorem 12.9, Lemma 12.1)). §12.5 builds the orientation bundle (Lemma 12.5.1, Definition 12.5.2, Theorem 12.5.3, Definition 12.5.4, Proposition 12.5.6 (2017: Lemma 12.2, Definition 12.11, Theorem 12.11, Definition 12.12, Proposition 12.4)). The rest of §12.2 (reflexive auxiliary norms), Theorem 12.3.9, the reflexive part of §12.4 and Theorem 12.5.7 are planned for Part III wave 2.

What is verified. §12.1 and Definition 12.2.1 are verified as stated (V12.1–V12.3). Theorem 12.2.2, Definitions 12.2.3, 12.2.4, Proposition 12.2.5 and Theorem 12.2.6 are verified as stated (V12.4–V12.8); Theorem 12.2.7 is verified with its local coordinate step as a hypothesis, the global part of the proof being formalized (V12.9; gap G.136). Definition 12.3.1 is verified as printed, with the pointwise variant kept (V12.10); Theorem 12.3.2 (1) is proved in each consistent pairing of Definition 12.3.1 with Part I's Definition 5.3.1 (V12.11); Theorem 12.3.2 (2) and Theorem 12.3.3 are verified with the pointwise reading of bump functions (V12.12, V12.13); the checkable claims of Remarks 12.3.4 and 12.3.5 are proved (V12.14, V12.15). Definition 12.3.6 is verified at chart level (V12.16; the ep-groupoid wrapper is gap G.137), Proposition 12.3.7 in a stronger form (V12.17) and Corollary 12.3.8 with the isotropy action made explicit (V12.18). §12.4 up to Lemma 12.4.4 is verified as stated (V12.19–V12.21). In §12.5 Lemma 12.5.1, Definitions 12.5.2, 12.5.4 are verified with Part I's hypothesis of sc⁺-sections through fibre points (V12.22, V12.23, V12.25); Theorem 12.5.3 is verified with Part I's hypotheses of Theorem 6.6.17, except its last clause (V12.24; gaps G.138, G.140); Proposition 12.5.6 (⇒) is verified, and (⇐) without the continuity of the lifted section (V12.26; gap G.139).

The hypotheses. `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.HasLocalExtensions` in Theorem 12.2.7, the local step of the text's proof (witness `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_7_hyp_witness`; every restriction of a global auxiliary norm satisfies it, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.hasLocalExtensions_of_isAuxNorm`). The pointwise reading of Definition 12.3.1, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.AdmitsBumpFunctionsPointwise`, in Theorems 12.3.2 (2) and 12.3.3 (witness `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.admitsBumpFunctionsPointwise_trivial_rn`). In §12.5, `Polyfold.StrongBundle.HasScPlusSectionsThrough` (a consequence of bump functions, `Polyfold.MPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctions.hasScPlusSectionsThrough`), and, in Theorem 12.5.3, the hypotheses of Part I's Theorem 6.6.17 (bump functions on the object M-polyfold and tame germ data), inherited from Part I (gap G.140). The all-charts definitions of the boundary sections have the zero section as witness (`Polyfold.isBoundaryScPlusSectionOn_zero`, `Polyfold.proposition_12_3_7_nonvacuous`), and the isotropy action of Corollary 12.3.8 the trivial action (`Polyfold.LocalBundleAction.trivial`).

The setting. Ep-groupoids, natural representations and orbit spaces are those of Chapter 7; strong bundles over ep-groupoids, section functors and auxiliary norms those of Chapter 8 (`Polyfold.EpStrongBundle`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsAuxNorm`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsScFredholmSectionFunctor`); sc⁺-sections, linearizations, the determinant bundle and the orientation space $O_f$ with its topology are Part I's (Chapters 5 and 6). Tame local strong bundle models are those of Chapter 2.

**V12.1 (Definition 12.1.1 (2017: 12.1), sc-Fredholm section functors; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.definition_12_1_1`).** `EpStrongBundle.definition_12_1_1`: `E.IsScFredholmSectionFunctor f ↔ E.IsScSmoothSectionFunctor f ∧ B.IsScFredholmSection f` (`Iff.rfl`, Definition 8.3.4 (3)). *Book:* §12.1, Definition 12.1.1, p. 569 (2017: Definition 12.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* The project's existing definition, unfolded.

**V12.2 (The remark after Definition 12.1.1: regularizing on objects and morphisms, germs; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.remark_12_1_1_regularizing_obj`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.remark_12_1_1_regularizing_mor`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.remark_12_1_1_germ`).** Objects: $x \in X_m$ and $f(x) \in W_{m,m+1}$ give $x \in X_{m+1}$ (`remark_12_1_1_regularizing_obj`). Morphisms: $\varphi \in \mathbf X_m$ and $f(\varphi) = (\varphi, f(s\varphi)) \in (\mathbf X\,{}_s\!\times_P W)_{m,m+1}$ give $\varphi \in \mathbf X_{m+1}$ (`remark_12_1_1_regularizing_mor`, through the pull-back projection, a strong bundle map). Germs: `IsScFredholmGerm` at each smooth $x$ (`remark_12_1_1_germ`). *Book:* §12.1, after Definition 12.1.1, p. 569 (2017: after Definition 12.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (explicit):* "$f(\varphi)$" is read as the induced section of the pull-back bundle $\mathbf X\,{}_s\!\times_P W \to \mathbf X$.

**V12.3 (Definition 12.2.1 (2017: 12.2), auxiliary norms; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.IsAuxNorm`).** The existing `EpStrongBundle.IsAuxNorm` (Definition 8.3.5): `B.IsAuxNorm N` (Definition 5.1.1: continuity, (1), (2)) and invariance under $\mu$ (3). *Book:* §12.2, Definition 12.2.1, p. 570 (2017: Definition 12.2). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* The text itself recalls Definition 8.3.5; no new declaration. Non-negativity follows from (1).

**V12.4 (Theorem 12.2.2 (2017: 12.1), existence of auxiliary norms; `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_2`, `Polyfold.SEP.theorem_12_2_2`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.avgNorm`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isLocalAuxNorm_avgNorm`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.avgNorm_actOne`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.transNorm`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isLocalAuxNorm_transNorm`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.transNorm_μ`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.glueNorm`, `Polyfold.EpStrongBundle.isAuxNorm_glueNorm`).** `EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_2 (h : X.HasParacompactOrbitSpace) : ∃ N, E.IsAuxNorm N`, and the form `SEP.theorem_12_2_2`. The proof follows the text's three steps: average a local norm over $G_x$ on $U(x)$ (`avgNorm`), transport it to the saturation (`transNorm`, invariant under all morphisms by `transNorm_μ`), glue with a partition of unity of $|X|$ (`isAuxNorm_glueNorm`). *Book:* §12.2, Theorem 12.2.2, p. 570 (proof pp. 572–574) (2017: Theorem 12.1). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* The local norm is a Part I auxiliary norm (Proposition 5.1.3) instead of a chart norm, and the transport through a chosen morphism uses the invariance under $G_x$, so Theorem 12.2.6 (5) is not needed. Completeness of the glued fibre norms comes from `StrongBundle.isAuxNorm_of_tendsto` (V12.29).

**V12.5 (Definition 12.2.3 (2017: 12.3) and the remark after it, continuous partitions of unity; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsContPartitionOfUnity`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isContPartitionOfUnity_comp_π`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsContPartitionOfUnity.descend`, `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.isSubordinate_comp_π`).** `EpGroupoid.IsContPartitionOfUnity β`, with fields `continuous`, `mem_Icc`, `map_mor`, `locallyFinite` and `sum_eq_one` (as `finsum`). Both directions of the remark: `isContPartitionOfUnity_comp_π` (Mathlib `PartitionOfUnity` on the orbit space composed with $\pi$) and `IsContPartitionOfUnity.descend` (a `PartitionOfUnity` on $|X|$ with $\beta'_i(\pi y) = \beta_i(y)$). *Book:* §12.2, Definition 12.2.3, pp. 570–571 (2017: Definition 12.3). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* The supports are closures in $X$. The paracompactness of $|X|$ in the preamble is not needed for the definition. The descent uses that $\pi$ is open (Proposition 7.1.8).

**V12.6 (Definition 12.2.4 (2017: 12.4), subordinate partitions of unity; `Polyfold.EpGroupoid.IsContPartitionOfUnity.IsSubordinate`).** `IsContPartitionOfUnity.IsSubordinate X U`: `∀ i, tsupport (β i) ⊆ U i`. *Book:* §12.2, Definition 12.2.4, p. 571 (2017: Definition 12.4). *Hidden hypotheses:* none. *Deviation (same):* none.
